49. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, bandhumassa rañño etadahosi – ‘mā heva kho vipassī kumāro na rajjaṃ kāresi, mā heva vipassī kumāro agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbaji, mā heva nemittānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ saccaṃ assa vacana’nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, bandhumā rājā vipassissa kumārassa bhiyyosomattāya pañca kāmaguṇāni upaṭṭhāpesi – ‘yathā vipassī [T 2.0029] kumāro rajjaṃ kareyya, yathā vipassī kumāro na agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya, yathā nemittānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ micchā assa vacana’nti.

49. Then, mendicants, it occurred to King Bandhumā: ‘May Prince Vipassī indeed administer the kingdom; may Prince Vipassī not go forth from the household life into homelessness; may the word of the omen-reading brahmins not be true.’ Then, mendicants, King Bandhumā provided Prince Vipassī with the five strands of sensual pleasure in greater abundance—‘so that Prince Vipassī might administer the kingdom, so that Prince Vipassī might not go forth from the household life into homelessness, so that the word of the omen-reading brahmins might be false.’

“Tatra sudaṃ, bhikkhave, vipassī kumāro pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī kumāro bahūnaṃ vassānaṃ…pe…

There, mendicants, Prince Vipassī, endowed and furnished with the five strands of sensual pleasure, enjoyed himself. Then, mendicants, after many years had passed...

50. “Addasā [M 2.0022] kho, bhikkhave, vipassī kumāro uyyānabhūmiṃ niyyanto mahājanakāyaṃ sannipatitaṃ [V 2.0020] nānārattānañca dussānaṃ vilātaṃ kayiramānaṃ. Disvā sārathiṃ āmantesi – ‘kiṃ nu kho, so, samma sārathi, mahājanakāyo sannipatito nānārattānañca dussānaṃ vilātaṃ kayiratī’ti? ‘Eso [P 2.0026] kho, deva, kālaṅkato nāmā’ti. ‘Tena hi, samma sārathi, yena so kālaṅkato tena rathaṃ pesehī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, sārathi vipassissa kumārassa paṭissutvā yena so kālaṅkato tena rathaṃ pesesi. Addasā kho, bhikkhave, vipassī kumāro petaṃ kālaṅkataṃ, disvā sārathiṃ āmantesi – ‘kiṃ panāyaṃ, samma sārathi, kālaṅkato nāmā’ti? ‘Eso kho, deva, kālaṅkato nāma. Na dāni taṃ dakkhanti mātā vā pitā vā aññe vā ñātisālohitā, sopi na dakkhissati mātaraṃ vā pitaraṃ vā aññe vā ñātisālohite’ti. ‘Kiṃ pana, samma sārathi, ahampi maraṇadhammo maraṇaṃ anatīto; mampi na dakkhanti devo vā devī vā aññe vā ñātisālohitā; ahampi na dakkhissāmi devaṃ vā deviṃ vā aññe vā ñātisālohite’ti? ‘Tvañca, deva, mayañcamha sabbe maraṇadhammā maraṇaṃ anatītā; tampi na dakkhanti devo vā devī vā aññe [T 2.0030] vā ñātisālohitā; tvampi na dakkhissasi devaṃ vā deviṃ vā aññe vā ñātisālohite’ti. ‘Tena hi, samma sārathi, alaṃ dānajja uyyānabhūmiyā, itova antepuraṃ paccaniyyāhī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, sārathi vipassissa kumārassa paṭissutvā tatova antepuraṃ paccaniyyāsi. Tatra sudaṃ, bhikkhave, vipassī kumāro antepuraṃ gato dukkhī dummano pajjhāyati – ‘dhiratthu kira, bho, jāti nāma, yatra hi nāma jātassa jarā paññāyissati, byādhi paññāyissati, maraṇaṃ paññāyissatī’ti.

50. Mendicants, Prince Vipassī, while proceeding to the pleasure garden, saw a great crowd assembled and a bier being made with various colored cloths. Seeing this, he addressed the charioteer: ‘Why, good charioteer, is this great crowd assembled, and why is a bier being made with various colored cloths?’ ‘That, sire, is what is called a dead person.’ ‘Then, good charioteer, drive the chariot to where that dead person is.’ ‘Yes, sire,’ replied the charioteer to Prince Vipassī, and he drove the chariot to where that dead person was. Mendicants, Prince Vipassī saw the departed, dead person. Seeing him, he addressed the charioteer: ‘But what, good charioteer, is this called a dead person?’ ‘That, sire, is called a dead person. Now neither his mother nor his father nor any other relatives will see him, nor will he see his mother, his father, or any other relatives.’ ‘But, good charioteer, am I too subject to death, not exempt from death? Will neither the king nor the queen nor any other relatives see me, nor will I see the king, the queen, or any other relatives?’ ‘You, sire, and we too—all are subject to death, not exempt from death. Neither the king nor the queen nor any other relatives will see you, nor will you see the king, the queen, or any other relatives.’ ‘Then, good charioteer, enough of the pleasure garden for today. Return to the inner palace from here.’ ‘Yes, sire,’ replied the charioteer to Prince Vipassī, and he returned to the inner palace from there. There, mendicants, Prince Vipassī, having gone to the inner palace, was sorrowful and dejected, and he pondered: ‘Contemptible indeed is this thing called birth, since for one who is born, aging will become apparent, sickness will become apparent, and death will become apparent.’

51. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, bandhumā rājā sārathiṃ āmantāpetvā etadavoca – ‘kacci, samma sārathi, kumāro uyyānabhūmiyā abhiramittha, kacci, samma sārathi, kumāro uyyānabhūmiyā attamano ahosī’ti? ‘Na [P 2.0027] kho, deva, kumāro uyyānabhūmiyā abhiramittha, na kho, deva, kumāro uyyānabhūmiyā attamano ahosī’ti. ‘Kiṃ pana, samma sārathi, addasa kumāro uyyānabhūmiṃ niyyanto’ti? ‘Addasā kho, deva, kumāro uyyānabhūmiṃ niyyanto mahājanakāyaṃ sannipatitaṃ nānārattānañca dussānaṃ vilātaṃ kayiramānaṃ. Disvā maṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, so[M 2.0023], samma sārathi, mahājanakāyo sannipatito nānārattānañca dussānaṃ vilātaṃ kayiratī”ti? “Eso kho, deva, kālaṅkato nāmā”ti. “Tena hi, samma sārathi, yena so kālaṅkato tena rathaṃ pesehī”ti. “Evaṃ devā”ti kho ahaṃ, deva, vipassissa kumārassa paṭissutvā yena so [T 2.0031] kālaṅkato tena rathaṃ pesesiṃ. Addasā kho, deva, kumāro petaṃ kālaṅkataṃ, disvā maṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ panāyaṃ, samma sārathi, kālaṅkato nāmā”ti[V 2.0021]? “Eso kho, deva, kālaṅkato nāma. Na dāni taṃ dakkhanti mātā vā pitā vā aññe vā ñātisālohitā, sopi na dakkhissati mātaraṃ vā pitaraṃ vā aññe vā ñātisālohite”ti. “Kiṃ pana, samma sārathi, ahampi maraṇadhammo maraṇaṃ anatīto; mampi na dakkhanti devo vā devī vā aññe vā ñātisālohitā; ahampi na dakkhissāmi devaṃ vā deviṃ vā aññe vā ñātisālohite”ti? “Tvañca, deva, mayañcamha sabbe maraṇadhammā maraṇaṃ anatītā; tampi na dakkhanti devo vā devī vā aññe vā ñātisālohitā, tvampi na dakkhissasi devaṃ vā deviṃ vā aññe vā ñātisālohite”ti. “Tena hi, samma sārathi, alaṃ dānajja uyyānabhūmiyā, itova antepuraṃ paccaniyyāhī’ti. “‘Evaṃ, devā”ti kho ahaṃ, deva, vipassissa kumārassa paṭissutvā tatova antepuraṃ paccaniyyāsiṃ. So kho, deva, kumāro antepuraṃ gato dukkhī dummano pajjhāyati – “dhiratthu kira bho jāti nāma, yatra hi nāma jātassa jarā paññāyissati, byādhi paññāyissati, maraṇaṃ paññāyissatī’”ti.

51. Then, monks, King Bandhuma had the charioteer summoned and said this: ‘Good charioteer, did the prince enjoy himself in the pleasure park? Good charioteer, was the prince pleased in the pleasure park?’ ‘No, sire, the prince did not enjoy himself in the pleasure park. No, sire, the prince was not pleased in the pleasure park.’ ‘But what, good charioteer, did the prince see while proceeding to the pleasure park?’ ‘Sire, while proceeding to the pleasure park, the prince saw a great crowd assembled and a bier being made with cloths of various colors. Seeing this, he said this to me: “Why, good charioteer, is this great crowd assembled, and why is a bier being made with cloths of various colors?” “That, sire, is what is called a dead person.” “Then, good charioteer, drive the chariot to where that dead person is.” “Yes, sire,” I replied to Prince Vipassī, and I drove the chariot to where that dead person was. Sire, the prince saw the departed, dead person. Seeing him, he said this to me: “But what, good charioteer, is this thing called a ‘dead person’?” “That, sire, is called a dead person. Now neither his mother nor his father nor any other relatives will see him, nor will he see his mother, his father, or any other relatives.” “But, good charioteer, am I too subject to death, not exempt from death? Will neither the king nor the queen nor any other relatives see me, nor will I see the king, the queen, or any other relatives?” “You, sire, and we too—all are subject to death, not exempt from death. Neither the king nor the queen nor any other relatives will see you, nor will you see the king, the queen, or any other relatives.” “Then, good charioteer, enough of the pleasure park for today. Return to the inner palace from here.” “Yes, sire,” I replied to Prince Vipassī, and I returned to the inner palace from there. Sire, that prince, having gone to the inner palace, is sorrowful and dejected, and he ponders: “Alas, truly wretched is this thing called birth, since for one who is born, aging will become apparent, sickness will become apparent, and death will become apparent.”’

Pabbajito

The Renunciant

52. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, bandhumassa rañño etadahosi – ‘mā heva kho vipassī kumāro na rajjaṃ kāresi, mā heva vipassī kumāro agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbaji, mā [P 2.0028] heva nemittānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ saccaṃ assa vacana’nti. Atha [T 2.0032] kho, bhikkhave, bandhumā rājā vipassissa kumārassa bhiyyosomattāya pañca kāmaguṇāni upaṭṭhāpesi – ‘yathā vipassī kumāro rajjaṃ kareyya, yathā vipassī kumāro na agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajeyya, yathā nemittānaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ micchā assa vacana’nti.

52. Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to King Bandhuma: ‘May it not be that Prince Vipassī fails to rule the kingdom; may it not be that Prince Vipassī goes forth from the household life into homelessness; may it not be that the words of the omen-reading brahmins prove true.’ Then, bhikkhus, King Bandhuma provided for Prince Vipassī the five strands of sensual pleasure in even greater measure, thinking: ‘So that Prince Vipassī might rule the kingdom, so that Prince Vipassī might not go forth from the household life into homelessness, so that the words of the omen-reading brahmins might prove false.’”

“Tatra sudaṃ, bhikkhave, vipassī kumāro pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī kumāro bahūnaṃ vassānaṃ [M 2.0024] bahūnaṃ vassasatānaṃ bahūnaṃ vassasahassānaṃ accayena sārathiṃ āmantesi – ‘yojehi, samma sārathi, bhaddāni bhaddāni yānāni, uyyānabhūmiṃ gacchāma subhūmidassanāyā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, sārathi vipassissa kumārassa paṭissutvā bhaddāni bhaddāni yānāni yojetvā vipassissa kumārassa paṭivedesi – ‘yuttāni kho te, deva, bhaddāni bhaddāni yānāni, yassa dāni kālaṃ maññasī’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī kumāro bhaddaṃ bhaddaṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhaddehi bhaddehi yānehi uyyānabhūmiṃ niyyāsi.

There, bhikkhus, Prince Vipassī enjoyed himself, being endowed and furnished with the five strands of sensual pleasure. Then, bhikkhus, after the passing of many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, Prince Vipassī addressed his charioteer: ‘Harness the excellent carriages, my dear charioteer, let us go to the park-land to see the beautiful grounds.’ ‘So be it, Your Highness,’ the charioteer, having assented to Prince Vipassī, harnessed the excellent carriages and informed Prince Vipassī: ‘The excellent carriages are harnessed for you, Your Highness; now is the time for whatever you deem fit.’ Then, bhikkhus, Prince Vipassī mounted an excellent carriage and set out for the park-land with excellent carriages.

53. “Addasā [V 2.0022] kho, bhikkhave, vipassī kumāro uyyānabhūmiṃ niyyanto purisaṃ bhaṇḍuṃ pabbajitaṃ kāsāyavasanaṃ. Disvā sārathiṃ āmantesi – ‘ayaṃ pana, samma sārathi, puriso kiṃkato? Sīsaṃpissa na yathā aññesaṃ, vatthānipissa na yathā aññesa’nti? ‘Eso kho, deva, pabbajito nāmā’ti. ‘Kiṃ paneso, samma sārathi, pabbajito nāmā’ti? ‘Eso kho, deva, pabbajito nāma sādhu dhammacariyā sādhu samacariyā sammacariyā (ka.) sādhu kusalakiriyā kusalacariyā (syā.) sādhu puññakiriyā sādhu avihiṃsā sādhu bhūtānukampā’ti. ‘Sādhu kho so, samma sārathi, pabbajito nāma, sādhu [P 2.0029] dhammacariyā sādhu samacariyā sādhu [T 2.0033] kusalakiriyā sādhu puññakiriyā sādhu avihiṃsā sādhu bhūtānukampā. Tena hi, samma sārathi, yena so pabbajito tena rathaṃ pesehī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, sārathi vipassissa kumārassa paṭissutvā yena so pabbajito tena rathaṃ pesesi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī kumāro taṃ pabbajitaṃ etadavoca – ‘tvaṃ pana, samma, kiṃkato, sīsampi te na yathā aññesaṃ, vatthānipi te na yathā aññesa’nti? ‘Ahaṃ kho, deva, pabbajito nāmā’ti. ‘Kiṃ pana tvaṃ, samma, pabbajito nāmā’ti? ‘Ahaṃ kho, deva, pabbajito nāma, sādhu dhammacariyā sādhu samacariyā sādhu kusalakiriyā sādhu puññakiriyā sādhu avihiṃsā sādhu bhūtānukampā’ti. ‘Sādhu kho tvaṃ, samma, pabbajito nāma sādhu dhammacariyā sādhu samacariyā sādhu kusalakiriyā sādhu puññakiriyā sādhu avihiṃsā sādhu bhūtānukampā’ti.

53. Indeed, bhikkhus, as Prince Vipassī was going out to the park-land, he saw a man who was shaven-headed, a renunciant, wearing ochre-dyed robes. Seeing him, he addressed the charioteer: ‘What has been done to this man, my dear charioteer? His head is not like that of others, and his clothes are not like that of others.’ ‘Your Highness, this is one called a renunciant.’ ‘But what, my dear charioteer, is one called a renunciant?’ ‘Your Highness, this is one called a renunciant, who holds that practicing the Dhamma is good, practicing right conduct is good, performing skillful actions is good, performing meritorious actions is good, non-harming is good, and compassion for beings is good.’ ‘Good indeed, my dear charioteer, is one called a renunciant. Good is the practice of Dhamma, good is right conduct, good is performing skillful actions, good is performing meritorious actions, good is non-harming, and good is compassion for beings. If so, my dear charioteer, drive the chariot to where that renunciant is.’ ‘So be it, Your Highness,’ the charioteer, having assented to Prince Vipassī, drove the chariot to where that renunciant was. Then, bhikkhus, Prince Vipassī said this to that renunciant: ‘What has been done to you, my friend? Your head is not like that of others, and your clothes are not like that of others.’ ‘Your Highness, I am one called a renunciant.’ ‘But what does it mean, my friend, to be one called a renunciant?’ ‘Your Highness, I am one called a renunciant, who holds that practicing the Dhamma is good, practicing right conduct is good, performing skillful actions is good, performing meritorious actions is good, non-harming is good, and compassion for beings is good.’ ‘Good indeed, my friend, are you, one called a renunciant. Good is the practice of Dhamma, good is right conduct, good is performing skillful actions, good is performing meritorious actions, good is non-harming, and good is compassion for beings.’”

Bodhisattapabbajjā

The Bodhisatta's Going Forth

54. “Atha [M 2.0025] kho, bhikkhave, vipassī kumāro sārathiṃ āmantesi – ‘tena hi, samma sārathi, rathaṃ ādāya itova antepuraṃ paccaniyyāhi. Ahaṃ pana idheva kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, sārathi vipassissa [T 2.0034] kumārassa paṭissutvā rathaṃ ādāya tatova antepuraṃ paccaniyyāsi. Vipassī pana kumāro tattheva kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbaji.

54. Then, bhikkhus, Prince Vipassī addressed the charioteer: ‘If so, my dear charioteer, take the chariot and return from this very place to the inner palace. As for me, right here I will shave off my hair and beard, put on ochre-dyed robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness.’ ‘So be it, Your Highness,’ the charioteer, having assented to Prince Vipassī, took the chariot and returned from that very place to the inner palace. Prince Vipassī, however, right there, shaved off his hair and beard, put on ochre-dyed robes, and went forth from the household life into homelessness.

Mahājanakāyaanupabbajjā

The Great Multitude's Following in Going Forth

55. “Assosi kho, bhikkhave, bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā mahājanakāyo caturāsīti pāṇasahassāni – ‘vipassī kira kumāro kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā [V 2.0023][P 2.0030] agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito’ti. Sutvāna tesaṃ etadahosi – ‘na hi nūna so orako dhammavinayo, na sā orakā orikā (sī. syā.) pabbajjā, yattha vipassī kumāro kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. Vipassīpi nāma kumāro kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissati, kimaṅgaṃ kimaṅga (sī.) pana maya’nti.

55. Bhikkhus, in the royal capital of Bandhumatī, a great multitude of eighty-four thousand beings heard: ‘Prince Vipassī, it is said, has shaved off his hair and beard, put on ochre-dyed robes, and gone forth from the household life into homelessness.’ Having heard this, the thought occurred to them: ‘Surely, that cannot be an inferior Dhamma and Discipline, that cannot be an inferior going forth, wherein Prince Vipassī has shaved off his hair and beard, put on ochre-dyed robes, and gone forth from the household life into homelessness. If even Prince Vipassī would shave off his hair and beard, put on ochre-dyed robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness, what then of us?’”

“Atha kho, so bhikkhave, mahājanakāyo mahājanakāyo (syā.) caturāsīti pāṇasahassāni kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā vipassiṃ bodhisattaṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitaṃ anupabbajiṃsu. Tāya sudaṃ, bhikkhave, parisāya parivuto vipassī bodhisatto gāmanigamajanapadarājadhānīsu cārikaṃ carati.

Then, bhikkhus, that great multitude of eighty-four thousand beings shaved off their hair and beard, put on ochre-dyed robes, and went forth in imitation of the Bodhisatta Vipassī, who had gone forth from the household life into homelessness. Surrounded by that assembly, bhikkhus, the Bodhisatta Vipassī wandered on tour among villages, market towns, country districts, and royal capitals.

56. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘na kho metaṃ na kho panetaṃ (syā.) patirūpaṃ yohaṃ ākiṇṇo viharāmi, yaṃnūnāhaṃ eko gaṇamhā vūpakaṭṭho vihareyya’nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bodhisatto aparena samayena eko [M 2.0026] gaṇamhā vūpakaṭṭho vihāsi[T 2.0035], aññeneva tāni caturāsīti pabbajitasahassāni agamaṃsu, aññena maggena vipassī bodhisatto.

56. Then, bhikkhus, while the Bodhisatta Vipassī was in a secluded place and dwelling in solitude, this thought arose in his mind: ‘It is not suitable for me to be living in a crowd. What if I were to dwell alone, withdrawn from the group?’ Then, bhikkhus, on a later occasion, the Bodhisatta Vipassī dwelt alone, withdrawn from the group. Those eighty-four thousand who had gone forth went one way, while the Bodhisatta Vipassī went another.

Bodhisattaabhiniveso

The Bodhisatta's Investigation

57. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa vāsūpagatassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘kicchaṃ vatāyaṃ loko āpanno, jāyati ca jīyati ca mīyati ca jiyyati ca miyyati ca (ka.) cavati ca upapajjati ca, atha ca panimassa dukkhassa [P 2.0031] nissaraṇaṃ nappajānāti jarāmaraṇassa, kudāssu nāma imassa dukkhassa nissaraṇaṃ paññāyissati jarāmaraṇassā’ti?

57. Then, bhikkhus, while the Bodhisatta Vipassī was in residence, having gone to a secluded place and dwelling in solitude, this reflection arose in his mind: ‘Alas, this world has fallen into hardship! It is born, grows old, dies, passes away, and is reborn. And yet, it does not know the escape from this suffering of aging and death. When, indeed, will an escape from this suffering of aging and death be discerned?’”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati jarāmaraṇaṃ hoti, kiṃpaccayā jarāmaraṇa’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘jātiyā kho sati jarāmaraṇaṃ hoti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇa’nti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists, does aging and death come to be? With what as a condition is there aging and death?’ Then, bhikkhus, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through proper attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When birth exists, aging and death come to be. With birth as a condition, there is aging and death.’”

“Atha [V 2.0024] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati jāti hoti, kiṃpaccayā jātī’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘bhave kho sati jāti hoti, bhavapaccayā jātī’ti.

Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists, does birth come to be? With what as a condition is there birth?’ Then, bhikkhus, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through proper attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When becoming exists, birth comes to be. With becoming as a condition, there is birth.’”

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati bhavo hoti, kiṃpaccayā bhavo’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘upādāne kho sati bhavo hoti, upādānapaccayā bhavo’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists, does becoming come to be? With what as a condition is there becoming?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through proper attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When there is clinging, becoming comes to be. With clinging as a condition, there is becoming.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati upādānaṃ hoti, kiṃpaccayā [T 2.0036] upādāna’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘taṇhāya kho sati upādānaṃ hoti, taṇhāpaccayā upādāna’nti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists, does clinging come to be? With what as a condition is there clinging?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through proper attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When there is craving, clinging comes to be. With craving as a condition, there is clinging.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati taṇhā hoti, kiṃpaccayā taṇhā’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa [M 2.0027] bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘vedanāya kho sati taṇhā hoti, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists, does craving come to be? With what as a condition is there craving?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through proper attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When there is feeling, craving comes to be. With feeling as a condition, there is craving.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati vedanā hoti, kiṃpaccayā vedanā’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa [P 2.0032] yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘phasse kho sati vedanā hoti, phassapaccayā vedanā’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists, does feeling come to be? With what as a condition is there feeling?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through proper attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When there is contact, feeling comes to be. With contact as a condition, there is feeling.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati phasso hoti, kiṃpaccayā phasso’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘saḷāyatane kho sati phasso hoti, saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists, does contact come to be? With what as a condition is there contact?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through proper attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When there are the six sense bases, contact comes to be. With the six sense bases as a condition, there is contact.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati saḷāyatanaṃ [V 2.0025] hoti, kiṃpaccayā saḷāyatana’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘nāmarūpe kho sati saḷāyatanaṃ hoti, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatana’nti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists, do the six sense bases come to be? With what as a condition are there the six sense bases?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through proper attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When there is name-and-form, the six sense bases come to be. With name-and-form as a condition, there are the six sense bases.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati nāmarūpaṃ hoti, kiṃpaccayā nāmarūpa’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa [T 2.0037] bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘viññāṇe kho sati nāmarūpaṃ hoti, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpa’nti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists, does name-and-form come to be? With what as a condition is there name-and-form?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through proper attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When there is consciousness, name-and-form comes to be. With consciousness as a condition, there is name-and-form.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho sati viññāṇaṃ hoti, kiṃpaccayā viññāṇa’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘nāmarūpe kho sati viññāṇaṃ hoti, nāmarūpapaccayā viññāṇa’nti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what exists, does consciousness come to be? With what as a condition is there consciousness?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through proper attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When there is name-and-form, consciousness comes to be. With name-and-form as a condition, there is consciousness.’

58. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘paccudāvattati kho idaṃ viññāṇaṃ nāmarūpamhā, nāparaṃ gacchati. Ettāvatā jāyetha [M 2.0028] vā jiyyetha vā miyyetha vā cavetha vā upapajjetha vā, yadidaṃ nāmarūpapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ, saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā[P 2.0033], taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti’.

58. Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘This consciousness turns back from name-and-form; it does not go beyond. To this extent one might be born, grow old, die, pass away, or be reborn—that is to say: with name-and-form as a condition, consciousness comes to be; with consciousness as a condition, name-and-form comes to be; with name-and-form as a condition, the six sense bases come to be; with the six sense bases as a condition, contact comes to be; with contact as a condition, feeling comes to be; with feeling as a condition, craving comes to be; with craving as a condition, clinging comes to be; with clinging as a condition, becoming comes to be; with becoming as a condition, birth comes to be; with birth as a condition, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come to be. Thus is the origination of this entire mass of suffering.’

59. “‘Samudayo samudayo’ti kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

59. ‘Origination, origination!’—thus, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, in regard to phenomena unheard before, vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, light arose.

60. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati jarāmaraṇaṃ na hoti, kissa nirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo [T 2.0038] – ‘jātiyā kho asati jarāmaraṇaṃ na hoti, jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇanirodho’ti.

60. Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does aging and death not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of aging and death occur?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When birth does not exist, aging and death do not occur; with the cessation of birth, there is the cessation of aging and death.’

“Atha [V 2.0026] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati jāti na hoti, kissa nirodhā jātinirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘bhave kho asati jāti na hoti, bhavanirodhā jātinirodho’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does birth not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of birth occur?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When becoming does not exist, birth does not occur; with the cessation of becoming, there is the cessation of birth.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati bhavo na hoti, kissa nirodhā bhavanirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘upādāne kho asati bhavo na hoti, upādānanirodhā bhavanirodho’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does becoming not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of becoming occur?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When clinging does not exist, becoming does not occur; with the cessation of clinging, there is the cessation of becoming.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati upādānaṃ na hoti, kissa nirodhā upādānanirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu [M 2.0029] paññāya abhisamayo – ‘taṇhāya kho asati upādānaṃ na hoti, taṇhānirodhā upādānanirodho’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does clinging not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of clinging occur?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When craving does not exist, clinging does not occur; with the cessation of craving, there is the cessation of clinging.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati taṇhā na hoti, kissa nirodhā taṇhānirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo [P 2.0034] – ‘vedanāya kho asati taṇhā na hoti, vedanānirodhā taṇhānirodho’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does craving not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of craving occur?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When feeling does not exist, craving does not occur; with the cessation of feeling, there is the cessation of craving.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati vedanā na hoti, kissa nirodhā vedanānirodho’ti? Atha [T 2.0039] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘phasse kho asati vedanā na hoti, phassanirodhā vedanānirodho’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does feeling not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of feeling occur?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When contact does not exist, feeling does not occur; with the cessation of contact, there is the cessation of feeling.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati phasso na hoti, kissa nirodhā phassanirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘saḷāyatane kho asati phasso na hoti, saḷāyatananirodhā phassanirodho’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does contact not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of contact occur?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When the six sense bases do not exist, contact does not occur; with the cessation of the six sense bases, there is the cessation of contact.’

“Atha [V 2.0027] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati saḷāyatanaṃ na hoti, kissa nirodhā saḷāyatananirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘nāmarūpe kho asati saḷāyatanaṃ na hoti, nāmarūpanirodhā saḷāyatananirodho’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, do the six sense bases not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of the six sense bases occur?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When name-and-form do not exist, the six sense bases do not occur; with the cessation of name-and-form, there is the cessation of the six sense bases.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati nāmarūpaṃ na hoti, kissa nirodhā nāmarūpanirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu paññāya abhisamayo – ‘viññāṇe kho asati nāmarūpaṃ na hoti, viññāṇanirodhā nāmarūpanirodho’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does name-and-form not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of name-and-form occur?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When consciousness does not exist, name-and-form does not occur; with the cessation of consciousness, there is the cessation of name-and-form.’

“Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘kimhi nu kho asati viññāṇaṃ na hoti, kissa nirodhā viññāṇanirodho’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa yoniso manasikārā ahu [M 2.0030] paññāya abhisamayo – ‘nāmarūpe kho asati viññāṇaṃ na hoti, nāmarūpanirodhā viññāṇanirodho’ti.

Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘When what does not exist, does consciousness not occur? With the cessation of what does the cessation of consciousness occur?’ Then, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, through wise attention, there was a breakthrough with wisdom: ‘When name-and-form do not exist, consciousness does not occur; with the cessation of name-and-form, there is the cessation of consciousness.’

61. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa etadahosi – ‘adhigato [T 2.0040] kho myāyaṃ maggo sambodhāya [P 2.0035] yadidaṃ – nāmarūpanirodhā viññāṇanirodho, viññāṇanirodhā nāmarūpanirodho, nāmarūpanirodhā saḷāyatananirodho, saḷāyatananirodhā phassanirodho, phassanirodhā vedanānirodho, vedanānirodhā taṇhānirodho, taṇhānirodhā upādānanirodho, upādānanirodhā bhavanirodho, bhavanirodhā jātinirodho, jātinirodhā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā nirujjhanti. Evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hoti’.

61. Then, monks, this thought occurred to the Bodhisatta Vipassī: ‘This path to awakening has been attained by me, that is: with the cessation of name-and-form, there is the cessation of consciousness; with the cessation of consciousness, there is the cessation of name-and-form; with the cessation of name-and-form, there is the cessation of the six sense bases; with the cessation of the six sense bases, there is the cessation of contact; with the cessation of contact, there is the cessation of feeling; with the cessation of feeling, there is the cessation of craving; with the cessation of craving, there is the cessation of clinging; with the cessation of clinging, there is the cessation of becoming; with the cessation of becoming, there is the cessation of birth; with the cessation of birth, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. Thus is the cessation of this entire mass of suffering.’

62. “‘Nirodho nirodho’ti kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bodhisattassa pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

62. ‘Cessation, cessation’—thus, monks, for the Bodhisatta Vipassī, regarding phenomena unheard of before, the eye arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, light arose.

63. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bodhisatto aparena samayena pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu udayabbayānupassī vihāsi – ‘iti rūpaṃ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo; iti vedanā, iti vedanāya samudayo, iti vedanāya atthaṅgamo; iti saññā, iti saññāya samudayo, iti saññāya atthaṅgamo; iti saṅkhārā, iti saṅkhārānaṃ samudayo, iti saṅkhārānaṃ [V 2.0028] atthaṅgamo; iti viññāṇaṃ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti, tassa pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu udayabbayānupassino viharato na cirasseva anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuccī”ti.

63. Then, monks, after some time, the Bodhisatta Vipassī dwelt contemplating the arising and passing away of the five aggregates of clinging: ‘Such is form, such is the arising of form, such is the cessation of form; such is feeling, such is the arising of feeling, such is the cessation of feeling; such is perception, such is the arising of perception, such is the cessation of perception; such are formations, such is the arising of formations, such is the cessation of formations; such is consciousness, such is the arising of consciousness, such is the cessation of consciousness.’ As he dwelt contemplating the arising and passing away of the five aggregates of clinging, before long his mind was liberated from the taints without clinging.

Dutiyabhāṇavāro.

The Second Section for Recitation.

Brahmayācanakathā

The Discourse on Brahmā’s Request

64. “Atha [T 2.0041] kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūnāhaṃ dhammaṃ deseyya’nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa [M 2.0031] bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa [P 2.0036] etadahosi – ‘adhigato kho myāyaṃ dhammo gambhīro duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo. Ālayarāmā kho panāyaṃ pajā ālayaratā ālayasammuditā. Ālayarāmāya kho pana pajāya ālayaratāya ālayasammuditāya duddasaṃ idaṃ ṭhānaṃ yadidaṃ idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppādo. Idampi kho ṭhānaṃ duddasaṃ yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, pare ca me na ājāneyyuṃ; so mamassa kilamatho, sā mamassa vihesā’ti.

64. Then, monks, this occurred to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘Suppose I were to teach the Dhamma.’ Then, monks, this occurred to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘This Dhamma realized by me is profound, difficult to see, difficult to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of logic, subtle, to be experienced by the wise. But this generation delights in attachment, is fond of attachment, and rejoices in attachment. For a generation that delights in attachment, is fond of attachment, and rejoices in attachment, this state is difficult to see: that is, specific conditionality, dependent origination. This state is also difficult to see: that is, the stilling of all formations, the relinquishing of all substrates of existence, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna. If I were to teach the Dhamma and others were not to understand me, that would be wearisome for me, that would be vexing for me.’

65. “Apissu, bhikkhave, vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ imā anacchariyā gāthāyo paṭibhaṃsu pubbe assutapubbā –

65. Furthermore, monks, these marvelous verses, never heard before, spontaneously occurred to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One:

‘Kicchena me adhigataṃ, halaṃ dāni pakāsituṃ;

Rāgadosaparetehi, nāyaṃ dhammo susambudho.

‘With difficulty was this attained by me; it is not fitting now to proclaim it. This Dhamma is not easily understood by those overcome by lust and hate.

‘Paṭisotagāmiṃ nipuṇaṃ, gambhīraṃ duddasaṃ aṇuṃ;

Rāgarattā na dakkhanti, tamokhandhena āvuṭā’ti.

‘Going against the stream, subtle, profound, difficult to see, and fine—those dyed in lust, shrouded by a mass of darkness, will not see it.’

“Itiha[V 2.0029], bhikkhave, vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa paṭisañcikkhato appossukkatāya cittaṃ nami, no dhammadesanāya.

“Thus, bhikkhus, as the Blessed One, Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, was reflecting, his mind inclined to inaction, not to teaching the Dhamma.”

66. “Atha [T 2.0042] kho, bhikkhave, aññatarassa mahābrahmuno vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya etadahosi [P 2.0037] – ‘nassati vata bho loko, vinassati vata bho loko, yatra hi nāma vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa appossukkatāya cittaṃ namati nami (syā. ka.), namissati (?), no dhammadesanāyā’ti. Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahābrahmā seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya; evameva brahmaloke antarahito vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa purato pāturahosi. Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahābrahmā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā dakkhiṇaṃ jāṇumaṇḍalaṃ pathaviyaṃ [M 2.0032] nihantvā nidahanto (syā.) yena vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘desetu, bhante, bhagavā dhammaṃ, desetu sugato dhammaṃ, santi santī (syā.) sattā apparajakkhajātikā; assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro’ti.

66. “Then, monks, a certain Great Brahmā, having understood with his mind the thought in the mind of Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, thought: ‘Alas, the world is perishing! Alas, the world is being destroyed! For the mind of Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, inclines to disinclination, not to teaching the Dhamma.’ Then, monks, just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm, so that Great Brahmā disappeared from the Brahmā world and appeared before Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Then, monks, that Great Brahmā, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and raising his joined hands in reverence toward Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, said this: ‘Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma! Let the Sugata teach the Dhamma! There are beings with little dust in their eyes. Through not hearing the Dhamma, they are declining. There will be those who will understand the Dhamma.’”

67. “Evaṃ vutte atha kho (ka.), bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho taṃ mahābrahmānaṃ etadavoca – ‘mayhampi kho, brahme, etadahosi – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ dhammaṃ deseyya”nti. Tassa mayhaṃ, brahme, etadahosi – “adhigato kho myāyaṃ dhammo gambhīro duddaso duranubodho santo paṇīto atakkāvacaro nipuṇo paṇḍitavedanīyo. Ālayarāmā kho panāyaṃ pajā ālayaratā ālayasammuditā. Ālayarāmāya kho pana pajāya ālayaratāya ālayasammuditāya [T 2.0043] duddasaṃ idaṃ ṭhānaṃ yadidaṃ idappaccayatāpaṭiccasamuppādo. Idampi kho ṭhānaṃ duddasaṃ yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, pare ca me na ājāneyyuṃ; so mamassa kilamatho, sā mamassa vihesā”ti. Apissu maṃ, brahme[P 2.0038], imā anacchariyā gāthāyo paṭibhaṃsu pubbe assutapubbā –

67. “When this was said, monks, Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, said this to that Great Brahmā: ‘To me also, Brahmā, this occurred: “What if I were to teach the Dhamma?” Then, Brahmā, this occurred to me: “This Dhamma realized by me is profound, difficult to see, difficult to understand, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of logic, subtle, to be experienced by the wise. But this generation delights in attachment, is fond of attachment, and rejoices in attachment. For a generation that delights in attachment, is fond of attachment, and rejoices in attachment, this state is difficult to see: that is, specific conditionality, dependent origination. This state is also difficult to see: that is, the stilling of all formations, the relinquishing of all substrates of existence, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna. If I were to teach the Dhamma and others were not to understand me, that would be wearisome for me, that would be vexing for me.” Furthermore, Brahmā, these marvelous verses, never heard before, spontaneously occurred to me:”

“Kicchena me adhigataṃ, halaṃ dāni pakāsituṃ;

Rāgadosaparetehi, nāyaṃ dhammo susambudho.

“With difficulty was this attained by me; it is not fitting now to proclaim it. This Dhamma is not easily understood by those overcome by lust and hate.”

“Paṭisotagāmiṃ nipuṇaṃ, gambhīraṃ duddasaṃ aṇuṃ;

Rāgarattā na dakkhanti, tamokhandhena āvuṭā”ti.

“Going against the stream, subtle, profound, difficult to see, and minute—those dyed in lust, shrouded by a mass of darkness, will not see it.”

‘Itiha [V 2.0030] me, brahme, paṭisañcikkhato appossukkatāya cittaṃ nami, no dhammadesanāyā’ti.

“Thus, Brahmā, as I reflected, my mind inclined to disinclination, not to teaching the Dhamma.”

68. “Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, so mahābrahmā…pe… tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, so mahābrahmā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘desetu, bhante, bhagavā dhammaṃ, desetu sugato dhammaṃ, santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro’ti.

68. “For a second time, monks, that Great Brahmā… For a third time, monks, that Great Brahmā said this to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘Venerable Sir, let the Blessed One teach the Dhamma! Let the Sugata teach the Dhamma! There are beings with little dust in their eyes. Through not hearing the Dhamma, they are declining. There will be those who will understand the Dhamma.’”

69. “Atha [M 2.0033] kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho brahmuno ca ajjhesanaṃ viditvā sattesu ca kāruññataṃ paṭicca buddhacakkhunā lokaṃ volokesi. Addasā kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho buddhacakkhunā lokaṃ volokento satte apparajakkhe mahārajakkhe tikkhindriye mudindriye svākāre dvākāre suviññāpaye duviññāpaye duviññāpaye bhabbe abhabbe (syā.) appekacce paralokavajjabhayadassāvine dassāvino (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.) viharante, appekacce na paralokavajjabhayadassāvine dassāvino (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.) viharante. Seyyathāpi nāma uppaliniyaṃ vā paduminiyaṃ [T 2.0044] vā puṇḍarīkiniyaṃ vā appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakānuggatāni anto nimuggaposīni. Appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni samodakaṃ ṭhitāni. Appekaccāni uppalāni vā padumāni vā puṇḍarīkāni vā udake jātāni udake saṃvaḍḍhāni udakā accuggamma ṭhitāni anupalittāni udakena. Evameva [P 2.0039] kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho buddhacakkhunā lokaṃ volokento addasa satte apparajakkhe mahārajakkhe tikkhindriye mudindriye svākāre dvākāre suviññāpaye duviññāpaye appekacce paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante, appekacce na paralokavajjabhayadassāvine viharante.

69. “Then, monks, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, having known Brahmā’s request and on account of compassion for beings, surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye. As the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, surveyed the world with the Buddha-eye, monks, he saw beings with little dust, with much dust, with sharp faculties, with dull faculties, with good dispositions, with bad dispositions, easy to instruct, difficult to instruct; some dwelling seeing fault and fear in the next world, and some not dwelling seeing fault and fear in the next world. Just as in a pond of blue lotuses, or red lotuses, or white lotuses, some blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses are born in the water, have grown in the water, have gone down into the water, and are nourished while submerged. Some blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses are born in the water, have grown in the water, and stand level with the water. Some blue lotuses, red lotuses, or white lotuses are born in the water, have grown in the water, and stand having risen up from the water, unsullied by the water. In the very same way, monks, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, surveying the world with the Buddha-eye, saw beings with little dust, with much dust, with sharp faculties, with dull faculties, with good dispositions, with bad dispositions, easy to instruct, difficult to instruct; some dwelling seeing fault and fear in the next world, and some not dwelling seeing fault and fear in the next world.”

70. “Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahābrahmā vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

70. “Then, monks, that Great Brahmā, having known with his own mind the thought in the mind of the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, addressed the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, with verses:”

‘Sele yathā pabbatamuddhaniṭṭhito, yathāpi passe janataṃ samantato;

Tathūpamaṃ dhammamayaṃ sumedha, pāsādamāruyha samantacakkhu.

“As one standing on a mountain peak of rock might see the people all around, so too, O wise one, O all-seeing one, having ascended the palace made of Dhamma, analogous to that,”

‘Sokāvatiṇṇaṃ [V 2.0031] sokāvakiṇṇaṃ (syā.) janatamapetasoko,

Avekkhassu jātijarābhibhūtaṃ;

Uṭṭhehi [T 2.0045] vīra vijitasaṅgāma,

Satthavāha aṇaṇa vicara loke.

Desassu desetu (syā. pī.) bhagavā dhammaṃ,

Aññātāro bhavissantī’ti.

‘You who are free from sorrow, behold the people immersed in sorrow, overcome by birth and aging. Arise, O hero, victorious in battle! O caravan leader, one without debt, wander in the world. Teach the Dhamma, O Blessed One; there will be those who will understand.’

71. “Atha [M 2.0034] kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho taṃ mahābrahmānaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

71. Then, monks, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, addressed that Great Brahmā with a verse:

‘Apārutā tesaṃ amatassa dvārā,

Ye sotavanto pamuñcantu saddhaṃ;

Vihiṃsasaññī paguṇaṃ na bhāsiṃ,

Dhammaṃ paṇītaṃ manujesu brahme’ti.

‘Open for them are the doors to the Deathless; let those with ears release their faith. Perceiving it as a vexation, O Brahmā, I did not speak this proficient and excellent Dhamma among humans.’

“Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahābrahmā ‘katāvakāso khomhi vipassinā bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dhammadesanāyā’ti vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ [P 2.0040] sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tattheva antaradhāyi.

Then, monks, that Great Brahmā, thinking, ‘The Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has granted the opportunity for the teaching of the Dhamma,’ paid homage to the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and having circumambulated him to the right, vanished right there.

Aggasāvakayugaṃ

The Pair of Chief Disciples

72. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa etadahosi – ‘kassa nu kho ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, ko imaṃ dhammaṃ khippameva ājānissatī’ti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho khaṇḍo ca rājaputto tisso ca purohitaputto bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā paṭivasanti paṇḍitā viyattā medhāvino dīgharattaṃ apparajakkhajātikā. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ khaṇḍassa ca rājaputtassa, tissassa ca purohitaputtassa paṭhamaṃ dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ[T 2.0046], te imaṃ dhammaṃ khippameva ājānissantī’ti.

72. Then, monks, this occurred to the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘To whom should I first teach the Dhamma? Who will quickly understand this Dhamma?’ Then, monks, this occurred to the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘This Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa, the son of the chaplain, reside in the royal capital of Bandhumatī. They are wise, accomplished, intelligent, and for a long time have had little dust in their eyes. What if I were to first teach the Dhamma to Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa, the son of the chaplain? They will quickly understand this Dhamma.’

73. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho seyyathāpi nāma balavā [V 2.0032] puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya; evameva bodhirukkhamūle antarahito bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā kheme migadāye pāturahosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho dāyapālaṃ migadāyapālaṃ (syā.) āmantesi – ‘ehi tvaṃ, samma dāyapāla, bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ pavisitvā khaṇḍañca rājaputtaṃ tissañca purohitaputtaṃ evaṃ vadehi – vipassī, bhante, bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ anuppatto kheme migadāye viharati, so [M 2.0035] tumhākaṃ dassanakāmo’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bhante’ti kho, bhikkhave, dāyapālo vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa paṭissutvā bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ pavisitvā khaṇḍañca rājaputtaṃ tissañca purohitaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘vipassī, bhante, bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ anuppatto kheme migadāye viharati; so tumhākaṃ dassanakāmo’ti.

73. Then, monks, Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—vanished from the foot of the Bodhi tree and appeared in the Khema Deer Park near the royal capital of Bandhumatī. Then, monks, Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, addressed the park keeper: ‘Come, good park keeper, enter the royal capital of Bandhumatī and say to Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa, the son of the chaplain: “Venerable sirs, Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has arrived at the royal capital of Bandhumatī and is staying in the Khema Deer Park. He wishes to see you.”’ ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ replied the park keeper to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. He then entered the royal capital of Bandhumatī and said to Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa, the son of the chaplain: ‘Venerable sirs, Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has arrived at the royal capital of Bandhumatī and is staying in the Khema Deer Park; he wishes to see you.’

74. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, khaṇḍo ca rājaputto tisso ca [P 2.0041] purohitaputto bhaddāni bhaddāni yānāni yojāpetvā bhaddaṃ bhaddaṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhaddehi bhaddehi yānehi bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā niyyiṃsu. Yena khemo migadāyo tena pāyiṃsu. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā yānā paccorohitvā pattikāva padikāva (syā.) yena vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Upasaṅkamitvā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ [T 2.0047] sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.

74. Then, monks, Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa, the son of the chaplain, had magnificent carriages harnessed, mounted a magnificent carriage, and set out from the royal capital of Bandhumatī with their magnificent carriages. They went toward the Khema Deer Park. They went by carriage as far as the ground was passable for carriages, then dismounted and approached on foot to where Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, was. Having approached, they paid homage to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and sat down to one side.

75. “Tesaṃ vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho anupubbiṃ kathaṃ ānupubbikathaṃ (sī. pī.) kathesi, seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā te bhagavā aññāsi kallacitte muducitte vinīvaraṇacitte udaggacitte pasannacitte, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva khaṇḍassa ca rājaputtassa tissassa ca purohitaputtassa tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti.

75. Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, gave them a graduated discourse, that is to say: a talk on giving, a talk on virtue, a talk on heaven; he explained the danger, worthlessness, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew their minds were receptive, gentle, devoid of hindrances, uplifted, and serene, he then taught the Dhamma teaching that is special to the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth, free of stains, would rightly take the dye, in the same way, as they sat there, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa, the son of the chaplain: ‘Whatever is subject to origination is all subject to cessation.’

76. “Te diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre [V 2.0033] vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya “cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī”ti. Evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo [M 2.0036] pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ [P 2.0042] gacchāma dhammañca. Labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyāma upasampada’nti.

76. Having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, known the Dhamma, plunged into the Dhamma, having crossed over doubt, dispelled uncertainty, attained to confidence, and become independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation, they said to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what was overturned, reveal what was hidden, show the way to one who was lost, or hold up a lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—in the same way the Blessed One has made the Dhamma clear in many ways. We go for refuge to the Blessed One, venerable sir, and to the Dhamma. May we receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, venerable sir; may we receive the higher ordination.’

77. “Alatthuṃ kho[T 2.0048], bhikkhave, khaṇḍo ca rājaputto, tisso ca purohitaputto vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike pabbajjaṃ alatthuṃ upasampadaṃ. Te vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi; saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nibbāne nekkhamme (syā.) ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Tesaṃ vipassinā bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dhammiyā kathāya sandassiyamānānaṃ samādapiyamānānaṃ samuttejiyamānānaṃ sampahaṃsiyamānānaṃ nacirasseva anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsu.

77. “Indeed, monks, Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa, the son of the chaplain, received the going forth and the higher ordination in the presence of Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, instructed, established, exhorted, and gladdened them with a talk on the Dhamma; he explained the danger, inferiority, and defilement of conditioned phenomena, and the benefit of Nibbāna. As they were being instructed, established, exhorted, and gladdened by Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, with a talk on the Dhamma, before long their minds were liberated from the taints without clinging.”

Mahājanakāyapabbajjā

The Going Forth of the Multitude

78. “Assosi kho, bhikkhave, bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā mahājanakāyo caturāsītipāṇasahassāni – ‘vipassī kira bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ anuppatto kheme migadāye viharati. Khaṇḍo ca kira rājaputto tisso ca purohitaputto vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā’ti. Sutvāna nesaṃ etadahosi – ‘na hi nūna so orako dhammavinayo, na sā orakā pabbajjā, yattha khaṇḍo ca rājaputto tisso ca purohitaputto kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā. Khaṇḍo ca rājaputto tisso ca purohitaputto kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissanti, kimaṅgaṃ pana maya’nti. Atha [T 2.0049] kho so, bhikkhave, mahājanakāyo caturāsītipāṇasahassāni bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā nikkhamitvā yena khemo migadāyo yena vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho [P 2.0043] tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.

78. “Monks, the great multitude in the royal city of Bandhumatī, eighty-four thousand living beings, heard: ‘The Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has arrived at the royal city of Bandhumatī and is staying in the Khema Deer Park. Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa the chaplain’s son have shaved off their hair and beards, put on the ochre robes, and gone forth from the householder’s life into homelessness in the presence of the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.’ Hearing this, they thought: ‘Surely this is no trivial Dhamma and Discipline, no trivial going forth, where Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa the chaplain’s son have shaved off their hair and beards, put on the ochre robes, and gone forth from the householder’s life into homelessness. If Prince Khaṇḍa and Tissa the chaplain’s son are going forth, why not us?’ Then, monks, that great multitude of eighty-four thousand living beings left Bandhumatī and went to the Khema Deer Park, where the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, was staying. Approaching the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, they paid homage and sat down to one side.”

79. “Tesaṃ [M 2.0037] vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi. Seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā te bhagavā aññāsi kallacitte muducitte vinīvaraṇacitte udaggacitte pasannacitte[V 2.0034], atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva tesaṃ caturāsītipāṇasahassānaṃ tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti.

79. “Then the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, gave them a graduated discourse—on generosity, on virtue, on the heavens; on the danger, the drawback, and the defilement of sensual pleasures; and on the benefits of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that their minds were ready, pliable, free from hindrances, uplifted, and confident, he revealed the teaching special to the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth, free from stains, would properly absorb dye, so too in those eighty-four thousand beings, right there in their seats, the dust-free, stainless vision of the Dhamma arose: ‘Whatever is subject to arising is all subject to cessation.’”

80. “Te diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya “cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī”ti. Evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca ( ) natthi aṭṭhakathāyaṃ, pāḷiyaṃ pana sabbatthapi dissati. Labheyyāma [T 2.0050] mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ labheyyāma upasampada”nti.

80. “Having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, known the Dhamma, fathomed the Dhamma, having crossed over doubt, being without perplexity, having attained intrepidity, being independent of others in the Teacher's Dispensation, they said this to the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: 'Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was covered, or point out the way to one who is lost, or hold up a lamp in the dark, thinking, “Those with eyes will see forms,” just so has the Dhamma been made clear in many ways by the Blessed One. We go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May we receive the going forth in the Blessed One’s presence, may we receive the full ordination!’”

81. “Alatthuṃ kho, bhikkhave, tāni caturāsītipāṇasahassāni vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike pabbajjaṃ, alatthuṃ upasampadaṃ. Te vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi; saṅkhārānaṃ [P 2.0044] ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nibbāne ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Tesaṃ vipassinā bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dhammiyā kathāya sandassiyamānānaṃ samādapiyamānānaṃ samuttejiyamānānaṃ sampahaṃsiyamānānaṃ nacirasseva anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsu.

81. “Indeed, monks, those eighty-four thousand beings received the going forth and the higher ordination in the presence of Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, instructed, established, exhorted, and gladdened them with a talk on the Dhamma; he explained the danger, inferiority, and defilement of conditioned phenomena, and the benefit of Nibbāna. As they were being instructed, established, exhorted, and gladdened by Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, with a talk on the Dhamma, before long their minds were liberated from the taints without clinging.”

Purimapabbajitānaṃ dhammābhisamayo

The Realization of the Dhamma by the Former Renunciates

82. “Assosuṃ kho, bhikkhave, tāni purimāni caturāsītipabbajitasahassāni – ‘vipassī kira bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ [M 2.0038] anuppatto kheme migadāye viharati, dhammañca kira desetī’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, tāni caturāsītipabbajitasahassāni yena bandhumatī rājadhānī yena khemo migadāyo yena vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.

82. “Monks, those eighty-four thousand former renunciates heard: ‘It is said that Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has arrived at the royal city of Bandhumatī and is dwelling in the Khema Deer Park, and it is said he is teaching the Dhamma.’ Then, monks, those eighty-four thousand renunciates went to where the royal city of Bandhumatī was, to where the Khema Deer Park was, to where Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, was. Having approached, they paid homage to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and sat down to one side.”

83. “Tesaṃ [V 2.0035] vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho anupubbiṃ kathaṃ kathesi. Seyyathidaṃ – dānakathaṃ sīlakathaṃ saggakathaṃ kāmānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nekkhamme ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Yadā te bhagavā aññāsi kallacitte muducitte [T 2.0051] vinīvaraṇacitte udaggacitte pasannacitte, atha yā buddhānaṃ sāmukkaṃsikā dhammadesanā, taṃ pakāsesi – dukkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ maggaṃ. Seyyathāpi nāma suddhaṃ vatthaṃ apagatakāḷakaṃ sammadeva rajanaṃ paṭiggaṇheyya, evameva tesaṃ caturāsītipabbajitasahassānaṃ tasmiṃyeva āsane virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – ‘yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma’nti.

83. To them, Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, gave a graduated discourse. That is to say, he gave a discourse on giving, a discourse on virtue, a discourse on heaven; he revealed the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefit of renunciation. When the Blessed One knew that their minds were ready, tender, free from hindrances, uplifted, and serene, he then revealed that Dhamma teaching which is the special discovery of the Buddhas: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth, free of stains, would properly take up dye, even so, for those eighty-four thousand renunciates, right in that very seat, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose: ‘Whatever is subject to arising is all subject to cessation.’

84. “Te diṭṭhadhammā pattadhammā viditadhammā pariyogāḷhadhammā tiṇṇavicikicchā vigatakathaṃkathā vesārajjappattā aparappaccayā satthusāsane vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘abhikkantaṃ[P 2.0045], bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya “cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī”ti. Evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Ete mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāma mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ labheyyāma upasampada”nti.

84. They, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, having crossed over doubt, being free from perplexity, having attained fearlessness, and being independent of others in the Teacher’s dispensation, said this to Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One: ‘Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—in the very same way, the Dhamma has been made clear by the Blessed One in many ways. We, venerable sir, go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May we, venerable sir, receive the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One, may we receive the full ordination!’

85. “Alatthuṃ kho, bhikkhave, tāni caturāsītipabbajitasahassāni vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike pabbajjaṃ alatthuṃ upasampadaṃ. Te vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi; saṅkhārānaṃ ādīnavaṃ okāraṃ saṃkilesaṃ nibbāne ānisaṃsaṃ pakāsesi. Tesaṃ vipassinā bhagavatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dhammiyā kathāya sandassiyamānānaṃ [T 2.0052] samādapiyamānānaṃ [M 2.0039] samuttejiyamānānaṃ sampahaṃsiyamānānaṃ nacirasseva anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsu.

85. Indeed, bhikkhus, those eighty-four thousand renunciates received the going forth, they received the full ordination in the presence of Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened them with a talk on the Dhamma; he revealed the danger, degradation, and defilement of conditioned formations, and the benefit of Nibbāna. For them, being instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened by Vipassī, the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, with a talk on the Dhamma, before long their minds were liberated from the taints without clinging.

Cārikāanujānanaṃ

Permission for Wandering

86. “Tena kho pana, bhikkhave, samayena bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā mahābhikkhusaṅgho paṭivasati aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – ‘mahā kho etarahi bhikkhusaṅgho bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā paṭivasati aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ, yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhū anujāneyyaṃ – ‘caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya [V 2.0036] atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ; mā ekena dve agamittha; desetha, bhikkhave[P 2.0046], dhammaṃ ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsetha. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro. Api ca channaṃ channaṃ vassānaṃ accayena bandhumatī rājadhānī upasaṅkamitabbā pātimokkhuddesāyā’”ti.

86. At that time, bhikkhus, in the royal capital of Bandhumatī, a great community of bhikkhus was residing—one hundred and sixty-eight thousand bhikkhus. Then, bhikkhus, while the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in his mind: ‘Now, a great community of bhikkhus is residing in the royal capital of Bandhumatī—one hundred and sixty-eight thousand bhikkhus. It would be good if I were to permit the bhikkhus: “Wander forth, bhikkhus, for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. Let not two go by the same path. Teach, bhikkhus, the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and wording. Proclaim the holy life, utterly complete and pure. There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are declining from not hearing the Dhamma; there will be those who will understand the Dhamma. Moreover, after every six years, the royal capital of Bandhumatī should be approached for the recitation of the Pātimokkha.”’

87. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro mahābrahmā vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya. Evameva brahmaloke antarahito vipassissa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa purato [T 2.0053] pāturahosi. Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahābrahmā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā vipassiṃ bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ etadavoca – ‘evametaṃ, bhagavā, evametaṃ, sugata. Mahā kho, bhante, etarahi bhikkhusaṅgho bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā paṭivasati aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ, anujānātu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhū – “caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ; mā ekena dve agamittha; desetha, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ ādikalyāṇaṃ [M 2.0040] majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsetha. Santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro”ti aññātāro (ssabbattha). Api ca, bhante, mayaṃ tathā karissāma yathā bhikkhū channaṃ channaṃ vassānaṃ accayena bandhumatiṃ rājadhāniṃ upasaṅkamissanti pātimokkhuddesāyā’ti. Idamavoca, bhikkhave, so mahābrahmā, idaṃ vatvā vipassiṃ [P 2.0047] bhagavantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tattheva antaradhāyi.

87. Then, bhikkhus, a certain Great Brahmā, having known with his mind the thought in the mind of the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, just as a strong man might stretch out his bent arm or bend his outstretched arm, so did he vanish from the Brahmā-world and appear before the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Then, bhikkhus, that Great Brahmā, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, raised his joined palms in salutation towards the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and said this: ‘So it is, Blessed One, so it is, Sugata. At present, venerable sir, a great community of bhikkhus resides in the royal capital of Bandhumatī—one hundred and sixty-eight thousand bhikkhus. Let the Blessed One, venerable sir, permit the bhikkhus: “Wander forth, bhikkhus, for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. Let not two go by the same path. Teach, bhikkhus, the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and wording. Proclaim the holy life, utterly complete and pure. There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are declining from not hearing the Dhamma; there will be those who will understand the Dhamma.” Moreover, venerable sir, we will act in such a way that the bhikkhus will come to the royal capital of Bandhumatī every six years for the recitation of the Pātimokkha.’ That Great Brahmā said this, bhikkhus. Having said this, he paid homage to the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, circumambulated him respectfully, and vanished right there.

88. “Atha kho, bhikkhave, vipassī bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘idha mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – mahā kho etarahi bhikkhusaṅgho bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā paṭivasati aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ[T 2.0054]. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ bhikkhū anujāneyyaṃ – ‘caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ; mā ekena dve agamittha; desetha, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsetha. Santi sattā [V 2.0037] apparajakkhajātikā, assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro. Api ca, channaṃ channaṃ vassānaṃ accayena bandhumatī rājadhānī upasaṅkamitabbā pātimokkhuddesāyāti.

88. Then, monks, the Blessed One Vipassī, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, having emerged from seclusion in the evening, addressed the monks: ‘Here, monks, while I was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in my mind: “At present, a great community of monks resides in the royal capital of Bandhumatī—one hundred and sixty-eight thousand monks. It would be good if I were to permit the monks: ‘Wander forth, monks, for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. Let not two go by the same path. Teach, monks, the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and wording. Proclaim the holy life, utterly complete and pure. There are beings with little dust in their eyes who are declining from not hearing the Dhamma; there will be those who will understand the Dhamma.’ Moreover, after every six years, the royal capital of Bandhumatī should be approached for the recitation of the Pātimokkha.”’

“‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro mahābrahmā mama cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva brahmaloke antarahito mama purato pāturahosi. Atha kho so, bhikkhave, mahābrahmā ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yenāhaṃ tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā maṃ etadavoca – “evametaṃ, bhagavā, evametaṃ, sugata. Mahā kho, bhante, etarahi bhikkhusaṅgho bandhumatiyā rājadhāniyā paṭivasati aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ. Anujānātu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhū – ‘caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya [M 2.0041] sukhāya devamanussānaṃ; mā ekena dve agamittha; desetha, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ…pe… santi sattā apparajakkhajātikā[T 2.0055], assavanatā dhammassa parihāyanti, bhavissanti dhammassa aññātāro’ti.
