129. “Aṭṭha [M 2.0060] kho ime, ānanda, vimokkhā. Katame aṭṭha? Rūpī rūpāni passati ayaṃ [V 2.0055] paṭhamo vimokkho. Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī bahiddhā rūpāni passati, ayaṃ dutiyo vimokkho. Subhanteva [P 2.0071] adhimutto hoti, ayaṃ tatiyo vimokkho. Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ catuttho vimokkho. Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ pañcamo vimokkho. Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi [T 2.0084] kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ chaṭṭho vimokkho. Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘nevasaññānāsaññā’yatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ sattamo vimokkho. Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ aṭṭhamo vimokkho. Ime kho, ānanda, aṭṭha vimokkhā.

129. “Ānanda, there are these eight liberations. What are the eight? Possessed of form, one sees forms; this is the first liberation. Not perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally; this is the second liberation. One is intent only on the beautiful; this is the third liberation. By completely transcending perceptions of form, by the cessation of perceptions of resistance, by not attending to perceptions of diversity, perceiving ‘space is infinite,’ one enters and dwells in the sphere of infinite space; this is the fourth liberation. By completely transcending the sphere of infinite space, perceiving ‘consciousness is infinite,’ one enters and dwells in the sphere of infinite consciousness; this is the fifth liberation. By completely transcending the sphere of infinite consciousness, perceiving ‘there is nothing,’ one enters and dwells in the sphere of nothingness; this is the sixth liberation. By completely transcending the sphere of nothingness, one enters and dwells in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; this is the seventh liberation. By completely transcending the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one enters and dwells in the cessation of perception and feeling; this is the eighth liberation. These, Ānanda, are the eight liberations.”

130. “Yato kho, ānanda, bhikkhu ime aṭṭha vimokkhe anulomampi samāpajjati, paṭilomampi samāpajjati, anulomapaṭilomampi samāpajjati, yatthicchakaṃ yadicchakaṃ yāvaticchakaṃ samāpajjatipi vuṭṭhātipi. Āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ vuccatānanda, bhikkhu ubhatobhāgavimutto. Imāya ca ānanda ubhatobhāgavimuttiyā aññā ubhatobhāgavimutti uttaritarā vā paṇītatarā vā natthī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

130. “When, Ānanda, a bhikkhu enters upon these eight liberations in forward order, in reverse order, and in forward and reverse order; when, wherever he wishes, in regard to whatever he wishes, for as long as he wishes, he both enters upon and emerges from them; and when, through the destruction of the taints, having realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, he enters and dwells in it—this bhikkhu, Ānanda, is called one liberated in both ways. And, Ānanda, there is no other liberation in both ways that is higher or more sublime than this liberation in both ways.” Thus the Blessed One spoke. The venerable Ānanda, delighted, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.

Mahānidānasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.

The second, the Great Discourse on Causation, is concluded.

3. Mahāparinibbānasuttaṃ

3. The Great Discourse on the Final Nibbāna

131. Evaṃ [T 2.0085][M 2.0061][V 2.0056] me [P 2.0072] sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tena kho pana samayena rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vajjī abhiyātukāmo hoti. So evamāha – “ahaṃ hime vajjī evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve ucchecchāmi ucchejjāmi (syā. pī.), ucchijjāmi (ka.) vajjī, vināsessāmi vajjī, anayabyasanaṃ āpādessāmi vajjī”ti āpādessāmi vajjīti (sabbattha) a. ni. 7.22 passitabbaṃ.

131. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Rājagaha on Vulture Peak Mountain. Now at that time, the king of Magadha, Ajātasattu, son of Vedehi, was desirous of attacking the Vajjis. He spoke thus: ‘I will uproot these Vajjis, so mighty and so powerful; I will destroy the Vajjis; I will bring the Vajjis to misfortune and ruin.’

132. Atha kho rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vassakāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ magadhamahāmattaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vandāhi, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ puccha – ‘rājā, bhante, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘rājā, bhante, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vajjī abhiyātukāmo. So evamāha – “ahaṃ hime vajjī evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve ucchecchāmi vajjī, vināsessāmi vajjī, anayabyasanaṃ [P 2.0073] āpādessāmī’”ti. Yathā te bhagavā byākaroti, taṃ sādhukaṃ uggahetvā mama āroceyyāsi. Na hi tathāgatā vitathaṃ bhaṇantī”ti.

132. Then the king of Magadha, Ajātasattu, son of Vedehi, addressed the brahmin Vassakāra, the great minister of Magadha: ‘Come, brahmin, go to the Blessed One. Having approached, bow down with your head to the Blessed One’s feet in my name and inquire about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, agility, strength, and dwelling in comfort, saying: “Venerable sir, the king of Magadha, Ajātasattu, son of Vedehi, bows down with his head to the Blessed One’s feet and inquires about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, agility, strength, and dwelling in comfort.” And also say this: “Venerable sir, the king of Magadha, Ajātasattu, son of Vedehi, is desirous of attacking the Vajjis. He speaks thus: ‘I will uproot these Vajjis, so mighty and so powerful; I will destroy the Vajjis; I will bring the Vajjis to misfortune and ruin.’” As the Blessed One explains it to you, learn that well and report it to me. For indeed, Tathāgatas do not speak falsely.’

Vassakārabrāhmaṇo

Vassakāra the Brahmin

133. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto rañño māgadhassa ajātasattussa vedehiputtassa paṭissutvā bhaddāni bhaddāni yānāni yojetvā bhaddaṃ bhaddaṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā [T 2.0086] bhaddehi bhaddehi yānehi rājagahamhā niyyāsi, yena gijjhakūṭo pabbato tena pāyāsi. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā, yānā paccorohitvā pattikova yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā [V 2.0057] ekamantaṃ [M 2.0062] nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “rājā, bho gotama, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto bhoto gotamassa pāde sirasā vandati, appābādhaṃ appātaṅkaṃ lahuṭṭhānaṃ balaṃ phāsuvihāraṃ pucchati. Rājā evañca vadeti rājā (ka.), bho gotama, māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto vajjī abhiyātukāmo. So evamāha – ‘ahaṃ hime vajjī evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve ucchecchāmi vajjī, vināsessāmi vajjī, anayabyasanaṃ āpādessāmī’”ti.

133. “Even so, good sir,” the brahmin Vassakāra, the great minister of Magadha, replied, assenting to the king of Magadha, Ajātasattu, son of Vedehi. He had excellent carriages harnessed, mounted an excellent carriage, and departed from Rājagaha with excellent carriages, proceeding towards Vulture Peak Mountain. He went by carriage as far as the ground was passable for carriages, then dismounted and approached the Blessed One on foot. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Blessed One. After concluding this friendly and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Vassakāra, the great minister of Magadha, said this to the Blessed One: “Good Gotama, the king of Magadha, Ajātasattu, son of Vedehi, bows down with his head to the good Gotama's feet and inquires about his freedom from illness, freedom from affliction, agility, strength, and dwelling in comfort. Good Gotama, the king of Magadha, Ajātasattu, son of Vedehi, is desirous of attacking the Vajjis. He speaks thus: ‘I will uproot these Vajjis, so mighty and so powerful; I will destroy the Vajjis; I will bring the Vajjis to misfortune and ruin.’”

Rājaaparihāniyadhammā

The Principles of Non-Decline for Rulers

134. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā ānando bhagavato piṭṭhito ṭhito hoti bhagavantaṃ bījayamāno vījayamāno (sī.), vījiyamāno (syā.). Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjī abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā sannipātabahulā’ti? “Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā sannipātabahulā”ti. “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā sannipātabahulā bhavissanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ [T 2.0087] pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

134. At that time, the Venerable Ānanda was standing behind the Blessed One, fanning him. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, what have you heard? That the Vajjis hold frequent and numerous assemblies?” “I have heard this, Lord: that the Vajjis hold frequent and numerous assemblies.” “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjis shall hold frequent and numerous assemblies, only growth is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline.

“Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ[P 2.0074], ‘vajjī samaggā sannipatanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahanti, samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karontī’ti? “Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī samaggā sannipatanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahanti, samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karontī”ti. “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī samaggā sannipatissanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahissanti, samaggā vajjikaraṇīyāni karissanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“What have you heard, Ānanda? That the Vajjis assemble in concord, rise in concord, and carry out their duties in concord?” “I have heard this, Lord: that the Vajjis assemble in concord, rise in concord, and carry out their duties in concord.” “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjis shall assemble in concord, rise in concord, and carry out their duties in concord, only growth is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline.

“Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjī apaññattaṃ na paññapenti, paññattaṃ na samucchindanti, yathāpaññatte porāṇe vajjidhamme samādāya vattantī’”ti? “Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī apaññattaṃ na paññapenti, paññattaṃ na samucchindanti, yathāpaññatte porāṇe vajjidhamme samādāya vattantī’”ti. “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, “vajjī apaññattaṃ na paññapessanti, paññattaṃ na samucchindissanti, yathāpaññatte porāṇe vajjidhamme samādāya vattissanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“What have you heard, Ānanda? That the Vajjis do not legislate what has not been legislated, do not abolish what has been legislated, and conduct themselves having undertaken the ancient Vajjian principles as they were legislated?” “I have heard this, Lord: that the Vajjis do not legislate what has not been legislated, do not abolish what has been legislated, and conduct themselves having undertaken the ancient Vajjian principles as they were legislated.” “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjis shall not legislate what has not been legislated, shall not abolish what has been legislated, and shall conduct themselves having undertaken the ancient Vajjian principles as they were legislated, only growth is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline.

“Kinti [M 2.0063] te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjī ye te vajjīnaṃ vajjimahallakā, te sakkaronti garuṃ karonti garukaronti (sī. syā. pī.) mānenti pūjenti, tesañca sotabbaṃ maññantī’”ti? “Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī ye [V 2.0058] te vajjīnaṃ vajjimahallakā, te sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tesañca sotabbaṃ maññantī’”ti. “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī ye te vajjīnaṃ vajjimahallakā[T 2.0088], te sakkarissanti garuṃ karissanti mānessanti pūjessanti, tesañca sotabbaṃ maññissanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“What have you heard, Ānanda? That the Vajjis honor, revere, esteem, and venerate the Vajjian elders, and consider that their words should be listened to?” “I have heard this, Lord: that the Vajjis honor, revere, esteem, and venerate the Vajjian elders, and consider that their words should be listened to.” “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjis shall honor, revere, esteem, and venerate the Vajjian elders, and shall consider that their words should be listened to, only growth is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline.

“Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjī yā tā kulitthiyo kulakumāriyo, tā na okkassa pasayha vāsentī’”ti? “Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī yā tā kulitthiyo kulakumāriyo tā na okkassa pasayha vāsentī’”ti. “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī yā tā kulitthiyo kulakumāriyo, tā na okkassa pasayha vāsessanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“What have you heard, Ānanda? That the Vajjis do not forcibly abduct and compel women and maidens of good family to live with them?” “I have heard this, Lord: that the Vajjis do not forcibly abduct and compel women and maidens of good family to live with them.” “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjis shall not forcibly abduct and compel women and maidens of good family to live with them, only growth is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline.

“Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjī yāni tāni

“What have you heard, Ānanda? That the Vajjis honor, revere, esteem, and venerate those Vajjian shrines that are both within and without the city, and do not allow the righteous offerings, formerly given and made to them, to diminish?”

Vajjīnaṃ vajjicetiyāni abbhantarāni ceva bāhirāni ca, tāni sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti, tesañca dinnapubbaṃ katapubbaṃ dhammikaṃ baliṃ no parihāpentī’”ti? “Sutaṃ [P 2.0075] metaṃ, bhante – ‘vajjī yāni tāni vajjīnaṃ vajjicetiyāni abbhantarāni ceva bāhirāni ca, tāni sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti tesañca dinnapubbaṃ katapubbaṃ dhammikaṃ baliṃ no parihāpentī’”ti. “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjī yāni tāni vajjīnaṃ vajjicetiyāni abbhantarāni ceva bāhirāni ca, tāni sakkarissanti garuṃ karissanti mānessanti pūjessanti, tesañca dinnapubbaṃ katapubbaṃ dhammikaṃ baliṃ no parihāpessanti, vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“I have heard this, Lord: that the Vajjis honor, revere, esteem, and venerate those Vajjian shrines that are both within and without the city, and do not allow the righteous offerings, formerly given and made to them, to diminish.” “For as long, Ānanda, as the Vajjis shall honor, revere, esteem, and venerate those Vajjian shrines that are both within and without the city, and shall not allow the righteous offerings, formerly given and made to them, to diminish, only growth is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline.”

“Kinti te, ānanda, sutaṃ, ‘vajjīnaṃ arahantesu dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti susaṃvihitā, kinti anāgatā ca arahanto vijitaṃ āgaccheyyuṃ, āgatā ca arahanto vijite phāsu vihareyyu’”nti? “Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante ‘vajjīnaṃ arahantesu dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti susaṃvihitā kinti anāgatā ca arahanto [T 2.0089] vijitaṃ āgaccheyyuṃ, āgatā ca arahanto vijite phāsu vihareyyu’”nti. “Yāvakīvañca, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ arahantesu dhammikā rakkhāvaraṇagutti susaṃvihitā bhavissati, kinti anāgatā ca arahanto vijitaṃ [M 2.0064] āgaccheyyuṃ, āgatā ca arahanto vijite phāsu vihareyyunti. Vuddhiyeva, ānanda, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti.

“What have you heard, Ānanda? That righteous protection, defense, and security are well-provided for the Arahants among the Vajjis, so that Arahants who have not yet come might come to their kingdom, and Arahants who have come might dwell comfortably in their kingdom?” “I have heard this, Lord: that righteous protection, defense, and security are well-provided for the Arahants among the Vajjis, so that Arahants who have not yet come might come to their kingdom, and Arahants who have come might dwell comfortably in their kingdom.” “For as long, Ānanda, as righteous protection, defense, and security shall be well-provided for the Arahants among the Vajjis, so that Arahants who have not yet come might come to their kingdom, and Arahants who have come might dwell comfortably in their kingdom, only growth is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline.”

135. Atha [V 2.0059] kho bhagavā vassakāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ magadhamahāmattaṃ āmantesi – “ekamidāhaṃ, brāhmaṇa, samayaṃ vesāliyaṃ viharāmi sārandade sānandare (ka.) cetiye. Tatrāhaṃ vajjīnaṃ ime satta aparihāniye dhamme desesiṃ. Yāvakīvañca, brāhmaṇa, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā vajjīsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu vajjī sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, brāhmaṇa, vajjīnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti.

135. Then the Blessed One addressed Vassakāra the brahmin, the chief minister of Magadha: “On one occasion, brahmin, I was dwelling in Vesālī at the Sārandada Cetiya. There I taught the Vajjis these seven principles of non-decline. For as long, brahmin, as these seven principles of non-decline shall endure among the Vajjis, and the Vajjis shall be seen to abide by these seven principles of non-decline, only growth is to be expected for the Vajjis, not decline.”

Evaṃ vutte, vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ekamekenapi, bho gotama, aparihāniyena dhammena samannāgatānaṃ vajjīnaṃ vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni[P 2.0076]. Ko pana vādo sattahi aparihāniyehi dhammehi. Akaraṇīyāva akaraṇīyā ca (syā. ka.), bho gotama, vajjī vajjīnaṃ (ka.) raññā māgadhena ajātasattunā vedehiputtena yadidaṃ yuddhassa, aññatra upalāpanāya aññatra mithubhedā. Handa ca dāni mayaṃ, bho gotama, gacchāma[T 2.0090], bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā”ti. “Yassadāni tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, kālaṃ maññasī”ti. Atha kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

When this was said, Vassakāra the brahmin, the chief minister of Magadha, said this to the Blessed One: 'Master Gotama, for the Vajjis who are endowed with even a single one of these principles of non-decline, only growth is to be expected, not decline. What then is to be said of the seven principles of non-decline? Master Gotama, the Vajjis cannot be acted against by the Magadhan king Ajātasattu, son of Vedehi, by means of war, except through conciliation or by sowing internal discord. And now, Master Gotama, we shall depart; we have many duties, much to do.' 'Brahmin, you may go at the time you think fit.' Then Vassakāra the brahmin, the chief minister of Magadha, having delighted in and rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat and departed.

Bhikkhuaparihāniyadhammā

The Principles of Non-Decline for Bhikkhus

136. Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkante vassakāre brāhmaṇe magadhamahāmatte āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “gaccha tvaṃ, ānanda, yāvatikā bhikkhū rājagahaṃ upanissāya viharanti, te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā yāvatikā bhikkhū rājagahaṃ upanissāya viharanti, te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sannipatito, bhante, bhikkhusaṅgho, yassadāni, bhante, bhagavā kālaṃ maññatī”ti.

136. Then, not long after Vassakāra the brahmin, the chief minister of Magadha, had departed, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: 'Go, Ānanda, and assemble in the assembly hall all the bhikkhus who are dwelling in dependence on Rājagaha.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable Ānanda replied, and having assented to the Blessed One, he assembled all the bhikkhus dwelling in dependence on Rājagaha in the assembly hall. Then he approached the Blessed One, paid homage, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, the Saṅgha of bhikkhus has assembled. Now, Venerable Sir, is the time for what the Blessed One sees fit.'

Atha [M 2.0065] kho bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena upaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “satta vo, bhikkhave, aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

Then the Blessed One, having risen from his seat, approached the assembly hall. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus, I will teach you seven principles of non-decline. Listen to them, pay close attention, and I will speak.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Yāvakīvañca[V 2.0060], bhikkhave, bhikkhū abhiṇhaṃ sannipātā sannipātabahulā bhavissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“As long as, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhus assemble frequently and hold frequent assemblies, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū samaggā sannipatissanti, samaggā vuṭṭhahissanti, samaggā saṅghakaraṇīyāni [T 2.0091] karissanti[P 2.0077], vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“As long as, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhus assemble in harmony, adjourn in harmony, and perform the duties of the Saṅgha in harmony, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū apaññattaṃ na paññapessanti, paññattaṃ na samucchindissanti, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vattissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“As long as, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhus do not enact what has not been enacted, do not abolish what has been enacted, and undertake and practice the training rules as they have been laid down, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ye te bhikkhū therā rattaññū cirapabbajitā saṅghapitaro saṅghapariṇāyakā, te sakkarissanti garuṃ karissanti mānessanti pūjessanti, tesañca sotabbaṃ maññissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“As long as, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhus respect, revere, esteem, and venerate those bhikkhus who are elders, long-experienced, long gone forth, fathers of the Saṅgha, and leaders of the Saṅgha, and consider their words worth listening to, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū uppannāya taṇhāya ponobbhavikāya na vasaṃ gacchissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“As long as, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhus do not come under the sway of craving that has arisen, which leads to renewed existence, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū āraññakesu senāsanesu sāpekkhā bhavissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“As long as, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhus have a longing for forest lodgings, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū paccattaññeva satiṃ upaṭṭhapessanti – ‘kinti anāgatā ca pesalā sabrahmacārī āgaccheyyuṃ, āgatā ca pesalā sabrahmacārī phāsu phāsuṃ (sī. syā. pī.) vihareyyu’nti. Vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“As long as, Bhikkhus, the bhikkhus establish mindfulness personally within themselves, thinking: 'How might it be that virtuous companions in the holy life who have not yet come might come, and that virtuous companions in the holy life who have come might dwell in comfort?', only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“As long as, Bhikkhus, these seven principles of non-decline stand firm among the bhikkhus, and the bhikkhus are seen to be in these seven principles of non-decline, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.”

137. “Aparepi [T 2.0092][M 2.0066] vo, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ [V 2.0061] manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

137. Bhikkhus, I will teach you another seven principles of non-decline. Listen to them, pay close attention, and I will speak.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na kammārāmā bhavissanti [P 2.0078] na kammaratā na kammārāmatamanuyuttā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will not delight in work, will not be fond of work, and will not be devoted to delighting in work, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na bhassārāmā bhavissanti na bhassaratā na bhassārāmatamanuyuttā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will not delight in talk, will not be fond of talk, and will not be devoted to delighting in talk, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na niddārāmā bhavissanti na niddāratā na niddārāmatamanuyuttā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will not delight in sleep, will not be fond of sleep, and will not be devoted to delighting in sleep, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na saṅgaṇikārāmā bhavissanti na saṅgaṇikaratā na saṅgaṇikārāmatamanuyuttā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will not delight in company, will not be fond of company, and will not be devoted to delighting in company, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na pāpicchā bhavissanti na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will not have evil desires and will not have come under the sway of evil desires, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na pāpamittā bhavissanti na pāpasahāyā na pāpasampavaṅkā, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will not have evil friends, will not have evil companions, and will not be inclined towards evil associates, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū na oramattakena visesādhigamena antarāvosānaṃ āpajjissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will not stop midway on account of some minor special attainment, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu [T 2.0093] ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as these seven principles of non-decline will be established among the bhikkhus, and the bhikkhus are seen to possess these seven principles of non-decline, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

138. “Aparepi vo, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi…pe… “yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū saddhā bhavissanti…pe… hirimanā bhavissanti… ottappī bhavissanti… [V 2.0062] bahussutā bhavissanti… [P 2.0079] āraddhavīriyā bhavissanti… upaṭṭhitassatī [M 2.0067] bhavissanti… paññavanto bhavissanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni. Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

138. Bhikkhus, I shall teach you another seven principles of non-decline... For as long, Bhikkhus, as the bhikkhus will have faith... will have a sense of shame... will have fear of wrongdoing... will be of great learning... will have aroused effort... will have established mindfulness... will be wise, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline. For as long, Bhikkhus, as these seven principles of non-decline will be established among the bhikkhus, and the bhikkhus are seen to possess these seven principles of non-decline, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

139. “Aparepi vo, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

139. Bhikkhus, I shall teach you another seven principles of non-decline. Listen to that, apply your minds well; I shall speak." "Very well, venerable sir," those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti…pe… dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti… vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti… pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti… passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti… samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvessanti, vuddhiyeva[T 2.0094], bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will develop the enlightenment factor of mindfulness... will develop the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena... will develop the enlightenment factor of energy... will develop the enlightenment factor of rapture... will develop the enlightenment factor of tranquility... will develop the enlightenment factor of concentration... will develop the enlightenment factor of equanimity, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as these seven principles of non-decline will be established among the bhikkhus, and the bhikkhus are seen to possess these seven principles of non-decline, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

140. “Aparepi vo, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

140. Bhikkhus, I shall teach you another seven principles of non-decline. Listen to that, apply your minds well; I shall speak." "Very well, venerable sir," those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū aniccasaññaṃ bhāvessanti…pe… anattasaññaṃ bhāvessanti… asubhasaññaṃ bhāvessanti… ādīnavasaññaṃ bhāvessanti… pahānasaññaṃ bhāvessanti… virāgasaññaṃ bhāvessanti… nirodhasaññaṃ bhāvessanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will develop the perception of impermanence... will develop the perception of not-self... will develop the perception of foulness... will develop the perception of danger... will develop the perception of abandoning... will develop the perception of dispassion... will develop the perception of cessation, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca[P 2.0080], bhikkhave, ime satta aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca [V 2.0063] sattasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

“Bhikkhus, as long as these seven principles of non-decline endure among the bhikkhus, and as long as the bhikkhus are seen to practice these seven principles of non-decline, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.”

141. “Cha, vo bhikkhave, aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

141. Bhikkhus, I shall teach you six principles of non-decline. Listen to that, apply your minds well; I shall speak." "Very well, venerable sir," those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Yāvakīvañca[M 2.0068], bhikkhave, bhikkhū mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpessanti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will maintain loving bodily action towards their companions in the holy life, both openly and in private, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpessanti [T 2.0095] …pe… mettaṃ manokammaṃ paccupaṭṭhāpessanti sabrahmacārīsu āvi ceva raho ca, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will maintain loving verbal action... will maintain loving mental action towards their companions in the holy life, both openly and in private, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū, ye te lābhā dhammikā dhammaladdhā antamaso pattapariyāpannamattampi tathārūpehi lābhehi appaṭivibhattabhogī bhavissanti sīlavantehi sabrahmacārīhi sādhāraṇabhogī, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus, with regard to such gains as are righteous and righteously obtained—even down to the contents of the alms-bowl—will partake of them without division and share them in common with their virtuous companions in the holy life, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yāni kāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññūpasatthāni viññuppasatthāni (sī.) aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṃvattanikāni tathārūpesu sīlesu sīlasāmaññagatā viharissanti sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will dwell in commonality of virtue with their companions in the holy life, both openly and in private, with regard to those virtues that are unbroken, without defect, unspotted, unmottled, liberating, praised by the wise, ungrasped, and conducive to concentration, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhū yāyaṃ diṭṭhi ariyā niyyānikā, niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya, tathārūpāya diṭṭhiyā diṭṭhisāmaññagatā viharissanti sabrahmacārīhi āvi ceva raho ca, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for as long as the bhikkhus will dwell in commonality of view with their companions in the holy life, both openly and in private, with regard to that view which is noble, leading outwards, and which leads one who acts upon it rightly to the complete destruction of suffering, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

“Yāvakīvañca[P 2.0081], bhikkhave, ime cha aparihāniyā dhammā bhikkhūsu ṭhassanti, imesu ca chasu aparihāniyesu dhammesu bhikkhū sandississanti, vuddhiyeva, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānī”ti.

Bhikkhus, for as long as these six principles of non-decline will be established among the bhikkhus, and the bhikkhus are seen to be in possession of these six principles of non-decline, only growth is to be expected for the bhikkhus, not decline.

142. Tatra [V 2.0064] sudaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharanto gijjhakūṭe pabbate etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – “iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā [T 2.0096] mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā”ti.

142. There, while the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, on the mountain Gijjhakūṭa, he frequently gave this Dhamma talk to the bhikkhus: 'Such is virtue, such is concentration, such is wisdom. Concentration, when imbued with virtue, is of great fruit and great benefit. Wisdom, when imbued with concentration, is of great fruit and great benefit. The mind, when imbued with wisdom, is rightly freed from the taints, namely: the taint of sensuality, the taint of becoming, and the taint of ignorance.'

143. Atha [M 2.0069] kho bhagavā rājagahe yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “āyāmānanda, yena ambalaṭṭhikā tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena ambalaṭṭhikā tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ viharati rājāgārake. Tatrāpi sudaṃ bhagavā ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ viharanto rājāgārake etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – “iti sīlaṃ iti samādhi iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā”ti.

143. Then, the Blessed One, having dwelt at Rājagaha for as long as he pleased, addressed the Venerable Ānanda: 'Come, Ānanda, let us go to Ambalaṭṭhikā.' 'Very well, venerable sir,' the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with a great community of bhikkhus, arrived at Ambalaṭṭhikā. There the Blessed One dwelt at Ambalaṭṭhikā in the royal rest house. There too, while the Blessed One was dwelling at Ambalaṭṭhikā in the royal rest house, he frequently gave this Dhamma talk to the bhikkhus: 'Such is virtue, such is concentration, such is wisdom. Concentration, when imbued with virtue, is of great fruit and great benefit. Wisdom, when imbued with concentration, is of great fruit and great benefit. The mind, when imbued with wisdom, is rightly freed from the taints, namely: the taint of sensuality, the taint of becoming, and the taint of ignorance.'

144. Atha kho bhagavā ambalaṭṭhikāyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “āyāmānanda, yena nāḷandā tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena nāḷandā tadavasari, tatra sudaṃ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṃ viharati pāvārikambavane[T 2.0097].

144. Then, the Blessed One, having dwelt at Ambalaṭṭhikā for as long as he pleased, addressed the Venerable Ānanda: 'Come, Ānanda, let us go to Nāḷandā.' 'Very well, venerable sir,' the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with a great community of bhikkhus, arrived at Nāḷandā. There the Blessed One dwelt at Nāḷandā in Pāvārika's mango grove.

Sāriputtasīhanādo

Sāriputta's Lion's Roar

145. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ [P 2.0082] nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati; na cāhu na ca bhavissati na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro yadidaṃ sambodhiya”nti. “Uḷārā kho te ayaṃ, sāriputta, āsabhī vācā āsabhivācā (syā.) bhāsitā, ekaṃso gahito, sīhanādo nadito – ‘evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati; na cāhu na ca bhavissati na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro yadidaṃ sambodhiya’nti.

145. Then the Venerable Sāriputta approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, I have such faith in the Blessed One that there has not been, there will not be, nor is there now any other ascetic or brahmin with more profound knowledge than the Blessed One, that is, with respect to supreme enlightenment.' 'Grand and bold, Sāriputta, is this fearless speech you have uttered, this categorical assertion you have made, this lion's roar you have roared: "Venerable sir, I have such faith in the Blessed One that there has not been, there will not be, nor is there now any other ascetic or brahmin with more profound knowledge than the Blessed One, that is, with respect to supreme enlightenment."

“Kiṃ [M 2.0070][V 2.0065] te kiṃ nu (syā. pī. ka.), sāriputta, ye te ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, sabbe te bhagavanto cetasā ceto paricca viditā – ‘evaṃsīlā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ itipi, evaṃdhammā evaṃpaññā evaṃvihārī evaṃvimuttā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ itipī’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

Sāriputta, as to those who were Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the past—were all those Blessed Ones known to you, having encompassed their minds with your mind, thus: 'Those Blessed Ones were of such virtue, of such qualities, of such wisdom, of such an abiding, and of such liberation'?' 'No, venerable sir.'

“Kiṃ pana te kiṃ pana (syā. pī. ka.), sāriputta, ye te bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, sabbe te bhagavanto cetasā ceto paricca viditā – ‘evaṃsīlā te bhagavanto bhavissanti itipi, evaṃdhammā evaṃpaññā evaṃvihārī evaṃvimuttā te bhagavanto bhavissanti itipī’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

Sāriputta, as to those who will be Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the future—were all those Blessed Ones known to you, having encompassed their minds with your mind, thus: 'Those Blessed Ones will be of such virtue, of such qualities, of such wisdom, of such an abiding, and of such liberation'?' 'No, venerable sir.'

“Kiṃ pana te, sāriputta, ahaṃ etarahi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho cetasā ceto paricca vidito – “evaṃsīlo bhagavā itipi[T 2.0098], evaṃdhammo evaṃpañño evaṃvihārī evaṃvimutto bhagavā itipī’”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

Sāriputta, as to myself, who am at present the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—am I known to you, having encompassed my mind with your mind, thus: 'The Blessed One is of such virtue, of such qualities, of such wisdom, of such an abiding, and of such liberation'?' 'No, venerable sir.'

“Ettha ca hi te, sāriputta, atītānāgatapaccuppannesu arahantesu sammāsambuddhesu cetopariyañāṇaṃ cetopariññāyañāṇaṃ (syā.), cetasā cetopariyāyañāṇaṃ (ka.) natthi. Atha kiñcarahi te ayaṃ, sāriputta, uḷārā āsabhī [P 2.0083] vācā bhāsitā, ekaṃso gahito, sīhanādo nadito – ‘evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati; na cāhu na ca bhavissati na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro yadidaṃ sambodhiya’”nti?

Since you have no knowledge, Sāriputta, that encompasses the minds of the Arahants, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones of the past, future, and present, for what reason then have you uttered this grand and bold fearless speech, made this categorical assertion, and roared this lion's roar: 'Venerable sir, I have such faith in the Blessed One that there has not been, there will not be, nor is there now any other ascetic or brahmin with more profound knowledge than the Blessed One, that is, with respect to supreme enlightenment'?

146. “Na kho me, bhante, atītānāgatapaccuppannesu arahantesu sammāsambuddhesu cetopariyañāṇaṃ atthi, api ca me dhammanvayo vidito. Seyyathāpi, bhante, rañño paccantimaṃ nagaraṃ daḷhuddhāpaṃ daḷhapākāratoraṇaṃ ekadvāraṃ, tatrassa dovāriko paṇḍito viyatto medhāvī aññātānaṃ nivāretā ñātānaṃ pavesetā. So tassa nagarassa samantā anupariyāyapathaṃ anucariyāyapathaṃ (syā.) anukkamamāno na passeyya pākārasandhiṃ vā pākāravivaraṃ vā, antamaso biḷāranikkhamanamattampi. Tassa evamassa na passeyya tassa evamassa (syā.) – ‘ye kho keci oḷārikā pāṇā imaṃ nagaraṃ pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā, sabbe te imināva dvārena pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā’ti. Evameva kho me, bhante, dhammanvayo vidito – ‘ye te, bhante, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ [T 2.0099] arahanto sammāsambuddhā[M 2.0071], sabbe te bhagavanto pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu supatiṭṭhitacittā sattabojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhiṃsu. Yepi te, bhante, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā[V 2.0066], sabbe te bhagavanto pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu supatiṭṭhitacittā satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhissanti. Bhagavāpi, bhante, etarahi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu supatiṭṭhitacitto satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’”ti.

146. Venerable sir, I do not possess the knowledge that penetrates the minds of the Arahants, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones of the past, future, and present; however, I have understood the sequence of the Dhamma. Just as, venerable sir, a king's frontier city might have strong ramparts, strong walls and gate-towers, with a single gate, and there would be a gatekeeper who is wise, competent, and intelligent, one who keeps out strangers and admits acquaintances. As he patrols the path encircling the city, he would not see any joint or gap in the wall, not even one large enough for a cat to slip out. It would occur to him: 'Whatever gross beings enter or leave this city, all do so only by this gate.' In the same way, venerable sir, I have understood the sequence of the Dhamma: 'All those Blessed Ones, Arahants, Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones who were in the past abandoned the five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—with minds well-established in the four foundations of mindfulness, and having developed the seven factors of enlightenment as they truly are, they all fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect self-enlightenment. All those Blessed Ones, Arahants, Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones who will be in the future will abandon the five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—with minds well-established in the four foundations of mindfulness, and having developed the seven factors of enlightenment as they truly are, they too will fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect self-enlightenment. The Blessed One, venerable sir, who is now the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, has abandoned the five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—with a mind well-established in the four foundations of mindfulness, and having developed the seven factors of enlightenment as they truly are, has fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect self-enlightenment.'

147. Tatrapi sudaṃ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṃ viharanto pāvārikambavane [P 2.0084] etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – “iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā”ti.

147. There too, while the Blessed One was dwelling at Nāḷandā in Pāvārika's mango grove, he frequently gave this Dhamma talk to the bhikkhus: "Such is virtue, such is concentration, such is wisdom. Concentration, when cultivated by virtue, is of great fruit and great benefit. Wisdom, when cultivated by concentration, is of great fruit and great benefit. The mind, when cultivated by wisdom, is rightly freed from the taints, namely, the taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance."

Dussīlaādīnavā

The Dangers of Immorality

148. Atha kho bhagavā nāḷandāyaṃ yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “āyāmānanda, yena pāṭaligāmo tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi[T 2.0100]. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena pāṭaligāmo tadavasari. Assosuṃ kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā – “bhagavā kira pāṭaligāmaṃ anuppatto”ti. Atha kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “adhivāsetu no, bhante, bhagavā āvasathāgāra”nti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena āvasathāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā sabbasanthariṃ [M 2.0072] sabbasantharitaṃ satthataṃ (syā.), sabbasanthariṃ santhataṃ (ka.) āvasathāgāraṃ santharitvā āsanāni paññapetvā udakamaṇikaṃ patiṭṭhāpetvā telapadīpaṃ āropetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “sabbasantharisanthataṃ sabbasanthariṃ santhataṃ (sī. syā. pī. ka.), bhante, āvasathāgāraṃ, āsanāni paññattāni, udakamaṇiko patiṭṭhāpito, telapadīpo āropito; yassadāni, bhante, bhagavā kālaṃ maññatī”ti. Atha [P 2.0085] kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ idaṃ padaṃ vinayamahāvagga na dissati. Nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena yena āvasathāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṃ pavisitvā [V 2.0067] majjhimaṃ thambhaṃ nissāya puratthābhimukho puratthimābhimukho (ka.) nisīdi. Bhikkhusaṅghopi kho pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṃ pavisitvā pacchimaṃ bhittiṃ [T 2.0101] nissāya puratthābhimukho nisīdi bhagavantameva purakkhatvā. Pāṭaligāmikāpi kho upāsakā pāde pakkhāletvā āvasathāgāraṃ pavisitvā puratthimaṃ bhittiṃ nissāya pacchimābhimukhā nisīdiṃsu bhagavantameva purakkhatvā.

148. Then the Blessed One, having stayed at Nāḷandā as long as he pleased, addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to Pāṭaligāma.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied the Venerable Ānanda to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, went to Pāṭaligāma. The lay followers of Pāṭaligāma heard, “The Blessed One, it is said, has arrived at Pāṭaligāma.” Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma said this to the Blessed One: “May the Blessed One, venerable sir, consent to our rest house.” The Blessed One consented by his silence. Then the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma, having understood the Blessed One’s consent, rose from their seats, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and approached the rest house. Having approached, they spread the rest house with all manner of coverings, prepared the seats, set up a large water pot, and lit an oil lamp. Then they approached the Blessed One, paid homage, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the rest house is spread with all manner of coverings, the seats are prepared, the large water pot is set up, and the oil lamp is lit. Now, venerable sir, it is for the Blessed One to do as he sees fit.” Then the Blessed One, in the evening, having dressed, took his bowl and robe and, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, approached the rest house. Having approached, he washed his feet, entered the rest house, and sat down facing east, leaning against the central pillar. The Saṅgha of bhikkhus also washed their feet, entered the rest house, and sat down facing east, leaning against the western wall, with the Blessed One before them. The lay followers of Pāṭaligāma also washed their feet, entered the rest house, and sat down facing west, leaning against the eastern wall, with the Blessed One before them.

149. Atha kho bhagavā pāṭaligāmike upāsake āmantesi – “pañcime, gahapatayo, ādīnavā dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā. Katame pañca? Idha, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno pamādādhikaraṇaṃ mahatiṃ bhogajāniṃ nigacchati. Ayaṃ paṭhamo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.

149. Then the Blessed One addressed the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma: “Householders, there are these five dangers for an immoral person due to failure in virtue. What are the five? Here, householders, an immoral person who has failed in virtue, on account of negligence, incurs a great loss of wealth. This is the first danger for an immoral person due to failure in virtue.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa pāpako kittisaddo abbhuggacchati. Ayaṃ dutiyo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.

“Furthermore, householders, for an immoral person who has failed in virtue, a bad reputation arises. This is the second danger for an immoral person due to failure in virtue.”

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno yaññadeva parisaṃ upasaṅkamati – yadi khattiyaparisaṃ yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṃ yadi gahapatiparisaṃ yadi samaṇaparisaṃ – avisārado upasaṅkamati maṅkubhūto. Ayaṃ tatiyo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.

“Furthermore, householders, an immoral person, one whose virtue has failed, approaches whatever assembly—whether an assembly of nobles, an assembly of brahmins, an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics—fearfully and disconcerted. This is the third danger for an immoral person, due to the failure in virtue.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno sammūḷho kālaṅkaroti. Ayaṃ catuttho ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.

“Furthermore, householders, an immoral person, one whose virtue has failed, dies bewildered. This is the fourth danger for an immoral person, due to the failure in virtue.

“Puna [M 2.0073] caparaṃ, gahapatayo, dussīlo sīlavipanno kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ pañcamo ādīnavo dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā. Ime kho, gahapatayo, pañca ādīnavā dussīlassa sīlavipattiyā.

“Furthermore, householders, an immoral person, one whose virtue has failed, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell. This is the fifth danger for an immoral person, due to the failure in virtue. These, householders, are the five dangers for an immoral person, due to the failure in virtue.

Sīlavantaānisaṃsa

The Benefits for the Virtuous

150. “Pañcime[T 2.0102][P 2.0086], gahapatayo, ānisaṃsā sīlavato sīlasampadāya. Katame pañca? Idha, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno appamādādhikaraṇaṃ mahantaṃ bhogakkhandhaṃ adhigacchati. Ayaṃ paṭhamo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.

150. “Householders, there are these five benefits for a virtuous person, through the accomplishment of virtue. What are the five? Here, householders, a virtuous person, one accomplished in virtue, on account of diligence, acquires a great mass of wealth. This is the first benefit for a virtuous person, through the accomplishment of virtue.

“Puna [V 2.0068] caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavato sīlasampannassa kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchati. Ayaṃ dutiyo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.

“Furthermore, householders, a good reputation spreads for a virtuous person, one accomplished in virtue. This is the second benefit for a virtuous person, through the accomplishment of virtue.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno yaññadeva parisaṃ upasaṅkamati – yadi khattiyaparisaṃ yadi brāhmaṇaparisaṃ yadi gahapatiparisaṃ yadi samaṇaparisaṃ visārado upasaṅkamati amaṅkubhūto. Ayaṃ tatiyo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.

“Furthermore, householders, a virtuous person, one accomplished in virtue, approaches whatever assembly—whether an assembly of nobles, an assembly of brahmins, an assembly of householders, or an assembly of ascetics—confidently and composed. This is the third benefit for a virtuous person, through the accomplishment of virtue.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno asammūḷho kālaṅkaroti. Ayaṃ catuttho ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya.

“Furthermore, householders, a virtuous person, one accomplished in virtue, dies unbewildered. This is the fourth benefit for a virtuous person, through the accomplishment of virtue.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, sīlavā sīlasampanno kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Ayaṃ pañcamo ānisaṃso sīlavato sīlasampadāya. Ime kho, gahapatayo, pañca ānisaṃsā sīlavato sīlasampadāyā”ti.

“Furthermore, householders, a virtuous person, one accomplished in virtue, on the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. This is the fifth benefit for a virtuous person, through the accomplishment of virtue. These, householders, are the five benefits for a virtuous person, through the accomplishment of virtue.”

151. Atha kho bhagavā pāṭaligāmike upāsake bahudeva rattiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uyyojesi – “abhikkantā kho, gahapatayo, ratti, yassadāni tumhe kālaṃ maññathā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho pāṭaligāmikā upāsakā bhagavato paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu. Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkantesu pāṭaligāmikesu upāsakesu [T 2.0103] suññāgāraṃ pāvisi.

151. Then the Blessed One, having instructed, established, sharpened, and gladdened the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma with a Dhamma talk for much of the night, dismissed them, saying: ‘The night is far advanced, householders. It is now time for what you deem fit.’ ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma replied to the Blessed One. Then they rose from their seats, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping their right side towards him, and departed. Soon after the lay followers of Pāṭaligāma had left, the Blessed One entered a secluded dwelling.

Pāṭaliputtanagaramāpanaṃ

The Building of the City of Pāṭaliputta

152. Tena [M 2.0074] kho pana samayena sunidhavassakārā sunīdhavassakārā (syā. ka.) magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpenti vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāya. Tena samayena sambahulā devatāyo [P 2.0087] sahasseva sahassasseva (sī. pī. ka.), sahassaseva (ṭīkāyaṃ pāṭhantaraṃ), sahassasahasseva (udānaṭṭhakathā) pāṭaligāme vatthūni pariggaṇhanti. Yasmiṃ padese mahesakkhā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, mahesakkhānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ padese majjhimā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, majjhimānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ padese nīcā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, nīcānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Addasā kho bhagavā dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena tā devatāyo sahasseva pāṭaligāme vatthūni pariggaṇhantiyo. Atha kho bhagavā [V 2.0069] rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “ke nu kho ko nu kho (sī. syā. pī. ka.), ānanda, pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpentī”ti māpetīti (sī. syā. pī. ka.)? “Sunidhavassakārā, bhante, magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpenti vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāyā”ti. “Seyyathāpi, ānanda, devehi tāvatiṃsehi saddhiṃ mantetvā, evameva kho, ānanda, sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṃ māpenti vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāya. Idhāhaṃ, ānanda, addasaṃ dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sambahulā devatāyo sahasseva pāṭaligāme vatthūni pariggaṇhantiyo. Yasmiṃ[T 2.0104], ānanda, padese mahesakkhā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, mahesakkhānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ padese majjhimā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, majjhimānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yasmiṃ padese nīcā devatā vatthūni pariggaṇhanti, nīcānaṃ tattha raññaṃ rājamahāmattānaṃ cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetuṃ. Yāvatā, ānanda, ariyaṃ āyatanaṃ yāvatā vaṇippatho idaṃ agganagaraṃ bhavissati pāṭaliputtaṃ puṭabhedanaṃ[P 2.0088]. Pāṭaliputtassa kho, ānanda, tayo antarāyā bhavissanti – aggito vā udakato vā mithubhedā vā”ti.

152. Now at that time, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, were building a city at the village of Pāṭali to repel the Vajjis. At that time, numerous devas in their thousands were taking possession of dwelling sites in the village of Pāṭali. In whatever region powerful devas take possession of dwelling sites, the minds of powerful kings and chief ministers incline toward having dwellings built there. In whatever region devas of middle rank take possession of dwelling sites, the minds of kings and chief ministers of middle rank incline toward having dwellings built there. In whatever region devas of low rank take possession of dwelling sites, the minds of kings and chief ministers of low rank incline toward having dwellings built there. The Blessed One, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human eye, saw those devas in their thousands taking possession of dwelling sites in the village of Pāṭali. Then the Blessed One, having risen at the time of dawn, addressed the Venerable Ānanda: 'Ānanda, who is building a city in the village of Pāṭali?' 'Venerable sir, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, are building a city in the village of Pāṭali to repel the Vajjis.' 'Ānanda, it is as if they were building after consulting with the devas of Tāvatiṃsa. Even so, Ānanda, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, are building a city in the village of Pāṭali to repel the Vajjis. Here, Ānanda, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human eye, I saw numerous devas in their thousands taking possession of dwelling sites in the village of Pāṭali. Ānanda, in whatever region powerful devas take possession of dwelling sites, the minds of powerful kings and chief ministers incline toward having dwellings built there. In whatever region devas of middle rank take possession of dwelling sites, the minds of kings and chief ministers of middle rank incline toward having dwellings built there. In whatever region devas of low rank take possession of dwelling sites, the minds of kings and chief ministers of low rank incline toward having dwellings built there. Ānanda, as far as the domain of the noble ones extends, as far as there is a trade route, this Pāṭaliputta will be the foremost city, a place for the unbinding of merchandise. For Pāṭaliputta, Ānanda, there will be three dangers: from fire, or from water, or from internal discord.'

153. Atha [M 2.0075] kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu, ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “adhivāsetu no bhavaṃ gotamo ajjatanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā yena sako āvasatho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā sake āvasathe paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesuṃ – “kālo, bho gotama, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti.

153. Then Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they exchanged joyful greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded their gladdening and memorable conversation, they stood to one side. Standing to one side, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, said this to the Blessed One: 'May the honorable Gotama consent to our meal for today, together with the community of monks.' The Blessed One consented through silence. Then Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, having understood the Blessed One's consent, went to their own rest house. Having gone there, and after having excellent hard and soft food prepared in their own rest house, they had the time announced to the Blessed One: 'It is time, honorable Gotama, the meal is ready.'

Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena yena sunidhavassakārānaṃ magadhamahāmattānaṃ [T 2.0105] āvasatho tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesuṃ sampavāresuṃ. Atha kho sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho sunidhavassakāre magadhamahāmatte bhagavā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and, together with the community of monks, went to the rest house of Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha. Having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, with their own hands, served and satisfied the community of monks, with the Buddha at its head, with excellent hard and soft food. Then, when the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, took a certain low seat and sat down to one side. To Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, who were seated to one side, the Blessed One expressed his appreciation with these verses:

“Yasmiṃ [V 2.0070] padese kappeti, vāsaṃ paṇḍitajātiyo;

Sīlavantettha bhojetvā, saññate brahmacārayo brahmacārino (syā.).

‘In whatever region a person of wise disposition makes their dwelling, having fed the virtuous, the restrained, the followers of the holy life there,

“Yā tattha devatā āsuṃ, tāsaṃ dakkhiṇamādise;

Tā pūjitā pūjayanti pūjitā pūjayanti naṃ (ka.), mānitā mānayanti naṃ.

To whatever devas were there, one should dedicate the offering. Being honored, they honor him; being respected, they respect him.

“Tato [P 2.0089] naṃ anukampanti, mātā puttaṃva orasaṃ;

Devatānukampito poso, sadā bhadrāni passatī”ti.

Thereupon, they have compassion for him, as a mother for her own-born son. A person for whom the devas have compassion always sees what is good.’

Atha kho bhagavā sunidhavassakāre magadhamahāmatte imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Then the Blessed One, having expressed his appreciation to Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, with these verses, rose from his seat and departed.

154. Tena [M 2.0076] kho pana samayena sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhā honti – “yenajja samaṇo gotamo dvārena nikkhamissati, taṃ gotamadvāraṃ nāma bhavissati. Yena titthena gaṅgaṃ nadiṃ tarissati, taṃ gotamatitthaṃ nāma bhavissatī”ti. Atha kho bhagavā yena dvārena nikkhami[T 2.0106], taṃ gotamadvāraṃ nāma ahosi. Atha kho bhagavā yena gaṅgā nadī tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena gaṅgā nadī pūrā hoti samatittikā kākapeyyā. Appekacce manussā nāvaṃ pariyesanti, appekacce uḷumpaṃ pariyesanti, appekacce kullaṃ bandhanti apārā pārā (sī. syā. ka.), orā (vi. mahāvagga), pāraṃ gantukāmā. Atha kho bhagavā – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – gaṅgāya nadiyā orimatīre antarahito pārimatīre paccuṭṭhāsi saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena. Addasā kho bhagavā te manusse appekacce nāvaṃ pariyesante appekacce uḷumpaṃ pariyesante appekacce kullaṃ bandhante apārā pāraṃ gantukāme. Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

154. Now at that time, Sunidha and Vassakāra, the chief ministers of Magadha, were following closely behind the Blessed One, thinking: 'The gate by which the ascetic Gotama departs today will be named the Gotama Gate. The ford by which he crosses the river Ganges will be named the Gotama Ford.' Then the Blessed One departed by a certain gate, and it came to be named the Gotama Gate. Then the Blessed One approached the river Ganges. At that time, the river Ganges was full, level with its banks, so that a crow could drink from it. Some people, desiring to go from this shore to the far shore, were searching for a boat, some were searching for a log-raft, and some were binding together a bamboo-raft. Then the Blessed One—just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm—vanished from this shore of the river Ganges and reappeared on the far shore together with the community of monks. The Blessed One saw those people, some searching for a boat, some searching for a log-raft, and some binding together a bamboo-raft, desiring to go from this shore to the far shore. Then, the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

“Ye taranti aṇṇavaṃ saraṃ, setuṃ katvāna visajja pallalāni;

Kullañhi jano bandhati kullaṃ jano ca bandhati (syā.), kullaṃ hi jano pabandhati (sī. pī. ka.), tiṇṇā nitiṇṇā, na tiṇṇā (ka.) medhāvino janā”ti.

They who cross the flood, the lake, having built a bridge and leaving the marshes behind; while the people bind a raft, the wise have crossed over.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro.

The First Recitation Section.

Ariyasaccakathā

The Discourse on the Noble Truths

155. Atha [V 2.0071][P 2.0090] kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “āyāmānanda, yena koṭigāmo tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena koṭigāmo tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ [T 2.0107] bhagavā koṭigāme viharati. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi –

155. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: 'Come, Ānanda, let us go to Koṭigāma.' 'Very well, Bhante,' the Venerable Ānanda assented to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with a large community of monks, arrived at Koṭigāma. There the Blessed One was dwelling in Koṭigāma. There, the Blessed One addressed the monks:

“Catunnaṃ[M 2.0077], bhikkhave, ariyasaccānaṃ ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Dukkhassa, bhikkhave, ariyasaccassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Dukkhasamudayassa, bhikkhave, ariyasaccassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Dukkhanirodhassa, bhikkhave, ariyasaccassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya, bhikkhave, ariyasaccassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ dukkhasamudayo (syā.) ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ dukkhanirodho (syā.) ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, ucchinnā bhavataṇhā, khīṇā bhavanetti, natthidāni punabbhavo”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

“Monks, it is through not understanding, not penetrating the four Noble Truths that both you and I have for a long time run on and wandered through saṃsāra. Which four? Monks, it is through not understanding, not penetrating the Noble Truth of suffering that both you and I have for a long time run on and wandered through saṃsāra. Monks, it is through not understanding, not penetrating the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering that both you and I have for a long time run on and wandered through saṃsāra. Monks, it is through not understanding, not penetrating the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering that both you and I have for a long time run on and wandered through saṃsāra. Monks, it is through not understanding, not penetrating the Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering that both you and I have for a long time run on and wandered through saṃsāra. This Noble Truth of suffering, monks, has been understood and penetrated; the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering has been understood and penetrated; the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering has been understood and penetrated; the Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering has been understood and penetrated. Craving for existence is cut off, the guide to existence is exhausted, now there is no more rebirth.” This the Blessed One said. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, further said this:

“Catunnaṃ [P 2.0091] ariyasaccānaṃ, yathābhūtaṃ adassanā;

Saṃsitaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ, tāsu tāsveva jātisu.

“Not seeing the four Noble Truths as they truly are, for a long time one has wandered in these and those very births.

Tāni etāni diṭṭhāni, bhavanetti samūhatā;

Ucchinnaṃ mūlaṃ dukkhassa, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti.

These have been seen, the guide to existence is uprooted; the root of suffering is cut off, now there is no more rebirth.”

Tatrapi [T 2.0108] sudaṃ bhagavā koṭigāme viharanto etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – “iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā”ti.

There also, while dwelling at Koṭigāma, the Blessed One frequently gave this very Dhamma talk to the monks: 'Such is virtue, such is concentration, such is wisdom. Concentration developed with virtue is of great fruit, of great benefit. Wisdom developed with concentration is of great fruit, of great benefit. The mind developed with wisdom is rightly freed from the taints, that is: from the taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance.'

Anāvattidhammasambodhiparāyaṇā

Not liable to return, destined for enlightenment.

156. Atha [V 2.0072] kho bhagavā koṭigāme yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “āyāmānanda, yena nātikā nādikā (syā. pī.) tenupaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato [M 2.0078] paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena nātikā tadavasari. Tatrapi sudaṃ bhagavā nātike viharati giñjakāvasathe. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sāḷho nāma, bhante, bhikkhu nātike kālaṅkato, tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo? Nandā nāma, bhante, bhikkhunī nātike kālaṅkatā, tassā kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo? Sudatto [P 2.0092] nāma, bhante, upāsako nātike kālaṅkato, tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo? Sujātā nāma, bhante, upāsikā nātike kālaṅkatā, tassā kā gati[T 2.0109], ko abhisamparāyo? Kukkuṭo kakudho (syā.) nāma, bhante, upāsako nātike kālaṅkato, tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo? Kāḷimbo kāliṅgo (pī.), kāraḷimbo (syā.) nāma, bhante, upāsako…pe… nikaṭo nāma, bhante, upāsako… kaṭissaho kaṭissabho (sī. pī.) nāma, bhante, upāsako… tuṭṭho nāma, bhante, upāsako… santuṭṭho nāma, bhante, upāsako… bhaddo bhaṭo (syā.) nāma, bhante, upāsako… subhaddo subhaṭo (syā.) nāma, bhante, upāsako nātike kālaṅkato, tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo”ti?

156. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt in Koṭigāma for as long as he wished, addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to Nātikā.” “Yes, Venerable Sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with a large Saṅgha of monks, arrived at Nātikā. There, the Blessed One dwelt at the brick hall in Nātikā. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, the monk named Sāḷha has passed away in Nātikā. What is his destination? What is his future state? The nun named Nandā has passed away in Nātikā. What is her destination? What is her future state? The layman named Sudatta has passed away in Nātikā. What is his destination? What is his future state? The laywoman named Sujātā has passed away in Nātikā. What is her destination? What is her future state? The layman named Kukkuṭa has passed away in Nātikā. What is his destination? What is his future state? The layman named Kāḷimba… the layman named Nikaṭa… the layman named Kaṭissaha… the layman named Tuṭṭha… the layman named Santuṭṭha… the layman named Bhadda… the layman named Subhadda has passed away in Nātikā. What is his destination? What is his future state?”

157. “Sāḷho, ānanda, bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. Nandā, ānanda, bhikkhunī pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyinī anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sudatto, ānanda, upāsako tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissati. Sujātā, ānanda, upāsikā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā parāyanā (sī. syā. pī. ka.). Kukkuṭo, ānanda, upāsako pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. Kāḷimbo, ānanda, upāsako…pe… nikaṭo, ānanda, upāsako… kaṭissaho[M 2.0079], ānanda, upāsako… tuṭṭho, ānanda, upāsako [T 2.0110] … santuṭṭho, ānanda, upāsako… bhaddo, ānanda, upāsako… subhaddo, ānanda, upāsako pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā[P 2.0093]. Paropaññāsaṃ, ānanda, nātike upāsakā [V 2.0073] kālaṅkatā, pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sādhikā navuti chādhikā navuti (syā.), ānanda, nātike upāsakā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Sātirekāni dasātirekāni (syā.), ānanda, pañcasatāni nātike upāsakā kālaṅkatā, tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā.

157. “Ānanda, the monk Sāḷha, through the destruction of the taints, has realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having attained it, he dwelt therein. Ānanda, the nun Nandā, through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, has arisen spontaneously and will attain final Nibbāna there, not being of a nature to return from that world. Ānanda, the layman Sudatta, through the complete destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of lust, hatred, and delusion, is a once-returner who, having returned to this world only once, will make an end of suffering. Ānanda, the laywoman Sujātā, through the complete destruction of the three fetters, is a stream-enterer, not of a nature to fall into states of woe, is assured, and is destined for enlightenment. Ānanda, the layman Kukkuṭa, through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, has arisen spontaneously and will attain final Nibbāna there, not being of a nature to return from that world. Ānanda, the layman Kāḷimba… Ānanda, the layman Nikaṭa… Ānanda, the layman Kaṭissaha… Ānanda, the layman Tuṭṭha… Ānanda, the layman Santuṭṭha… Ānanda, the layman Bhadda… Ānanda, the layman Subhadda, through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, has arisen spontaneously and will attain final Nibbāna there, not being of a nature to return from that world. Ānanda, more than fifty laymen in Nātikā have passed away who, through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, have arisen spontaneously and will attain final Nibbāna there, not being of a nature to return from that world. Ānanda, more than ninety laymen in Nātikā have passed away who, through the complete destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of lust, hatred, and delusion, have become once-returners and, having returned to this world only once, will make an end of suffering. Ānanda, more than five hundred laymen in Nātikā have passed away who, through the complete destruction of the three fetters, have become stream-enterers, not of a nature to fall into states of woe, are assured, and are destined for enlightenment.”

Dhammādāsadhammapariyāyā

The Discourse on the Mirror of the Dhamma

158. “Anacchariyaṃ kho panetaṃ, ānanda, yaṃ manussabhūto kālaṅkareyya. Tasmiṃyeva tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ce (sī. pī.), tasmiṃ tasmiṃ kho (syā.) kālaṅkate tathāgataṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ pucchissatha, vihesā hesā, ānanda, tathāgatassa. Tasmātihānanda, dhammādāsaṃ nāma dhammapariyāyaṃ desessāmi, yena samannāgato ariyasāvako ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni [T 2.0111] khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti.

158. “It is no wonder, Ānanda, that a human being should pass away. If, for each and every one who passes away, you were to approach the Tathāgata to ask about this matter, that would be a weariness for the Tathāgata.
