Therefore, Ānanda, I will teach a discourse on the Dhamma called the Mirror of the Dhamma, endowed with which a noble disciple, should he wish, could declare of himself: ‘I am one for whom hell is destroyed, the animal womb is destroyed, the realm of ghosts is destroyed, the plane of misery, the bad destinations, and the state of ruin are destroyed. I am a stream-enterer, not of a nature to fall into states of woe, am assured, and am destined for enlightenment.’”

159. “Katamo ca so, ānanda, dhammādāso dhammapariyāyo, yena samannāgato ariyasāvako ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti?

159. “And what, Ānanda, is that discourse on the Dhamma, the Mirror of the Dhamma, endowed with which a noble disciple, should he wish, could declare of himself: ‘I am one for whom hell is destroyed, the animal womb is destroyed, the realm of ghosts is destroyed, the plane of misery, the bad destinations, and the state of ruin are destroyed. I am a stream-enterer, not of a nature to fall into states of woe, am assured, and am destined for enlightenment’?”

“Idhānanda[M 2.0080], ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti.

“Herein, Ānanda, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Thus indeed is the Blessed One: an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, a Well-Gone One, a Knower of the worlds, an unsurpassed Trainer of persons to be tamed, a Teacher of gods and humans, an Enlightened One, a Blessed One.’”

“Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.

“He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma thus: ‘The Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One, visible here and now, immediate, inviting one to come and see, leading onwards, to be realized for oneself by the wise.’”

“Saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno [P 2.0094] bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato [V 2.0074] sāvakasaṅgho yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā, esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti.

He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha thus: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the straightforward way; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the way to Nibbāna; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the proper way. That is, the four pairs of noble persons, the eight individual persons. This Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’

“Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññūpasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṃvattanikehi.

He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken, unpierced, unspotted, unblotched, liberating, praised by the wise, ungrasped, and conducive to concentration.

“Ayaṃ kho so, ānanda, dhammādāso dhammapariyāyo, yena samannāgato ariyasāvako ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti.

This, Ānanda, is that Dhamma-mirror, that discourse on the Dhamma, possessed of which a noble disciple, should he wish, can declare of himself: ‘I am one for whom hell is destroyed, the animal realm is destroyed, the realm of ghosts is destroyed, the planes of deprivation, unhappy destinations, and the lower realms are destroyed. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to fall, assured, and destined for enlightenment.’

Tatrapi [T 2.0112] sudaṃ bhagavā nātike viharanto giñjakāvasathe etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti –

There too, the Blessed One, while dwelling at Nātika in the Brick Hall, frequently gave this very Dhamma talk to the bhikkhus:

“Iti sīlaṃ iti samādhi iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā”ti.

‘Thus is virtue, thus is concentration, thus is wisdom. Concentration, when developed by virtue, is of great fruit and great benefit. Wisdom, when developed by concentration, is of great fruit and great benefit. The mind, when developed by wisdom, is completely freed from the taints, namely: the taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance.’

160. Atha [M 2.0081] kho bhagavā nātike yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “āyāmānanda, yena vesālī tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena vesālī tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati ambapālivane. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi –

160. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt at Nātika for as long as he wished, addressed the Venerable Ānanda: ‘Come, Ānanda, let us go to Vesālī.’ ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, arrived at Vesālī. There the Blessed One dwelt in Vesālī, in Ambapālī’s grove. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus:

“Sato, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vihareyya sampajāno, ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sato hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā [P 2.0095] vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu vedanānupassī…pe… citte cittānupassī…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sato hoti.

‘Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending; this is our instruction to you. And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu mindful? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful—having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings… mind in mind… phenomena in phenomena—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful—having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. This, bhikkhus, is how a bhikkhu is mindful.

“Kathañca[V 2.0075], bhikkhave, bhikkhu sampajāno hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abhikkante paṭikkante sampajānakārī hoti, ālokite vilokite sampajānakārī hoti, samiñjite [T 2.0113] pasārite sampajānakārī hoti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇe sampajānakārī hoti, asite pīte khāyite sāyite sampajānakārī hoti, uccārapassāvakamme sampajānakārī hoti, gate ṭhite nisinne sutte jāgarite bhāsite tuṇhībhāve sampajānakārī hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sampajāno hoti. Sato, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vihareyya sampajāno, ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī”ti.

‘And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu clearly comprehending? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu acts with clear comprehension when going forward and returning; when looking ahead and looking around; when bending and stretching his limbs; when wearing his double robe, bowl, and outer robe; when eating, drinking, chewing, and savoring; when defecating and urinating; when walking, standing, sitting, sleeping, waking, speaking, and keeping silent. This, bhikkhus, is how a bhikkhu is clearly comprehending. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell mindful and clearly comprehending—this is our instruction to you.’

Ambapālīgaṇikā

Ambapālī the Courtesan

161. Assosi kho ambapālī gaṇikā – “bhagavā kira vesāliṃ anuppatto vesāliyaṃ viharati mayhaṃ ambavane”ti. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhaddāni bhaddāni yānāni yojāpetvā bhaddaṃ bhaddaṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhaddehi bhaddehi yānehi vesāliyā niyyāsi. Yena sako ārāmo tena pāyāsi. Yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā, yānā paccorohitvā pattikāva yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [M 2.0082] nisinnaṃ kho ambapāliṃ gaṇikaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

161. The courtesan Ambapālī heard: “The Blessed One, it seems, has arrived at Vesālī and is dwelling in my mango grove.” Then Ambapālī the courtesan had fine carriages harnessed, and mounting a fine carriage, with fine carriages, she set out from Vesālī. She went to where her own park was. As far as the ground was passable for a carriage, she went by carriage; then dismounting from the carriage, she approached the Blessed One on foot. Having approached, she paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened Ambapālī the courtesan, who was sitting to one side, with a Dhamma talk. Then Ambapālī the courtesan, having been instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One’s Dhamma talk, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, accept tomorrow’s meal from me.” The Blessed One consented by means of silence. Then Ambapālī the courtesan, understanding the Blessed One’s consent, rose from her seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed.

Assosuṃ [T 2.0114] kho vesālikā licchavī – “bhagavā kira vesāliṃ [P 2.0096] anuppatto vesāliyaṃ viharati ambapālivane”ti. Atha kho te licchavī bhaddāni bhaddāni yānāni yojāpetvā bhaddaṃ bhaddaṃ yānaṃ abhiruhitvā bhaddehi bhaddehi yānehi vesāliyā niyyiṃsu. Tatra ekacce licchavī nīlā honti nīlavaṇṇā nīlavatthā nīlālaṅkārā, ekacce licchavī pītā honti pītavaṇṇā pītavatthā pītālaṅkārā, ekacce licchavī lohitā honti lohitavaṇṇā lohitavatthā lohitālaṅkārā, ekacce licchavī odātā honti odātavaṇṇā odātavatthā odātālaṅkārā. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā daharānaṃ daharānaṃ licchavīnaṃ akkhena akkhaṃ cakkena cakkaṃ yugena yugaṃ paṭivaṭṭesi parivattesi (vi. mahāvagga). Atha kho te licchavī ambapāliṃ gaṇikaṃ etadavocuṃ – “kiṃ, je ambapāli[V 2.0076], daharānaṃ daharānaṃ licchavīnaṃ akkhena akkhaṃ cakkena cakkaṃ yugena yugaṃ paṭivaṭṭesī”ti? “Tathā hi pana me, ayyaputtā, bhagavā nimantito svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. “Dehi, je ambapāli, etaṃ ekaṃ (ka.) bhattaṃ satasahassenā”ti. “Sacepi me, ayyaputtā, vesāliṃ sāhāraṃ dassatha dajjeyyātha (vi. mahāvagga), evamahaṃ taṃ evampi mahantaṃ (syā.), evaṃ mahantaṃ (sī. pī.) bhattaṃ na dassāmī”ti neva dajjāhaṃ taṃ bhattanti (vi. mahāvagga). Atha kho te licchavī aṅguliṃ phoṭesuṃ – “jitamha jitamhā (bahūsu) vata bho ambakāya, jitamha vata bho ambakāyā”ti “jitamhā vata bho ambapālikāya vañcitamhā vata bho ambapālikāyā”ti (syā.).

The Licchavis of Vesālī heard: “The Blessed One, it seems, has arrived at Vesālī and is dwelling in Ambapālī’s grove.” Then those Licchavis had fine carriages harnessed, and mounting a fine carriage, with fine carriages, they set out from Vesālī. Among them, some Licchavis were blue, of blue complexion, with blue clothes and blue ornaments; some Licchavis were yellow, of yellow complexion, with yellow clothes and yellow ornaments; some Licchavis were red, of red complexion, with red clothes and red ornaments; some Licchavis were white, of white complexion, with white clothes and white ornaments. Then the courtesan Ambapālī collided with the young Licchavis, axle to axle, wheel to wheel, yoke to yoke. Then those Licchavis said to Ambapālī the courtesan: “Why, Ambapālī, do you collide with the young Licchavis, axle to axle, wheel to wheel, yoke to yoke?” “It is because, my lords, the Blessed One has been invited by me for tomorrow’s meal, together with the community of monks.” “Ambapālī, give us this meal for a hundred thousand!” “My lords, even if you were to give me Vesālī with its territories, I would not give up that meal.” Then those Licchavis snapped their fingers, saying: “Sirs, we have indeed been defeated by a woman! Sirs, we have indeed been defeated by a woman!”

Atha kho te licchavī yena [T 2.0115] ambapālivanaṃ tena pāyiṃsu. Addasā kho bhagavā te licchavī dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna bhikkhū āmantesi – “yesaṃ [M 2.0083] yehi (vi. mahāvagga), bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ devā tāvatiṃsā adiṭṭhapubbā, oloketha, bhikkhave, licchaviparisaṃ; apaloketha, bhikkhave[P 2.0097], licchaviparisaṃ; upasaṃharatha, bhikkhave, licchaviparisaṃ – tāvatiṃsasadisa”nti. Atha kho te licchavī yāvatikā yānassa bhūmi, yānena gantvā, yānā paccorohitvā pattikāva yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te licchavī bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho te licchavī bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassitā samādapitā samuttejitā sampahaṃsitā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “adhivāsetu no, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā te licchavī etadavoca – “adhivutthaṃ adhivāsitaṃ (syā.) kho me, licchavī, svātanāya ambapāliyā gaṇikāya bhatta”nti. Atha kho te licchavī aṅguliṃ phoṭesuṃ – “jitamha vata bho ambakāya, jitamha vata bho ambakāyā”ti. Atha kho te licchavī bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu.

Then those Licchavis proceeded to Ambapālī’s grove. The Blessed One saw those Licchavis coming from afar. Seeing them, he addressed the monks: “Monks, those among you who have not previously seen the Tāvatiṃsa gods, look at this assembly of Licchavis; observe this assembly of Licchavis; compare this assembly of Licchavis to the assembly of the Tāvatiṃsa gods.” Then those Licchavis went as far as the carriage-road extended, then dismounted from their carriages and approached the Blessed One on foot. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened those Licchavis, who were sitting to one side, with a Dhamma talk. Then those Licchavis, having been instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One’s Dhamma talk, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One, together with the community of monks, accept tomorrow’s meal from us.” Then the Blessed One said to those Licchavis: “Licchavis, I have already accepted tomorrow’s meal from the courtesan Ambapālī.” Then those Licchavis snapped their fingers, saying: “Sirs, we have indeed been defeated by a woman! Sirs, we have indeed been defeated by a woman!” Then those Licchavis, having delighted in and rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words, rose from their seats, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed.

162. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā tassā rattiyā accayena sake ārāme paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā bhagavato kālaṃ [T 2.0116] ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena yena ambapāliyā gaṇikāya nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi. Atha kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ [P 2.0098] nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho ambapālī gaṇikā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “imāhaṃ, bhante, ārāmaṃ buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa dammī”ti. Paṭiggahesi bhagavā ārāmaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā ambapāliṃ gaṇikaṃ dhammiyā kathāya [V 2.0077] sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Tatrapi sudaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharanto ambapālivane etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti [M 2.0084] – “iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā”ti.

162. Then, when that night had passed, the courtesan Ambapālī had fine hard and soft food prepared in her own park and had the time announced to the Blessed One: “It is time, Venerable Sir, the meal is ready.” Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed, took his bowl and robe, and together with the community of monks, went to the dwelling of the courtesan Ambapālī. Having gone there, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then the courtesan Ambapālī, with her own hands, served and satisfied the community of monks headed by the Buddha with fine hard and soft food. When the Blessed One had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, the courtesan Ambapālī took a low seat and sat to one side. Seated to one side, the courtesan Ambapālī said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, I give this park to the community of monks with the Buddha at its head.” The Blessed One accepted the park. Then the Blessed One, having instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened the courtesan Ambapālī with a talk on the Dhamma, rose from his seat and departed. There too, while the Blessed One was dwelling in Vesālī in Ambapālī’s Grove, he often gave this talk on the Dhamma to the monks: “Such is virtue, such is concentration, such is wisdom. Concentration, when developed by virtue, is of great fruit and great benefit. Wisdom, when developed by concentration, is of great fruit and great benefit. The mind, when developed by wisdom, is rightly liberated from the taints, namely: the taint of sensual desire, the taint of becoming, and the taint of ignorance.”

Veḷuvagāmavassūpagamanaṃ

Entering the Rains-Residence at Veḷuvagāma

163. Atha kho bhagavā ambapālivane yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “āyāmānanda, yena veḷuvagāmako beḷuvagāmako (sī. pī.) tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando [T 2.0117] bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena veḷuvagāmako tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā veḷuvagāmake viharati. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “etha tumhe, bhikkhave, samantā vesāliṃ yathāmittaṃ yathāsandiṭṭhaṃ yathāsambhattaṃ vassaṃ upetha upagacchatha (syā.). Ahaṃ pana idheva veḷuvagāmake vassaṃ upagacchāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā samantā vesāliṃ yathāmittaṃ yathāsandiṭṭhaṃ yathāsambhattaṃ [P 2.0099] vassaṃ upagacchiṃsu. Bhagavā pana tattheva veḷuvagāmake vassaṃ upagacchi.

163. Then the Blessed One, having dwelt in Ambapālī’s Grove for as long as he wished, addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to the village of Veḷuva.” “Yes, Venerable Sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with a large community of monks, went to the village of Veḷuva. There the Blessed One dwelt in the village of Veḷuva. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Come, monks, enter upon the rains-residence around Vesālī, wherever you have friends, acquaintances, or intimates. I, however, will enter upon the rains-residence right here in the village of Veḷuva.” “Yes, Venerable Sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One, and they entered upon the rains-residence around Vesālī, wherever they had friends, acquaintances, or intimates. The Blessed One, however, entered upon the rains-residence right there in the village of Veḷuva.

164. Atha kho bhagavato vassūpagatassa kharo ābādho uppajji, bāḷhā vedanā vattanti māraṇantikā. Tā sudaṃ bhagavā sato sampajāno adhivāsesi avihaññamāno. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “na kho metaṃ patirūpaṃ, yvāhaṃ anāmantetvā upaṭṭhāke anapaloketvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ parinibbāyeyyaṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ ābādhaṃ vīriyena paṭipaṇāmetvā jīvitasaṅkhāraṃ adhiṭṭhāya vihareyya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā taṃ ābādhaṃ vīriyena paṭipaṇāmetvā jīvitasaṅkhāraṃ adhiṭṭhāya vihāsi. Atha kho bhagavato so ābādho paṭipassambhi. Atha kho bhagavā gilānā vuṭṭhito gilānavuṭṭhito (saddanīti) aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā vihārā nikkhamma vihārapacchāyāyaṃ paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ [T 2.0118] nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ [M 2.0085] etadavoca – “diṭṭho me, bhante, bhagavato phāsu; diṭṭhaṃ me, bhante, bhagavato khamanīyaṃ, api ca me, bhante, madhurakajāto viya kāyo. Disāpi me na pakkhāyanti; dhammāpi maṃ na paṭibhanti bhagavato gelaññena, api ca me, bhante, ahosi kācideva assāsamattā [V 2.0078] – ‘na tāva bhagavā parinibbāyissati, na yāva bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ārabbha kiñcideva udāharatī’”ti.

164. Then, after the Blessed One had entered upon the rains-residence, a severe illness arose in him, and sharp, death-like pains occurred. But the Blessed One endured them, mindful, clearly comprehending, and untroubled. Then this thought occurred to the Blessed One: “It would not be proper for me to attain final Nibbāna without addressing my attendants and without taking leave of the community of monks. Why don’t I, by means of energy, suppress this illness, resolve upon the life-formation, and remain?” Then the Blessed One, by means of energy, suppressed the illness, resolved upon the life-formation, and remained. Then the Blessed One’s illness subsided. Then the Blessed One, having recovered from the illness, not long after his recovery, came out from his dwelling and sat down on a prepared seat in the shade behind the dwelling. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, I have seen the Blessed One’s comfort; I have seen the Blessed One’s well-being. And yet, Venerable Sir, on account of the Blessed One’s illness, my body felt as if it were drugged. The directions were not clear to me, and the teachings were not apparent to me. But, Venerable Sir, I had this one small measure of comfort: ‘The Blessed One will not attain final Nibbāna so long as he has not made some statement concerning the community of monks.’”

165. “Kiṃ [P 2.0100] panānanda, bhikkhusaṅgho mayi paccāsīsati paccāsiṃsati (sī. syā.)? Desito, ānanda, mayā dhammo anantaraṃ abāhiraṃ karitvā. Natthānanda, tathāgatassa dhammesu ācariyamuṭṭhi. Yassa nūna, ānanda, evamassa – ‘ahaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharissāmī’ti vā ‘mamuddesiko bhikkhusaṅgho’ti vā, so nūna, ānanda, bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ārabbha kiñcideva udāhareyya. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharissāmī’ti vā ‘mamuddesiko bhikkhusaṅgho’ti vā. Sakiṃ kiṃ (sī. pī.), ānanda, tathāgato bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ārabbha kiñcideva udāharissati. Ahaṃ kho panānanda, etarahi jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto. Āsītiko me vayo vattati. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, jajjarasakaṭaṃ veṭhamissakena veḷumissakena (syā.), veghamissakena (pī.), vedhamissakena, vekhamissakena (ka.) yāpeti, evameva kho, ānanda, veṭhamissakena maññe tathāgatassa kāyo yāpeti. Yasmiṃ, ānanda, samaye tathāgato sabbanimittānaṃ amanasikārā ekaccānaṃ vedanānaṃ nirodhā animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ upasampajja viharati, phāsutaro, ānanda, tasmiṃ samaye tathāgatassa [T 2.0119] kāyo hoti. Tasmātihānanda, attadīpā viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā. Kathañcānanda, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo? Idhānanda, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati atāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo[M 2.0086]. Ye [P 2.0101] hi keci, ānanda, etarahi vā mama vā accayena attadīpā viharissanti attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, tamatagge me te, ānanda, bhikkhū bhavissanti ye keci sikkhākāmā”ti.

165. “But what, Ānanda, does the community of monks expect from me? The Dhamma has been taught by me, Ānanda, without making it internal or external. There is no ‘teacher’s fist,’ Ānanda, in the Tathāgata’s teachings. For the one, Ānanda, who might think, ‘I will lead the community of monks,’ or ‘The community of monks is directed by me,’ it is he, Ānanda, who would surely make some pronouncement concerning the community of monks. But for the Tathāgata, Ānanda, it is not so that he thinks, ‘I will lead the community of monks,’ or ‘The community of monks is directed by me.’ For what reason, Ānanda, will the Tathāgata make any pronouncement concerning the community of monks? I, Ānanda, am now old, aged, elderly, far-gone in years, and have reached the final stage of life. My age is eighty. Just as, Ānanda, a decrepit cart is kept going with the help of bindings, so too, Ānanda, I think the Tathāgata’s body is kept going with the help of bindings. At the time, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata, by not attending to any signs and by the cessation of certain feelings, enters and abides in the signless concentration of mind, at that time, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s body is more comfortable. Therefore, Ānanda, dwell with yourselves as an island, with yourselves as a refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge. And how, Ānanda, does a monk dwell with himself as an island, with himself as a refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge? Here, Ānanda, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings… the mind in the mind… dhammas in dhammas—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. In this way, Ānanda, a monk dwells with himself as an island, with himself as a refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge. Whoever, Ānanda, either now or after my passing, shall dwell with themselves as an island, with themselves as a refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge—those monks of mine, Ānanda, will be in the highest place, that is, whoever are desirous of the training.”

Dutiyabhāṇavāro.

The Second Recitation Section.

Nimittobhāsakathā

The Discourse on the Hint and the Sign

166. Atha [V 2.0079][P 2.0102] kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “gaṇhāhi, ānanda, nisīdanaṃ, yena cāpālaṃ cetiyaṃ pāvālaṃ (cetiyaṃ (syā.) tenupasaṅkamissāma divā vihārāyā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā nisīdanaṃ ādāya bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi. Atha [T 2.0120] kho bhagavā yena cāpālaṃ cetiyaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Āyasmāpi kho ānando bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi.

166. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and entered Vesālī for alms. Having wandered for alms in Vesālī, after the meal, on returning from the alms-round, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Take a sitting mat, Ānanda. We will go to the Cāpāla Shrine to spend the day.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One, and taking a sitting mat, he followed closely behind the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One went to the Cāpāla Shrine. Having gone there, he sat down on the prepared seat. The Venerable Ānanda, too, having paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side.

167. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “ramaṇīyā, ānanda, vesālī, ramaṇīyaṃ udenaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ gotamakaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sattambaṃ sattambakaṃ (pī.) cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ bahuputtaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sārandadaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ cāpālaṃ cetiyaṃ. Yassa [P 2.0103] kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno ākaṅkhamāno (?), ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā”ti. Evampi kho āyasmā ānando bhagavatā oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ; na bhagavantaṃ yāci – “tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna”nti, yathā taṃ mārena pariyuṭṭhitacitto. Dutiyampi [M 2.0087] kho bhagavā…pe… tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “ramaṇīyā, ānanda, vesālī, ramaṇīyaṃ udenaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ gotamakaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sattambaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ bahuputtaṃ [T 2.0121] cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sārandadaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ cāpālaṃ cetiyaṃ. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā”ti. Evampi kho āyasmā ānando bhagavatā oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ[P 2.0104]; na bhagavantaṃ yāci – “tiṭṭhatu[V 2.0080], bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna”nti, yathā taṃ mārena pariyuṭṭhitacitto. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “gaccha tvaṃ, ānanda, yassadāni kālaṃ maññasī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā avidūre aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi.

167. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable Ānanda, who was sitting to one side: “Ānanda, Vesālī is delightful, the Udena Shrine is delightful, the Gotamaka Shrine is delightful, the Sattamba Shrine is delightful, the Bahuputta Shrine is delightful, the Sārandada Shrine is delightful, and the Cāpāla Shrine is delightful. Ānanda, for anyone who has developed the four bases of spiritual power, frequently practiced them, made them a vehicle, made them a basis, established them, consolidated them, and properly undertaken them, they could, should they wish, remain for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon. The Tathāgata, Ānanda, has developed the four bases of spiritual power, frequently practiced them, made them a vehicle, made them a basis, established them, consolidated them, and properly undertaken them. Should he wish, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could remain for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon.” Even so, when such an obvious sign was being made by the Blessed One, when such a clear hint was being given, the Venerable Ānanda was not able to penetrate it. He did not request the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One remain for an aeon, may the Sugata remain for an aeon, for the welfare and happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans,” as his mind was overcome by Māra. A second time… and a third time the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, Vesālī is delightful… Should he wish, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could remain for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon.” Even so, when such an obvious sign was being made by the Blessed One, when such a clear hint was being given, the Venerable Ānanda was not able to penetrate it. He did not request the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One remain for an aeon, may the Sugata remain for an aeon, for the welfare and happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans,” as his mind was overcome by Māra. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Go now, Ānanda, and do what you deem it is time for.” “So be it, Venerable Sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied, and having assented to the Blessed One, he rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him with his right side toward him, and sat down at the foot of a certain tree not far away.

Mārayācanakathā

The Account of Māra's Entreaty

168. Atha kho māro pāpimā acirapakkante āyasmante ānande yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho māro pāpimā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālo [T 2.0122] dāni, bhante, bhagavato. Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me bhikkhū na sāvakā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānī uttāniṃ (ka.), uttāni (sī. pī.) karissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessantī’ti[M 2.0088]. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, bhikkhū bhagavato sāvakā viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā [P 2.0105] sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhanti desenti paññapenti paṭṭhapenti vivaranti vibhajanti uttānīkaronti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desenti. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato.

168. Then, not long after the Venerable Ānanda had left, Māra the Evil One approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, Māra the Evil One said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One now attain final parinibbāna; may the Sugata attain final parinibbāna. Now, Venerable Sir, is the time for the Blessed One’s final parinibbāna. For, Venerable Sir, this statement was made by the Blessed One: ‘I will not attain final parinibbāna, Evil One, until my bhikkhu disciples are skilled, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing properly, and living in conformity with the Dhamma; and until, having learned their own teacher’s doctrine, they can expound, teach, proclaim, establish, reveal, analyze, and make it clear; and until they can thoroughly refute with reason any opposing doctrines that have arisen and teach the Dhamma with its wonders.’ But now, Venerable Sir, the bhikkhu disciples of the Blessed One are skilled, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing properly, and living in conformity with the Dhamma. Having learned their own teacher’s doctrine, they expound, teach, proclaim, establish, reveal, analyze, and make it clear; and they thoroughly refute with reason any opposing doctrines that have arisen and teach the Dhamma with its wonders. Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One now attain final parinibbāna; may the Sugata attain final parinibbāna. Now, Venerable Sir, is the time for the Blessed One’s final parinibbāna.”

“Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me bhikkhuniyo na sāvikā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessantī’ti[T 2.0123]. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, bhikkhuniyo bhagavato sāvikā viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo[V 2.0081], sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhanti desenti paññapenti paṭṭhapenti vivaranti vibhajanti uttānīkaronti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desenti. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato.

Venerable Sir, these words were spoken by the Blessed One: ‘O Evil One, I will not attain final Parinibbāna as long as my female disciples, the bhikkhunīs, have not become skilled, disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing the proper practice, and habitually practicing in conformity with the Dhamma; as long as they will not, having learned their own teacher's doctrine, declare it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, analyze it, and make it clear; and as long as they will not, having thoroughly refuted an arisen opposing doctrine rightfully, teach the wondrous Dhamma.’ But now, Venerable Sir, the Blessed One's female disciples, the bhikkhunīs, are skilled, disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing the proper practice, and habitually practicing in conformity with the Dhamma. Having learned their own teacher's doctrine, they declare, teach, make known, establish, reveal, analyze, and make it clear. Having thoroughly refuted an arisen opposing doctrine rightfully, they teach the wondrous Dhamma. Let the Blessed One now attain final Parinibbāna, Venerable Sir, let the Well-farer attain final Parinibbāna. Now, Venerable Sir, is the time for the Blessed One's final Parinibbāna.

“Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me upāsakā na sāvakā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessantī’ti. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, upāsakā bhagavato sāvakā viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhanti desenti paññapenti paṭṭhapenti vivaranti vibhajanti uttānīkaronti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desenti. Parinibbātudāni[M 2.0089], bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni[T 2.0124], bhante, bhagavato.

Venerable Sir, these words were spoken by the Blessed One: ‘O Evil One, I will not attain final Parinibbāna as long as my male lay disciples have not become skilled, disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing the proper practice, and habitually practicing in conformity with the Dhamma; as long as they will not, having learned their own teacher's doctrine, declare it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, analyze it, and make it clear; and as long as they will not, having thoroughly refuted an arisen opposing doctrine rightfully, teach the wondrous Dhamma.’ But now, Venerable Sir, the Blessed One's male lay disciples are skilled, disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing the proper practice, and habitually practicing in conformity with the Dhamma. Having learned their own teacher's doctrine, they declare, teach, make known, establish, reveal, analyze, and make it clear. Having thoroughly refuted an arisen opposing doctrine rightfully, they teach the wondrous Dhamma. Let the Blessed One now attain final Parinibbāna, Venerable Sir, let the Well-farer attain final Parinibbāna. Now, Venerable Sir, is the time for the Blessed One's final Parinibbāna.

“Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me upāsikā na sāvikā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessantī’ti. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, upāsikā bhagavato sāvikā viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ [P 2.0106] uggahetvā ācikkhanti desenti paññapenti paṭṭhapenti vivaranti vibhajanti uttānīkaronti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desenti. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato.

Venerable Sir, these words were spoken by the Blessed One: ‘O Evil One, I will not attain final Parinibbāna as long as my female lay disciples have not become skilled, disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing the proper practice, and habitually practicing in conformity with the Dhamma; as long as they will not, having learned their own teacher's doctrine, declare it, teach it, make it known, establish it, reveal it, analyze it, and make it clear; and as long as they will not, having thoroughly refuted an arisen opposing doctrine rightfully, teach the wondrous Dhamma.’ But now, Venerable Sir, the Blessed One's female lay disciples are skilled, disciplined, confident, learned, bearers of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing the proper practice, and habitually practicing in conformity with the Dhamma. Having learned their own teacher's doctrine, they declare, teach, make known, establish, reveal, analyze, and make it clear. Having thoroughly refuted an arisen opposing doctrine rightfully, they teach the wondrous Dhamma. Let the Blessed One now attain final Parinibbāna, Venerable Sir, let the Well-farer attain final Parinibbāna. Now, Venerable Sir, is the time for the Blessed One's final Parinibbāna.

“Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – ‘na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi[V 2.0082], yāva me idaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na iddhaṃ ceva bhavissati phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita’nti. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, bhagavato brahmacariyaṃ iddhaṃ ceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ, yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato”ti[T 2.0125].

Venerable Sir, these words were spoken by the Blessed One: ‘O Evil One, I will not attain final Parinibbāna as long as this holy life of mine has not become prosperous, flourishing, widespread, known to many, extensive, and well-proclaimed among gods and humans.’ But now, Venerable Sir, the Blessed One's holy life is prosperous, flourishing, widespread, known to many, extensive, and well-proclaimed among gods and humans. Let the Blessed One now attain final Parinibbāna, Venerable Sir, let the Well-farer attain final Parinibbāna. Now, Venerable Sir, is the time for the Blessed One's final Parinibbāna.

Evaṃ vutte bhagavā māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavoca – “appossukko tvaṃ, pāpima, hohi, na ciraṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī”ti.

When this was said, the Blessed One said this to Māra the Evil One: ‘Be without anxiety, Evil One. The final Parinibbāna of the Tathāgata will not be long from now. After the passing of three months from now, the Tathāgata will attain final Parinibbāna.’

Āyusaṅkhāraossajjanaṃ

The Relinquishing of the Life-Formation

169. Atha kho bhagavā cāpāle cetiye sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossaji. Ossaṭṭhe ca bhagavatā āyusaṅkhāre mahābhūmicālo ahosi bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso lomahaṃso (syā.), devadundubhiyo devadudrabhiyo (ka.) ca phaliṃsu[M 2.0090]. Atha kho bhagavā [P 2.0107] etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

169. Then the Blessed One, at the Cāpāla Shrine, mindful and clearly comprehending, relinquished the life-formation. And when the life-formation was relinquished by the Blessed One, there was a great earthquake, terrifying and hair-raising, and the celestial drums burst. Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

“Tulamatulañca sambhavaṃ, bhavasaṅkhāramavassaji muni;

Ajjhattarato samāhito, abhindi kavacamivattasambhava”nti.

“The Sage relinquished the measurable and the immeasurable, the cause of becoming, the formation of existence. Delighting inwardly, composed, he shattered what arose in himself, as one shatters armor.”

Mahābhūmicālahetu

The Cause of the Great Earthquake

170. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – “acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, mahā vatāyaṃ bhūmicālo; sumahā vatāyaṃ bhūmicālo bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso; devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsu. Ko nu kho hetu ko paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāyā”ti?

170. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Ānanda: “How wonderful, sirs, how amazing, sirs! This earthquake is great, this earthquake is truly great, terrifying and hair-raising! And the celestial drums have burst. What, I wonder, is the cause, what is the condition for the manifestation of a great earthquake?”

Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi, ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, mahā vatāyaṃ, bhante, bhūmicālo; sumahā vatāyaṃ[V 2.0083], bhante, bhūmicālo bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso; devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsu. Ko nu kho, bhante[T 2.0126], hetu ko paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāyā”ti?

Then the Venerable Ānanda went to the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated thus, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “It is wonderful, venerable sir, it is amazing, venerable sir! This earthquake is great, venerable sir; this earthquake is truly great, venerable sir, terrifying and hair-raising! And the celestial drums have resounded. What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition for the manifestation of a great earthquake?”

171. “Aṭṭha kho ime, ānanda, hetū, aṭṭha paccayā mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya. Katame aṭṭha? Ayaṃ, ānanda, mahāpathavī udake patiṭṭhitā, udakaṃ vāte patiṭṭhitaṃ, vāto ākāsaṭṭho. Hoti kho so, ānanda, samayo, yaṃ mahāvātā vāyanti. Mahāvātā vāyantā udakaṃ kampenti. Udakaṃ kampitaṃ pathaviṃ kampeti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo [P 2.0108] hetu paṭhamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

171. “Ānanda, there are these eight causes, these eight conditions for the manifestation of a great earthquake. What are the eight? This great earth, Ānanda, is established on water, the water is established on wind, and the wind is established in space. There is, Ānanda, a time when great winds blow. When the great winds blow, they cause the water to quake. The quaking water causes the earth to quake. This is the first cause, the first condition for the manifestation of a great earthquake.

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, samaṇo vā hoti brāhmaṇo vā iddhimā cetovasippatto, devo vā mahiddhiko mahānubhāvo, tassa parittā pathavīsaññā bhāvitā hoti, appamāṇā āposaññā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ kampeti saṅkampeti sampakampeti sampavedheti. Ayaṃ dutiyo hetu dutiyo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, there is an ascetic or a brahmin who is possessed of psychic power, who has attained mastery of mind, or a deva of great psychic power and great might. He has developed a limited perception of earth and an immeasurable perception of water. He makes this earth shake, quake, convulse, and tremble. This is the second cause, the second condition for the manifestation of a great earthquake.

“Puna [M 2.0091] caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā bodhisatto tusitakāyā cavitvā sato sampajāno mātukucchiṃ okkamati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ tatiyo hetu tatiyo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta, mindful and clearly comprehending, passes away from the host of Tusita devas and descends into his mother’s womb, then this earth shakes, quakes, convulses, and trembles. This is the third cause, the third condition for the manifestation of a great earthquake.

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā bodhisatto sato sampajāno mātukucchismā nikkhamati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ catuttho hetu catuttho paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Bodhisatta, mindful and clearly comprehending, emerges from his mother’s womb, then this earth shakes, quakes, convulses, and trembles. This is the fourth cause, the fourth condition for the manifestation of a great earthquake.

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā [T 2.0127] tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ pañcamo hetu pañcamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata awakens to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, then this earth shakes, quakes, convulses, and trembles. This is the fifth cause, the fifth condition for the manifestation of a great earthquake.

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā tathāgato anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavatteti, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ chaṭṭho hetu chaṭṭho paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata sets in motion the unsurpassed Wheel of Dhamma, then this earth shakes, quakes, convulses, and trembles. This is the sixth cause, the sixth condition for the manifestation of a great earthquake.

“Puna [V 2.0084] caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā tathāgato sato sampajāno āyusaṅkhāraṃ ossajjati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ sattamo hetu sattamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata, mindful and clearly comprehending, relinquishes the life-formation, then this earth shakes, quakes, convulses, and trembles. This is the seventh cause, the seventh condition for the manifestation of a great earthquake.

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, yadā tathāgato anupādisesāya [P 2.0109] nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati, tadāyaṃ pathavī kampati saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhati. Ayaṃ aṭṭhamo hetu aṭṭhamo paccayo mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāya. Ime kho, ānanda, aṭṭha hetū, aṭṭha paccayā mahato bhūmicālassa pātubhāvāyā”ti.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata passes into final Nibbāna with the Nibbāna-element that has no residue remaining, then this earth shakes, quakes, convulses, and trembles. This is the eighth cause, the eighth condition for the manifestation of a great earthquake. These, Ānanda, are the eight causes, the eight conditions for the manifestation of a great earthquake.”

Aṭṭha parisā

The Eight Assemblies

172. “Aṭṭha kho imā, ānanda, parisā. Katamā aṭṭha? Khattiyaparisā, brāhmaṇaparisā, gahapatiparisā, samaṇaparisā, cātumahārājikaparisā cātummahārājikaparisā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), tāvatiṃsaparisā, māraparisā, brahmaparisā. Abhijānāmi kho panāhaṃ, ānanda[M 2.0092], anekasataṃ khattiyaparisaṃ upasaṅkamitā. Tatrapi mayā sannisinnapubbaṃ ceva sallapitapubbañca sākacchā ca samāpajjitapubbā[T 2.0128]. Tattha yādisako tesaṃ vaṇṇo hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ vaṇṇo hoti. Yādisako tesaṃ saro hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ saro hoti. Dhammiyā kathāya sandassemi samādapemi samuttejemi sampahaṃsemi. Bhāsamānañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ bhāsati devo vā manusso vā’ti? Dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā antaradhāyāmi. Antarahitañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ antarahito devo vā manusso vā’ti? Abhijānāmi kho panāhaṃ, ānanda, anekasataṃ brāhmaṇaparisaṃ…pe… gahapatiparisaṃ… samaṇaparisaṃ… cātumahārājikaparisaṃ… tāvatiṃsaparisaṃ… māraparisaṃ… brahmaparisaṃ upasaṅkamitā. Tatrapi mayā sannisinnapubbaṃ ceva sallapitapubbañca sākacchā ca samāpajjitapubbā. Tattha yādisako tesaṃ vaṇṇo hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ vaṇṇo hoti. Yādisako tesaṃ saro hoti, tādisako mayhaṃ saro hoti. Dhammiyā kathāya sandassemi samādapemi samuttejemi sampahaṃsemi. Bhāsamānañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ bhāsati devo vā manusso vā’ti? Dhammiyā [P 2.0110] kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā antaradhāyāmi. Antarahitañca maṃ na jānanti – ‘ko nu kho ayaṃ antarahito devo vā manusso vā’ti? Imā kho, ānanda, aṭṭha parisā.

172. “Ānanda, there are these eight assemblies. What are the eight? The assembly of nobles, the assembly of brahmins, the assembly of householders, the assembly of ascetics, the assembly of the devas of the Four Great Kings, the assembly of the Tāvatiṃsa devas, the assembly of Māra, and the assembly of Brahmās. Indeed, Ānanda, I recall having approached many hundreds of assemblies of nobles. There, I have sat with them, conversed with them, and engaged in discussion with them. Whatever their appearance was, such was my appearance. Whatever their voice was, such was my voice. I instruct, urge, inspire, and gladden them with a talk on the Dhamma. While I am speaking, they do not know me, thinking: ‘Who is this that speaks—a deva or a human?’ Then, having instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened them with a talk on the Dhamma, I disappear. And when I have disappeared, they do not know me, thinking: ‘Who is this that has disappeared—a deva or a human?’ Indeed, Ānanda, I recall having approached many hundreds of assemblies of brahmins… of householders… of ascetics… of the devas of the Four Great Kings… of the Tāvatiṃsa devas… of Māra… of Brahmās. There, I have sat with them, conversed with them, and engaged in discussion with them. Whatever their appearance was, such was my appearance. Whatever their voice was, such was my voice. I instruct, urge, inspire, and gladden them with a talk on the Dhamma. While I am speaking, they do not know me, thinking: ‘Who is this that speaks—a deva or a human?’ Then, having instructed, urged, inspired, and gladdened them with a talk on the Dhamma, I disappear. And when I have disappeared, they do not know me, thinking: ‘Who is this that has disappeared—a deva or a human?’ These, Ānanda, are the eight assemblies.”

Aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni

The Eight Bases of Mastery

173. “Aṭṭha [V 2.0085] kho imāni, ānanda, abhibhāyatanāni. Katamāni aṭṭha[T 2.0129]? Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

173. “Ānanda, there are these eight bases of overcoming. What are the eight? A certain person, being one who perceives form internally, sees forms externally, limited, of beautiful and ugly appearance. One has the perception: ‘Having overcome them, I know, I see.’ This is the first base of overcoming.”

“Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ dutiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

“A certain person, being one who perceives form internally, sees forms externally, immeasurable, of beautiful and ugly appearance. One has the perception: ‘Having overcome them, I know, I see.’ This is the second base of overcoming.”

“Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ tatiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

“A certain person, not perceiving form internally, sees forms externally, limited, of beautiful and ugly appearance. One has the perception: ‘Having overcome them, I know, I see.’ This is the third base of overcoming.”

“Ajjhattaṃ [M 2.0093] arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ catutthaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

“A certain person, not perceiving form internally, sees forms externally, immeasurable, of beautiful and ugly appearance. One has the perception: ‘Having overcome them, I know, I see.’ This is the fourth base of overcoming.”

“Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma umāpupphaṃ nīlaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ nīlanidassanaṃ nīlanibhāsaṃ. Seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ nīlaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ nīlanidassanaṃ nīlanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ pañcamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

“A certain person, not perceiving form internally, sees forms externally that are blue, of blue appearance, blue in manifestation, and with a blue radiance. Just as a flax flower is blue, of blue appearance, blue in manifestation, and with a blue radiance; or just as a cloth from Bārāṇasī, smooth on both sides, is blue, of blue appearance, blue in manifestation, and with a blue radiance. In the same way, a certain person, not perceiving form internally, sees forms externally that are blue, of blue appearance, blue in manifestation, and with a blue radiance. One has the perception: ‘Having overcome them, I know, I see.’ This is the fifth base of overcoming.”

“Ajjhattaṃ [P 2.0111] arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma kaṇikārapupphaṃ pītaṃ pītavaṇṇaṃ pītanidassanaṃ pītanibhāsaṃ. Seyyathā [T 2.0130] vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ pītaṃ pītavaṇṇaṃ pītanidassanaṃ pītanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

“A certain person, not perceiving form internally, sees forms externally that are yellow, of yellow appearance, yellow in manifestation, and with a yellow radiance. Just as a kaṇikāra flower is yellow, of yellow appearance, yellow in manifestation, and with a yellow radiance; or just as a cloth from Bārāṇasī, smooth on both sides, is yellow, of yellow appearance, yellow in manifestation, and with a yellow radiance. In the same way, a certain person, not perceiving form internally, sees forms externally that are yellow, of yellow appearance, yellow in manifestation, and with a yellow radiance. One has the perception: ‘Having overcome them, I know, I see.’ This is the sixth base of overcoming.”

“Ajjhattaṃ [V 2.0086] arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma bandhujīvakapupphaṃ lohitakaṃ lohitakavaṇṇaṃ lohitakanidassanaṃ lohitakanibhāsaṃ. Seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ lohitakaṃ lohitakavaṇṇaṃ lohitakanidassanaṃ lohitakanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ sattamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

“A certain person, not perceiving form internally, sees forms externally that are red, of red appearance, red in manifestation, and with a red radiance. Just as a bandhujīvaka flower is red, of red appearance, red in manifestation, and with a red radiance; or just as a cloth from Bārāṇasī, smooth on both sides, is red, of red appearance, red in manifestation, and with a red radiance. In the same way, a certain person, not perceiving form internally, sees forms externally that are red, of red appearance, red in manifestation, and with a red radiance. One has the perception: ‘Having overcome them, I know, I see.’ This is the seventh base of overcoming.”

“Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma osadhitārakā [M 2.0094] odātā odātavaṇṇā odātanidassanā odātanibhāsā. Seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ odātaṃ odātavaṇṇaṃ odātanidassanaṃ odātanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni. ‘Tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ[T 2.0131]. Imāni kho, ānanda, aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni.

“A certain person, not perceiving form internally, sees forms externally that are white, of white appearance, white in manifestation, and with a white radiance. Just as the morning star is white, of white appearance, white in manifestation, and with a white radiance; or just as a cloth from Bārāṇasī, smooth on both sides, is white, of white appearance, white in manifestation, and with a white radiance. In the same way, a certain person, not perceiving form internally, sees forms externally that are white, of white appearance, white in manifestation, and with a white radiance. One has the perception: ‘Having overcome them, I know, I see.’ This is the eighth base of overcoming. These, Ānanda, are the eight bases of overcoming.”

Aṭṭha vimokkhā

The Eight Liberations

174. “Aṭṭha kho ime, ānanda, vimokkhā. Katame aṭṭha? Rūpī rūpāni passati, ayaṃ paṭhamo vimokkho. Ajjhattaṃ [P 2.0112] arūpasaññī bahiddhā rūpāni passati, ayaṃ dutiyo vimokkho. Subhanteva adhimutto hoti, ayaṃ tatiyo vimokkho. Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ catuttho vimokkho. Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ pañcamo vimokkho. Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ chaṭṭho vimokkho. Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ sattamo vimokkho. Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati, ayaṃ aṭṭhamo vimokkho. Ime kho, ānanda, aṭṭha vimokkhā.

174. “Ānanda, there are these eight liberations. What are the eight? Possessing form, one sees forms; this is the first liberation. Not perceiving form internally, one sees forms externally; this is the second liberation. One is intent only on the beautiful; this is the third liberation. With the complete transcendence of perceptions of form, with the cessation of perceptions of resistance, with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, perceiving ‘space is infinite,’ one enters and dwells in the sphere of infinite space; this is the fourth liberation. By completely transcending the sphere of infinite space, perceiving ‘consciousness is infinite,’ one enters and dwells in the sphere of infinite consciousness; this is the fifth liberation. By completely transcending the sphere of infinite consciousness, perceiving ‘there is nothing,’ one enters and dwells in the sphere of nothingness; this is the sixth liberation. By completely transcending the sphere of nothingness, one enters and dwells in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; this is the seventh liberation. By completely transcending the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one enters and dwells in the cessation of perception and feeling; this is the eighth liberation. These, Ānanda, are the eight liberations.”

175. “Ekamidāhaṃ[V 2.0087], ānanda, samayaṃ uruvelāyaṃ viharāmi najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhe paṭhamābhisambuddho. Atha kho, ānanda, māro pāpimā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, ānanda, māro pāpimā maṃ [T 2.0132] etadavoca – ‘parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā; parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato’ti. Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, ānanda, māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavocaṃ –

175. “Once, Ānanda, I was dwelling at Uruvelā, on the bank of the Nerañjarā River, at the Goatherd’s Banyan Tree, having just attained full enlightenment. Then, Ānanda, Māra the Evil One approached me; having approached, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, Ānanda, Māra the Evil One said this to me: ‘Venerable sir, let the Blessed One now attain final Nibbāna! Let the Well-farer attain final Nibbāna! Now, venerable sir, is the time for the Blessed One’s final Nibbāna.’ When this was said, I, Ānanda, said this to Māra the Evil One:

“‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me bhikkhū na sāvakā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā [M 2.0095] sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti [P 2.0113] vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.

“‘Evil One, I will not attain final Nibbāna so long as my bhikkhu disciples have not become competent, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing properly, and living in accordance with the Dhamma; so long as they have not, after learning their own teacher’s doctrine, been able to explain, teach, proclaim, establish, disclose, analyze, and clarify it; and so long as they have not been able to thoroughly refute with the Dhamma any contrary doctrine that has arisen and teach the Dhamma with its wonders.’

“‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me bhikkhuniyo na sāvikā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena [T 2.0133] suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.

“‘Evil One, I will not attain final Nibbāna so long as my bhikkhunī disciples have not become competent, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing properly, and living in accordance with the Dhamma; so long as they have not, after learning their own teacher’s doctrine, been able to explain, teach, proclaim, establish, disclose, analyze, and clarify it; and so long as they have not been able to thoroughly refute with the Dhamma any contrary doctrine that has arisen and teach the Dhamma with its wonders.’

“‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me upāsakā na sāvakā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārino, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.

“‘Evil One, I will not attain final Nibbāna so long as my male lay disciples have not become competent, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing properly, and living in accordance with the Dhamma; so long as they have not, after learning their own teacher’s doctrine, been able to explain, teach, proclaim, establish, disclose, analyze, and clarify it; and so long as they have not been able to thoroughly refute with the Dhamma any contrary doctrine that has arisen and teach the Dhamma with its wonders.’

“‘Na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me upāsikā na sāvikā bhavissanti viyattā vinītā visāradā bahussutā dhammadharā dhammānudhammappaṭipannā sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacāriniyo, sakaṃ ācariyakaṃ uggahetvā ācikkhissanti desessanti paññapessanti paṭṭhapessanti vivarissanti vibhajissanti uttānīkarissanti, uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desessanti.

“‘Evil One, I will not attain final Nibbāna so long as my female lay disciples have not become competent, disciplined, confident, learned, upholders of the Dhamma, practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing properly, and living in accordance with the Dhamma; so long as they have not, after learning their own teacher’s doctrine, been able to explain, teach, proclaim, establish, disclose, analyze, and clarify it; and so long as they have not been able to thoroughly refute with the Dhamma any contrary doctrine that has arisen and teach the Dhamma with its wonders.’

“‘Na [V 2.0088] tāvāhaṃ, pāpima, parinibbāyissāmi, yāva me idaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na iddhañceva bhavissati phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita’nti.

“‘Evil One, I will not attain final Nibbāna so long as this holy life of mine has not become successful, flourishing, widespread, known to many, extensive, and well proclaimed among gods and humans.’”

176. “Idāneva kho, ānanda, ajja cāpāle cetiye māro pāpimā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho, ānanda, māro pāpimā maṃ etadavoca – ‘parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato. Bhāsitā kho panesā, bhante, bhagavatā vācā – “na tāvāhaṃ, pāpima[M 2.0096], parinibbāyissāmi[P 2.0114], yāva me bhikkhū na sāvakā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me bhikkhuniyo na sāvikā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me upāsakā na sāvakā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me upāsikā na sāvikā bhavissanti…pe… yāva me idaṃ brahmacariyaṃ na iddhañceva bhavissati phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ, yāva devamanussehi suppakāsita”nti. Etarahi kho pana, bhante, bhagavato brahmacariyaṃ [T 2.0134] iddhañceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ, yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ. Parinibbātudāni, bhante, bhagavā, parinibbātu sugato, parinibbānakālodāni, bhante, bhagavato’ti.

176. “Just now, Ānanda, today at the Cāpāla Shrine, Māra the Evil One approached me; having approached, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, Ānanda, Māra the Evil One said this to me: ‘Venerable sir, let the Blessed One now attain final Nibbāna, let the Well-farer attain final Nibbāna. Now, venerable sir, is the time for the Blessed One’s final Nibbāna. For this word, venerable sir, was spoken by the Blessed One: “Evil One, I will not attain final Nibbāna so long as my bhikkhu disciples have not become... so long as my bhikkhunī disciples have not become... so long as my male lay disciples have not become... so long as my female lay disciples have not become... so long as this holy life of mine has not become successful, flourishing, widespread, known to many, extensive, and well-proclaimed among gods and humans.” But now, venerable sir, the Blessed One’s holy life is successful, flourishing, widespread, known to many, extensive, and well-proclaimed among gods and humans. Venerable sir, let the Blessed One now attain final Nibbāna, let the Well-farer attain final Nibbāna. Now, venerable sir, is the time for the Blessed One’s final Nibbāna.’”

177. “Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, ānanda, māraṃ pāpimantaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘appossukko tvaṃ, pāpima, hohi, naciraṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’ti. Idāneva kho, ānanda, ajja cāpāle cetiye tathāgatena satena sampajānena āyusaṅkhāro ossaṭṭho”ti.

177. “When this was said, Ānanda, I said this to Māra the Evil One: ‘Be unconcerned, Evil One. The final Nibbāna of the Tathāgata will not be long from now. After the passing of three months from now, the Tathāgata will attain final Nibbāna.’ Just now, Ānanda, today at the Cāpāla Shrine, the Tathāgata, being mindful and clearly comprehending, has relinquished the life-formation.”

Ānandayācanakathā

The Chapter on Ānanda's Request

178. Evaṃ [P 2.0115] vutte āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna”nti.

178. When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One remain for the aeon! May the Well-farer remain for the aeon, for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans!”

“Alaṃdāni, ānanda. Mā tathāgataṃ yāci, akālodāni, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yācanāyā”ti. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā ānando…pe… tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna”nti.

“Enough now, Ānanda. Do not entreat the Tathāgata. Now is not the time, Ānanda, for entreating the Tathāgata.” For a second time... For a third time, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One remain for the aeon! May the Well-farer remain for the aeon, for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans!”

“Saddahasi [V 2.0089] tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatassa bodhi”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Atha kiñcarahi tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāvatatiyakaṃ abhinippīḷesī”ti? “Sammukhā metaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno [T 2.0135] kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā. So [M 2.0097] ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’”ti. “Saddahasi tvaṃ, ānandā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ tathāgatena evaṃ oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna”nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.

“Do you have faith, Ānanda, in the Tathāgata's enlightenment?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Then why, Ānanda, did you harass the Tathāgata up to a third time?” “Venerable sir, this was heard by me in the presence of the Blessed One, received in his presence: ‘Ānanda, anyone who has developed, cultivated, made a vehicle of, made a basis of, established, become familiar with, and properly undertaken the four bases of spiritual power could, if he so wishes, remain for an aeon or for the remainder of the aeon. The Tathāgata, Ānanda, has developed, cultivated, made a vehicle of, made a basis of, established, become familiar with, and properly undertaken the four bases of spiritual power. If he so wishes, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could remain for an aeon or for the remainder of the aeon.’ “Do you have faith, Ānanda?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Therefore, Ānanda, this is your own wrongdoing, your own fault, that when such a gross sign, such a gross hint was being made by the Tathāgata, you were not able to penetrate it and did not entreat the Tathāgata: ‘Venerable sir, may the Blessed One remain for the aeon! May the Sugata remain for the aeon, for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans!’ If you, Ānanda, had entreated the Tathāgata, he would have rejected your words twice, but the third time he would have consented. Therefore, Ānanda, this is your own wrongdoing, your own fault.”

179. “Ekamidāhaṃ, ānanda, samayaṃ rājagahe viharāmi gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tatrāpi kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, āmantesiṃ [P 2.0116] – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, ānanda, rājagahaṃ, ramaṇīyo, ānanda, gijjhakūṭo pabbato. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya [T 2.0136] kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dve te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.

179. “On one occasion, Ānanda, I was dwelling in Rājagaha on Vulture Peak mountain. There too, Ānanda, I addressed you: ‘Delightful, Ānanda, is Rājagaha; delightful, Ānanda, is Vulture Peak mountain. Whoever, Ānanda, has developed, cultivated, made a vehicle of, made a basis of, established, become familiar with, and properly undertaken the four bases of spiritual power could, if he so wishes, remain for an aeon or for the remainder of the aeon. The Tathāgata, Ānanda, has developed, cultivated, made a vehicle of, made a basis of, established, become familiar with, and properly undertaken the four bases of spiritual power. If he so wishes, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could remain for an aeon or for the remainder of the aeon.’ Even so, Ānanda, when such a gross sign, such a gross hint was being made by the Tathāgata, you were not able to penetrate it and did not entreat the Tathāgata: ‘Venerable sir, may the Blessed One remain for the aeon! May the Sugata remain for the aeon, for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans!’ If you, Ānanda, had entreated the Tathāgata, he would have rejected your words twice, but the third time he would have consented. Therefore, Ānanda, this is your own wrongdoing, your own fault.”

180. “Ekamidāhaṃ, ānanda, samayaṃ tattheva rājagahe viharāmi gotamanigrodhe…pe… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi corapapāte… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi vebhārapasse sattapaṇṇiguhāyaṃ… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi isigilipasse kāḷasilāyaṃ… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi [V 2.0090] sītavane sappasoṇḍikapabbhāre… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi tapodārāme… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi jīvakambavane… tattheva rājagahe viharāmi maddakucchismiṃ migadāye [M 2.0098] tatrāpi kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, āmantesiṃ – ‘ramaṇīyaṃ, ānanda, rājagahaṃ, ramaṇīyo gijjhakūṭo pabbato, ramaṇīyo gotamanigrodho, ramaṇīyo corapapāto, ramaṇīyā vebhārapasse sattapaṇṇiguhā, ramaṇīyā isigilipasse kāḷasilā, ramaṇīyo sītavane sappasoṇḍikapabbhāro[P 2.0117], ramaṇīyo tapodārāmo, ramaṇīyo veḷuvane [T 2.0137] kalandakanivāpo, ramaṇīyaṃ jīvakambavanaṃ, ramaṇīyo maddakucchismiṃ migadāyo. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā…pe… ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.
