180. “On one occasion, Ānanda, I was dwelling right there in Rājagaha at the Gotama Banyan... and so on... right there in Rājagaha I was dwelling at the Robbers' Cliff... right there in Rājagaha I was dwelling at the Sattapaṇṇi Cave on the side of Mount Vebhāra... right there in Rājagaha I was dwelling at the Black Rock on the side of Mount Isigili... right there in Rājagaha I was dwelling at the Sappasoṇḍika Ravine in the Sītavana... right there in Rājagaha I was dwelling at the Tapodārāma... right there in Rājagaha I was dwelling at the Kalandakanivāpa in the Veḷuvana... right there in Rājagaha I was dwelling in Jīvaka's Mango Grove... right there in Rājagaha I was dwelling at the Migadāya in Maddakucchi. There too, Ānanda, I addressed you: 'Delightful, Ānanda, is Rājagaha; delightful is the Gijjhakūṭa mountain; delightful is the Gotama Banyan; delightful is the Robbers' Cliff; delightful is the Sattapaṇṇi Cave on the side of Mount Vebhāra; delightful is the Black Rock on the side of Mount Isigili; delightful is the Sappasoṇḍika Ravine in the Sītavana; delightful is the Tapodārāma; delightful is the Kalandakanivāpa in the Veḷuvana; delightful is Jīvaka's Mango Grove; delightful is the Migadāya in Maddakucchi. Anyone, Ānanda, who has developed the four bases of spiritual power... and so on... The Tathāgata, Ānanda, if he so wishes, could remain for an aeon or for the remainder of the aeon.’ Even so, Ānanda, when such a gross sign, such a gross hint was being made by the Tathāgata, you were not able to penetrate it, and you did not entreat the Tathāgata: 'Venerable sir, may the Blessed One remain for an aeon! May the Sugata remain for an aeon for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, benefit, and happiness of gods and humans!' If you, Ānanda, had entreated the Tathāgata, the Tathāgata would have rejected your words twice, but the third time he would have consented. Therefore, Ānanda, this is your own wrongdoing, this is your own fault.”

181. “Ekamidāhaṃ, ānanda, samayaṃ idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi udene cetiye. Tatrāpi kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, āmantesiṃ – ‘ramaṇīyā, ānanda, vesālī, ramaṇīyaṃ udenaṃ cetiyaṃ. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā [T 2.0138] bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu, bhante, bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya, tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.

181. On one occasion, Ānanda, I was dwelling right here in Vesālī at the Udena Shrine. There too, Ānanda, I addressed you: 'Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī; delightful is the Udena Shrine. For whosoever, Ānanda, the four bases of psychic power have been developed, frequently practiced, made a vehicle, made a foundation, established, familiarized, and well undertaken, if he so wishes, he could remain for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon. The Tathāgata, Ānanda, has the four bases of psychic power that have been developed, frequently practiced, made a vehicle, made a foundation, established, familiarized, and well undertaken. If he so wishes, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could remain for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon.' Even so, Ānanda, when such a gross sign was being made by the Tathāgata, when such a gross hint was being given, you were not able to comprehend it, and you did not beseech the Tathāgata: 'Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One remain for an aeon! May the Sugata remain for an aeon for the welfare of the multitude, for the happiness of the multitude, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans!' If you, Ānanda, had beseeched the Tathāgata, the Tathāgata would have rejected your words twice, and only then, the third time, would he have consented. Therefore, Ānanda, this is your own wrongdoing, this is your own fault.

182. “Ekamidāhaṃ[M 2.0099][P 2.0118], ānanda, samayaṃ idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi gotamake cetiye [V 2.0091] …pe… idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi sattambe cetiye… idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi bahuputte cetiye… idheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi sārandade cetiye… idāneva kho tāhaṃ, ānanda, ajja cāpāle cetiye āmantesiṃ – ‘ramaṇīyā, ānanda, vesālī, ramaṇīyaṃ udenaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ gotamakaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sattambaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ bahuputtaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ sārandadaṃ cetiyaṃ, ramaṇīyaṃ cāpālaṃ cetiyaṃ. Yassa kassaci, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā [T 2.0139] anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā, so ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, tathāgato kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā’ti. Evampi kho tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena oḷārike nimitte kayiramāne oḷārike obhāse kayiramāne nāsakkhi paṭivijjhituṃ, na tathāgataṃ yāci – ‘tiṭṭhatu bhagavā kappaṃ, tiṭṭhatu sugato kappaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Sace tvaṃ, ānanda, tathāgataṃ yāceyyāsi, dveva te vācā tathāgato paṭikkhipeyya, atha tatiyakaṃ adhivāseyya. Tasmātihānanda, tuyhevetaṃ dukkaṭaṃ, tuyhevetaṃ aparaddhaṃ.

182. On one occasion, Ānanda, I was dwelling right here in Vesālī at the Gotamaka Shrine... right here in Vesālī I was dwelling at the Sattamba Shrine... right here in Vesālī I was dwelling at the Bahuputta Shrine... right here in Vesālī I was dwelling at the Sārandada Shrine... and just now, Ānanda, today at the Cāpāla Shrine, I addressed you: 'Delightful, Ānanda, is Vesālī; delightful is the Udena Shrine; delightful is the Gotamaka Shrine; delightful is the Sattamba Shrine; delightful is the Bahuputta Shrine; delightful is the Sārandada Shrine; delightful is the Cāpāla Shrine. For whosoever, Ānanda, the four bases of psychic power have been developed, frequently practiced, made a vehicle, made a foundation, established, familiarized, and well undertaken, if he so wishes, he could remain for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon. The Tathāgata, Ānanda, has the four bases of psychic power that have been developed, frequently practiced, made a vehicle, made a foundation, established, familiarized, and well undertaken. If he so wishes, Ānanda, the Tathāgata could remain for an aeon or for the remainder of an aeon.' Even so, Ānanda, when such a gross sign was being made by the Tathāgata, when such a gross hint was being given, you were not able to comprehend it, and you did not beseech the Tathāgata: 'May the Blessed One remain for an aeon! May the Sugata remain for an aeon for the welfare of the multitude, for the happiness of the multitude, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans!' If you, Ānanda, had beseeched the Tathāgata, the Tathāgata would have rejected your words twice, and only then, the third time, would he have consented. Therefore, Ānanda, this is your own wrongdoing, this is your own fault.

183. “Nanu etaṃ evaṃ (syā. pī.), ānanda, mayā paṭikacceva paṭigacceva (sī. pī.) akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo. Taṃ kutettha, ānanda, labbhā, yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata mā palujjīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati’. Yaṃ kho panetaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatena cattaṃ vantaṃ muttaṃ pahīnaṃ paṭinissaṭṭhaṃ ossaṭṭho āyusaṅkhāro, ekaṃsena vācā bhāsitā – ‘na ciraṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ [P 2.0119] bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī’ti. Tañca taṃ vacanaṃ (sī.) tathāgato jīvitahetu puna paccāvamissatīti paccāgamissatīti (syā. ka.) netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Āyāmānanda, yena mahāvanaṃ kūṭāgārasālā tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho [M 2.0100] āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.

183. “Ānanda, has it not been declared by me from the very beginning: ‘With all that is dear and beloved, there is separation, parting, and alteration’? Whence, Ānanda, could it be obtained here that what is born, come into being, conditioned, and of a nature to perish, should not perish? That condition does not exist. Moreover, Ānanda, the life-formation has been relinquished, disgorged, released, abandoned, and rejected by the Tathāgata. A word has been spoken unequivocally: ‘Not long from now, the Parinibbāna of the Tathāgata will take place. After the passing of three months from now, the Tathāgata will attain Parinibbāna.’ That the Tathāgata would take that back again for the sake of life—this condition does not exist. Come, Ānanda, let us go to the hall with the peaked roof in the Great Wood.” “So be it, Venerable Sir,” the Venerable Ānanda consented to the Blessed One.

Atha kho bhagavā [T 2.0140] āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ yena mahāvanaṃ kūṭāgārasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “gaccha tvaṃ, ānanda, yāvatikā bhikkhū vesāliṃ upanissāya viharanti, te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā yāvatikā bhikkhū vesāliṃ upanissāya viharanti, te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca [V 2.0092] – “sannipatito, bhante, bhikkhusaṅgho, yassadāni, bhante, bhagavā kālaṃ maññatī”ti.

Then the Blessed One, together with the Venerable Ānanda, approached the hall with the peaked roof in the Great Wood. Having approached, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Go, Ānanda, and have all the monks who are dwelling in the vicinity of Vesālī assemble in the assembly hall.” “So be it, Venerable Sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. And having had all the monks who were dwelling in the vicinity of Vesālī assemble in the assembly hall, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, the community of monks has assembled. Now, Venerable Sir, is the time for that which the Blessed One deems fit.”

184. Atha kho bhagavā yenupaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ye te mayā dhammā abhiññā desitā, te vo sādhukaṃ uggahetvā āsevitabbā bhāvetabbā bahulīkātabbā, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Katame ca te, bhikkhave, dhammā mayā abhiññā desitā, ye vo sādhukaṃ uggahetvā āsevitabbā bhāvetabbā bahulīkātabbā, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ [P 2.0120] addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya [T 2.0141] devamanussānaṃ. Seyyathidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā cattāro sammappadhānā cattāro iddhipādā pañcindriyāni pañca balāni satta bojjhaṅgā ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo. Ime kho te, bhikkhave, dhammā mayā abhiññā desitā, ye vo sādhukaṃ uggahetvā āsevitabbā bhāvetabbā bahulīkātabbā, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna”nti.

184. Then the Blessed One approached the assembly hall. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Therefore, monks, those teachings that have been taught by me through direct knowledge, you should grasp them well, practice them, develop them, and make much of them, so that this holy life may be long-lasting and endure for a long time. That would be for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans. And what, monks, are those teachings taught by me through direct knowledge, which you should grasp well, practice, develop, and make much of, so that this holy life may be long-lasting and endure for a long time, for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans? They are: the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right strivings, the four bases of spiritual power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the Noble Eightfold Path. These, monks, are the teachings taught by me through direct knowledge, which you should grasp well, practice, develop, and make much of, so that this holy life may be long-lasting and endure for a long time, for the welfare of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”

185. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “handadāni, bhikkhave, āmantayāmi vo, vayadhammā saṅkhārā, appamādena sampādetha. Naciraṃ tathāgatassa [M 2.0101] parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ito tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ accayena tathāgato parinibbāyissatī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā ito paraṃ syāmapotthake evaṃpi pāṭho dissati –§daharāpi ca ye vuddhā, ye bālā ye ca paṇḍitā.§aḍḍhāceva daliddā ca, sabbe maccuparāyanā.§yathāpi kumbhakārassa, kataṃ mattikabhājanaṃ.§khuddakañca mahantañca, yañca pakkaṃ yañca āmakaṃ.§sabbaṃ bhedapariyantaṃ, evaṃ maccāna jīvitaṃ.§athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā. –

185. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Now, monks, I address you: conditioned things are of a nature to perish; strive on with diligence. Not long will the Parinibbāna of the Tathāgata be. After the passing of three months from now, the Tathāgata will attain Parinibbāna.” The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, further said this:

“Paripakko [T 2.0142] vayo mayhaṃ, parittaṃ mama jīvitaṃ;

Pahāya vo gamissāmi, kataṃ me saraṇamattano.

“My age is ripe, my life is short; leaving you, I will go. I have made a refuge for myself.”

“Appamattā satīmanto, susīlā hotha bhikkhavo;

Susamāhitasaṅkappā, sacittamanurakkhatha.

“Be diligent, mindful, and of excellent virtue, O monks. With well-composed thoughts, guard your own minds.”

“Yo [V 2.0093][P 2.0121] imasmiṃ dhammavinaye, appamatto vihassati;

Pahāya jātisaṃsāraṃ, dukkhassantaṃ karissatī”ti viharissati (syā.), vihessati (sī.).

“Whoever in this Dhamma and Vinaya will dwell diligently, having abandoned the round of births, will make an end of suffering.”

Tatiyo bhāṇavāro.

The Third Chapter for Recitation.

Nāgāpalokitaṃ

The Elephant’s Gaze

186. Atha [P 2.0122] kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto nāgāpalokitaṃ vesāliṃ apaloketvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “idaṃ pacchimakaṃ, ānanda, tathāgatassa vesāliyā dassanaṃ bhavissati. Āyāmānanda, yena bhaṇḍagāmo bhaṇḍugāmo (ka.) tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.

186. Then, in the morning, the Blessed One, having dressed, took his bowl and robe and entered Vesālī for alms. Having wandered for alms in Vesālī, after the meal, upon returning from the alms-round, he gazed upon Vesālī with the elephant’s gaze and addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying: 'Ānanda, this will be the Tathāgata's final sight of Vesālī. Come, Ānanda, let us approach Bhaṇḍagāma.' 'So be it, venerable sir,' the Venerable Ānanda assented to the Blessed One.

Atha [M 2.0102] kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena bhaṇḍagāmo tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bhaṇḍagāme viharati. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “catunnaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Ariyassa, bhikkhave, sīlassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Ariyassa, bhikkhave, samādhissa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ [T 2.0143] mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Ariyāya, bhikkhave, paññāya ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Ariyāya, bhikkhave, vimuttiyā ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamaṃ ceva tumhākañca. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ sīlaṃ anubuddhaṃ [P 2.0123] paṭividdhaṃ, ariyo samādhi anubuddho paṭividdho, ariyā paññā anubuddhā paṭividdhā, ariyā vimutti anubuddhā paṭividdhā, ucchinnā bhavataṇhā, khīṇā bhavanetti, natthi dāni punabbhavo”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

Then the Blessed One, together with a great Saṅgha of monks, arrived at Bhaṇḍagāma. There the Blessed One stayed in Bhaṇḍagāma. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Monks, it is through not understanding and not penetrating four things that I as well as you have for this long time run on and transmigrated. What four? Monks, it is through not understanding and not penetrating noble virtue that I as well as you have for this long time run on and transmigrated. Monks, it is through not understanding and not penetrating noble concentration that I as well as you have for this long time run on and transmigrated. Monks, it is through not understanding and not penetrating noble wisdom that I as well as you have for this long time run on and transmigrated. Monks, it is through not understanding and not penetrating noble liberation that I as well as you have for this long time run on and transmigrated. But now, monks, this noble virtue has been understood and penetrated; noble concentration has been understood and penetrated; noble wisdom has been understood and penetrated; noble liberation has been understood and penetrated. Craving for existence has been cut off, the guide to existence is exhausted, and now there is no further becoming.' This the Blessed One said. Having said this, the Well-Gone One, the Teacher, further said this:

“Sīlaṃ samādhi paññā ca, vimutti ca anuttarā;

Anubuddhā ime dhammā, gotamena yasassinā.

“Virtue, concentration, and wisdom, and liberation unsurpassed; these qualities have been realized by the glorious Gotama.

“Iti [V 2.0094] buddho abhiññāya, dhammamakkhāsi bhikkhunaṃ;

Dukkhassantakaro satthā, cakkhumā parinibbuto”ti.

“Thus the Buddha, having realized through direct knowledge, declared the Dhamma to the monks; the Teacher, the maker of an end to suffering, the One with Vision, is fully quenched.”

Tatrāpi sudaṃ bhagavā bhaṇḍagāme viharanto etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – “iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā”ti.

There also, while the Blessed One was dwelling at Bhaṇḍagāma, he frequently gave this discourse on the Dhamma to the monks: 'Such is virtue, such is concentration, such is wisdom. Concentration, when developed through virtue, is of great fruit and great benefit. Wisdom, when developed through concentration, is of great fruit and great benefit. The mind, when developed through wisdom, is completely liberated from the taints—namely, the taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance.'

Catumahāpadesakathā

The Discourse on the Four Great References

187. Atha [T 2.0144] kho bhagavā bhaṇḍagāme yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “āyāmānanda, yena hatthigāmo, yena ambagāmo, yena jambugāmo, yena bhoganagaraṃ tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho [M 2.0103] bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena bhoganagaraṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā bhoganagare viharati ānande sānandare (ka.) cetiye. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “cattārome, bhikkhave, mahāpadese desessāmi, taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ[P 2.0124], bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

187. Then, after staying at Bhaṇḍagāma as long as he pleased, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to Hatthigāma, to Ambagāma, to Jambugāma, and to Bhoganagara.” “Yes, Bhante,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, arrived at Bhoganagara. There, the Blessed One stayed at the Ānanda Cetiya in Bhoganagara. There, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you these four great authorities. Listen to it, attend to it well, I will speak.” “Yes, Bhante,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

188. “Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ, ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ. Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṃ uggahetvā sutte osāretabbāni otāretabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni otāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte osaranti otaranti (sī. pī. a. ni. 4.180, na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; imassa ca bhikkhuno duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni sutte ceva [T 2.0145] osaranti, vinaye ca sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; imassa ca bhikkhuno suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha.

188. “Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu might say: ‘Friends, I have heard this in the presence of the Blessed One, I have received it in his presence: This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s Dispensation.’ Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu’s statement should neither be approved nor rejected. Without approving or rejecting it, having learned those words and phrases well, they should be checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya. If, when being checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya, they neither conform with the Suttas nor are found in the Vinaya, the conclusion should be reached: ‘Surely, this is not the word of the Blessed One, and it has been wrongly grasped by this bhikkhu.’ Thus, bhikkhus, you should discard it. But if, when being checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya, they both conform with the Suttas and are found in the Vinaya, the conclusion should be reached: ‘Surely, this is the word of the Blessed One, and it has been well grasped by this bhikkhu.’ Bhikkhus, you should bear in mind this first great authority.

“Idha [V 2.0095] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘amukasmiṃ nāma āvāse saṅgho viharati sathero sapāmokkho. Tassa me saṅghassa sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā [T 2.0146] paṭiggahitaṃ, ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ. Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṃ uggahetvā sutte osāretabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte osaranti, na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca saṅghassa duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni sutte ceva [M 2.0104] osaranti vinaye ca sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā[P 2.0125], idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca saṅghassa suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, dutiyaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha.

“Furthermore, here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu might say: ‘In such-and-such a residence, the Saṅgha dwells with its elders and leaders. I have heard and received this in the presence of that Saṅgha: This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s Dispensation.’ Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu’s statement should neither be approved nor rejected. Without approving or rejecting it, having learned those words and phrases well, they should be checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya. If, when being checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya, they neither conform with the Suttas nor are found in the Vinaya, the conclusion should be reached: ‘Surely, this is not the word of the Blessed One, and it has been wrongly grasped by that Saṅgha.’ Thus, bhikkhus, you should discard it. But if, when being checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya, they both conform with the Suttas and are found in the Vinaya, the conclusion should be reached: ‘Surely, this is the word of the Blessed One, and it has been well grasped by that Saṅgha.’ Bhikkhus, you should bear in mind this second great authority.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘amukasmiṃ nāma āvāse sambahulā therā bhikkhū viharanti bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā. Tesaṃ me therānaṃ sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ…pe… na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tesañca therānaṃ duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni…pe… vinaye ca sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tesañca therānaṃ suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, tatiyaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha.

“Furthermore, here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu might say: ‘In such-and-such a residence, many elder bhikkhus dwell who are very learned, versed in the traditions, upholders of the Dhamma, upholders of the Vinaya, and upholders of the Mātikā. I have heard and received this in the presence of those elders: “This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s Dispensation.”’ Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu’s statement should neither be approved nor rejected. Without approving or rejecting it, having learned those words and phrases well, they should be checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya. If, when being checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya, they neither conform with the Suttas nor are found in the Vinaya, the conclusion should be reached: ‘Surely, this is not the word of the Blessed One, and it has been wrongly grasped by those elders.’ Thus, bhikkhus, you should discard it. But if, when being checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya, they both conform with the Suttas and are found in the Vinaya, the conclusion should be reached: ‘Surely, this is the word of the Blessed One, and it has been well grasped by those elders.’ Bhikkhus, you should bear in mind this third great authority.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṃ vadeyya – ‘amukasmiṃ nāma āvāse eko thero bhikkhu viharati bahussuto āgatāgamo dhammadharo vinayadharo mātikādharo. Tassa me therassa sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ayaṃ dhammo ayaṃ vinayo idaṃ satthusāsana’nti. Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṃ neva abhinanditabbaṃ nappaṭikkositabbaṃ. Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṃ uggahetvā sutte osāritabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni. Tāni ce sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte osaranti, na ca vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā, idaṃ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca therassa duggahita’nti. Itihetaṃ, bhikkhave, chaḍḍeyyātha. Tāni ca sutte osāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni sutte ceva osaranti, vinaye ca sandissanti[V 2.0096], niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ – ‘addhā[P 2.0126], idaṃ tassa bhagavato vacanaṃ; tassa ca therassa suggahita’nti. Idaṃ, bhikkhave, catutthaṃ mahāpadesaṃ dhāreyyātha. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro mahāpadese dhāreyyāthā”ti.

“Furthermore, here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu might say: ‘In such-and-such a residence, a single elder bhikkhu dwells who is very learned, versed in the traditions, an upholder of the Dhamma, an upholder of the Vinaya, and an upholder of the Mātikā. I have heard and received this in the presence of that elder: “This is the Dhamma, this is the Vinaya, this is the Teacher’s Dispensation.”’ Bhikkhus, that bhikkhu’s statement should neither be approved nor rejected. Without approving or rejecting it, having learned those words and phrases well, they should be checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya. If, when being checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya, they neither conform with the Suttas nor are found in the Vinaya, the conclusion should be reached: ‘Surely, this is not the word of the Blessed One, and it has been wrongly grasped by that elder.’ Thus, bhikkhus, you should discard it. But if, when being checked against the Suttas and compared with the Vinaya, they both conform with the Suttas and are found in the Vinaya, the conclusion should be reached: ‘Surely, this is the word of the Blessed One, and it has been well grasped by that elder.’ Bhikkhus, you should bear in mind this fourth great authority. Bhikkhus, you should bear in mind these four great authorities.”

Tatrapi sudaṃ bhagavā bhoganagare viharanto [T 2.0147] ānande cetiye etadeva bahulaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiṃ kathaṃ karoti – “iti sīlaṃ, iti samādhi, iti paññā. Sīlaparibhāvito samādhi mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso[M 2.0105]. Samādhiparibhāvitā paññā mahapphalā hoti mahānisaṃsā. Paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sammadeva āsavehi vimuccati, seyyathidaṃ – kāmāsavā, bhavāsavā, avijjāsavā”ti.

There, too, while the Blessed One was dwelling at Bhoganagara, at the Ānanda Cetiya, he often gave this Dhamma talk to the bhikkhus: “Such is virtue, such is concentration, such is wisdom. Concentration, when developed through virtue, is of great fruit and great benefit. Wisdom, when developed through concentration, is of great fruit and great benefit. The mind, when developed through wisdom, is rightly liberated from the taints, that is to say, from the taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance.”

Kammāraputtacundavatthu

The Story of Cunda the Goldsmith’s Son

189. Atha kho bhagavā bhoganagare yathābhirantaṃ viharitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “āyāmānanda, yena pāvā tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena pāvā tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā pāvāyaṃ viharati cundassa kammāraputtassa ambavane. Assosi kho cundo kammāraputto – “bhagavā kira pāvaṃ anuppatto, pāvāyaṃ viharati mayhaṃ ambavane”ti. Atha kho cundo kammāraputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho cundaṃ kammāraputtaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “adhivāsetu me, bhante, bhagavā svātanāya bhattaṃ saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghenā”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ [P 2.0127] viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā [T 2.0148] bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

189. Then, having stayed at Bhoganagara as long as he wished, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to Pāvā.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, arrived at Pāvā. There, at Pāvā, the Blessed One dwelt in the mango grove of Cunda the goldsmith’s son. Cunda the goldsmith’s son heard: ‘The Blessed One, it seems, has arrived at Pāvā and is dwelling at Pāvā in my mango grove.’ Then Cunda the goldsmith’s son approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One instructed, established, roused, and gladdened Cunda the goldsmith’s son, who was sitting to one side, with a Dhamma talk. Then Cunda the goldsmith’s son, having been instructed, established, roused, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a Dhamma talk, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to accept tomorrow’s meal from me, together with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.” The Blessed One consented by silence. Then Cunda the goldsmith’s son, knowing of the Blessed One’s consent, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed.

Atha kho cundo kammāraputto tassā rattiyā accayena sake nivesane paṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyādāpetvā pahūtañca sūkaramaddavaṃ bhagavato kālaṃ ārocāpesi – “kālo, bhante, niṭṭhitaṃ bhatta”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena yena cundassa kammāraputtassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā cundaṃ kammāraputtaṃ āmantesi – “yaṃ te, cunda, sūkaramaddavaṃ paṭiyattaṃ, tena maṃ parivisa. Yaṃ panaññaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyattaṃ, tena bhikkhusaṅghaṃ [V 2.0097] parivisā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavato paṭissutvā yaṃ ahosi sūkaramaddavaṃ paṭiyattaṃ, tena bhagavantaṃ parivisi. Yaṃ panaññaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ paṭiyattaṃ[M 2.0106], tena bhikkhusaṅghaṃ parivisi. Atha kho bhagavā cundaṃ kammāraputtaṃ āmantesi – “yaṃ te, cunda, sūkaramaddavaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ, taṃ sobbhe nikhaṇāhi. Nāhaṃ taṃ, cunda, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, yassa taṃ paribhuttaṃ sammā pariṇāmaṃ gaccheyya aññatra tathāgatassā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavato paṭissutvā yaṃ ahosi sūkaramaddavaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ, taṃ sobbhe nikhaṇitvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ [T 2.0149] kho cundaṃ kammāraputtaṃ bhagavā dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Then, when that night had passed, Cunda the goldsmith’s son had excellent hard and soft foods prepared in his own home, together with an abundance of sūkaramaddava. He had the time announced to the Blessed One: “It is time, venerable sir, the meal is ready.” Then, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his bowl and outer robe, the Blessed One went with the Saṅgha of bhikkhus to the home of Cunda the goldsmith’s son. Having arrived, he sat down on the seat prepared for him. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed Cunda the goldsmith’s son: “Cunda, serve me with the sūkaramaddava you have prepared. Serve the Saṅgha of bhikkhus with the other hard and soft foods you have prepared.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Cunda the goldsmith’s son to the Blessed One, and he served the Blessed One with the sūkaramaddava that had been prepared, and the Saṅgha of bhikkhus with the other hard and soft foods that had been prepared. Then the Blessed One addressed Cunda the goldsmith’s son: “Cunda, bury whatever remains of the sūkaramaddava in a pit. For I do not see anyone in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, who could properly digest it after eating it, except for the Tathāgata.” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied Cunda the goldsmith’s son to the Blessed One, and he buried the remaining sūkaramaddava in a pit. Then he approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. While Cunda the goldsmith’s son was sitting to one side, the Blessed One instructed, established, roused, and gladdened him with a Dhamma talk. Then, rising from his seat, he departed.

190. Atha kho bhagavato cundassa kammāraputtassa bhattaṃ bhuttāvissa kharo ābādho uppajji, lohitapakkhandikā pabāḷhā vedanā vattanti māraṇantikā. Tā sudaṃ [P 2.0128] bhagavā sato sampajāno adhivāsesi avihaññamāno. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “āyāmānanda, yena kusinārā tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.

190. Then, after the Blessed One had eaten the meal of Cunda the goldsmith’s son, a severe illness arose for him: a bloody dysentery. Severe, deadly feelings occurred. The Blessed One endured them, being mindful and fully aware, without being afflicted. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to Kusinārā.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Cundassa bhattaṃ bhuñjitvā, kammārassāti me sutaṃ;

Ābādhaṃ samphusī dhīro, pabāḷhaṃ māraṇantikaṃ.

Having eaten the meal of Cunda the goldsmith, so I have heard, the wise one was afflicted by a severe, deadly illness.

Bhuttassa ca sūkaramaddavena,

Byādhippabāḷho udapādi satthuno;

Virecamāno viriccamāno (sī. syā. ka.), viriñcamāno (?) bhagavā avoca,

Gacchāmahaṃ kusināraṃ nagaranti.

After eating the sūkaramaddava, a severe illness arose in the Teacher. While purging, the Blessed One said: ‘I shall go to the city of Kusinārā.’

Pānīyāharaṇaṃ

The Fetching of Water

191. Atha kho bhagavā maggā okkamma yena aññataraṃ rukkhamūlaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “iṅgha me tvaṃ, ānanda, catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapehi, kilantosmi, ānanda, nisīdissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando [V 2.0098] bhagavato paṭissutvā catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapesi. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ [T 2.0150][M 2.0107] ānandaṃ āmantesi – “iṅgha me tvaṃ, ānanda, pānīyaṃ āhara, pipāsitosmi, ānanda, pivissāmī”ti. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idāni, bhante, pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni atikkantāni, taṃ cakkacchinnaṃ udakaṃ parittaṃ luḷitaṃ āvilaṃ sandati. Ayaṃ, bhante, kakudhā kakuthā (sī. pī.) nadī avidūre acchodakā sātodakā [P 2.0129] sītodakā setodakā setakā (sī.) suppatitthā ramaṇīyā. Ettha bhagavā pānīyañca pivissati, gattāni ca sītī sītaṃ (sī. pī. ka.) karissatī”ti.

191. Then the Blessed One, turning aside from the road, went to the foot of a certain tree. Having gone there, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Please, Ānanda, spread out for me the outer robe, folded in four. I am tired, Ānanda, I shall sit down.” “Very well, Venerable Sir,” the Venerable Ānanda assented to the Blessed One and spread out the outer robe, folded in four. The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Please, Ānanda, bring me some water. I am thirsty, Ānanda, I shall drink.” When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, just now five hundred carts have passed by. That little water, churned up by the wheels, flows stirred up and turbid. Venerable Sir, not far from here is the Kakudhā River with clear water, pleasant water, cool water, pure water, with good fords, and delightful. There the Blessed One may drink water and cool his limbs.”

Dutiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “iṅgha me tvaṃ, ānanda, pānīyaṃ āhara, pipāsitosmi, ānanda, pivissāmī”ti. Dutiyampi kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idāni, bhante, pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni atikkantāni, taṃ cakkacchinnaṃ udakaṃ parittaṃ luḷitaṃ āvilaṃ sandati. Ayaṃ, bhante, kakudhā nadī avidūre acchodakā sātodakā sītodakā setodakā suppatitthā ramaṇīyā. Ettha bhagavā pānīyañca pivissati, gattāni ca sītīkarissatī”ti.

For a second time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Please, Ānanda, bring me some water. I am thirsty, Ānanda, I shall drink.” For a second time, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, just now five hundred carts have passed by. That little water, churned up by the wheels, flows stirred up and turbid. Venerable Sir, not far from here is the Kakudhā River with clear water, pleasant water, cool water, pure water, with good fords, and delightful. There the Blessed One may drink water and cool his limbs.”

Tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “iṅgha me tvaṃ, ānanda, pānīyaṃ āhara, pipāsitosmi, ānanda, pivissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā [T 2.0151] pattaṃ gahetvā yena sā nadikā tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho sā nadikā cakkacchinnā parittā luḷitā āvilā sandamānā, āyasmante ānande upasaṅkamante acchā vippasannā anāvilā sandittha sandati (syā.). Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – “acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho, tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā. Ayañhi sā nadikā cakkacchinnā parittā luḷitā āvilā sandamānā mayi upasaṅkamante acchā vippasannā anāvilā sandatī”ti. Pattena pānīyaṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, tathāgatassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā. Idāni sā bhante nadikā cakkacchinnā parittā luḷitā āvilā sandamānā mayi upasaṅkamante acchā vippasannā anāvilā sandittha. Pivatu bhagavā pānīyaṃ pivatu sugato pānīya”nti. Atha kho bhagavā pānīyaṃ apāyi.

For a third time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Please, Ānanda, bring me some water. I am thirsty, Ānanda, I shall drink.” “Very well, Venerable Sir,” the Venerable Ānanda assented to the Blessed One, and taking the bowl, he went to that small river. Now that small river, which was churned up by wheels, with little water, flowing stirred up and turbid, as the Venerable Ānanda approached, flowed clear, very clear, and untroubled. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Ānanda: “Truly, it is wonderful! Truly, it is marvelous, the great power and great might of the Tathāgata! For this very river, which was churned up by wheels, with little water, flowing stirred up and turbid, as I approached, flows clear, very clear, and untroubled.” Taking water with the bowl, he went to the Blessed One. Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: “It is wonderful, Venerable Sir! It is marvelous, Venerable Sir, the great power and great might of the Tathāgata! Just now, Venerable Sir, that river which was churned up by wheels, with little water, flowing stirred up and turbid, as I approached, flowed clear, very clear, and untroubled. May the Blessed One drink the water! May the Sugata drink the water!” Then the Blessed One drank the water.

Pukkusamallaputtavatthu

The Story of Pukkusa the Mallan

192. Tena [M 2.0108][V 2.0099][P 2.0130] rokho pana samayena pukkuso mallaputto āḷārassa kālāmassa sāvako kusinārāya pāvaṃ addhānamaggappaṭippanno hoti. Addasā kho pukkuso mallaputto bhagavantaṃ aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisinnaṃ. Disvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho pukkuso mallaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, santena vata, bhante, pabbajitā vihārena viharanti. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhante[T 2.0152], āḷāro kālāmo addhānamaggappaṭippanno maggā okkamma avidūre aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle divāvihāraṃ nisīdi. Atha kho, bhante, pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni āḷāraṃ kālāmaṃ nissāya nissāya atikkamiṃsu. Atha kho, bhante, aññataro puriso tassa sakaṭasatthassa sakaṭasatassa (ka.) piṭṭhito piṭṭhito āgacchanto yena āḷāro kālāmo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āḷāraṃ kālāmaṃ etadavoca – ‘api, bhante, pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni atikkantāni addasā’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, addasa’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, saddaṃ assosī’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, saddaṃ assosi’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, sutto ahosī’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sutto ahosi’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, saññī ahosī’ti? ‘Evamāvuso’ti. ‘So tvaṃ, bhante, saññī samāno jāgaro pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni nissāya nissāya atikkantāni neva addasa, na pana saddaṃ assosi; apisu api hi (sī. syā. pī.) te, bhante, saṅghāṭi rajena okiṇṇā’ti? ‘Evamāvuso’ti. Atha kho, bhante, tassa purisassa etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, santena vata bho pabbajitā vihārena viharanti. Yatra hi nāma saññī samāno [P 2.0131] jāgaro pañcamattāni sakaṭasatāni nissāya nissāya atikkantāni neva dakkhati, na pana saddaṃ sossatī’ti! Āḷāre kālāme uḷāraṃ pasādaṃ pavedetvā pakkāmī”ti.

192. At that time, Pukkusa the Mallan, a disciple of Āḷāra Kālāma, was traveling along the road from Kusinārā to Pāvā. Pukkusa the Mallan saw the Blessed One seated at the foot of a tree. Having seen him, he approached the Blessed One, paid homage, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Pukkusa the Mallan said to the Blessed One: 'It is wonderful, venerable sir! It is astonishing, venerable sir! How peacefully, indeed, do the renunciants dwell! Once, venerable sir, Āḷāra Kālāma was traveling along a road. He stepped off the road and sat down at the foot of a certain tree for his day's abiding. Then, venerable sir, five hundred carts passed by very close to Āḷāra Kālāma. Then, venerable sir, a certain man who was following behind that train of carts approached Āḷāra Kālāma and said: ‘Venerable sir, did you see the five hundred carts that passed by?’ ‘No, friend, I did not see them.’ ‘But, venerable sir, did you hear the sound?’ ‘No, friend, I did not hear the sound.’ ‘Then, venerable sir, were you asleep?’ ‘No, friend, I was not asleep.’ ‘Then, venerable sir, were you conscious?’ ‘Yes, friend.’ ‘So, venerable sir, while being conscious and awake, you neither saw the five hundred carts that passed by very closely, nor did you hear the sound? And is your outer robe, venerable sir, also covered with dust?’ ‘Yes, friend.’ Then, venerable sir, it occurred to that man: ‘It is truly wonderful! It is truly astonishing! How peacefully, indeed, do the renunciants dwell! For though being conscious and awake, one will neither see the five hundred carts that pass by very closely, nor will one hear the sound!’ Having declared his profound confidence in Āḷāra Kālāma, he departed.'

193. “Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, pukkusa, katamaṃ nu kho dukkarataraṃ vā durabhisambhavataraṃ vā – yo vā saññī samāno jāgaro pañcamattāni [T 2.0153] sakaṭasatāni nissāya nissāya atikkantāni neva passeyya, na pana saddaṃ [M 2.0109] suṇeyya; yo vā saññī samāno jāgaro deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatāsu vijjutāsu (sī. syā. pī.) niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā neva passeyya, na pana saddaṃ suṇeyyā”ti? “Kiñhi, bhante, karissanti pañca vā sakaṭasatāni cha vā sakaṭasatāni satta vā sakaṭasatāni aṭṭha vā sakaṭasatāni nava vā sakaṭasatāni nava vā sakaṭasatāni dasa vā sakaṭasatāni (sī.), sakaṭasahassaṃ vā sakaṭasatasahassaṃ vā. Atha kho etadeva dukkarataraṃ ceva durabhisambhavatarañca yo [V 2.0100] saññī samāno jāgaro deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatāsu niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā neva passeyya, na pana saddaṃ suṇeyyā”ti.

193. “What do you think, Pukkusa? Which is more difficult to do, more difficult to accomplish: for one who is conscious and awake neither to see five hundred carts passing very close by, nor to hear the sound; or for one who is conscious and awake, while it is raining, thunder is rumbling, lightning is flashing, and a thunderbolt is striking, neither to see it, nor to hear the sound?” “Venerable sir, what do five hundred carts matter, or six hundred, or seven hundred, or eight hundred, or nine hundred, or a thousand, or even a hundred thousand carts? Indeed, it is far more difficult to do, far more difficult to accomplish, for one who is conscious and awake, while it is raining, thunder is rumbling, lightning is flashing, and a thunderbolt is striking, neither to see it, nor to hear the sound.”

“Ekamidāhaṃ, pukkusa, samayaṃ ātumāyaṃ viharāmi bhusāgāre. Tena kho pana samayena deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatāsu niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā avidūre bhusāgārassa dve kassakā bhātaro hatā cattāro ca balibaddā balibaddā (sī. pī.). Atha kho, pukkusa, ātumāya mahājanakāyo nikkhamitvā yena te dve kassakā bhātaro hatā cattāro ca balibaddā tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho panāhaṃ, pukkusa, samayena bhusāgārā nikkhamitvā bhusāgāradvāre abbhokāse caṅkamāmi. Atha kho, pukkusa, aññataro puriso tamhā mahājanakāyā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ [T 2.0154] ṭhitaṃ kho ahaṃ, pukkusa, taṃ purisaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘kiṃ nu kho eso, āvuso, mahājanakāyo sannipatito’ti? ‘Idāni[P 2.0132], bhante, deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatāsu niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā dve kassakā bhātaro hatā cattāro ca balibaddā. Ettheso mahājanakāyo sannipatito. Tvaṃ pana, bhante, kva ahosī’ti? ‘Idheva kho ahaṃ, āvuso, ahosi’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, addasā’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, addasa’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, saddaṃ assosī’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, saddaṃ assosi’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, sutto ahosī’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, āvuso, sutto ahosi’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, saññī ahosī’ti? ‘Evamāvuso’ti. ‘So tvaṃ, bhante, saññī samāno jāgaro deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante [M 2.0110] vijjullatāsu niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā neva addasa, na pana saddaṃ assosī’ti? “Evamāvuso”ti?

“Once, Pukkusa, I was staying in Ātumā in a threshing shed. At that time, while it was raining, thunder was rumbling, lightning was flashing, and a thunderbolt was striking, not far from the threshing shed, two farmer brothers and four draft oxen were killed. Then, Pukkusa, a great crowd of people came out from Ātumā and went to the place where the two farmer brothers and four draft oxen had been killed. At that time, Pukkusa, I had come out of the threshing shed and was practicing walking meditation in the open at the door of the shed. Then, Pukkusa, a certain man from that great crowd approached me. Having approached, he paid homage to me and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Pukkusa, I said to that man: ‘Why, friend, has this great crowd of people gathered?’ ‘Just now, venerable sir, while it was raining, thunder was rumbling, lightning was flashing, and a thunderbolt was striking, two farmer brothers and four draft oxen were killed. That is why this great crowd has gathered here. But where were you, venerable sir?’ ‘I was right here, friend.’ ‘But, venerable sir, did you see it?’ ‘No, friend, I did not see it.’ ‘But, venerable sir, did you hear the sound?’ ‘No, friend, I did not hear the sound.’ ‘But, venerable sir, were you asleep?’ ‘No, friend, I was not asleep.’ ‘But, venerable sir, were you conscious?’ ‘Yes, friend.’ ‘So, venerable sir, while being conscious and awake, as it was raining, thunder was rumbling, lightning was flashing, and a thunderbolt was striking, you neither saw it, nor heard the sound?’ ‘Yes, friend.’”

“Atha kho, pukkusa, purisassa etadahosi – ‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, santena vata bho pabbajitā vihārena viharanti. Yatra hi nāma saññī samāno jāgaro deve vassante deve gaḷagaḷāyante vijjullatāsu niccharantīsu asaniyā phalantiyā neva dakkhati, na pana saddaṃ sossatī’ti suṇissati (syā.). Mayi uḷāraṃ pasādaṃ pavedetvā maṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmī”ti.

“Then, Pukkusa, this thought occurred to that man: ‘It is wonderful, sirs! It is amazing, sirs! How peacefully indeed do the renunciants dwell! For this renunciant, while conscious and awake, when it was raining, when thunder was rumbling, when lightning was flashing, and when a thunderbolt was striking, neither saw it, nor heard the sound.’ Having expressed his profound confidence in me, he paid homage to me, circumambulated me respectfully, and departed.”

Evaṃ vutte pukkuso mallaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “esāhaṃ, bhante, yo me āḷāre kālāme pasādo taṃ mahāvāte vā ophuṇāmi sīghasotāya [T 2.0155] siṅghasotāya (ka.) vā nadiyā pavāhemi. Abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ [V 2.0101] vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca [P 2.0133] bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti.

When this was said, Pukkusa the Mallan said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, whatever confidence I had in Āḷāra Kālāma, I now scatter it in a great wind or let it be washed away in a swift-flowing river. It is magnificent, venerable sir! It is magnificent! It is as if, venerable sir, one were to set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms. In the very same way, the Dhamma has been made clear by the Blessed One in many ways. I go to the Blessed One for refuge, venerable sir, and to the Dhamma and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts."

194. Atha kho pukkuso mallaputto aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – “iṅgha me tvaṃ, bhaṇe, siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ āharā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho so puriso pukkusassa mallaputtassa paṭissutvā taṃ siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ āhari āharasi (ka.). Atha kho pukkuso mallaputto taṃ siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ bhagavato upanāmesi – “idaṃ, bhante, siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ, taṃ me bhagavā paṭiggaṇhātu anukampaṃ upādāyā”ti. “Tena hi, pukkusa, ekena maṃ acchādehi, ekena ānanda”nti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho pukkuso mallaputto bhagavato paṭissutvā ekena bhagavantaṃ acchādeti, ekena āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā pukkusaṃ mallaputtaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho pukkuso mallaputto bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

194. Then Pukkusa the Mallan addressed a certain man: "Come, my good man, bring me the pair of smooth, wearable robes the color of refined gold." "Yes, venerable sir," that man replied to Pukkusa the Mallan, and he brought the pair of smooth, wearable robes the color of refined gold. Then Pukkusa the Mallan presented that pair of smooth, wearable robes the color of refined gold to the Blessed One, saying: "Venerable sir, this is a pair of smooth, wearable robes the color of refined gold. May the Blessed One accept it from me, out of compassion." "In that case, Pukkusa, clothe me with one, and Ānanda with the other." "Yes, venerable sir," replied Pukkusa the Mallan to the Blessed One, and he clothed the Blessed One with one robe and the Venerable Ānanda with the other. Then the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened Pukkusa the Mallan with a talk on the Dhamma. Then Pukkusa the Mallan, having been instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One's talk on the Dhamma, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and departed.

195. Atha [T 2.0156][M 2.0111] kho āyasmā ānando acirapakkante pukkuse mallaputte taṃ siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ bhagavato kāyaṃ upanāmesi. Taṃ bhagavato kāyaṃ upanāmitaṃ hataccikaṃ viya vītaccikaṃviya (sī. pī.) khāyati. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, yāva parisuddho, bhante, tathāgatassa chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto. Idaṃ, bhante, siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ yugamaṭṭhaṃ dhāraṇīyaṃ bhagavato [P 2.0134] kāyaṃ upanāmitaṃ hataccikaṃ viya khāyatī”ti. “Evametaṃ, ānanda, evametaṃ, ānanda dvīsu kālesu ativiya tathāgatassa kāyo parisuddho hoti chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto. Katamesu dvīsu? Yañca, ānanda, rattiṃ tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati, yañca rattiṃ anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati. Imesu kho, ānanda, dvīsu kālesu ativiya tathāgatassa kāyo parisuddho hoti chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto. “Ajja kho, panānanda, rattiyā pacchime yāme kusinārāyaṃ upavattane mallānaṃ sālavane antarena antare (syā.) yamakasālānaṃ tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati bhavissatīti (ka.). Āyāmānanda, yena kakudhā nadī tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.

195. Then, not long after Pukkusa the Mallan had departed, the Venerable Ānanda placed the pair of smooth, wearable robes the color of refined gold onto the Blessed One’s body. When placed on the Blessed One’s body, it seemed to have lost its radiance. Then the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: "It is wonderful, venerable sir, it is amazing! The complexion of the Tathāgata is so very pure and bright. Venerable sir, when this pair of smooth, wearable robes the color of refined gold was placed on the Blessed One’s body, it seemed to have lost its radiance." "It is so, Ānanda, it is so. On two occasions the Tathāgata’s body becomes exceedingly pure and his complexion exceedingly bright. What are the two? The night, Ānanda, when the Tathāgata awakens to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, and the night he passes into the Nibbāna-element with no residue remaining. On these two occasions, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s body becomes exceedingly pure and his complexion exceedingly bright. Today, Ānanda, in the last watch of the night, in the Sāla grove of the Mallas at Upavattana in Kusinārā, between the twin Sāla trees, the Tathāgata’s final passing away will take place. Come, Ānanda, let us go to the Kakudhā river." "Yes, venerable sir," the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One.

Siṅgīvaṇṇaṃ [V 2.0102] yugamaṭṭhaṃ, pukkuso abhihārayi;

Tena acchādito satthā, hemavaṇṇo asobhathāti.

The pair of smooth robes, the color of refined gold, Pukkusa brought forth; clothed in them, the Teacher shone, like the color of gold.

196. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena kakudhā nadī tenupasaṅkami[T 2.0157]; upasaṅkamitvā kakudhaṃ nadiṃ ajjhogāhetvā nhatvā ca pivitvā ca paccuttaritvā yena ambavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ cundakaṃ āmantesi – “iṅgha me tvaṃ, cundaka, catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapehi, kilantosmi, cundaka, nipajjissāmī”ti.

196. Then the Blessed One, together with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, went to the Kakudhā river. Having gone there, he entered the Kakudhā river, bathed and drank, and then came out on the other side and went to the mango grove. Having arrived, he addressed the Venerable Cundaka: "Come, Cundaka, prepare my outer robe folded in four. I am tired, Cundaka, and will lie down."

“Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā cundako bhagavato paṭissutvā catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapesi. Atha kho bhagavā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi pāde pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṃ [P 2.0135] manasikaritvā. Āyasmā pana cundako tattheva bhagavato purato nisīdi.

"Yes, venerable sir," the Venerable Cundaka replied to the Blessed One, and he prepared the outer robe folded in four. Then the Blessed One adopted the lion's posture, lying on his right side, with one foot placed on the other, mindful and fully aware, having established in his mind the perception of rising. And the Venerable Cundaka sat down right in front of the Blessed One.

Gantvāna [M 2.0112] buddho nadikaṃ kakudhaṃ,

Acchodakaṃ sātudakaṃ vippasannaṃ;

Ogāhi satthā akilantarūpo sukilantarūpo (sī. pī.),

Tathāgato appaṭimo ca appaṭimodha (pī.) loke.

Having gone to the little Kakudhā river, with its clear, pleasant, and very limpid water, the Teacher, unwearied in form, entered it; the Tathāgata, without equal in the world.

Nhatvā ca pivitvā cudatāri satthā pivitvā cundakena, pivitvā ca uttari (ka.),

Purakkhato bhikkhugaṇassa majjhe;

Vattā satthā (sī. syā. pī.) pavattā bhagavā idha dhamme,

Upāgami ambavanaṃ mahesi.

Having bathed and drunk, the Teacher emerged, revered in the midst of the assembly of bhikkhus. The Blessed One, the great sage, speaker and expounder of the Dhamma here, approached the mango grove.

Āmantayi cundakaṃ nāma bhikkhuṃ,

Catugguṇaṃ [T 2.0158] santhara me nipajjaṃ;

So codito bhāvitattena cundo,

Catugguṇaṃ santhari khippameva.

He addressed the bhikkhu named Cunda: "Spread my robe, folded in four, for me to lie down." Urged by him whose being is developed, Cunda quickly spread the robe folded in four.

Nipajji satthā akilantarūpo,

Cundopi tattha pamukhe samukhe (ka.) nisīdīti.

The Teacher, unwearied in form, lay down, and Cunda too sat there before him.

197. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “siyā kho yo kho (ka.), panānanda, cundassa [V 2.0103] kammāraputtassa koci vippaṭisāraṃ uppādeyya – ‘tassa te, āvuso cunda, alābhā tassa te dulladdhaṃ, yassa te tathāgato pacchimaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā parinibbuto’ti. Cundassa, ānanda, kammāraputtassa evaṃ vippaṭisāro paṭivinetabbo – ‘tassa te, āvuso cunda, lābhā tassa te suladdhaṃ, yassa te tathāgato pacchimaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā parinibbuto. Sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso cunda, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – dve me piṇḍapātā samasamaphalā [P 2.0136] samā samaphalā (ka.) samavipākā samasamavipākā (sī. syā. pī.), ativiya aññehi piṇḍapātehi mahapphalatarā ca mahānisaṃsatarā ca. Katame dve? Yañca piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati, yañca piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñjitvā tathāgato anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati. Ime dve piṇḍapātā samasamaphalā samavipākā[M 2.0113], ativiya aññehi piṇḍapātehi mahapphalatarā ca mahānisaṃsatarā ca. Āyusaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, vaṇṇasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, sukhasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, yasasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, saggasaṃvattanikaṃ [T 2.0159] āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacitaṃ, ādhipateyyasaṃvattanikaṃ āyasmatā cundena kammāraputtena kammaṃ upacita’nti. Cundassa, ānanda, kammāraputtassa evaṃ vippaṭisāro paṭivinetabbo”ti. Atha kho bhagavā etamatthaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi –

197. Then the Blessed One addressed Venerable Ānanda: 'Ānanda, it is possible that someone might arouse remorse in Cunda the smith's son, saying: “It is your loss, friend Cunda, it is your misfortune that the Tathāgata, having partaken of his last alms-meal from you, attained Parinibbāna.” Ānanda, the remorse of Cunda the smith's son should be dispelled thus: “It is your gain, friend Cunda, it is your good fortune that the Tathāgata, having partaken of his last alms-meal from you, attained Parinibbāna. Friend Cunda, I have heard this in the presence of the Blessed One, I have received it in his presence: ‘These two alms-meals have equal fruit and equal result, and are of much greater fruit and much greater benefit than other alms-meals. Which two? The alms-meal after partaking of which the Tathāgata awakens to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment, and the alms-meal after partaking of which the Tathāgata attains Parinibbāna with the Nibbāna-element without remainder. These two alms-meals have equal fruit and equal result, and are of much greater fruit and much greater benefit than other alms-meals. Venerable Cunda the smith's son has accumulated kamma that leads to long life, has accumulated kamma that leads to beauty, has accumulated kamma that leads to happiness, has accumulated kamma that leads to a large following, has accumulated kamma that leads to heaven, has accumulated kamma that leads to sovereignty.’ Ānanda, the remorse of Cunda the smith's son should be dispelled in this way.”' Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

“Dadato puññaṃ pavaḍḍhati,

Saṃyamato veraṃ na cīyati;

Kusalo ca jahāti pāpakaṃ,

Rāgadosamohakkhayā sanibbuto”ti.

For one who gives, merit increases; for one who is restrained, enmity is not amassed. The wise one abandons evil; through the destruction of lust, hatred, and delusion, one is extinguished.

Catuttho bhāṇavāro.

The Fourth Recitation Section.

Yamakasālā

The Twin Sāla Trees

198. Atha [P 2.0137] kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “āyāmānanda, yena hiraññavatiyā nadiyā pārimaṃ tīraṃ, yena kusinārā upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ tenupasaṅkamissāmā”ti[V 2.0104]. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena hiraññavatiyā nadiyā pārimaṃ tīraṃ, yena kusinārā upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “iṅgha me tvaṃ, ānanda, antarena yamakasālānaṃ uttarasīsakaṃ mañcakaṃ paññapehi, kilantosmi, ānanda, nipajjissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā antarena yamakasālānaṃ uttarasīsakaṃ mañcakaṃ paññapesi. Atha kho bhagavā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi pāde [T 2.0160] pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno.

198. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Come, Ānanda, let us go to the farther bank of the Hiraññavatī River, to the Upavattana sāla grove of the Mallas at Kusinārā.” “Yes, Venerable Sir,” replied the Venerable Ānanda to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, together with a great community of monks, went to the farther bank of the Hiraññavatī River, to the Upavattana sāla grove of the Mallas at Kusinārā. Upon arriving, he addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Please, Ānanda, prepare a couch for me between the twin sāla trees with its head to the north. I am tired, Ānanda, I will lie down.” “Yes, Venerable Sir,” replied the Venerable Ānanda to the Blessed One and prepared a couch between the twin sāla trees with its head to the north. Then the Blessed One lay down on his right side in the lion’s posture, with one foot placed slightly over the other, mindful and fully aware.

Tena [M 2.0114] kho pana samayena yamakasālā sabbaphāliphullā honti akālapupphehi. Te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi mandāravapupphāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi candanacuṇṇāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti [P 2.0138] ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi tūriyāni antalikkhe vajjanti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi saṅgītāni antalikkhe vattanti tathāgatassa pūjāya.

At that time, the twin sāla trees were in full bloom with unseasonal flowers. In homage to the Tathāgata, they scattered, sprinkled, and strewed them over the Tathāgata's body. Divine mandārava flowers fell from the sky, and in homage to the Tathāgata, they scattered, sprinkled, and strewed them over the Tathāgata's body. Divine sandalwood powder fell from the sky, and in homage to the Tathāgata, it scattered, sprinkled, and strewed over the Tathāgata's body. Divine musical instruments played in the sky in homage to the Tathāgata. Divine songs arose in the sky in homage to the Tathāgata.

199. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “sabbaphāliphullā kho, ānanda, yamakasālā akālapupphehi. Te tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi mandāravapupphāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi candanacuṇṇāni antalikkhā papatanti, tāni tathāgatassa sarīraṃ okiranti ajjhokiranti abhippakiranti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi tūriyāni antalikkhe vajjanti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Dibbānipi saṅgītāni antalikkhe vattanti tathāgatassa pūjāya. Na kho, ānanda, ettāvatā tathāgato sakkato vā hoti garukato vā mānito vā pūjito vā apacito vā. Yo kho, ānanda, bhikkhu [T 2.0161] vā bhikkhunī vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharati sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, so tathāgataṃ sakkaroti garuṃ karoti māneti pūjeti apaciyati idaṃ padaṃ sīsyāipotthakesu na dissati, paramāya pūjāya. Tasmātihānanda, dhammānudhammappaṭipannā viharissāma sāmīcippaṭipannā anudhammacārinoti. Evañhi vo, ānanda, sikkhitabba”nti.

199. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Ānanda, the twin sāla trees are in full bloom with unseasonal flowers. In homage to the Tathāgata, they scatter, sprinkle, and strew them over the Tathāgata's body. Divine mandārava flowers fall from the sky, and in homage to the Tathāgata, they scatter, sprinkle, and strew them over the Tathāgata's body. Divine sandalwood powder falls from the sky, and in homage to the Tathāgata, it scatters, sprinkles, and strews over the Tathāgata's body. Divine musical instruments play in the sky in homage to the Tathāgata. Divine songs arise in the sky in homage to the Tathāgata. Yet, Ānanda, not by this much is the Tathāgata respected, revered, honored, worshipped, or venerated. But whoever—be it a monk, a nun, a layman, or a laywoman—dwells practicing the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing what is proper, and living in conformity with the Dhamma, that one respects, reveres, honors, worships, and venerates the Tathāgata with the highest form of worship. Therefore, Ānanda, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will dwell practicing the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing what is proper, and living in conformity with the Dhamma.’”

Upavāṇatthero

The Elder Upavāṇa

200. Tena [V 2.0105] kho pana samayena āyasmā upavāṇo bhagavato purato ṭhito hoti bhagavantaṃ bījayamāno. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāresi – “apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī”ti. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho [M 2.0115] āyasmā [P 2.0139] upavāṇo dīgharattaṃ bhagavato upaṭṭhāko santikāvacaro samīpacārī. Atha ca pana bhagavā pacchime kāle āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – ‘apehi bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’ti. Ko nu kho hetu, ko paccayo, yaṃ bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – ‘apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī’ti? Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘ayaṃ, bhante, āyasmā upavāṇo dīgharattaṃ bhagavato upaṭṭhāko santikāvacaro samīpacārī. Atha ca pana bhagavā pacchime kāle āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – “apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī”ti. Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yaṃ bhagavā āyasmantaṃ upavāṇaṃ apasāreti – “apehi, bhikkhu, mā me purato aṭṭhāsī”ti? “Yebhuyyena, ānanda, dasasu lokadhātūsu devatā sannipatitā [T 2.0162] tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Yāvatā, ānanda, kusinārā upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ samantato dvādasa yojanāni, natthi so padeso vālaggakoṭinitudanamattopi mahesakkhāhi devatāhi apphuṭo. Devatā, ānanda, ujjhāyanti – ‘dūrā ca vatamha āgatā tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Kadāci karahaci tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā. Ajjeva rattiyā pacchime yāme tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Ayañca mahesakkho bhikkhu bhagavato purato ṭhito ovārento, na mayaṃ labhāma pacchime kāle tathāgataṃ dassanāyā’”ti.

200. At that time, the Venerable Upavāṇa was standing before the Blessed One, fanning him. Then the Blessed One dismissed the Venerable Upavāṇa, saying, “Step aside, monk, do not stand before me.” Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Ānanda: “This Venerable Upavāṇa has for a long time been the Blessed One’s attendant, one who is near and in his presence. And yet, at this final time, the Blessed One dismisses the Venerable Upavāṇa, saying, ‘Step aside, monk, do not stand before me.’ What, indeed, is the cause, what is the reason, that the Blessed One dismisses the Venerable Upavāṇa, saying, ‘Step aside, monk, do not stand before me’?” Then the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, this Venerable Upavāṇa has for a long time been the Blessed One’s attendant, one who is near and in his presence. And yet, at this final time, the Blessed One dismisses him, saying, ‘Step aside, monk, do not stand before me.’ What, Venerable Sir, is the cause, what is the reason, that the Blessed One dismisses the Venerable Upavāṇa, saying, ‘Step aside, monk, do not stand before me’?” “Ānanda, for the most part, deities from the ten thousand world-systems have assembled to see the Tathāgata. Ānanda, for a distance of twelve yojanas all around the Upavattana sāla grove of the Mallas at Kusinārā, there is not a spot even the size of a hair-tip’s point that is not filled with powerful deities. And the deities, Ānanda, are complaining: ‘Indeed, we have come from afar to see the Tathāgata. Only rarely, on some occasion, do Tathāgatas, Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, arise in the world. And today, in the last watch of the night, the final passing of the Tathāgata will take place. But this powerful monk stands before the Blessed One, obstructing the view, and we are unable to see the Tathāgata in this final time!’”

201. “Kathaṃbhūtā pana, bhante, bhagavā devatā manasikarotī”ti manasi karontīti (syā. ka.)? “Santānanda, devatā ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti chinnaṃpādaṃviya papatanti (syā.), āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ cakkhumā (syā. ka.) loke antaradhaṃāyissatī’ti.

201. “Venerable Sir, of what nature are the deities the Blessed One has in mind?” “Ānanda, there are deities in the sky who perceive the earth; with their hair disheveled they weep, with their arms upraised they weep, they fall down as if from a precipice, they roll back and forth and from side to side, lamenting: ‘Too soon the Blessed One will attain Parinibbāna! Too soon the Well-gone One will attain Parinibbāna! Too soon the Eye of the World will disappear!’”

“Santānanda, devatā pathaviyaṃ pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ [P 2.0140] papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antaradhāyissatī’”ti.

“Ānanda, there are deities on the earth who perceive the earth; with their hair disheveled they weep, with their arms upraised they weep, they fall down as if from a precipice, they roll back and forth and from side to side, lamenting: ‘Too soon the Blessed One will attain Parinibbāna! Too soon the Well-gone One will attain Parinibbāna! Too soon the Eye of the World will disappear!’”

“Yā [M 2.0116][V 2.0106] pana tā devatā vītarāgā, tā satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – ‘aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti.

“But those deities who are free from passion, being mindful and clearly comprehending, endure patiently, reflecting: ‘Conditioned things are impermanent. How, in this case, could it be otherwise?’”

Catusaṃvejanīyaṭṭhānāni

The Four Places Inspiring Spiritual Urgency

202. “Pubbe[T 2.0163], bhante, disāsu vassaṃ vuṭṭhā vassaṃvutthā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) bhikkhū āgacchanti tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Te mayaṃ labhāma manobhāvanīye bhikkhū dassanāya, labhāma payirupāsanāya. Bhagavato pana mayaṃ, bhante, accayena na labhissāma manobhāvanīye bhikkhū dassanāya, na labhissāma payirupāsanāyā”ti.

202. “Venerable Sir, formerly, monks who had completed the rains retreat in the various regions would come to see the Tathāgata. We would get to see those mentally inspiring monks, and we would get to attend upon them. But, Venerable Sir, on account of the Blessed One's passing away, we will no longer get to see those mentally inspiring monks, nor will we get to attend upon them.”

“Cattārimāni, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyāni saṃvejanīyāni ṭhānāni. Katamāni cattāri? ‘Idha tathāgato jāto’ti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. ‘Idha tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. ‘Idha tathāgatena anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattita’nti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. ‘Idha tathāgato anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbuto’ti, ānanda, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṃ saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānaṃ. Imāni kho[P 2.0141], ānanda, cattāri saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyāni saṃvejanīyāni ṭhānāni.

“Ānanda, there are these four places for a faithful clansman that are worthy of being seen and are inspiring of spiritual urgency. Which four? ‘Here the Tathāgata was born’—this, Ānanda, is a place for a faithful clansman that is worthy of being seen and is inspiring of spiritual urgency. ‘Here the Tathāgata awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment’—this, Ānanda, is a place for a faithful clansman that is worthy of being seen and is inspiring of spiritual urgency. ‘Here the Tathāgata set in motion the unsurpassed Wheel of the Dhamma’—this, Ānanda, is a place for a faithful clansman that is worthy of being seen and is inspiring of spiritual urgency. ‘Here the Tathāgata passed away into the Nibbāna-element with no residue remaining’—this, Ānanda, is a place for a faithful clansman that is worthy of being seen and is inspiring of spiritual urgency. These, indeed, Ānanda, are the four places for a faithful clansman that are worthy of being seen and are inspiring of spiritual urgency.

“Āgamissanti kho, ānanda, saddhā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo – ‘idha tathāgato jāto’tipi, ‘idha tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’tipi, ‘idha tathāgatena anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattita’ntipi, ‘idha tathāgato anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbuto’tipi. Ye hi keci, ānanda, cetiyacārikaṃ āhiṇḍantā pasannacittā kālaṅkarissanti, sabbe te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjissantī”ti.

“Ānanda, faithful monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen will come, thinking: ‘Here the Tathāgata was born,’ and ‘Here the Tathāgata awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment,’ and ‘Here the Tathāgata set in motion the unsurpassed Wheel of the Dhamma,’ and ‘Here the Tathāgata passed away into the Nibbāna-element with no residue remaining.’ And whoever, Ānanda, while wandering on pilgrimage to these shrines, passes away with a serene mind, all of them, on the breaking up of the body, after death, will be reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world.”

Ānandapucchākathā

The Discourse on the Questions of Ānanda

203. “Kathaṃ [T 2.0164] mayaṃ, bhante, mātugāme paṭipajjāmā”ti? “Adassanaṃ, ānandā”ti. “Dassane, bhagavā, sati kathaṃ paṭipajjitabba”nti? “Anālāpo, ānandā”ti[M 2.0117]. “Ālapantena pana, bhante, kathaṃ paṭipajjitabba”nti? “Sati, ānanda, upaṭṭhāpetabbā”ti.

203. “Venerable Sir, how are we to conduct ourselves with regard to womenfolk?” “By not seeing them, Ānanda.” “But if there is seeing, Blessed One, how should one conduct oneself?” “By not speaking, Ānanda.” “But when one is speaking, Venerable Sir, how should one conduct oneself?” “Mindfulness, Ānanda, should be established.”

204. “Kathaṃ [V 2.0107] mayaṃ, bhante, tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjāmā”ti? “Abyāvaṭā tumhe, ānanda, hotha tathāgatassa sarīrapūjāya. Iṅgha tumhe, ānanda, sāratthe ghaṭatha anuyuñjatha sadatthe anuyuñjatha (sī. syā.), sadatthaṃ anuyuñjatha (pī.), sāratthe anuyuñjatha (ka.), sāratthe appamattā ātāpino pahitattā viharatha. Santānanda, khattiyapaṇḍitāpi brāhmaṇapaṇḍitāpi gahapatipaṇḍitāpi tathāgate abhippasannā, te tathāgatassa sarīrapūjaṃ karissantī”ti.

204. “Venerable Sir, how are we to proceed regarding the Tathāgata's body?” “Do not be occupied, Ānanda, with the veneration of the Tathāgata's body. Come now, Ānanda, strive and exert yourselves for the essential goal; dwell heedful, ardent, and with minds sent forth. There are, Ānanda, wise nobles, wise brahmins, and wise householders who are deeply confident in the Tathāgata; they will perform the veneration of the Tathāgata's body.”

205. “Kathaṃ pana, bhante, tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabba”nti? “Yathā kho, ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabba”nti. “Kathaṃ pana, bhante, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjantī”ti? “Rañño, ānanda, cakkavattissa sarīraṃ ahatena vatthena veṭhenti, ahatena vatthena veṭhetvā vihatena kappāsena veṭhenti, vihatena kappāsena veṭhetvā ahatena vatthena [P 2.0142] veṭhenti. Etenupāyena pañcahi yugasatehi rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ sarīre (syā. ka.) veṭhetvā āyasāya teladoṇiyā pakkhipitvā aññissā āyasāya doṇiyā paṭikujjitvā sabbagandhānaṃ citakaṃ karitvā rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ jhāpenti. Cātumahāpathe cātummahāpathe (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) rañño cakkavattissa thūpaṃ karonti[T 2.0165]. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti. Yathā kho, ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Cātumahāpathe tathāgatassa thūpo kātabbo. Tattha ye mālaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā cuṇṇakaṃ vaṇṇakaṃ (sī. pī.) vā āropessanti vā abhivādessanti vā cittaṃ vā pasādessanti tesaṃ taṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya.
