205. “But how, Venerable Sir, should one proceed regarding the Tathāgata's body?” “As, Ānanda, they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch, so should one proceed with the body of the Tathāgata.” “And how, Venerable Sir, do they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch?” “Ānanda, they wrap the body of a wheel-turning monarch with new cloth. Having wrapped it with new cloth, they wrap it with carded cotton. Having wrapped it with carded cotton, they wrap it with new cloth. By this method, having wrapped the body of the wheel-turning monarch with five hundred pairs of such cloths, they place it in a golden oil trough, cover it with another golden trough, make a pyre of all fragrant woods, and cremate the body of the wheel-turning monarch. At a crossroads of four great highways, they build a stupa for the wheel-turning monarch. This, Ānanda, is how they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch. Just as, Ānanda, they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch, so should one proceed with the body of the Tathāgata. A stupa for the Tathāgata should be built at a crossroads of four great highways. There, for whoever shall offer a garland, or incense, or fragrant powder, or shall pay homage, or shall make their mind serene, that will be for their welfare and happiness for a long time.

Thūpārahapuggalo

Persons Worthy of a Stupa

206. “Cattārome, ānanda, thūpārahā. Katame cattāro? Tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho thūpāraho, paccekasambuddho thūpāraho, tathāgatassa sāvako thūpāraho, rājā cakkavattī cakkavatti (syā. ka.) thūpārahoti.

206. “Ānanda, these four are worthy of a stupa. Which four? The Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, is worthy of a stupa; a Paccekasambuddha is worthy of a stupa; a disciple of the Tathāgata is worthy of a stupa; and a wheel-turning monarch is worthy of a stupa.”

“Kiñcānanda[M 2.0118], atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa thūpo’ti, ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho thūpāraho.

“For what reason, Ānanda, is the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, worthy of a stupa? ‘This is the stupa of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One,’ thinking thus, Ānanda, many people gladden their minds. Having gladdened their minds there, upon the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. This, indeed, Ānanda, is the reason on account of which the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, is worthy of a stupa.”

“Kiñcānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca paccekasambuddho thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa bhagavato paccekasambuddhassa [V 2.0108][P 2.0143] thūpo’ti, ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca paccekasambuddho thūpāraho.

“For what reason, Ānanda, is a Paccekasambuddha worthy of a stupa? ‘This is the stupa of that Blessed One, the Paccekasambuddha,’ thinking thus, Ānanda, many people gladden their minds. Having gladdened their minds there, upon the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. This, indeed, Ānanda, is the reason on account of which a Paccekasambuddha is worthy of a stupa.”

“Kiñcānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgatassa sāvako [T 2.0166] thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa sāvakassa thūpo’ti ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca tathāgatassa sāvako thūpāraho.

“For what reason, Ānanda, is a disciple of the Tathāgata worthy of a stupa? ‘This is the stupa of a disciple of that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One,’ thinking thus, Ānanda, many people gladden their minds. Having gladdened their minds there, upon the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. This, indeed, Ānanda, is the reason on account of which a disciple of the Tathāgata is worthy of a stupa.”

“Kiñcānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca rājā cakkavattī thūpāraho? ‘Ayaṃ tassa dhammikassa dhammarañño thūpo’ti, ānanda, bahujanā cittaṃ pasādenti. Te tattha cittaṃ pasādetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Idaṃ kho, ānanda, atthavasaṃ paṭicca rājā cakkavattī thūpāraho. Ime kho, ānanda cattāro thūpārahā”ti.

“For what reason, Ānanda, is a wheel-turning monarch worthy of a stupa? ‘This is the stupa of that righteous king, that king of Dhamma,’ thinking thus, Ānanda, many people gladden their minds. Having gladdened their minds there, upon the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. This, indeed, Ānanda, is the reason on account of which a wheel-turning monarch is worthy of a stupa. These, Ānanda, are the four who are worthy of a stupa.”

Ānandaacchariyadhammo

The Wondrous Qualities of Ānanda

207. Atha kho āyasmā ānando vihāraṃ pavisitvā kapisīsaṃ ālambitvā rodamāno aṭṭhāsi – “ahañca vatamhi sekho sakaraṇīyo, satthu ca me parinibbānaṃ bhavissati, yo mama anukampako”ti. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “kahaṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, ānando”ti? “Eso, bhante, āyasmā ānando vihāraṃ pavisitvā kapisīsaṃ ālambitvā rodamāno ṭhito – ‘ahañca vatamhi sekho sakaraṇīyo, satthu ca me parinibbānaṃ bhavissati, yo mama anukampako’”ti. Atha kho bhagavā aññataraṃ bhikkhuṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, bhikkhu, mama vacanena ānandaṃ āmantehi [M 2.0119] – ‘satthā taṃ, āvuso ānanda, āmantetī’”ti. “Evaṃ[P 2.0144], bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato paṭissutvā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca [T 2.0167] – “satthā taṃ, āvuso ānanda, āmantetī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā ānando tassa bhikkhuno paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “alaṃ, ānanda, mā soci mā paridevi, nanu etaṃ, ānanda, mayā paṭikacceva akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo’; taṃ kutettha, ānanda, labbhā. Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ [V 2.0109] palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata tathāgatassāpi sarīraṃ mā palujjī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Dīgharattaṃ kho te, ānanda, tathāgato paccupaṭṭhito mettena kāyakammena hitena sukhena advayena appamāṇena, mettena vacīkammena hitena sukhena advayena appamāṇena, mettena manokammena hitena sukhena advayena appamāṇena. Katapuññosi tvaṃ, ānanda, padhānamanuyuñja, khippaṃ hohisi anāsavo”ti.

207. Then the Venerable Ānanda entered the monastery and, leaning against the doorpost, stood weeping: “Alas, I am still a learner with more to do, and my Teacher—who is so compassionate toward me—is about to attain final Nibbāna.” Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Where, monks, is Ānanda?” “Venerable Sir, the Venerable Ānanda has entered the monastery and, leaning against the doorpost, stands weeping, saying: ‘Alas, I am still a learner with more to do, and my Teacher—who is so compassionate toward me—is about to attain final Nibbāna.’” Then the Blessed One addressed a certain monk: “Come, monk, and in my name summon Ānanda, saying: ‘The Teacher summons you, friend Ānanda.’” “Yes, Venerable Sir,” that monk replied to the Blessed One. He went to the Venerable Ānanda and said, “The Teacher summons you, friend Ānanda.” “Yes, friend,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to that monk. He went to the Blessed One, paid homage, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One then said to the Venerable Ānanda as he sat there: “Enough, Ānanda, do not grieve, do not lament. Have I not declared to you from the very beginning, Ānanda, that with all that is dear and beloved there must be separation, severance, and otherness? How, Ānanda, could it be otherwise? For that which is born, come into being, conditioned, and subject to decay—to wish, ‘May the Tathāgata’s body not perish!’—such a condition does not exist. For a long time, Ānanda, you have attended upon the Tathāgata with loving bodily action that is beneficial, pleasant, undivided, and boundless; with loving verbal action that is beneficial, pleasant, undivided, and boundless; with loving mental action that is beneficial, pleasant, undivided, and boundless. You have made merit, Ānanda. Apply yourself to the endeavor, and you will soon be free from the taints.”

208. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “yepi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etapparamāyeva upaṭṭhākā ahesuṃ, seyyathāpi mayhaṃ ānando. Yepi te, bhikkhave, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etapparamāyeva upaṭṭhākā bhavissanti, seyyathāpi mayhaṃ ānando. Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, ānando; medhāvī, bhikkhave, ānando. Jānāti ‘ayaṃ kālo tathāgataṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, ayaṃ kālo bhikkhunīnaṃ, ayaṃ kālo upāsakānaṃ[T 2.0168], ayaṃ [P 2.0145] kālo upāsikānaṃ, ayaṃ kālo rañño rājamahāmattānaṃ titthiyānaṃ titthiyasāvakāna’nti.

208. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, whatever Arahants, Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones there were in the past, for those Blessed Ones too, their attendants were of the highest measure, just as Ānanda is for me. And whatever Arahants, Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones there will be in the future, for those Blessed Ones too, their attendants will be of the highest measure, just as Ānanda is for me. Ānanda is wise, monks; Ānanda is intelligent. He knows: ‘This is the time for monks to approach the Tathāgata for an audience; this is the time for nuns; this is the time for male lay followers; this is the time for female lay followers; this is the time for kings, royal ministers, other sectarians, and their disciples.’”

209. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, acchariyā abbhutā dhammā abbhutadhammā (syā. ka.) ānande. Katame cattāro? Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ [M 2.0120] bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhunīparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, upāsakaparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsakaparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce, ānando, dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā hoti, atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande.

209. Monks, there are these four amazing and wondrous qualities in Ānanda. What four? If, monks, an assembly of monks approaches Ānanda to see him, they are delighted by the sight. And if Ānanda speaks the Dhamma to them there, they are delighted by his speech. The assembly of monks remains unsatisfied when Ānanda becomes silent. If, monks, an assembly of nuns approaches Ānanda to see him, they are delighted by the sight. And if Ānanda speaks the Dhamma to them there, they are delighted by his speech. The assembly of nuns remains unsatisfied when Ānanda becomes silent. If, monks, an assembly of male lay followers approaches Ānanda to see him, they are delighted by the sight. And if Ānanda speaks the Dhamma to them there, they are delighted by his speech. The assembly of male lay followers remains unsatisfied when Ānanda becomes silent. If, monks, an assembly of female lay followers approaches Ānanda to see him, they are delighted by the sight. And if Ānanda speaks the Dhamma to them there, they are delighted by his speech. The assembly of female lay followers remains unsatisfied when Ānanda becomes silent. These, monks, are the four amazing and wondrous qualities in Ānanda.

“Cattārome, bhikkhave, acchariyā abbhutā dhammā raññe cakkavattimhi. Katame cattāro[V 2.0110]? Sace, bhikkhave, khattiyaparisā rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ dassanāya [T 2.0169] upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce rājā cakkavattī bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, khattiyaparisā hoti. Atha kho rājā cakkavattī tuṇhī hoti. Sace bhikkhave, brāhmaṇaparisā…pe… gahapatiparisā…pe… samaṇaparisā rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce rājā cakkavattī bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, samaṇaparisā hoti, atha kho rājā cakkavattī tuṇhī hoti. Evameva [P 2.0146] kho, bhikkhave, cattārome acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande. Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā hoti. Atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Sace, bhikkhave bhikkhunīparisā…pe… upāsakaparisā…pe… upāsikāparisā ānandaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanena sā attamanā [M 2.0121] hoti. Tatra ce ānando dhammaṃ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti. Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā hoti. Atha kho ānando tuṇhī hoti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande”ti.

“Monks, there are these four amazing and wondrous qualities in a wheel-turning monarch. What four? If, monks, an assembly of nobles approaches a wheel-turning monarch to see him, they are pleased by the sight. And if the wheel-turning monarch speaks, they are pleased by his speech. The assembly of nobles remains unsated, monks, and then the wheel-turning monarch becomes silent. If, monks, an assembly of brahmins… an assembly of householders… an assembly of ascetics approaches a wheel-turning monarch to see him, they are pleased by the sight. And if the wheel-turning monarch speaks, they are pleased by his speech. The assembly of ascetics remains unsated, monks, and then the wheel-turning monarch becomes silent. In the same way, monks, there are these four amazing and wondrous qualities in Ānanda. If, monks, an assembly of monks approaches Ānanda to see him, they are pleased by the sight. And if Ānanda speaks the Dhamma, they are pleased by his speech. The assembly of monks remains unsated, monks, and then Ānanda becomes silent. If, monks, an assembly of nuns… an assembly of male lay followers… an assembly of female lay followers approaches Ānanda to see him, they are pleased by the sight. And if Ānanda speaks the Dhamma, they are pleased by his speech. The assembly of female lay followers remains unsated, monks, and then Ānanda becomes silent. These, monks, are the four amazing and wondrous qualities in Ānanda.”

Mahāsudassanasuttadesanā

The Exposition of the Mahāsudassana Sutta

210. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “mā, bhante, bhagavā imasmiṃ khuddakanagarake ujjaṅgalanagarake sākhānagarake parinibbāyi. Santi, bhante, aññāni mahānagarāni, seyyathidaṃ – campā [T 2.0170] rājagahaṃ sāvatthī sāketaṃ kosambī bārāṇasī; ettha bhagavā parinibbāyatu. Ettha bahū khattiyamahāsālā, brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatimahāsālā tathāgate abhippasannā. Te tathāgatassa sarīrapūjaṃ karissantī”ti “māhevaṃ, ānanda, avaca; māhevaṃ, ānanda, avaca – ‘khuddakanagarakaṃ ujjaṅgalanagarakaṃ sākhānagaraka’nti.

210. When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, may the Blessed One not attain final Nibbāna in this little town, this wilderness town, this branch town. There are, venerable sir, other great cities, such as Campā, Rājagaha, Sāvatthī, Sāketa, Kosambī, and Bārāṇasī; let the Blessed One attain final Nibbāna there. There, many wealthy nobles, wealthy brahmins, and wealthy householders have deep faith in the Tathāgata. They will perform the veneration of the Tathāgata’s relics.” “Do not speak thus, Ānanda. Do not speak thus, Ānanda, calling it ‘a little town, a wilderness town, a branch town.’”

“Bhūtapubbaṃ, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano nāma ahosi cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janappadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Rañño, ānanda, mahāsudassanassa ayaṃ kusinārā kusāvatī nāma rājadhānī ahosi, puratthimena ca pacchimena ca dvādasayojanāni āyāmena; uttarena ca dakkhiṇena ca sattayojanāni vitthārena. Kusāvatī, ānanda, rājadhānī iddhā ceva ahosi phītā ca [P 2.0147] bahujanā ca ākiṇṇamanussā ca subhikkhā ca. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, devānaṃ āḷakamandā nāma rājadhānī iddhā ceva hoti phītā [V 2.0111] ca bahujanā ca ākiṇṇayakkhā ca subhikkhā ca; evameva kho, ānanda, kusāvatī rājadhānī iddhā ceva ahosi phītā ca bahujanā ca ākiṇṇamanussā ca subhikkhā ca. Kusāvatī, ānanda, rājadhānī dasahi saddehi avivittā ahosi divā ceva rattiñca, seyyathidaṃ – hatthisaddena assasaddena rathasaddena bherisaddena mudiṅgasaddena vīṇāsaddena gītasaddena saṅkhasaddena sammasaddena pāṇitāḷasaddena ‘asnātha pivatha khādathā’ti dasamena saddena.

“Formerly, Ānanda, there was a king named Mahāsudassana, a wheel-turning monarch, a righteous king of righteousness, a conqueror of the four quarters, who had achieved stability in his country, and was endowed with the seven treasures. For King Mahāsudassana, Ānanda, this Kusinārā was the royal capital named Kusāvatī. It was twelve yojanas in length from east to west, and seven yojanas in width from north to south. The royal capital Kusāvatī, Ānanda, was prosperous and flourishing, populous, crowded with people, and well-supplied with food. Just as, Ānanda, the royal capital of the devas named Āḷakamandā is prosperous and flourishing, populous, crowded with yakkhas, and well-supplied with food, so too, Ānanda, the royal capital Kusāvatī was prosperous and flourishing, populous, crowded with people, and well-supplied with food. The royal capital Kusāvatī, Ānanda, was never free, day or night, of ten sounds—namely, the sound of elephants, the sound of horses, the sound of chariots, the sound of kettle drums, the sound of tabors, the sound of lutes, the sound of singing, the sound of conches, the sound of cymbals and hand-clapping, and with the tenth sound, the cry: ‘Eat, drink, and consume!’”

“Gaccha tvaṃ, ānanda, kusināraṃ pavisitvā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ [T 2.0171] ārocehi – ‘ajja kho, vāseṭṭhā, rattiyā pacchime yāme tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ [M 2.0122] bhavissati. Abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā, abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā. Mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha – amhākañca no gāmakkhette tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ ahosi, na mayaṃ labhimhā pacchime kāle tathāgataṃ dassanāyā’”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya attadutiyo kusināraṃ pāvisi.

“Go, Ānanda, enter Kusinārā and announce to the Mallas of Kusinārā: ‘Today, Vāseṭṭhas, in the last watch of the night, the Tathāgata’s final Nibbāna will occur. Approach, Vāseṭṭhas, approach! Do not later be regretful, thinking: “The Tathāgata’s final Nibbāna occurred in our own village territory, and we did not get to see the Tathāgata at his last moment.”’” “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Then, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, he entered Kusinārā with a companion.

Mallānaṃ vandanā

The Homage of the Mallas

211. Tena kho pana samayena kosinārakā mallā sandhāgāre santhāgāre (sī. syā. pī.) sannipatitā honti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ sandhāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ ārocesi – “ajja kho, vāseṭṭhā, rattiyā pacchime yāme tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā abhikkamatha vāseṭṭhā. Mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha – ‘amhākañca no gāmakkhette tathāgatassa parinibbānaṃ [P 2.0148] ahosi, na mayaṃ labhimhā pacchime kāle tathāgataṃ dassanāyā’”ti. Idamāyasmato ānandassa vacanaṃ sutvā mallā ca mallaputtā ca mallasuṇisā ca mallapajāpatiyo ca aghāvino dummanā cetodukkhasamappitā appekacce kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbāyissati, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ [T 2.0172] loke antaradhāyissatī’ti. Atha kho mallā ca mallaputtā ca mallasuṇisā ca mallapajāpatiyo ca aghāvino dummanā cetodukkhasamappitā yena upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – “sace kho ahaṃ kosinārake malle ekamekaṃ bhagavantaṃ vandāpessāmi, avandito bhagavā kosinārakehi mallehi bhavissati, athāyaṃ ratti vibhāyissati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ kosinārake malle kulaparivattaso kulaparivattaso [V 2.0112] ṭhapetvā bhagavantaṃ vandāpeyyaṃ – ‘itthannāmo, bhante, mallo saputto sabhariyo sapariso sāmacco bhagavato pāde [M 2.0123] sirasā vandatī’ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando kosinārake malle kulaparivattaso kulaparivattaso ṭhapetvā bhagavantaṃ vandāpesi – ‘itthannāmo, bhante, mallo saputto sabhariyo sapariso sāmacco bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’”ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando etena upāyena paṭhameneva yāmena kosinārake malle bhagavantaṃ vandāpesi.

211. Now at that time the Mallas of Kusinārā were assembled in their council hall on some business. Then the Venerable Ānanda went to the council hall of the Mallas of Kusinārā. Having gone there, he informed the Mallas of Kusinārā: ‘Today, Vāseṭṭhas, in the last watch of the night, the Tathāgata’s final Nibbāna will occur. Approach, Vāseṭṭhas, approach! Do not later be regretful, thinking: “The Tathāgata’s final Nibbāna occurred in our own village territory, and we did not get to see the Tathāgata at his last moment.”’ Hearing these words of the Venerable Ānanda, the Mallas, their sons, their daughters-in-law, and their wives became afflicted, dejected, and overcome by mental anguish. Some, with disheveled hair, wept; some, with arms upraised, wept; some fell down as if cut down; they rolled about, to and fro, lamenting: ‘Too soon the Blessed One will attain final Nibbāna! Too soon the Sugata will attain final Nibbāna! Too soon the Eye of the World will disappear from the world!’ Then the Mallas, their sons, their daughters-in-law, and their wives, being afflicted, dejected, and overcome by mental anguish, went to the Upavattana sāl grove of the Mallas, to where the Venerable Ānanda was. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Ānanda: ‘If I were to have the Mallas of Kusinārā pay homage to the Blessed One one by one, they would not finish paying homage before this night dawns. What if I were to arrange the Mallas of Kusinārā by family group and have them pay homage to the Blessed One, announcing: “Venerable sir, the Malla named so-and-so, with his son, his wife, his retinue, and his ministers, venerates the Blessed One’s feet with his head.”’ Then the Venerable Ānanda arranged the Mallas of Kusinārā by family group and had them pay homage to the Blessed One, announcing: ‘Venerable sir, the Malla named so-and-so, with his son, his wife, his retinue, and his ministers, venerates the Blessed One’s feet with his head.’ In this way, by this method, the Venerable Ānanda had the Mallas of Kusinārā pay homage to the Blessed One within the first watch of the night.

Subhaddaparibbājakavatthu

The Story of the Wanderer Subhadda

212. Tena kho pana samayena subhaddo nāma paribbājako kusinārāyaṃ paṭivasati. Assosi kho subhaddo paribbājako – “ajja kira rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissatī”ti. Atha [P 2.0149] kho subhaddassa paribbājakassa etadahosi – “sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘kadāci karahaci tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā’ti. Ajjeva [T 2.0173] rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Atthi ca me ayaṃ kaṅkhādhammo uppanno, evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ samaṇe gotame, ‘pahoti me samaṇo gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ, yathāhaṃ imaṃ kaṅkhādhammaṃ pajaheyya’”nti. Atha kho subhaddo paribbājako yena upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bho ānanda, paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘kadāci karahaci tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto [T 2.0174] sammāsambuddhā’ti. Ajjeva rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Atthi ca me ayaṃ kaṅkhādhammo uppanno – evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ samaṇe gotame ‘pahoti me samaṇo gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ, yathāhaṃ imaṃ kaṅkhādhammaṃ pajaheyya’nti. Sādhāhaṃ, bho ānanda, labheyyaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāyā”ti. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā ānando subhaddaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – “alaṃ, āvuso subhadda, mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesi, kilanto bhagavā”ti. Dutiyampi kho subhaddo paribbājako…pe… tatiyampi kho subhaddo paribbājako āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bho ānanda, paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘kadāci karahaci tathāgatā [M 2.0124] loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā’ti. Ajjeva rattiyā pacchime yāme samaṇassa [P 2.0150] gotamassa parinibbānaṃ bhavissati. Atthi ca me ayaṃ kaṅkhādhammo uppanno – evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ samaṇe gotame, ‘pahoti me samaṇo gotamo tathā [V 2.0113] dhammaṃ desetuṃ, yathāhaṃ imaṃ kaṅkhādhammaṃ pajaheyya’nti. Sādhāhaṃ, bho ānanda, labheyyaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ dassanāyā”ti. Tatiyampi kho āyasmā ānando subhaddaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – “alaṃ, āvuso subhadda, mā tathāgataṃ viheṭhesi, kilanto bhagavā”ti.

212. Now at that time a wanderer named Subhadda was dwelling in Kusinārā. The wanderer Subhadda heard: 'It is said that today, in the last watch of the night, the ascetic Gotama's final Nibbāna will occur.' Then this thought occurred to the wanderer Subhadda: 'I have heard this from wanderers who are elders, seniors, and teachers of teachers, as they were speaking: “Rarely, from time to time, do Tathāgatas, Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, arise in the world.” And today, in the last watch of the night, the ascetic Gotama's final Nibbāna will occur. A state of doubt has arisen in me, and I have such confidence in the ascetic Gotama that he is able to teach me the Dhamma in such a way that I might abandon this state of doubt.' Then the wanderer Subhadda went to the sāl grove of the Mallas at Upavattana, to where the Venerable Ānanda was. Having approached, he said this to the Venerable Ānanda: 'Venerable Ānanda, I have heard this from wanderers who are elders, seniors, and teachers of teachers, as they were speaking: “Rarely, from time to time, do Tathāgatas, Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, arise in the world.” And today, in the last watch of the night, the ascetic Gotama's final Nibbāna will occur. A state of doubt has arisen in me, and I have such confidence in the ascetic Gotama that he is able to teach me the Dhamma in such a way that I might abandon this state of doubt. It would be well, Venerable Ānanda, if I might get to see the ascetic Gotama.' When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the wanderer Subhadda: 'Enough, friend Subhadda. Do not trouble the Tathāgata. The Blessed One is weary.' For a second time, the wanderer Subhadda… For a third time, the wanderer Subhadda said this to the Venerable Ānanda: 'Venerable Ānanda, I have heard this from wanderers who are elders, seniors, and teachers of teachers, as they were speaking: “Rarely, from time to time, do Tathāgatas, Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, arise in the world.” And today, in the last watch of the night, the ascetic Gotama's final Nibbāna will occur. A state of doubt has arisen in me, and I have such confidence in the ascetic Gotama that he is able to teach me the Dhamma in such a way that I might abandon this state of doubt. It would be well, Venerable Ānanda, if I might get to see the ascetic Gotama.' For a third time, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the wanderer Subhadda: 'Enough, friend Subhadda. Do not trouble the Tathāgata. The Blessed One is weary.'

213. Assosi kho bhagavā āyasmato ānandassa subhaddena paribbājakena saddhiṃ imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “alaṃ, ānanda, mā subhaddaṃ vāresi, labhataṃ, ānanda, subhaddo tathāgataṃ dassanāya. Yaṃ kiñci maṃ subhaddo pucchissati, sabbaṃ taṃ aññāpekkhova pucchissati, no vihesāpekkho. Yaṃ cassāhaṃ puṭṭho byākarissāmi, taṃ khippameva ājānissatī”ti. Atha kho āyasmā ānando subhaddaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – “gacchāvuso subhadda, karoti te bhagavā okāsa”nti. Atha kho subhaddo paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho subhaddo paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yeme, bho gotama, samaṇabrāhmaṇā saṅghino gaṇino gaṇācariyā ñātā yasassino titthakarā sādhusammatā bahujanassa, seyyathidaṃ [T 2.0175] – pūraṇo kassapo, makkhali gosālo, ajito kesakambalo, pakudho kaccāyano, sañcayo belaṭṭhaputto, nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto, sabbete sakāya paṭiññāya abbhaññiṃsu, sabbeva na abbhaññiṃsu[P 2.0151], udāhu ekacce abbhaññiṃsu, ekacce na abbhaññiṃsū”ti? “Alaṃ, subhadda, tiṭṭhatetaṃ – ‘sabbete sakāya paṭiññāya abbhaññiṃsu, sabbeva na abbhaññiṃsu, udāhu ekacce abbhaññiṃsu, ekacce na abbhaññiṃsū’ti. Dhammaṃ te, subhadda, desessāmi; taṃ suṇāhi sādhukaṃ manasikarohi, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho subhaddo paribbājako bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

213. The Blessed One heard this conversation between the Venerable Ānanda and the wanderer Subhadda. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Enough, Ānanda, do not prevent Subhadda. Let Subhadda, Ānanda, have the opportunity to see the Tathāgata. Whatever Subhadda asks me, he will ask with a desire for knowledge, not with a desire to vex me. And whatever I, being asked, shall explain, that he will quickly understand.” Then the Venerable Ānanda said to the wanderer Subhadda: “Go, friend Subhadda, the Blessed One grants you an opportunity.” Then the wanderer Subhadda approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One, and after exchanging pleasant and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Subhadda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Gotama, there are these ascetics and brahmins who have communities, have followings, are teachers of followings, are well-known, have renown, are founders of sects, and are regarded as virtuous by many people—namely, Pūraṇa Kassapa, Makkhali Gosāla, Ajita Kesakambala, Pakudha Kaccāyana, Sañcaya Belaṭṭhaputta, and the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta. Did they all, according to their own declaration, fully understand, or did they all not fully understand, or did some fully understand and some not?” “Enough, Subhadda, let this be: ‘Did they all, according to their own declaration, fully understand, or did they all not fully understand, or did some fully understand and some not?’ I will teach you the Dhamma, Subhadda; listen to it and pay close attention, I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the wanderer Subhadda replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

214. “Yasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo na upalabbhati, samaṇopi tattha na upalabbhati. Dutiyopi tattha samaṇo [M 2.0125] na upalabbhati. Tatiyopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati. Catutthopi tattha samaṇo na upalabbhati. Yasmiñca kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhati, samaṇopi tattha upalabbhati, dutiyopi tattha samaṇo upalabbhati, tatiyopi tattha samaṇo upalabbhati, catutthopi tattha samaṇo upalabbhati. Imasmiṃ kho, subhadda, dhammavinaye ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo upalabbhati, idheva, subhadda, samaṇo, idha dutiyo samaṇo, idha tatiyo samaṇo, idha catuttho samaṇo, suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi [V 2.0114] aññehi aññe (pī.). Ime [T 2.0176] ca idheva (ka.), subhadda, bhikkhū sammā vihareyyuṃ, asuñño loko arahantehi assāti.

214. “In whatever Dhamma and Discipline, Subhadda, the Noble Eightfold Path is not found, an ascetic is not found there either. A second ascetic is not found there. A third ascetic is not found there. A fourth ascetic is not found there. And in whatever Dhamma and Discipline, Subhadda, the Noble Eightfold Path is found, an ascetic is found there, a second ascetic is found there, a third ascetic is found there, and a fourth ascetic is found there. In this Dhamma and Discipline, Subhadda, the Noble Eightfold Path is found. Right here, Subhadda, there is an ascetic, here a second ascetic, here a third ascetic, here a fourth ascetic. The doctrines of others are devoid of ascetics. If these monks, Subhadda, were to live rightly, the world would not be devoid of arahants.”

“Ekūnatiṃso vayasā subhadda,

Yaṃ pabbajiṃ kiṃkusalānuesī;

Vassāni paññāsa samādhikāni,

Yato ahaṃ pabbajito subhadda.

“At twenty-nine years of age, Subhadda, I went forth, seeking what is wholesome. More than fifty years have passed, Subhadda, since I went forth.

Ñāyassa dhammassa padesavattī,

Ito bahiddhā samaṇopi natthi.

Outside of this dispensation, there is no one who practices even a portion of the rightful Dhamma, nor is there even an ascetic.

“Dutiyopi [P 2.0152] samaṇo natthi. Tatiyopi samaṇo natthi. Catutthopi samaṇo natthi. Suññā parappavādā samaṇebhi aññehi. Ime ca, subhadda, bhikkhū sammā vihareyyuṃ, asuñño loko arahantehi assā”ti.

“A second ascetic is not found. A third ascetic is not found. A fourth ascetic is not found. The doctrines of others are devoid of ascetics. If these monks, Subhadda, were to live rightly, the world would not be devoid of arahants.”

215. Evaṃ vutte subhaddo paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante, abhikkantaṃ, bhante. Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya, ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti, evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Labheyyāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, labheyyaṃ upasampada”nti. “Yo kho, subhadda, aññatitthiyapubbo imasmiṃ dhammavinaye [T 2.0177] ākaṅkhati pabbajjaṃ, ākaṅkhati upasampadaṃ, so cattāro [M 2.0126] māse parivasati. Catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya. Api ca mettha puggalavemattatā viditā”ti. “Sace, bhante, aññatitthiyapubbā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ākaṅkhantā pabbajjaṃ ākaṅkhantā upasampadaṃ cattāro māse parivasanti, catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājenti upasampādenti bhikkhubhāvāya. Ahaṃ cattāri vassāni parivasissāmi, catunnaṃ vassānaṃ accayena āraddhacittā bhikkhū pabbājentu upasampādentu bhikkhubhāvāyā”ti.

215. When this was said, the wanderer Subhadda said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! It is as if, venerable sir, one were to set upright what was overturned, or to reveal what was hidden, or to point out the way to one who was lost, or to hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms. In the very same way, the Dhamma has been made clear by the Blessed One in many ways. I, venerable sir, go to the Blessed One for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks. May I, venerable sir, receive the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One, may I receive the higher ordination.” “Whoever, Subhadda, having been a follower of another sect, desires the going forth and the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline, he undergoes probation for four months. At the end of four months, the monks, being pleased, give him the going forth and the higher ordination to the state of a monk. However, I have also recognized the individual differences in this matter.” “Venerable sir, if those who were formerly followers of other sects, desiring the going forth and the higher ordination in this Dhamma and Discipline, undergo probation for four months, and at the end of four months the monks, being pleased, give them the going forth and the higher ordination to the state of a monk, then I will undergo probation for four years. At the end of four years, let the monks, being pleased, give me the going forth and the higher ordination to the state of a monk.”

Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “tenahānanda, subhaddaṃ pabbājehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho subhaddo [V 2.0115] paribbājako āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “lābhā vo, āvuso ānanda; suladdhaṃ vo, āvuso ānanda, ye ettha satthu satthārā (syā.) sammukhā antevāsikābhisekena abhisittā”ti. Alattha [P 2.0153] kho subhaddo paribbājako bhagavato santike pabbajjaṃ, alattha upasampadaṃ. Acirūpasampanno kho panāyasmā subhaddo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – ‘yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti’ tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti [T 2.0178] abbhaññāsi. Aññataro kho panāyasmā subhaddo arahataṃ ahosi. So bhagavato pacchimo sakkhisāvako ahosīti.

Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Then, Ānanda, give the going forth to Subhadda.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. Then the wanderer Subhadda said this to the Venerable Ānanda: “It is a gain for you, friend Ānanda; it is well-gained for you, friend Ānanda, that you have been consecrated with the consecration of a resident disciple in the Teacher’s presence.” The wanderer Subhadda received the going forth in the presence of the Blessed One; he received the higher ordination. Not long after his higher ordination, the Venerable Subhadda, dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute, soon realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, and having attained it, he dwelled therein. He knew directly: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is nothing further for this state of being.” And the Venerable Subhadda became one of the arahants. He was the last direct disciple of the Blessed One.

Pañcamo bhāṇavāro.

The Fifth Recitation Section is finished.

Tathāgatapacchimavācā

The Tathāgata’s Last Words

216. Atha [P 2.0154] kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “siyā kho panānanda, tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘atītasatthukaṃ pāvacanaṃ, natthi no satthā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, ānanda, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yo vo, ānanda, mayā dhammo ca vinayo [M 2.0127] ca desito paññatto, so vo mamaccayena satthā. Yathā kho panānanda, etarahi bhikkhū aññamaññaṃ āvusovādena samudācaranti, na kho mamaccayena evaṃ samudācaritabbaṃ. Theratarena, ānanda, bhikkhunā navakataro bhikkhu nāmena vā gottena vā āvusovādena vā samudācaritabbo. Navakatarena bhikkhunā therataro bhikkhu ‘bhante’ti vā ‘āyasmā’ti vā samudācaritabbo. Ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanatu. Channassa, ānanda, bhikkhuno mamaccayena brahmadaṇḍo dātabbo”ti. “Katamo pana, bhante, brahmadaṇḍo”ti? “Channo, ānanda, bhikkhu yaṃ iccheyya, taṃ vadeyya. So bhikkhūhi neva vattabbo, na ovaditabbo, na anusāsitabbo”ti.

216. Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “It may be, Ānanda, that you think: ‘The Teacher’s instruction has passed; we have no Teacher.’ But it should not be seen like this, Ānanda. The Dhamma and the Vinaya that I have taught and laid down for you will be your Teacher after I am gone. And, Ānanda, whereas the monks now address one another with the term ‘friend,’ they should not do so after I am gone. A more senior monk, Ānanda, should address a more junior monk by his name, by his clan name, or with the term ‘friend.’ A more junior monk should address a more senior monk as ‘venerable sir’ or ‘venerable.’ If it wishes, Ānanda, the Saṅgha may abolish the minor and lesser training rules after I am gone. And, Ānanda, after I am gone, the brahma-penalty should be imposed on the monk Channa.” “But what, venerable sir, is the brahma-penalty?” “Ānanda, the monk Channa may say what he wishes. He is not to be spoken to, admonished, or instructed by the monks.”

217. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā, pucchatha, bhikkhave, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino [P 2.0155] ahuvattha – ‘sammukhībhūto no satthā ahosi[V 2.0116], na mayaṃ sakkhimhā bhagavantaṃ sammukhā paṭipucchitu’” nti. Evaṃ vutte te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā…pe… tatiyampi kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā, pucchatha, bhikkhave, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha – ‘sammukhībhūto no satthā ahosi[T 2.0179], na mayaṃ sakkhimhā bhagavantaṃ sammukhā paṭipucchitu’” nti. Tatiyampi kho te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, satthugāravenapi na puccheyyātha. Sahāyakopi, bhikkhave, sahāyakassa ārocetū”ti. Evaṃ vutte te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, evaṃ pasanno ahaṃ, bhante, imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe, ‘natthi ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā’”ti. “Pasādā kho tvaṃ, ānanda, vadesi, ñāṇameva hettha, ānanda, tathāgatassa. Natthi imasmiṃ bhikkhusaṅghe ekabhikkhussāpi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā. Imesañhi, ānanda, pañcannaṃ bhikkhusatānaṃ yo pacchimako bhikkhu, so sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti.

217. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “It may be, monks, that even one monk has doubt or uncertainty about the Buddha, the Dhamma, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice. Ask, monks. Do not be regretful later, thinking: ‘Our Teacher was face to face with us, but we were not able to ask the Blessed One directly.’” When this was said, those monks were silent. A second time... and a third time the Blessed One addressed the monks: “It may be, monks, that even one monk has doubt or uncertainty about the Buddha, the Dhamma, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice. Ask, monks. Do not be regretful later, thinking: ‘Our Teacher was face to face with us, but we were not able to ask the Blessed One directly.’” A third time, those monks were silent. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “It may be, monks, that you do not ask out of reverence for the Teacher. Then, monks, let a friend inform a friend.” When this was said, those monks were silent. Then the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “It is wonderful, Venerable Sir! It is marvelous, Venerable Sir! I am so confident in this community of monks that there is not even one monk who has doubt or uncertainty about the Buddha, the Dhamma, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice.” “You speak out of confidence, Ānanda, but the Tathāgata has direct knowledge in this matter. In this community of monks, there is not even one monk who has doubt or uncertainty about the Buddha, the Dhamma, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice. For, Ānanda, of these five hundred monks, the one who is last is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into a lower state, assured, and bound for enlightenment.”

218. Atha [T 2.0180][M 2.0128] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “handa [P 2.0156] dāni, bhikkhave, āmantayāmi vo, vayadhammā saṅkhārā appamādena sampādethā”ti. Ayaṃ tathāgatassa pacchimā vācā.

218. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Now then, monks, I declare this to you: all conditioned phenomena are subject to decay. Strive on with diligence!” This was the Tathāgata’s last utterance.

Parinibbutakathā

The Account of the Final Nibbāna

219. Atha kho bhagavā paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, paṭhamajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, dutiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji. Catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajji.

219. Then the Blessed One entered the first jhāna. Emerging from the first jhāna, he entered the second jhāna. Emerging from the second jhāna, he entered the third jhāna. Emerging from the third jhāna, he entered the fourth jhāna. Emerging from the fourth jhāna, he entered the base of infinite space. Emerging from the attainment of the base of infinite space, he entered the base of infinite consciousness. Emerging from the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness, he entered the base of nothingness. Emerging from the attainment of the base of nothingness, he entered the base of neither perception nor non-perception. Emerging from the attainment of the base of neither perception nor non-perception, he entered the cessation of perception and feeling.

Atha kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – “parinibbuto, bhante anuruddha[V 2.0117], bhagavā”ti. “Nāvuso ānanda, bhagavā parinibbuto, saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpanno”ti.

Then the Venerable Ānanda said to the Venerable Anuruddha: "Venerable Anuruddha, has the Blessed One passed away into final Nibbāna?" "No, friend Ānanda, the Blessed One has not passed away into final Nibbāna; he has entered the cessation of perception and feeling."

Atha kho bhagavā saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, viññāṇañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpajji, ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattiyā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ [T 2.0181] samāpajji, catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, dutiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, paṭhamajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, dutiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, tatiyajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajji, catutthajjhānā vuṭṭhahitvā samanantarā bhagavā parinibbāyi.

Then the Blessed One, emerging from the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, entered the base of neither perception nor non-perception. Emerging from the attainment of the base of neither perception nor non-perception, he entered the base of nothingness. Emerging from the attainment of the base of nothingness, he entered the base of infinite consciousness. Emerging from the attainment of the base of infinite consciousness, he entered the base of infinite space. Emerging from the attainment of the base of infinite space, he entered the fourth jhāna. Emerging from the fourth jhāna, he entered the third jhāna. Emerging from the third jhāna, he entered the second jhāna. Emerging from the second jhāna, he entered the first jhāna. Emerging from the first jhāna, he entered the second jhāna. Emerging from the second jhāna, he entered the third jhāna. Emerging from the third jhāna, he entered the fourth jhāna. Immediately after emerging from the fourth jhāna, the Blessed One passed away into final Nibbāna.

220. Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā mahābhūmicālo ahosi bhiṃsanako salomahaṃso. Devadundubhiyo ca phaliṃsu. Parinibbute [P 2.0157] bhagavati saha parinibbānā brahmāsahampati imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

220. When the Blessed One passed away into final Nibbāna, simultaneously with his passing away, there was a great earthquake, dreadful and hair-raising, and the celestial drums resounded. When the Blessed One passed away into final Nibbāna, simultaneously with his passing away, Brahmā Sahampati recited this verse:

“Sabbeva [M 2.0129] nikkhipissanti, bhūtā loke samussayaṃ;

Yattha etādiso satthā, loke appaṭipuggalo;

Tathāgato balappatto, sambuddho parinibbuto”ti.

All beings in the world will lay down the body, for even such a Teacher—peerless in the world, the Tathāgata who has attained the powers, the Perfectly Enlightened One—has passed away into final Nibbāna.

221. Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā sakko devānamindo imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

221. When the Blessed One passed away into final Nibbāna, simultaneously with his passing away, Sakka, the ruler of the gods, uttered this verse:

“Aniccā vata saṅkhārā, uppādavayadhammino;

Uppajjitvā nirujjhanti, tesaṃ vūpasamo sukho”ti.

Impermanent, indeed, are conditioned things, subject to arising and passing away. Having arisen, they cease; their stilling is bliss.

222. Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā āyasmā anuruddho imā gāthāyo abhāsi –

222. When the Blessed One passed away into final Nibbāna, simultaneously with his passing away, the Venerable Anuruddha recited these verses:

“Nāhu [T 2.0182][V 2.0118] assāsapassāso, ṭhitacittassa tādino;

Anejo santimārabbha, yaṃ kālamakarī muni.

There was no in-breath nor out-breath for him of steadfast mind, the Such-like one. Free from agitation, intent on peace, the Sage has met his end.

“Asallīnena cittena, vedanaṃ ajjhavāsayi;

Pajjotasseva nibbānaṃ, vimokkho cetaso ahū”ti.

With an unwavering mind, he endured the feeling. Like the extinguishing of a lamp, so was the liberation of his mind.

223. Parinibbute bhagavati saha parinibbānā āyasmā ānando imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

223. When the Blessed One passed away into final Nibbāna, simultaneously with his passing away, the Venerable Ānanda recited this verse:

“Tadāsi yaṃ bhiṃsanakaṃ, tadāsi lomahaṃsanaṃ;

Sabbākāravarūpete, sambuddhe parinibbute”ti.

Then there was terror, then it was hair-raising, when the Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with all excellent qualities, passed away into final Nibbāna.

224. Parinibbute bhagavati ye te tattha bhikkhū avītarāgā appekacce bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti vivaṭṭanti, “atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto[P 2.0158], atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito”ti. Ye pana te bhikkhū vītarāgā, te satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – “aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā”ti.

224. When the Blessed One had attained Parinibbāna, some monks there who were not free from passion raised their arms and wept, fell down as if from a precipice, rolled back and forth, lamenting: 'Too soon the Blessed One has attained Parinibbāna! Too soon the Well-Gone One has attained Parinibbāna! Too soon the Eye has vanished from the world!' But those monks who were free from passion, being mindful and fully aware, endured, reflecting: 'Impermanent are conditioned formations; how could that be obtained here?'

225. Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho bhikkhū āmantesi – “alaṃ, āvuso, mā socittha mā paridevittha. Nanu etaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā paṭikacceva akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo’. Taṃ kutettha, āvuso, labbhā. ‘Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata mā palujjī’ti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ [T 2.0183] vijjati[M 2.0130]. Devatā, āvuso, ujjhāyantī”ti. “Kathaṃbhūtā pana, bhante, āyasmā anuruddho devatā manasi karotī”ti bhante anuruddha devatā manasi karontīti (syā. ka.)?

225. Then the Venerable Anuruddha addressed the monks: "Enough, friends, do not grieve, do not lament. Has not the Blessed One declared this beforehand: 'From all that is dear and beloved there is separation, parting, and otherness'? How, friends, could that be obtained here? As for that which is born, has come into being, is conditioned, and is of a nature to perish, the wish 'May it not perish!'—such a condition does not exist. The deities, friends, are complaining." "But what kind of deities, venerable sir, does the Venerable Anuruddha have in mind?"

“Santāvuso ānanda, devatā ākāse pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’ti. Santāvuso ānanda, devatā pathaviyā pathavīsaññiniyo kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – ‘atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto[V 2.0119], atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito’ti. Yā pana tā devatā vītarāgā, tā satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – ‘aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti. Atha kho āyasmā ca anuruddho āyasmā ca ānando taṃ rattāvasesaṃ dhammiyā kathāya vītināmesuṃ.

“Friend Ānanda, there are deities in the sky who perceive the earth, who with disheveled hair weep, raise their arms and weep, fall down as if from a precipice, and roll back and forth, lamenting: 'Too soon the Blessed One has attained Parinibbāna! Too soon the Well-Gone One has attained Parinibbāna! Too soon the Eye has vanished from the world!' Friend Ānanda, there are deities on the earth who perceive the earth, who with disheveled hair weep, raise their arms and weep, fall down as if from a precipice, and roll back and forth, lamenting: 'Too soon the Blessed One has attained Parinibbāna! Too soon the Well-Gone One has attained Parinibbāna! Too soon the Eye has vanished from the world!' But those deities who are free from passion, being mindful and fully aware, endure, reflecting: 'Impermanent are conditioned formations; how could that be obtained here?'” Then the Venerable Anuruddha and the Venerable Ānanda spent the remainder of the night in discussion on the Dhamma.

226. Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “gacchāvuso ānanda, kusināraṃ pavisitvā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ ārocehi – ‘parinibbuto, vāseṭṭhā, bhagavā, yassadāni kālaṃ maññathā’”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando āyasmato anuruddhassa paṭissutvā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya attadutiyo kusināraṃ pāvisi. Tena [P 2.0159] kho pana samayena kosinārakā mallā sandhāgāre sannipatitā honti teneva karaṇīyena. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ sandhāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [T 2.0184] kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ ārocesi – ‘parinibbuto, vāseṭṭhā, bhagavā, yassadāni kālaṃ maññathā’ti. Idamāyasmato ānandassa vacanaṃ sutvā mallā ca mallaputtā ca mallasuṇisā ca mallapajāpatiyo ca aghāvino dummanā cetodukkhasamappitā appekacce kese pakiriya kandanti, bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – “atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito”ti.

226. Then the Venerable Anuruddha addressed the Venerable Ānanda: “Go, friend Ānanda, enter Kusinārā and announce to the Mallas of Kusinārā: ‘The Blessed One, Vāseṭṭhas, has attained Parinibbāna. Now do what you deem it is time for.’” “Yes, venerable sir,” replied the Venerable Ānanda to the Venerable Anuruddha. Then, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robe, with a companion, he entered Kusinārā. At that time, the Mallas of Kusinārā had gathered in the assembly hall for that very purpose. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the assembly hall of the Mallas of Kusinārā and announced to them: “The Blessed One, Vāseṭṭhas, has attained Parinibbāna. Now do what you deem it is time for.” Hearing the Venerable Ānanda’s words, the Mallas, their sons, their daughters-in-law, and their wives were distressed, sorrowful, and afflicted with mental pain. Some tore their hair and wept, some raised their arms and wailed, some fell down as if from a precipice, rolling back and forth, crying: “Too soon has the Blessed One attained Parinibbāna! Too soon has the Well-Gone One attained Parinibbāna! Too soon has the Eye in the world vanished!”

Buddhasarīrapūjā

Honoring the Buddha’s Body

227. Atha [M 2.0131] kho kosinārakā mallā purise āṇāpesuṃ – “tena hi, bhaṇe, kusinārāyaṃ gandhamālañca sabbañca tāḷāvacaraṃ sannipātethā”ti. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā gandhamālañca sabbañca tāḷāvacaraṃ pañca ca dussayugasatāni ādāya yena upavattanaṃ mallānaṃ sālavanaṃ, yena bhagavato sarīraṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā celavitānāni karontā maṇḍalamāḷe paṭiyādentā ekadivasaṃ vītināmesuṃ.

227. Then the Mallas of Kusinārā ordered their men: “Go now, gather perfumes, garlands, and all musical instruments in Kusinārā.” Then the Mallas of Kusinārā, taking perfumes, garlands, all the musical instruments, and five hundred pairs of cloths, went to the Mallas’ sāla grove at Upavattana, where the Blessed One’s body was. Having gone there, honoring, respecting, revering, and venerating the Blessed One’s body with dances, songs, music, garlands, and perfumes, making cloth canopies and preparing circular pavilions, they passed one day.

Atha kho kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ etadahosi – “ativikālo kho ajja bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpetuṃ, sve dāni mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā”ti. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā [V 2.0120] pūjentā celavitānāni karontā maṇḍalamāḷe paṭiyādentā dutiyampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, tatiyampi [T 2.0185] divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, catutthampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, pañcamampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ, chaṭṭhampi divasaṃ vītināmesuṃ.

Then the Mallas of Kusinārā thought: “It is too late today to cremate the Blessed One’s body; tomorrow, then, we will cremate the Blessed One’s body.” Then the Mallas of Kusinārā, honoring, respecting, revering, and venerating the Blessed One’s body with dances, songs, music, garlands, and perfumes, making cloth canopies and preparing circular pavilions, passed the second day, the third day, the fourth day, the fifth day, and the sixth day.

Atha kho sattamaṃ divasaṃ kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ [P 2.0160] etadahosi – “mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇaṃ nagarassa haritvā bāhirena bāhiraṃ dakkhiṇato nagarassa bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā”ti.

Then, on the seventh day, the Mallas of Kusinārā had this thought: “Honoring, respecting, revering, and venerating the Blessed One’s body with dances, songs, music, garlands, and perfumes, let us carry it south by the southern gate of the city, and outside the city by the outer route, and cremate the Blessed One’s body to the south of the city.”

228. Tena kho pana samayena aṭṭha mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā “mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ uccāressāmā”ti na sakkonti uccāretuṃ. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ko nu kho, bhante anuruddha, hetu ko paccayo, yenime aṭṭha mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā ‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ uccāressāmā’ti na sakkonti uccāretu”nti? “Aññathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, tumhākaṃ adhippāyo, aññathā devatānaṃ adhippāyo”ti. “Kathaṃ pana, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo”ti? “Tumhākaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, adhippāyo – ‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi [M 2.0132] sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā dakkhiṇena dakkhiṇaṃ nagarassa haritvā bāhirena bāhiraṃ dakkhiṇato nagarassa bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā’ti; devatānaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, adhippāyo – ‘mayaṃ bhagavato sarīraṃ dibbehi naccehi [T 2.0186] gītehi vāditehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā uttarena uttaraṃ nagarassa haritvā uttarena dvārena nagaraṃ pavesetvā majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvā puratthimena dvārena nikkhamitvā puratthimato nagarassa makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ ettha bhagavato sarīraṃ jhāpessāmā’ti. “Yathā, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo, tathā hotū”ti.

228. Now at that time, eight leading Mallas, having bathed their heads and dressed in new clothes, were unable to lift the Blessed One’s body, though they intended, “We will lift the Blessed One’s body.” Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said to the Venerable Anuruddha: “What is the reason, Venerable Anuruddha, what is the cause, that these eight leading Mallas, having bathed their heads and dressed in new clothes, are unable to lift the Blessed One’s body, though they intend, ‘We will lift the Blessed One’s body’?” “Your intention, Vāseṭṭhas, is one way, and the intention of the devas is another.” “But what, venerable sir, is the intention of the devas?” “Your intention, Vāseṭṭhas, is this: ‘Honoring, respecting, revering, and venerating the Blessed One’s body with dances, songs, music, garlands, and perfumes, let us carry it southwards by the south of the city, and keeping outside the city, cremate the Blessed One’s body to the south of the city.’ But the intention of the devas, Vāseṭṭhas, is this: ‘Honoring, respecting, revering, and venerating the Blessed One’s body with divine dances, songs, music, garlands, and perfumes, let us carry it northwards by the north of the city, enter the city by the northern gate, proceed through the center of the city, exit by the eastern gate, and cremate the Blessed One’s body at the Mallas’ shrine named Makuṭabandhana to the east of the city.’” “Venerable sir, let it be as the devas intend.”

229. Tena kho pana samayena kusinārā yāva sandhisamalasaṃkaṭīrā jaṇṇumattena odhinā mandāravapupphehi santhatā saṇṭhitā (syā.) hoti. Atha kho devatā ca kosinārakā ca mallā bhagavato sarīraṃ dibbehi ca mānusakehi ca naccehi [P 2.0161] gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkarontā garuṃ karontā mānentā pūjentā uttarena uttaraṃ nagarassa haritvā uttarena dvārena nagaraṃ pavesetvā majjhena majjhaṃ nagarassa haritvā puratthimena dvārena nikkhamitvā puratthimato nagarassa makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ ettha ca bhagavato sarīraṃ nikkhipiṃsu.

229. At that time, Kusinārā was strewn knee-deep with mandārava flowers, even to the junctions of roads, the sewers, and the rubbish heaps. Then the devas and the Mallas of Kusinārā, honoring, respecting, revering, and venerating the Blessed One’s body with divine and human dances, songs, music, garlands, and perfumes, carried it northwards by the north of the city, entered the city by the northern gate, proceeded through the center of the city, exited by the eastern gate, and at the Mallas’ shrine named Makuṭabandhana, to the east of the city, they laid down the Blessed One’s body.

230. Atha [V 2.0121] kho kosinārakā mallā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocuṃ – “kathaṃ mayaṃ, bhante ānanda, tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjāmā”ti? “Yathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabba”nti. “Kathaṃ pana, bhante ānanda, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjantī”ti? “Rañño, vāseṭṭhā, cakkavattissa sarīraṃ ahatena vatthena veṭhenti, ahatena vatthena veṭhetvā vihatena kappāsena veṭhenti, vihatena kappāsena [T 2.0187] veṭhetvā ahatena vatthena veṭhenti. Etena upāyena pañcahi yugasatehi rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ veṭhetvā āyasāya teladoṇiyā pakkhipitvā aññissā āyasāya doṇiyā paṭikujjitvā sabbagandhānaṃ citakaṃ karitvā rañño cakkavattissa sarīraṃ jhāpenti. Cātumahāpathe rañño cakkavattissa thūpaṃ karonti[M 2.0133]. Evaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti. Yathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, rañño cakkavattissa sarīre paṭipajjanti, evaṃ tathāgatassa sarīre paṭipajjitabbaṃ. Cātumahāpathe tathāgatassa thūpo kātabbo. Tattha ye mālaṃ vā gandhaṃ vā cuṇṇakaṃ vā āropessanti vā abhivādessanti vā cittaṃ vā pasādessanti, tesaṃ taṃ bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā purise āṇāpesuṃ – “tena hi, bhaṇe, mallānaṃ vihataṃ kappāsaṃ sannipātethā”ti.

230. Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said to the Venerable Ānanda: “How, Venerable Ānanda, should we proceed with the Tathāgata’s body?” “As, Vāseṭṭhas, they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch, so should you proceed with the Tathāgata’s body.” “But how, Venerable Ānanda, do they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch?” “The body of a wheel-turning monarch, Vāseṭṭhas, is wrapped in new cloth. Having wrapped it in new cloth, they wrap it in carded cotton. Having wrapped it in carded cotton, they wrap it in new cloth. By this method, having wrapped the body of the wheel-turning monarch with five hundred pairs of cloths, they place it in a golden oil vessel, cover it with another golden vessel, build a pyre of all kinds of fragrant substances, and cremate the body of the wheel-turning monarch. A stupa is erected for the wheel-turning monarch at a major crossroads. Thus, Vāseṭṭhas, they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch. As they proceed with the body of a wheel-turning monarch, so should you proceed with the Tathāgata’s body. A stupa for the Tathāgata should be built at a major crossroads. Those who there offer garlands, perfumes, or powders, or pay homage, or gladden their minds—that will be for their long-term welfare and happiness.” Then the Mallas of Kusinārā ordered their men: “Well then, sirs, gather the Mallas’ carded cotton.”

Atha kho kosinārakā mallā bhagavato sarīraṃ ahatena vatthena veṭhetvā vihatena kappāsena veṭhesuṃ, vihatena kappāsena veṭhetvā ahatena vatthena [P 2.0162] veṭhesuṃ. Etena upāyena pañcahi yugasatehi bhagavato sarīraṃ veṭhetvā āyasāya teladoṇiyā pakkhipitvā aññissā āyasāya doṇiyā paṭikujjitvā sabbagandhānaṃ citakaṃ karitvā bhagavato sarīraṃ citakaṃ āropesuṃ.

Then the Mallas of Kusinārā wrapped the Blessed One’s body with new cloth, and having wrapped it with new cloth, they wrapped it with carded cotton. Having wrapped it with carded cotton, they wrapped it with new cloth. By this method, having wrapped the Blessed One’s body with five hundred pairs of cloths, they placed it in a golden oil vessel, covered it with another golden vessel, built a pyre of all kinds of fragrant substances, and placed the Blessed One’s body on the pyre.

Mahākassapattheravatthu

The Story of the Elder Mahākassapa

231. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahākassapo pāvāya kusināraṃ addhānamaggappaṭippanno hoti mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi [T 2.0188] bhikkhusatehi. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīdi. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro ājīvako kusinārāya mandāravapupphaṃ gahetvā pāvaṃ addhānamaggappaṭippanno hoti. Addasā kho āyasmā mahākassapo taṃ ājīvakaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ, disvā taṃ ājīvakaṃ etadavoca – “apāvuso, amhākaṃ satthāraṃ jānāsī”ti? “Āmāvuso, jānāmi, ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo. Tato me idaṃ mandāravapupphaṃ gahita”nti. Tattha ye te [V 2.0122] bhikkhū avītarāgā appekacce bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṃ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti – “atikhippaṃ bhagavā parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṃ cakkhuṃ loke antarahito”ti. Ye pana te bhikkhū vītarāgā, te satā sampajānā adhivāsenti – “aniccā saṅkhārā, taṃ kutettha labbhā”ti.

231. At that time, the Venerable Mahākassapa was traveling on the high road from Pāvā to Kusinārā with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, about five hundred in number. Then, the Venerable Mahākassapa left the road and sat down at the foot of a certain tree. At that time, a certain Ājīvaka, having taken a mandārava flower in Kusinārā, was traveling on the high road to Pāvā. The Venerable Mahākassapa saw that Ājīvaka coming from a distance, and upon seeing him, he said to that Ājīvaka, “Friend, do you know our Teacher?” “Yes, friend, I know. Today it is seven days since the ascetic Gotama attained parinibbāna. From there I have taken this mandārava flower.” There, those bhikkhus who were not free from passion, some of them, raising their arms, wept; they fell down as if cut down; they rolled forwards and backwards, crying, “Too soon has the Blessed One attained parinibbāna! Too soon has the Sugata attained parinibbāna! Too soon has the Eye of the World vanished!” But those bhikkhus who were free from passion, being mindful and fully aware, endured it, reflecting: “Conditioned phenomena are impermanent. How could it be possible to obtain that here?”

232. Tena kho pana samayena subhaddo nāma vuddhapabbajito tassaṃ parisāyaṃ nisinno hoti. Atha kho subhaddo vuddhapabbajito te [M 2.0134] bhikkhū etadavoca – “alaṃ, āvuso, mā socittha, mā paridevittha, sumuttā mayaṃ tena mahāsamaṇena. Upaddutā ca homa – ‘idaṃ vo kappati, idaṃ vo na kappatī’ti. Idāni pana mayaṃ yaṃ icchissāma, taṃ karissāma, yaṃ na icchissāma, na taṃ karissāmā”ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo [T 2.0189] bhikkhū āmantesi – “alaṃ, āvuso, mā socittha, mā paridevittha. Nanu etaṃ[P 2.0163], āvuso, bhagavatā paṭikacceva akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo’. Taṃ kutettha, āvuso, labbhā. ‘Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ tathāgatassāpi sarīraṃ mā palujjī’ti, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī”ti.

232. Now at that time, a man named Subhadda, who had gone forth in old age, was sitting in that assembly. Then Subhadda, who had gone forth in old age, said this to those bhikkhus: “Enough, friends, do not grieve, do not lament. We are well freed from that great ascetic. We were oppressed by him, who would say: ‘This is allowable for you, this is not allowable for you.’ But now we shall do what we wish, and what we do not wish, we shall not do.” Then the Venerable Mahākassapa addressed the bhikkhus: “Enough, friends, do not grieve, do not lament. Has not the Blessed One declared this from the very beginning: ‘There is difference, separation, and otherness from all that is dear and beloved’? How, friends, could it be possible to obtain that here? That which is born, has come into being, is conditioned, and is of a nature to perish—that the body of the Tathāgata should not perish is a state of affairs that does not exist.”

233. Tena kho pana samayena cattāro mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā – “mayaṃ bhagavato citakaṃ āḷimpessāmā”ti na sakkonti āḷimpetuṃ. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavocuṃ – “ko nu kho, bhante anuruddha, hetu ko paccayo, yenime cattāro mallapāmokkhā sīsaṃnhātā ahatāni vatthāni nivatthā – ‘mayaṃ bhagavato citakaṃ āḷimpessāmā’ti na sakkonti āḷimpetu”nti? “Aññathā kho, vāseṭṭhā, devatānaṃ adhippāyo”ti. “Kathaṃ pana, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo”ti? “Devatānaṃ kho, vāseṭṭhā, adhippāyo – ‘ayaṃ āyasmā mahākassapo pāvāya kusināraṃ addhānamaggappaṭippanno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Na tāva bhagavato citako pajjalissati, yāvāyasmā mahākassapo bhagavato pāde sirasā na vandissatī’”ti. “Yathā, bhante, devatānaṃ adhippāyo, tathā hotū”ti.

233. At that time, four Malla chieftains, having bathed their heads and put on new clothes, were unable to light the Blessed One’s pyre, though they intended, “We will light the Blessed One’s pyre.” Then the Mallas of Kusinārā said to the Venerable Anuruddha, “What, Venerable Anuruddha, is the reason, what is the cause, that these four Malla chieftains, having bathed their heads and put on new clothes, are unable to light the Blessed One’s pyre, though they intend, ‘We will light the Blessed One’s pyre’?” “Vāseṭṭhas, the intention of the deities is otherwise.” “But what, Venerable Sir, is the intention of the deities?” “Vāseṭṭhas, the intention of the deities is this: ‘The Venerable Mahākassapa is traveling on the high road from Pāvā to Kusinārā with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, about five hundred in number. The Blessed One’s pyre shall not ignite until the Venerable Mahākassapa has venerated the Blessed One’s feet with his head.’” “Venerable Sir, let it be as the deities intend.”

234. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo yena kusinārā makuṭabandhanaṃ nāma mallānaṃ cetiyaṃ, yena bhagavato [T 2.0190] citako tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ katvā añjaliṃ paṇāmetvā tikkhattuṃ citakaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā bhagavato pāde sirasā vandi. Tānipi kho pañcabhikkhusatāni ekaṃsaṃ cīvaraṃ katvā añjaliṃ paṇāmetvā tikkhattuṃ citakaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ katvā [V 2.0123] bhagavato pāde sirasā vandiṃsu. Vandite [P 2.0164] ca panāyasmatā mahākassapena tehi ca pañcahi bhikkhusatehi sayameva bhagavato citako pajjali.

234. Then the Venerable Mahākassapa went to the Mallas' shrine named Makuṭabandhana in Kusinārā, to where the Blessed One's pyre was. Having approached, and having arranged his robe over one shoulder, he joined his hands in homage, circumambulated the pyre three times to the right, and venerated the Blessed One's feet with his head. Those five hundred bhikkhus also, having arranged their robes over one shoulder, joined their hands in homage, circumambulated the pyre three times to the right, and venerated the Blessed One's feet with their heads. And when the Venerable Mahākassapa and those five hundred bhikkhus had venerated them, the Blessed One's pyre ignited by itself.

235. Jhāyamānassa [M 2.0135] kho pana bhagavato sarīrassa yaṃ ahosi chavīti vā cammanti vā maṃsanti vā nhārūti vā lasikāti vā, tassa neva chārikā paññāyittha, na masi; sarīrāneva avasissiṃsu. Seyyathāpi nāma sappissa vā telassa vā jhāyamānassa neva chārikā paññāyati, na masi; evameva bhagavato sarīrassa jhāyamānassa yaṃ ahosi chavīti vā cammanti vā maṃsanti vā nhārūti vā lasikāti vā, tassa neva chārikā paññāyittha, na masi; sarīrāneva avasissiṃsu. Tesañca pañcannaṃ dussayugasatānaṃ dveva dussāni na ḍayhiṃsu yañca sabbaabbhantarimaṃ yañca bāhiraṃ. Daḍḍhe ca kho pana bhagavato sarīre antalikkhā udakadhārā pātubhavitvā bhagavato citakaṃ nibbāpesi. Udakasālatopi udakaṃ sālatopi (sī. syā. kaṃ.) abbhunnamitvā bhagavato citakaṃ nibbāpesi. Kosinārakāpi mallā sabbagandhodakena bhagavato citakaṃ nibbāpesuṃ. Atha kho kosinārakā mallā bhagavato sarīrāni sattāhaṃ sandhāgāre sattipañjaraṃ karitvā dhanupākāraṃ parikkhipāpetvā [T 2.0191] parikkhipitvā (syā.) naccehi gītehi vāditehi mālehi gandhehi sakkariṃsu garuṃ kariṃsu mānesuṃ pūjesuṃ.

235. Now, of the Blessed One's body that was burning, of what was outer skin, inner skin, flesh, sinews, or synovial fluid, neither ash nor soot was perceived; only the bodily relics remained. Just as of ghee or oil that is burning, neither ash nor soot is perceived, even so, of the Blessed One's body that was burning, of what was outer skin, inner skin, flesh, sinews, or synovial fluid, neither ash nor soot was perceived; only the bodily relics remained. And of those five hundred pairs of cloths, only two cloths were not burnt: that which was the very innermost and that which was the outermost. And when the Blessed One's body had been burnt, a stream of water appeared from the sky and extinguished the Blessed One's pyre. Water also gushed forth from the sāl trees and extinguished the Blessed One's pyre. The Mallas of Kusinārā also extinguished the Blessed One's pyre with all kinds of fragrant water. Then, for seven days, the Mallas of Kusinārā, having made a cage of spears and having had it surrounded by a rampart of bows in their council hall, paid respect, paid reverence, esteemed, and made offerings to the Blessed One's bodily relics with dancing, singing, music, garlands, and perfumes.

Sarīradhātuvibhājanaṃ

The Distribution of the Bodily Relics

236. Assosi kho rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto – “bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto”ti. Atha kho rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesi – “bhagavāpi khattiyo ahampi khattiyo, ahampi arahāmi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, ahampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmī”ti.

236. The king of Magadha, Ajātasattu, son of Vedehī, heard: 'The Blessed One, it is said, has attained parinibbāna in Kusinārā.' Then the king of Magadha, Ajātasattu, son of Vedehī, sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kusinārā, saying: 'The Blessed One was of the warrior class, and I too am of the warrior class. I am worthy to receive a share of the Blessed One's bodily relics. I too will make a stūpa and hold a festival for the Blessed One's bodily relics.'

Assosuṃ kho vesālikā licchavī – “bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto”ti. Atha kho vesālikā licchavī kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – “bhagavāpi khattiyo mayampi khattiyā, mayampi arahāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ [P 2.0165] bhāgaṃ, mayampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmā”ti.

The Licchavis of Vesālī heard: 'The Blessed One, it is said, has attained parinibbāna in Kusinārā.' Then the Licchavis of Vesālī sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kusinārā, saying: 'The Blessed One was of the warrior class, and we too are of the warrior class. We are worthy to receive a share of the Blessed One's bodily relics. We too will make a stūpa and hold a festival for the Blessed One's bodily relics.'

Assosuṃ kho kapilavatthuvāsī sakyā – “bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto”ti. Atha kho kapilavatthuvāsī sakyā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ [M 2.0136] dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – “bhagavā amhākaṃ ñātiseṭṭho[V 2.0124], mayampi arahāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, mayampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmā”ti.

The Sakyans dwelling in Kapilavatthu heard: 'The Blessed One, it is said, has attained parinibbāna in Kusinārā.' Then the Sakyans dwelling in Kapilavatthu sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kusinārā, saying: 'The Blessed One is our most excellent kinsman. We are worthy to receive a share of the Blessed One's bodily relics. We too will make a stūpa and hold a festival for the Blessed One's bodily relics.'

Assosuṃ kho allakappakā bulayo thūlayo (syā.) – “bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto”ti. Atha kho allakappakā bulayo kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – “bhagavāpi khattiyo mayampi khattiyā, mayampi arahāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, mayampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmā”ti[T 2.0192].

The Bulis of Allakappa heard: 'The Blessed One, it is said, has attained parinibbāna in Kusinārā.' Then the Bulis of Allakappa sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kusinārā, saying: 'The Blessed One was of the warrior class, and we too are of the warrior class. We are worthy to receive a share of the Blessed One's bodily relics. We too will make a stūpa and hold a festival for the Blessed One's bodily relics.'

Assosuṃ kho rāmagāmakā koḷiyā – “bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto”ti. Atha kho rāmagāmakā koḷiyā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – “bhagavāpi khattiyo mayampi khattiyā, mayampi arahāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, mayampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmā”ti.

The Koḷiyas of Rāmagāma heard: 'The Blessed One, it is said, has attained parinibbāna in Kusinārā.' Then the Koḷiyas of Rāmagāma sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kusinārā, saying: 'The Blessed One was of the warrior class, and we too are of the warrior class. We are worthy to receive a share of the Blessed One's bodily relics. We too will make a stūpa and hold a festival for the Blessed One's bodily relics.'

Assosi kho veṭṭhadīpako brāhmaṇo – “bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto”ti. Atha kho veṭṭhadīpako brāhmaṇo kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesi – “bhagavāpi khattiyo ahaṃ pismi brāhmaṇo, ahampi arahāmi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, ahampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmī”ti.

The brahmin of Veṭṭhadīpa heard: 'The Blessed One, it is said, has attained parinibbāna in Kusinārā.' Then the brahmin of Veṭṭhadīpa sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kusinārā, saying: 'The Blessed One was of the warrior class, and I am a brahmin. I am worthy to receive a share of the Blessed One's bodily relics. I too will make a stūpa and hold a festival for the Blessed One's bodily relics.'

Assosuṃ kho pāveyyakā mallā – “bhagavā kira kusinārāyaṃ parinibbuto”ti. Atha kho pāveyyakā mallā kosinārakānaṃ mallānaṃ dūtaṃ pāhesuṃ – “bhagavāpi khattiyo mayampi khattiyā, mayampi arahāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāgaṃ, mayampi bhagavato sarīrānaṃ thūpañca mahañca karissāmā”ti.

The Mallas of Pāvā heard: 'The Blessed One, it is said, has attained parinibbāna in Kusinārā.' Then the Mallas of Pāvā sent a messenger to the Mallas of Kusinārā, saying: 'The Blessed One was of the warrior class, and we too are of the warrior class. We are worthy to receive a share of the Blessed One's bodily relics. We too will make a stūpa and hold a festival for the Blessed One's bodily relics.'

Evaṃ vutte kosinārakā mallā te saṅghe gaṇe etadavocuṃ – “bhagavā [P 2.0166] amhākaṃ gāmakkhette parinibbuto, na mayaṃ dassāma bhagavato sarīrānaṃ bhāga”nti.
