These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand couches—made of gold, silver, ivory, and heartwood; covered with long-haired rugs, woolen covers, embroidered spreads, and excellent antelope-hide spreads; with canopies above and red cushions at both ends. Here, O king, abandon desire; do not have longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand elephants—adorned with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with golden nets—with Uposatha, the king of elephants, as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; do not have longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand horses—adorned with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with golden nets—with Valāhaka, the king of horses, as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; do not have longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand chariots—draped with lion skins, tiger skins, leopard skins, and pale woolen blankets; adorned with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with golden nets—with the Vejayanta chariot as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; do not have longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand jewels, with the jewel-treasure as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; do not have longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand women, with Queen Subhaddā as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; do not have longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand householders, with the householder-treasure as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; do not have longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand khattiyas who are your followers, with the advisor-treasure as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; do not have longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand milk cows, yielding milk easily, with bronze milk pails. Here, O king, abandon desire; do not have longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand crores of garments—of fine linen, fine cotton, fine silk, and fine wool. Here, O king, abandon desire; do not have longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand portions of cooked rice, from which meals are brought to you morning and evening. Here, O king, abandon desire; do not have longing for life.’”

268. “Evaṃ [M 2.0158] vutte, ānanda, subhaddā devī parodi assūni pavattesi. Atha kho, ānanda, subhaddā devī assūni puñchitvā pamajjitvā (sī. syā. pī.), puñjitvā (ka.) rājānaṃ mahāsudassanaṃ etadavoca –

268. When this was said, Ānanda, Queen Subhaddā wept and shed tears. Then, Ānanda, Queen Subhaddā, wiping away her tears, said this to King Mahāsudassana:

‘Sabbeheva[V 2.0144], deva, piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo, mā kho tvaṃ, deva, sāpekkho kālamakāsi, dukkhā sāpekkhassa kālaṅkiriyā, garahitā ca sāpekkhassa kālaṅkiriyā. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti nagarasahassāni kusāvatīrājadhānippamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti pāsādasahassāni dhammapāsādappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti kūṭāgārasahassāni mahāviyūhakūṭāgārappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti pallaṅkasahassāni sovaṇṇamayāni rūpiyamayāni dantamayāni sāramayāni gonakatthatāni paṭikatthatāni paṭalikatthatāni kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇāni sauttaracchadāni ubhatolohitakūpadhānāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti nāgasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni uposathanāgarājappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te[T 2.0224], deva, caturāsīti assasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni valāhakaassarājappamukhāni[P 2.0195]. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha, jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti rathasahassāni sīhacammaparivārāni byagghacammaparivārāni dīpicammaparivārāni paṇḍukambalaparivārāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni vejayantarathappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti maṇisahassāni maṇiratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti itthisahassāni itthiratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha, jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te[M 2.0159], deva, caturāsīti gahapatisahassāni gahapatiratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti khattiyasahassāni anuyantāni pariṇāyakaratanappamukhāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti dhenusahassāni duhasandanāni kaṃsūpadhāraṇāni. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti vatthakoṭisahassāni khomasukhumānaṃ kappāsikasukhumānaṃ koseyyasukhumānaṃ kambalasukhumānaṃ. Ettha, deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsi. Imāni te, deva, caturāsīti thālipākasahassāni sāyaṃ pātaṃ bhattābhihāro abhihariyati. Ettha[T 2.0225], deva, chandaṃ pajaha jīvite apekkhaṃ mākāsī’ti.

‘O king, all that is dear and pleasing is subject to becoming different, to separation, to becoming otherwise. Do not, O king, pass away with attachment; painful is the death of one with attachment, and censured is the death of one with attachment. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand cities, with Kusāvatī the royal capital as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand palaces, with the Dhamma Palace as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand gabled mansions, with the Great Viyūha gabled mansion as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand couches—made of gold, silver, ivory, and heartwood; spread with long-fleeced rugs, woolen covers, floral-patterned spreads, and excellent antelope-hide coverings; with canopies above and red cushions at both ends. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand elephants—with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with golden nets—with Uposatha, the king of elephants, as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand horses—with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with golden nets—with Valāhaka, the king of horses, as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand chariots—draped with lion skins, tiger skins, leopard skins, and pale woolen blankets; with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with golden nets—with the Vejayanta chariot as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand jewels, with the gem-treasure as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand women, with the woman-treasure as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand householders, with the householder-treasure as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand khattiyas who are your followers, with the advisor-treasure as their chief. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand cows whose milk flows readily into bronze pails. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand crores of garments of fine linen, fine cotton, fine silk, and fine wool. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life. These, O king, are your eighty-four thousand cooking pots, from which meals are brought to you morning and evening. Here, O king, abandon desire; have no longing for life.’

Brahmalokūpagamaṃ

Going to the Brahma World

269. “Atha [V 2.0145] kho, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano nacirasseva kālamakāsi. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā manuññaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuttāvissa bhattasammado hoti, evameva kho, ānanda, rañño mahāsudassanassa [P 2.0196] māraṇantikā vedanā ahosi. Kālaṅkato ca, ānanda, rājā mahāsudassano sugatiṃ brahmalokaṃ upapajji. Rājā, ānanda, mahāsudassano caturāsīti vassasahassāni kumārakīḷaṃ kīḷitaṃ (ka.), kīḷikaṃ (sī. pī.) kīḷi. Caturāsīti vassasahassāni oparajjaṃ kāresi. Caturāsīti vassasahassāni rajjaṃ kāresi. Caturāsīti vassasahassāni gihibhūto gihībhūto (sī. pī.) dhamme pāsāde brahmacariyaṃ cari brahmacariyamacari (ka.). So cattāro brahmavihāre bhāvetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā brahmalokūpago ahosi.

269. Then, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana passed away not long after. Just as, Ānanda, a householder or a householder’s son might experience food-drowsiness after eating a delightful meal, even so, Ānanda, was the feeling of King Mahāsudassana at the point of death. And having passed away, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana was reborn in a good destination, the Brahma world. For eighty-four thousand years, Ānanda, King Mahāsudassana played the games of a prince. For eighty-four thousand years, he acted as viceroy. For eighty-four thousand years, he reigned as king. For eighty-four thousand years, living as a householder, he practiced the holy life in the Dhamma Palace. Having developed the four divine abodes, with the breakup of the body, after death, he became one who had gone to the Brahma world.

270. “Siyā kho panānanda, evamassa – ‘añño nūna tena samayena rājā mahāsudassano ahosī’ti, na kho panetaṃ, ānanda, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ahaṃ tena samayena rājā mahāsudassano ahosiṃ. Mama tāni caturāsīti nagarasahassāni kusāvatīrājadhānippamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti pāsādasahassāni dhammapāsādappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti kūṭāgārasahassāni mahāviyūhakūṭāgārappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti pallaṅkasahassāni sovaṇṇamayāni rūpiyamayāni dantamayāni sāramayāni gonakatthatāni paṭikatthatāni paṭalikatthatāni kadalimigapavarapaccattharaṇāni [T 2.0226] sauttaracchadāni [M 2.0160] ubhatolohitakūpadhānāni, mama tāni caturāsīti nāgasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni uposathanāgarājappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti assasahassāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni valāhakaassarājappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti rathasahassāni sīhacammaparivārāni [P 2.0197] byagghacammaparivārāni dīpicammaparivārāni paṇḍukambalaparivārāni sovaṇṇālaṅkārāni sovaṇṇadhajāni hemajālapaṭicchannāni vejayantarathappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti maṇisahassāni maṇiratanappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti itthisahassāni subhaddādevippamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti gahapatisahassāni gahapatiratanappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti khattiyasahassāni anuyantāni pariṇāyakaratanappamukhāni, mama tāni caturāsīti dhenusahassāni duhasandanāni kaṃsūpadhāraṇāni, mama tāni caturāsīti vatthakoṭisahassāni khomasukhumānaṃ kappāsikasukhumānaṃ koseyyasukhumānaṃ kambalasukhumānaṃ, mama tāni caturāsīti thālipākasahassāni sāyaṃ pātaṃ bhattābhihāro abhihariyittha.

270. “Indeed, Ānanda, it might occur to you: ‘Surely, at that time, King Mahāsudassana was someone else.’ But, Ānanda, it should not be regarded so. I myself was King Mahāsudassana at that time. Those eighty-four thousand cities, with the royal capital Kusāvatī as the foremost, were mine. Those eighty-four thousand palaces, with the Dhamma Palace as the foremost, were mine. Those eighty-four thousand gabled mansions, with the Great Hall of Variety as the foremost, were mine. Those eighty-four thousand couches—made of gold, silver, ivory, and heartwood; spread with long-fleeced coverlets, white woolen coverlets, woolen coverlets with floral embroidery, and choice rugs of antelope hide; with canopies above and red cushions at both ends—were mine. Those eighty-four thousand elephants—adorned with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with golden nets, with Uposatha, the elephant king, as the foremost—were mine. Those eighty-four thousand horses—adorned with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with golden nets, with Valāhaka, the horse king, as the foremost—were mine. Those eighty-four thousand chariots—furnished with lion skins, tiger skins, leopard skins, and pale woolen blankets; adorned with gold ornaments and gold banners, covered with golden nets, with the Vejayanta chariot as the foremost—were mine. Those eighty-four thousand jewels, with the jewel-treasure as the foremost, were mine. Those eighty-four thousand women, with Queen Subhaddā as the foremost, were mine. Those eighty-four thousand householders, with the householder-treasure as the foremost, were mine. Those eighty-four thousand nobles, who were followers, with the counselor-treasure as the foremost, were mine. Those eighty-four thousand cows, with milk that flowed freely into bronze pails held underneath, were mine. Those eighty-four thousand koṭis of cloths—of fine linen, fine cotton, fine silk, and fine wool—were mine. Those eighty-four thousand pots of cooked rice were mine, from which a meal was brought morning and evening.”

271. “Tesaṃ [V 2.0146] kho panānanda, caturāsītinagarasahassānaṃ ekaññeva taṃ nagaraṃ hoti, yaṃ tena samayena ajjhāvasāmi yadidaṃ kusāvatī rājadhānī. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītipāsādasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so pāsādo hoti, yaṃ tena samayena [T 2.0227] ajjhāvasāmi yadidaṃ dhammo pāsādo. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītikūṭāgārasahassānaṃ ekaññeva taṃ kūṭāgāraṃ hoti, yaṃ tena samayena ajjhāvasāmi yadidaṃ mahāviyūhaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītipallaṅkasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so pallaṅko hoti, yaṃ tena samayena paribhuñjāmi yadidaṃ sovaṇṇamayo vā rūpiyamayo vā dantamayo vā sāramayo vā. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītināgasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so nāgo hoti, yaṃ tena samayena abhiruhāmi yadidaṃ uposatho nāgarājā. Tesaṃ [P 2.0198] kho panānanda, caturāsītiassasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so asso hoti, yaṃ tena samayena abhiruhāmi yadidaṃ valāhako assarājā. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītirathasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so ratho hoti, yaṃ tena samayena abhiruhāmi yadidaṃ vejayantaratho. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītiitthisahassānaṃ ekāyeva [M 2.0161] sā itthī hoti, yā tena samayena paccupaṭṭhāti khattiyānī vā vessinī vessāyinī (syā.), velāmikānī (ka. sī. pī.) velāmikā (saṃ. ni. 3.96) vā. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, vā. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītivatthakoṭisahassānaṃ ekaṃyeva taṃ dussayugaṃ hoti, yaṃ tena samayena paridahāmi khomasukhumaṃ vā kappāsikasukhumaṃ vā koseyyasukhumaṃ vā kambalasukhumaṃ vā. Tesaṃ kho panānanda, caturāsītithālipākasahassānaṃ ekoyeva so thālipāko hoti, yato nāḷikodanaparamaṃ bhuñjāmi tadupiyañca sūpeyyaṃ.

271. “And, Ānanda, of those eighty-four thousand cities, there was only one city where I dwelt at that time, that is, the royal capital Kusāvatī. Of those eighty-four thousand palaces, there was only one palace where I dwelt at that time, that is, the Dhamma Palace. Of those eighty-four thousand gabled mansions, there was only one gabled mansion where I dwelt at that time, that is, the Great Hall of Variety. Of those eighty-four thousand couches, there was only one couch that I used at that time, that is, one made of gold, or silver, or ivory, or heartwood. Of those eighty-four thousand elephants, there was only one elephant that I mounted at that time, that is, Uposatha, the elephant king. Of those eighty-four thousand horses, there was only one horse that I mounted at that time, that is, Valāhaka, the horse king. Of those eighty-four thousand chariots, there was only one chariot that I rode at that time, that is, the Vejayanta chariot. Of those eighty-four thousand women, there was only one woman who attended me at that time, whether a noblewoman or a woman of the merchant caste. Of those eighty-four thousand koṭis of cloths, there was only one set of garments that I wore at that time, whether of fine linen, fine cotton, fine silk, or fine wool. Of those eighty-four thousand pots of cooked rice, there was only one pot of cooked rice from which I ate, at most a measure of one nāḷikā of rice and a suitable curry.”

272. “Passānanda, sabbete saṅkhārā atītā niruddhā vipariṇatā. Evaṃ aniccā kho, ānanda, saṅkhārā; evaṃ addhuvā kho, ānanda, saṅkhārā; evaṃ anassāsikā kho, ānanda, saṅkhārā! Yāvañcidaṃ, ānanda[T 2.0228], alameva sabbasaṅkhāresu nibbindituṃ, alaṃ virajjituṃ, alaṃ vimuccituṃ.

272. “See, Ānanda, all those formations have passed, ceased, and altered. Thus, Ānanda, are formations impermanent; thus, Ānanda, are formations not lasting; thus, Ānanda, are formations no solace! To such an extent, Ānanda, it is enough to become disenchanted with all formations, enough to become dispassionate, enough to be liberated.”

“Chakkhattuṃ kho panāhaṃ, ānanda, abhijānāmi imasmiṃ padese sarīraṃ nikkhipitaṃ, tañca kho rājāva samāno cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyapatto sattaratanasamannāgato, ayaṃ sattamo sarīranikkhepo. Na kho panāhaṃ, ānanda, taṃ padesaṃ samanupassāmi sadevake loke samārake [P 2.0199] sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya yattha tathāgato aṭṭhamaṃ sarīraṃ nikkhipeyyā”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

“Six times, Ānanda, I recall having laid down my body in this very place—and on each occasion as a king, a wheel-turning monarch, righteous, a king of Dhamma, conqueror of the four quarters, victorious, who had attained stability in the country, and was endowed with the seven treasures. This is the seventh laying down of the body. But, Ānanda, I do not see any place in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, where the Tathāgata would lay down his body an eighth time.” The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, then spoke further:

“Aniccā [V 2.0147] vata saṅkhārā, uppādavayadhammino;

Uppajjitvā nirujjhanti, tesaṃ vūpasamo sukho”ti.

“Impermanent, alas, are formations; their nature is to arise and pass away. Having arisen, they cease; their stilling is bliss.”

Mahāsudassanasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Mahāsudassana Sutta, the fourth, is concluded.

5. Janavasabhasuttaṃ

5. The Janavasabha Sutta

Nātikiyādibyākaraṇaṃ

The Exposition of Predictions Concerning the People of Nātikā and Others

273. Evaṃ [T 2.0229][M 2.0162][V 2.0148][P 2.0200] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā nātike nādike (sī. syā. pī.) viharati giñjakāvasathe. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā parito parito janapadesu paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti kāsikosalesu vajjimallesu cetivaṃsesu cetiyavaṃsesu (ka.) kurupañcālesu majjhasūrasenesu macchasurasenesu (syā.), macchasūrasenesu (sī. pī.) – “asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno upapannoti (ka.). Paropaññāsa nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sādhikā navuti nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino, sakideva sakiṃdeva (ka.) imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Sātirekāni pañcasatāni nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti.

273. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Nātika in the Brick Hall. At that time, the Blessed One was declaring the rebirths of the attendants who had passed away, in the various surrounding provinces—in Kāsi and Kosala, in Vajji and Malla, in Ceti and Vaṃsa, in Kuru and Pañcāla, and in Majjha and Sūrasena—saying, “Such-and-such a person has been reborn there, such-and-such a person has been reborn there.” More than fifty attendants from Nātika who have passed away, with the destruction of the five lower fetters, have been reborn spontaneously; there they will attain final Nibbāna, not being of a nature to return from that world. More than ninety attendants from Nātika who have passed away, with the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, have become once-returners; returning to this world just once, they will make an end of suffering. More than five hundred attendants from Nātika who have passed away, with the destruction of the three fetters, have become stream-enterers, not of a nature to fall into a state of woe, assured, with enlightenment as their destination.

274. Assosuṃ [P 2.0201] kho nātikiyā paricārakā – “bhagavā kira parito parito janapadesu paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti kāsikosalesu vajjimallesu cetivaṃsesu kurupañcālesu majjhasūrasenesu – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno. Paropaññāsa nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā [T 2.0230] opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sādhikā navuti nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Sātirekāni pañcasatāni nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā [M 2.0163] sotāpannā [V 2.0149] avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti. Tena ca nātikiyā paricārakā attamanā ahesuṃ pamuditā [T 2.0231] pītisomanassajātā bhagavato pañhaveyyākaraṇaṃ pañhāveyyākaraṇaṃ (syā. ka.) sutvā.

274. The attendants of Nātika heard: “It is said that the Blessed One is declaring the rebirths of the attendants who have passed away, in the various surrounding provinces—in Kāsi and Kosala, in Vajji and Malla, in Ceti and Vaṃsa, in Kuru and Pañcāla, and in Majjha and Sūrasena—saying, ‘Such-and-such a person has been reborn there, such-and-such a person has been reborn there.’ More than fifty attendants from Nātika who have passed away, with the destruction of the five lower fetters, have been reborn spontaneously; there they will attain final Nibbāna, not being of a nature to return from that world. More than ninety attendants from Nātika who have passed away, with the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, have become once-returners; returning to this world just once, they will make an end of suffering. More than five hundred attendants from Nātika who have passed away, with the destruction of the three fetters, have become stream-enterers, not of a nature to fall into a state of woe, assured, with enlightenment as their destination.” And so, having heard the Blessed One’s explanation, the attendants of Nātika were pleased, delighted, and became joyful and glad.

275. Assosi kho āyasmā ānando – “bhagavā kira parito parito janapadesu paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti kāsikosalesu vajjimallesu cetivaṃsesu kurupañcālesu majjhasūrasenesu – ‘asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno. Paropaññāsa nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sādhikā navuti nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Sātirekāni pañcasatāni nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti. Tena ca nātikiyā paricārakā attamanā ahesuṃ pamuditā pītisomanassajātā bhagavato pañhaveyyākaraṇaṃ sutvā”ti.

275. The Venerable Ānanda heard: “It is said that the Blessed One is declaring the rebirths of the attendants who have passed away, in the various surrounding provinces—in Kāsi and Kosala, in Vajji and Malla, in Ceti and Vaṃsa, in Kuru and Pañcāla, and in Majjha and Sūrasena—saying, ‘Such-and-such a person has been reborn there, such-and-such a person has been reborn there.’ More than fifty attendants from Nātika who have passed away, with the destruction of the five lower fetters, have been reborn spontaneously; there they will attain final Nibbāna, not being of a nature to return from that world. More than ninety attendants from Nātika who have passed away, with the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, have become once-returners; returning to this world just once, they will make an end of suffering. More than five hundred attendants from Nātika who have passed away, with the destruction of the three fetters, have become stream-enterers, not of a nature to fall into a state of woe, assured, with enlightenment as their destination. And so, having heard the Blessed One’s explanation, the attendants of Nātika were pleased, delighted, and became joyful and glad.”

Ānandaparikathā

Ānanda's Deliberation

276. Atha kho āyasmato ānandassa etadahosi – “ime kho [P 2.0202] panāpi ahesuṃ māgadhakā paricārakā bahū ceva rattaññū ca abbhatītā kālaṅkatā. Suññā maññe aṅgamagadhā aṅgamāgadhakehi aṅgamāgadhikehi (syā.) paricārakehi abbhatītehi kālaṅkatehi. Te kho panāpi tena kho panāpi (syā.) ahesuṃ buddhe pasannā dhamme pasannā saṅghe pasannā sīlesu paripūrakārino. Te abbhatītā kālaṅkatā bhagavatā abyākatā; tesampissa sādhu veyyākaraṇaṃ, bahujano pasīdeyya, tato gaccheyya sugatiṃ. Ayaṃ kho panāpi ahosi rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro dhammiko dhammarājā hito brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ negamānañceva jānapadānañca. Apissudaṃ manussā kittayamānarūpā viharanti – ‘evaṃ no so dhammiko dhammarājā sukhāpetvā [M 2.0164] kālaṅkato, evaṃ mayaṃ tassa dhammikassa dhammarañño vijite phāsu phāsukaṃ (syā.) viharimhā’ti. So kho panāpi ahosi buddhe pasanno dhamme pasanno saṅghe pasanno sīlesu paripūrakārī. Apissudaṃ manussā evamāhaṃsu – ‘yāva maraṇakālāpi rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro bhagavantaṃ kittayamānarūpo kālaṅkato’ti. So abbhatīto kālaṅkato bhagavatā abyākato. Tassapissa sādhu veyyākaraṇaṃ bahujano pasīdeyya, tato gaccheyya sugatiṃ. Bhagavato kho pana sambodhi magadhesu. Yattha kho pana bhagavato sambodhi magadhesu, kathaṃ tatra bhagavā [T 2.0232] māgadhake paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu [V 2.0150] na byākareyya. Bhagavā ce kho pana māgadhake paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu na byākareyya, dīnamanā ninnamanā (syā.), dīnamānā (sī. pī.) tenassu māgadhakā paricārakā; yena kho [P 2.0203] panassu dīnamanā māgadhakā paricārakā kathaṃ te bhagavā na byākareyyā”ti?

276. Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Ānanda: “These Magadhan attendants were many and of long standing, and they have passed away. Aṅga and Magadha seem empty now that the Aṅga-Magadhan attendants have passed away. They too were confident in the Buddha, confident in the Dhamma, confident in the Saṅgha, and were fulfillers of the precepts. They have passed away, but have not been declared by the Blessed One. It would be good if there were a declaration concerning them; many people would gain confidence and thereby go to a good destination. And this King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha was a righteous king, a king of Dhamma, beneficial to brahmins and householders, and to the townspeople and country folk. People still praise him, saying: ‘Thus did that righteous king of Dhamma pass away after making us happy; thus did we dwell at ease in the realm of that righteous king of Dhamma.’ He too was confident in the Buddha, confident in the Dhamma, confident in the Saṅgha, and was a fulfiller of the precepts. People even say: ‘King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha passed away while praising the Blessed One, even up to the time of his death.’ He has passed away, but has not been declared by the Blessed One. It would be good if there were a declaration concerning him; many people would gain confidence and thereby go to a good destination. Moreover, the Blessed One’s full awakening was in Magadha. Since the Blessed One’s full awakening was in Magadha, how could the Blessed One not declare the rebirths of the Magadhan attendants who have passed away? If the Blessed One were not to declare the rebirths of the Magadhan attendants who have passed away, the Magadhan attendants would be disheartened. And if the Magadhan attendants were to be disheartened, how could the Blessed One not declare them?”

277. Idamāyasmā ānando māgadhake paricārake ārabbha eko raho anuvicintetvā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante – ‘bhagavā kira parito parito janapadesu paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu byākaroti kāsikosalesu vajjimallesu cetivaṃsesu kurupañcālesu majjhasūrasenesu – “asu amutra upapanno, asu amutra upapanno. Paropaññāsa nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sādhikā navuti nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Sātirekāni pañcasatāni nātikiyā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā [T 2.0233] avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇāti. Tena ca nātikiyā paricārakā attamanā ahesuṃ pamuditā pītisomanassajātā bhagavato pañhaveyyākaraṇaṃ sutvā”ti[M 2.0165]. Ime kho panāpi, bhante, ahesuṃ māgadhakā paricārakā bahū ceva rattaññū ca abbhatītā kālaṅkatā. Suññā maññe aṅgamagadhā aṅgamāgadhakehi paricārakehi abbhatītehi kālaṅkatehi. Te kho panāpi, bhante, ahesuṃ buddhe pasannā dhamme pasannā saṅghe pasannā sīlesu paripūrakārino, te abbhatītā kālaṅkatā bhagavatā abyākatā. Tesampissa sādhu veyyākaraṇaṃ, bahujano pasīdeyya, tato gaccheyya sugatiṃ. Ayaṃ kho panāpi, bhante, ahosi rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro dhammiko dhammarājā hito brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ negamānañceva [P 2.0204] jānapadānañca. Apissudaṃ manussā kittayamānarūpā viharanti – ‘evaṃ no so dhammiko dhammarājā sukhāpetvā kālaṅkato. Evaṃ mayaṃ tassa dhammikassa dhammarañño vijite phāsu viharimhā’ti. So kho panāpi, bhante, ahosi buddhe pasanno dhamme pasanno saṅghe pasanno sīlesu paripūrakārī. Apissudaṃ manussā evamāhaṃsu – ‘yāva maraṇakālāpi rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro bhagavantaṃ kittayamānarūpo kālaṅkato’ti. So abbhatīto kālaṅkato bhagavatā abyākato; tassapissa sādhu veyyākaraṇaṃ, bahujano pasīdeyya, tato gaccheyya sugatiṃ. Bhagavato kho pana, bhante, sambodhi magadhesu. Yattha kho pana[T 2.0234], bhante, bhagavato sambodhi magadhesu, kathaṃ tatra bhagavā māgadhake paricārake abbhatīte [V 2.0151] kālaṅkate upapattīsu na byākareyya? Bhagavā ce kho pana, bhante, māgadhake paricārake abbhatīte kālaṅkate upapattīsu na byākareyya dīnamanā tenassu māgadhakā paricārakā; yena kho panassu dīnamanā māgadhakā paricārakā kathaṃ te bhagavā na byākareyyā”ti. Idamāyasmā ānando māgadhake paricārake ārabbha bhagavato sammukhā parikathaṃ katvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

277. The Venerable Ānanda, having reflected on the Magadhan attendants alone in a secluded place, rose at dawn and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I have heard this: ‘The Blessed One, it is said, declares the rebirths of attendants who have passed on and died in the surrounding regions—in Kāsi and Kosala, in Vajji and Malla, in Ceti and Vaṃsa, in Kuru and Pañcāla, and in Majjha and Sūrasena—stating, “This one was reborn here, that one was reborn there.” More than fifty Nātika attendants who have passed on and died, with the destruction of the five lower fetters, are of spontaneous birth, will attain final Nibbāna there, and are not liable to return from that world. More than ninety Nātika attendants who have passed on and died, with the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of lust, hatred, and delusion, are once-returners who, having come to this world only once more, will make an end of suffering. Over five hundred Nātika attendants who have passed on and died, with the destruction of the three fetters, are stream-enterers, not liable to fall into states of deprivation, are assured, and have enlightenment as their destination.’ And those Nātika attendants were pleased, joyful, and filled with gladness upon hearing the Blessed One’s explanation. But, venerable sir, there were also these Magadhan attendants, many of whom were of long standing, who have passed on and died. I think Aṅga and Magadha are as if empty of those departed Aṅgan and Magadhan attendants. Those attendants, venerable sir, had faith in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha, and were fulfillers of the precepts. They have passed on and died, yet have not been declared by the Blessed One. It would be good if there were an explanation about them too; many people would gain faith, and thereby go to a good destination. Moreover, venerable sir, there was this King of Magadha, Seniya Bimbisāra, a righteous king, a king of righteousness, who was a benefactor to brahmins and householders, and to townspeople and country-dwellers. People still dwell praising him, saying: ‘That righteous king, that king of righteousness, made us happy before he died. We lived in comfort in the realm of that righteous king.’ He too, venerable sir, had faith in the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha, and was a fulfiller of the precepts. People even said this: ‘Even up to the time of his death, King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha died while praising the Blessed One.’ He has passed on and died, yet has not been declared by the Blessed One. It would be good if there were an explanation about him too; many people would gain faith, and thereby go to a good destination. Furthermore, venerable sir, the Blessed One's full awakening was in Magadha. Since, venerable sir, the Blessed One’s full awakening was in Magadha, how is it that the Blessed One would not declare the rebirths of the Magadhan attendants who have passed on and died there? If, venerable sir, the Blessed One were not to declare the rebirths of the Magadhan attendants who have passed on and died, the Magadhan attendants would be disheartened by that. Since the Magadhan attendants would be disheartened, how could the Blessed One not declare them?” Having made this circumlocutory speech concerning the Magadhan attendants in the presence of the Blessed One, the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him to the right, and departed.

278. Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkante āyasmante ānande pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya nātikaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Nātike piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto pāde pakkhāletvā giñjakāvasathaṃ pavisitvā māgadhake paricārake ārabbha aṭṭhiṃ katvā aṭṭhikatvā (sī. syā. pī.) manasikatvā sabbaṃ cetasā sabbacetasā (pī.) samannāharitvā paññatte āsane [M 2.0166] nisīdi – “gatiṃ nesaṃ jānissāmi abhisamparāyaṃ, yaṃgatikā te bhavanto yaṃabhisamparāyā”ti. Addasā kho bhagavā māgadhake paricārake “yaṃgatikā te bhavanto [P 2.0205] yaṃabhisamparāyā”ti. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito giñjakāvasathā nikkhamitvā vihārapacchāyāyaṃ paññatte āsane nisīdi.

278. Then, not long after the Venerable Ānanda had departed, the Blessed One, in the morning, dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Nātika for alms. Having wandered for alms in Nātika, after the meal, on returning from the alms-round, he washed his feet, entered the brick hall, and concerning the Magadhan attendants, having made it a matter of importance, having brought them to mind, and having comprehended it all with his mind, he sat down on the prepared seat, thinking: “I shall know their destination, their future life—what destination these venerable ones have, what future life they have.” The Blessed One indeed saw of the Magadhan attendants what their destination was and what their future life was. Then, in the evening, the Blessed One, having arisen from seclusion, left the brick hall and sat down on the prepared seat in the shade of the monastery.

279. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno [T 2.0235] kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “upasantapadisso upasantapatiso (ka.) bhante bhagavā bhātiriva bhagavato mukhavaṇṇo vippasannattā indriyānaṃ. Santena nūnajja bhante bhagavā vihārena vihāsī”ti? “Yadeva kho me tvaṃ, ānanda, māgadhake paricārake ārabbha sammukhā parikathaṃ katvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkanto, tadevāhaṃ nātike piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto pāde pakkhāletvā giñjakāvasathaṃ pavisitvā māgadhake paricārake ārabbha aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasikatvā sabbaṃ cetasā samannāharitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṃ – ‘gatiṃ nesaṃ jānissāmi abhisamparāyaṃ, yaṃgatikā te bhavanto yaṃabhisamparāyā’ti. Addasaṃ kho ahaṃ, ānanda, māgadhake paricārake ‘yaṃgatikā te bhavanto yaṃabhisamparāyā’”ti.

279. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, the Blessed One’s appearance is serene, and the color of the Blessed One’s face shines exceedingly due to the special clarity of his faculties. Surely today, Venerable Sir, the Blessed One has been abiding in a peaceful abiding?” “Ānanda, regarding the very discussion you had with me face to face concerning the Magadhan devotees, after which you rose from your seat and departed—after that, I went for alms in Nātika. After the meal, on returning from the alms-round, I washed my feet, entered the brick hall, and concerning the Magadhan devotees, giving attention, bringing it to mind, and contemplating it all with my mind, I sat down on the prepared seat, thinking: ‘I shall know their destination and future state—what destination those venerable ones have, what future state they have.’ And indeed, Ānanda, I saw of the Magadhan devotees what their destination is and what their future state is.”

Janavasabhayakkho

Janavasabha the Yakkha

280. “Atha kho, ānanda, antarahito yakkho saddamanussāvesi – ‘janavasabho ahaṃ bhagavā[V 2.0152]; janavasabho ahaṃ sugatā’ti. Abhijānāsi no tvaṃ, ānanda, ito pubbe evarūpaṃ nāmadheyyaṃ sutaṃ sutvā (pī.) yadidaṃ janavasabho”ti?

280. “Then, Ānanda, an invisible yakkha made a sound heard, saying: ‘I am Janavasabha, Blessed One; I am Janavasabha, Well-Gone One.’ Do you recall, Ānanda, having heard before this time such a name as Janavasabha?”

“Na kho ahaṃ, bhante, abhijānāmi ito pubbe evarūpaṃ nāmadheyyaṃ sutaṃ yadidaṃ janavasabhoti, api ca me, bhante, lomāni haṭṭhāni ‘janavasabho’ti nāmadheyyaṃ sutvā. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – ‘na hi [P 2.0206] nūna so orako yakkho bhavissati yadidaṃ evarūpaṃ nāmadheyyaṃ supaññattaṃ yadidaṃ janavasabho”ti. “Anantarā kho, ānanda, saddapātubhāvā uḷāravaṇṇo [M 2.0167] me yakkho sammukhe pāturahosi[T 2.0236]. Dutiyampi saddamanussāvesi – ‘bimbisāro ahaṃ bhagavā; bimbisāro ahaṃ sugatāti. Idaṃ sattamaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, vessavaṇassa mahārājassa sahabyataṃ upapajjāmi, so tato cuto manussarājā bhavituṃ pahomi so tato cuto manussarājā, amanussarājā divi homi (sī. pī.).

“Indeed, Venerable Sir, I do not recall having heard before this time such a name as ‘Janavasabha.’ But, Venerable Sir, upon hearing the name ‘Janavasabha,’ my hairs stood on end. Then, Venerable Sir, this thought occurred to me: ‘Surely that yakkha will not be an inferior one, for such a name as “Janavasabha” is so well-designated!’” “Immediately after the appearance of the sound, Ānanda, a yakkha of splendid complexion appeared before me. A second time, he made a sound heard, saying: ‘I am Bimbisāra, Blessed One; I am Bimbisāra, Well-Gone One. This is the seventh time, Venerable Sir, that I have been reborn into the companionship of the great king Vessavaṇa. Having passed away from there, I am able to become a human king.”

Ito satta tato satta, saṃsārāni catuddasa;

Nivāsamabhijānāmi, yattha me vusitaṃ pure.

“Seven from here, seven from there—fourteen rounds of existence; I recollect the dwelling where I have lived before.”

281. ‘Dīgharattaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, avinipāto avinipātaṃ sañjānāmi, āsā ca pana me santiṭṭhati sakadāgāmitāyā’ti. ‘Acchariyamidaṃ āyasmato janavasabhassa yakkhassa, abbhutamidaṃ āyasmato janavasabhassa yakkhassa. “Dīgharattaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, avinipāto avinipātaṃ sañjānāmī”ti ca vadesi, “āsā ca pana me santiṭṭhati sakadāgāmitāyā”ti ca vadesi, kutonidānaṃ panāyasmā janavasabho yakkho evarūpaṃ uḷāraṃ visesādhigamaṃ sañjānātīti? Na aññatra, bhagavā, tava sāsanā, na aññatra aññattha (sī. pī.), sugata, tava sāsanā; yadagge ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati ekantikato ekantato (syā.), ekantagato (pī.) abhippasanno, tadagge ahaṃ, bhante, dīgharattaṃ [P 2.0207] avinipāto avinipātaṃ sañjānāmi, āsā ca pana me santiṭṭhati sakadāgāmitāya. Idhāhaṃ, bhante, vessavaṇena mahārājena pesito virūḷhakassa mahārājassa santike kenacideva karaṇīyena addasaṃ bhagavantaṃ antarāmagge giñjakāvasathaṃ [T 2.0237] pavisitvā māgadhake paricārake ārabbha aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasikatvā sabbaṃ cetasā samannāharitvā nisinnaṃ – “gatiṃ nesaṃ jānissāmi abhisamparāyaṃ, yaṃgatikā te bhavanto yaṃabhisamparāyā”ti. Anacchariyaṃ kho panetaṃ, bhante, yaṃ vessavaṇassa mahārājassa tassaṃ parisāyaṃ bhāsato sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – “yaṃgatikā te bhavanto yaṃabhisamparāyā”ti. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, etadahosi – bhagavantañca dakkhāmi, idañca bhagavato ārocessāmīti. Ime kho me, bhante, dvepaccayā bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ’.

281. “For a long time, Venerable Sir, I have been one not destined for downfall, and I know this state of being not destined for downfall. And my hope for once-returning is established.” “This is wonderful, Venerable Janavasabha the yakkha, this is amazing, Venerable Janavasabha the yakkha, that you say, ‘For a long time, Venerable Sir, I have been one not destined for downfall, and I know this state of being not destined for downfall,’ and also say, ‘And my hope for once-returning is established.’ From what cause, Venerable Janavasabha the yakkha, do you know such an eminent, special attainment?” “Not apart from your teaching, Blessed One; not apart from your teaching, Well-Gone One. From the time, Venerable Sir, that I had unwavering and special faith in the Blessed One, from that time on, Venerable Sir, for a long time I have been one not destined for downfall, and I know this state of being not destined for downfall. And my hope for once-returning is established. Just now, Venerable Sir, I was sent by the great king Vessavaṇa on some business to the great king Virūḷhaka. On the way, I saw the Blessed One entering the brick hall and sitting down, concerning the Magadhan devotees, giving attention, bringing it to mind, and contemplating it all with his mind, thinking: ‘I shall know their destination and future state—what destination those venerable ones have, what future state they have.’ It is indeed wonderful, Venerable Sir, that what was spoken by the great king Vessavaṇa in that assembly was heard face-to-face and received face-to-face: ‘what destination those venerable ones have, what future state they have.’ Then, Venerable Sir, this thought occurred to me: ‘I will see the Blessed One and report this to the Blessed One.’ These, Venerable Sir, are the two reasons for my approaching to see the Blessed One.”

Devasabhā

The Assembly of the Devas

282. ‘Purimāni[M 2.0168][V 2.0153], bhante, divasāni purimatarāni tadahuposathe pannarase vassūpanāyikāya puṇṇāya puṇṇamāya rattiyā kevalakappā ca devā tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā. Mahatī ca dibbaparisā dibbā parisā (sī. pī.) samantato nisinnā honti nisinnā hoti (sī.), sannisinnā honti sannipatitā (ka.), cattāro ca mahārājāno catuddisā nisinnā honti. Puratthimāya disāya dhataraṭṭho mahārājā pacchimābhimukho pacchābhimukho (ka.) nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; dakkhiṇāya disāya virūḷhako mahārājā uttarābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; pacchimāya disāya virūpakkho mahārājā puratthābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; uttarāya disāya vessavaṇo mahārājā dakkhiṇābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā[P 2.0208]. Yadā, bhante, kevalakappā ca devā tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā, mahatī ca dibbaparisā samantato nisinnā honti, cattāro ca mahārājāno catuddisā nisinnā [T 2.0238] honti. Idaṃ nesaṃ hoti āsanasmiṃ; atha pacchā amhākaṃ āsanaṃ hoti. Ye te, bhante, devā bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ caritvā adhunūpapannā tāvatiṃsakāyaṃ, te aññe deve atirocanti vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Tena sudaṃ, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā attamanā honti pamuditā pītisomanassajātā “dibbā vata bho kāyā paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyā”ti. Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sampasādaṃ viditvā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

282. “Venerable sir, on former days, on days even more former, on the fifteenth Uposatha day, on the night of the full moon at the time of entering the Rains-residence, all the devas of Tāvatiṃsa were seated and assembled together in the Sudhammā assembly hall. A great divine assembly was seated all around, and the four Great Kings were seated in the four directions. In the eastern direction, Dhataraṭṭha the Great King was seated facing west, with the devas before him. In the southern direction, Virūḷhaka the Great King was seated facing north, with the devas before him. In the western direction, Virūpakkha the Great King was seated facing east, with the devas before him. In the northern direction, Vessavaṇa the Great King was seated facing south, with the devas before him. When, venerable sir, all the devas of Tāvatiṃsa were seated and assembled together in the Sudhammā assembly hall, and the great divine assembly was seated all around, and the four Great Kings were seated in the four directions, this is their seating; only afterwards is our seating. Venerable sir, those devas who, having practiced the holy life under the Blessed One, have recently been reborn into the Tāvatiṃsa host, they outshine the other devas in both complexion and glory. Because of this, venerable sir, the Tāvatiṃsa devas are pleased, joyful, and filled with rapture and gladness, thinking: ‘Sirs, the divine hosts are indeed being filled, while the asura hosts are declining!’ Then, venerable sir, Sakka, lord of the devas, knowing the great satisfaction of the Tāvatiṃsa devas, rejoiced with these verses:”

“Modanti vata bho devā, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā saindakā (sī.);

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammataṃ.

“Sirs, the Tāvatiṃsa devas, together with their Indra, truly rejoice, paying homage to the Tathāgata and to the excellent nature of the Dhamma.

Nave deve ca passantā, vaṇṇavante yasassine yasassino (syā.);

Sugatasmiṃ brahmacariyaṃ, caritvāna idhāgate.

And seeing the new devas who have come here, possessed of beauty and glory, after having practiced the holy life under the Sugata.

Te aññe atirocanti, vaṇṇena yasasāyunā;

Sāvakā bhūripaññassa, visesūpagatā idha.

They, the disciples of the one with extensive wisdom, having attained distinction here, outshine the others in complexion, glory, and lifespan.

Idaṃ [M 2.0169] disvāna nandanti, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammata”nti.

Seeing this, the Tāvatiṃsa devas, together with their Indra, rejoice, paying homage to the Tathāgata and to the excellent nature of the Dhamma.”

‘Tena [V 2.0154][P 2.0209] sudaṃ, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā bhiyyosomattāya attamanā honti pamuditā pītisomanassajātā “dibbā vata, bho, kāyā paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyā”ti. Atha kho, bhante, yenatthena devā tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā, taṃ atthaṃ cintayitvā taṃ atthaṃ mantayitvā vuttavacanāpi taṃ vuttavacanā nāmidaṃ (ka.) cattāro mahārājāno [T 2.0239] tasmiṃ atthe honti. Paccānusiṭṭhavacanāpi taṃ paccānusiṭṭhavacanā nāmidaṃ (ka.) cattāro mahārājāno tasmiṃ atthe honti, sakesu sakesu āsanesu ṭhitā avipakkantā adhipakkantā (ka.).

“Because of this, venerable sir, the Tāvatiṃsa devas were, to an even greater degree, pleased, joyful, and filled with rapture and gladness, thinking: ‘Sirs, the divine hosts are indeed being filled, while the asura hosts are declining!’ Then, venerable sir, for whatever purpose the Tāvatiṃsa devas were seated and assembled together in the Sudhammā assembly hall, having considered that matter and consulted on that matter, the four Great Kings have been instructed and advised regarding it. They stand at their own respective seats, not having departed.

Te vuttavākyā rājāno, paṭiggayhānusāsaniṃ;

Vippasannamanā santā, aṭṭhaṃsu samhi āsaneti.

Those kings, having been addressed and having accepted the instruction, stood at their own seats with serene and peaceful minds.

283. ‘Atha kho, bhante, uttarāya disāya uḷāro āloko sañjāyi, obhāso pāturahosi atikkammeva devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ. Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – “yathā kho, mārisā, nimittāni dissanti, uḷāro āloko sañjāyati, obhāso pātubhavati, brahmā pātubhavissati. Brahmuno hetaṃ pubbanimittaṃ pātubhāvāya yadidaṃ āloko sañjāyati obhāso pātubhavatīti.

283. “Then, venerable sir, in the northern direction a great light arose, a radiance appeared, surpassing the divine majesty of the devas. Then, venerable sir, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed the Tāvatiṃsa devas: ‘Sirs, just as these portents are seen—a great light arises, a radiance appears—Brahmā will manifest. For this is the prior portent for the manifestation of Brahmā: that a light arises and a radiance appears.’”

“Yathā nimittā dissanti, brahmā pātubhavissati;

Brahmuno hetaṃ nimittaṃ, obhāso vipulo mahā”ti.

“Just as the portents are seen, Brahmā will manifest. This is the portent of Brahmā: the vast and great radiance.”

Sanaṅkumārakathā

The Account of Sanaṅkumāra

284. ‘Atha kho, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā yathāsakesu āsanesu nisīdiṃsu – “obhāsametaṃ ñassāma, yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva naṃ gamissāmā”ti. Cattāropi mahārājāno yathāsakesu āsanesu nisīdiṃsu – “obhāsametaṃ ñassāma yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva [M 2.0170] naṃ gamissāmā”ti. Idaṃ sutvā devā tāvatiṃsā ekaggā [P 2.0210] samāpajjiṃsu – “obhāsametaṃ ñassāma, yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva naṃ gamissāmā”ti.

284. “Then, venerable sir, the devas of Tāvatiṃsa sat down on their respective seats, resolving thus: ‘We shall know this radiance and what its result will be; only after having directly realized it shall we depart.’ The Four Great Kings also sat down on their respective seats, resolving thus: ‘We shall know this radiance and what its result will be; only after having directly realized it shall we depart.’ Having heard this, the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, with unified minds, became as if entering absorption, resolving thus: ‘We shall know this radiance and what its result will be; only after having directly realized it shall we depart.’”

‘Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ [T 2.0240] tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, oḷārikaṃ attabhāvaṃ abhinimminitvā pātubhavati. Yo kho pana, bhante, brahmuno pakativaṇṇo anabhisambhavanīyo so devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ cakkhupathasmiṃ. Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati[V 2.0155], so aññe deve atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Seyyathāpi, bhante, sovaṇṇo viggaho mānusaṃ viggahaṃ atirocati; evameva kho, bhante, yadā brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, so aññe deve atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, na tassaṃ parisāyaṃ koci devo abhivādeti vā paccuṭṭheti vā āsanena vā nimanteti. Sabbeva tuṇhībhūtā pañjalikā pallaṅkena nisīdanti – “yassadāni devassa pallaṅkaṃ icchissati brahmā sanaṅkumāro, tassa devassa pallaṅke nisīdissatī”ti.

“When, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra appears before the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, he appears having manifested a gross physical form. For, venerable sir, the natural complexion of a Brahmā is unattainable to the vision of the devas of Tāvatiṃsa. When, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra appears before the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, he outshines the other devas in both complexion and glory. Just as, venerable sir, a golden form outshines a human form, even so, venerable sir, when Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra appears before the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, he outshines the other devas in both complexion and glory. When, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra appears before the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, no deva in that assembly pays homage to him, or rises for him, or invites him with a seat. All of them, becoming silent, with hands joined in reverence, sit cross-legged, thinking: ‘On whichever deva’s seat Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra now wishes to sit, on that deva’s seat he will sit.’”

‘Yassa kho pana, bhante, devassa brahmā sanaṅkumāro pallaṅke nisīdati, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo vedapaṭilābhaṃ; uḷāraṃ so labhati devo somanassapaṭilābhaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhante, rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto adhunābhisitto rajjena, uḷāraṃ so labhati vedapaṭilābhaṃ, uḷāraṃ so labhati somanassapaṭilābhaṃ. Evameva kho, bhante, yassa devassa brahmā sanaṅkumāro pallaṅke nisīdati, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo vedapaṭilābhaṃ, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo somanassapaṭilābhaṃ. Atha[T 2.0241][P 2.0211], bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro oḷārikaṃ attabhāvaṃ abhinimminitvā kumāravaṇṇī kumāravaṇṇo (syā. ka.) hutvā pañcasikho devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pāturahosi. So vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīdi. Seyyathāpi, bhante, balavā puriso supaccatthate vā pallaṅke same vā bhūmibhāge pallaṅkena nisīdeyya; evameva kho, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīditvā devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sampasādaṃ viditvā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

'Venerable Sir, on whichever deva's seat Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra sits, that deva gains a great experience of delight; that deva gains a great experience of mental joy. Just as, Venerable Sir, a Khattiya king, anointed on the head, having just been consecrated to kingship, gains a great experience of delight and a great experience of mental joy; even so, Venerable Sir, on whichever deva's seat Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra sits, that deva gains a great experience of delight and a great experience of mental joy. Then, Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, having manifested a gross physical form, appeared before the devas of Tāvatiṃsa in the guise of a youth with five topknots. He ascended into the sky and sat cross-legged in the open space of the firmament. Just as, Venerable Sir, a strong man might sit cross-legged on a well-spread seat or on level ground; even so, Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, having ascended into the sky and sat cross-legged in the open space of the firmament, perceiving the serene confidence of the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, expressed his appreciation with these verses:

“Modanti [M 2.0171] vata bho devā, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammataṃ.

“Indeed, sirs, the Tāvatiṃsa devas, together with Inda, rejoice, paying homage to the Tathāgata and to the excellent nature of the Dhamma.

“Nave deve ca passantā, vaṇṇavante yasassine;

Sugatasmiṃ brahmacariyaṃ, caritvāna idhāgate.

They rejoice, seeing the new devas who have come here, possessed of complexion and glory, after having practiced the holy life under the Sugata.

“Te aññe atirocanti, vaṇṇena yasasāyunā;

Sāvakā bhūripaññassa, visesūpagatā idha.

Having attained distinction here, these disciples of the One of Vast Wisdom outshine the other devas in complexion, glory, and lifespan.

“Idaṃ [V 2.0156] disvāna nandanti, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammata”nti.

Seeing this, the Tāvatiṃsa devas, together with Inda, delight, paying homage to the Tathāgata and to the excellent nature of the Dhamma.”

285. ‘Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha; imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhāsato aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato saro hoti vissaṭṭho ca viññeyyo ca mañju ca savanīyo ca bindu ca avisārī ca gambhīro ca ninnādī ca. Yathāparisaṃ kho pana, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro sarena viññāpeti; na cassa bahiddhā parisāya [T 2.0242] ghoso niccharati. Yassa kho pana, bhante, evaṃ aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato saro hoti, so vuccati “brahmassaro”ti.

285. 'Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra spoke on this matter. And, Venerable Sir, as Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra spoke on this matter, his voice was endowed with eight qualities: it was distinct, intelligible, sweet, pleasant to hear, compact, not diffuse, deep, and resonant. Furthermore, Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra makes himself understood with his voice only as far as the assembly extends, and his voice does not travel outside the assembly. Venerable Sir, one whose voice is endowed with these eight qualities is said to have a “Brahmā-voice.”

‘Atha kho, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro tettiṃse attabhāve abhinimminitvā devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ paccekapallaṅkesu [P 2.0212] pallaṅkena paccekapallaṅkena (ka.) nisīditvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – “taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāvañca so bhagavā bahujanahitāya paṭipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Ye hi keci, bho, buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gatā sīlesu paripūrakārino te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā appekacce paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti, appekacce nimmānaratīnaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti, appekacce tusitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti, appekacce yāmānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti, appekacce tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti, appekacce cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjanti. Ye sabbanihīnaṃ kāyaṃ paripūrenti, te gandhabbakāyaṃ paripūrentī’”ti.

'Then, Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, having manifested thirty-three forms of himself, sat cross-legged on each of the individual seats of the devas of Tāvatiṃsa and addressed them: “What do you think, sirs, devas of Tāvatiṃsa? To what great extent has that Blessed One practiced for the welfare of many beings, for the happiness of many beings, out of compassion for the world, for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. Indeed, sirs, whoever has gone for refuge to the Buddha, gone for refuge to the Dhamma, gone for refuge to the Saṅgha, and are fulfillers of the precepts—some of them, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn into the company of the devas Who Wield Power over Others' Creations; some are reborn into the company of the devas Who Delight in Creating; some are reborn into the company of the Tusita devas; some are reborn into the company of the Yāma devas; some are reborn into the company of the Tāvatiṃsa devas; some are reborn into the company of the devas of the Four Great Kings. And those who fulfill the requirements for the very lowest celestial body, they fulfill the requirements for a Gandhabba body.”'

286. ‘Imamatthaṃ[M 2.0172], bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha; imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhāsato ghosoyeva devā maññanti – “yvāyaṃ mama pallaṅke svāyaṃ ekova bhāsatī”ti.

286. 'Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra spoke on this matter. And, Venerable Sir, as Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra was speaking on this matter, the devas thought it was just a voice, thinking: “This one on my seat—it is he alone who is speaking.”

Ekasmiṃ bhāsamānasmiṃ, sabbe bhāsanti nimmitā;

Ekasmiṃ tuṇhimāsīne, sabbe tuṇhī bhavanti te.

When one is speaking, all the created ones speak; when one is sitting in silence, they all become silent.

Tadāsu [T 2.0243] devā maññanti, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Yvāyaṃ mama pallaṅkasmiṃ, svāyaṃ ekova bhāsatīti.

At that time, the Tāvatiṃsa devas, together with Inda, thought: 'This one on my throne—it is he alone who is speaking.'

‘Atha [V 2.0157] kho, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro ekattena attānaṃ upasaṃharati, ekattena attānaṃ upasaṃharitvā sakkassa [P 2.0213] devānamindassa pallaṅke pallaṅkena nisīditvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi –

'Then, Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra withdrew himself into a single form. Having withdrawn himself into a single form, and having sat cross-legged on the throne of Sakka, lord of the devas, he addressed the Tāvatiṃsa devas:

Bhāvitaiddhipādo

One Who Has Developed the Bases of Power

287. “‘Taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāva supaññattā cime tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro iddhipādā paññattā iddhipahutāya iddhibahulīkatāya (syā.) iddhivisavitāya iddhivisevitāya (syā.) iddhivikubbanatāya. Katame cattāro? Idha bho bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Vīriyasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Cittasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Ime kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro iddhipādā paññattā iddhipahutāya iddhivisavitāya iddhivikubbanatāya.

287. “‘What do you think, sirs, you Tāvatiṃsa devas? How well proclaimed by that Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—are these four bases of power, proclaimed for proficiency in psychic power, for mastery of psychic power, and for the diverse manifestations of psychic power. Which four? Here, sirs, a bhikkhu develops the basis of power endowed with concentration founded on zeal and formations of striving. He develops the basis of power endowed with concentration founded on energy and formations of striving. He develops the basis of power endowed with concentration founded on consciousness and formations of striving. He develops the basis of power endowed with concentration founded on investigation and formations of striving. These, sirs, are the four bases of power proclaimed by that Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—for proficiency in psychic power, for mastery of psychic power, and for the diverse manifestations of psychic power.’”

“‘Ye hi keci bho atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhosuṃ, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Yepi hi keci bho anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhossanti, sabbe [T 2.0244] te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Yepi hi keci bho etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhonti, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Passanti no bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā mamapimaṃ [M 2.0173] evarūpaṃ iddhānubhāva”nti? “Evaṃ mahābrahme”ti. “Ahampi kho bho imesaṃyeva catunnañca iddhipādānaṃ [P 2.0214] bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā evaṃ mahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo”ti. Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha. Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsitvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi –

‘Sirs, whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past have experienced various kinds of psychic power, all of them have done so by having developed and cultivated these four bases of psychic power. Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the future will experience various kinds of psychic power, all of them will do so by having developed and cultivated these four bases of psychic power. Whatever ascetics or brahmins at present experience various kinds of psychic power, all of them do so by having developed and cultivated these four bases of psychic power. Do you, sirs, you Tāvatiṃsā devas, see this potency of my psychic power?’ ‘Yes, Great Brahmā.’ ‘And I too, sirs, by having developed and cultivated these four bases of psychic power, am of such great psychic power and great might.’ This, venerable sir, is what the Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra said. Having said this, venerable sir, the Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra addressed the Tāvatiṃsā devas:

Tividho okāsādhigamo

The Threefold Attainment of Opportunity

288. “‘Taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāvañcidaṃ tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tayo okāsādhigamā anubuddhā sukhassādhigamāya. Katame tayo? Idha bho ekacco saṃsaṭṭho viharati kāmehi saṃsaṭṭho akusalehi dhammehi. So aparena samayena [V 2.0158] ariyadhammaṃ suṇāti, yoniso manasi karoti, dhammānudhammaṃ paṭipajjati. So ariyadhammassavanaṃ āgamma yonisomanasikāraṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipattiṃ asaṃsaṭṭho viharati kāmehi asaṃsaṭṭho akusalehi dhammehi. Tassa asaṃsaṭṭhassa kāmehi asaṃsaṭṭhassa akusalehi dhammehi uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bho, pamudā pāmojjaṃ pāmujjaṃ (pī. ka.) jāyetha, evameva [T 2.0245] kho, bho, asaṃsaṭṭhassa kāmehi asaṃsaṭṭhassa akusalehi dhammehi uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Ayaṃ kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena paṭhamo okāsādhigamo anubuddho sukhassādhigamāya.

288. ‘What do you think of this, O devas of Tāvatiṃsa? By that Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—three attainments of opportunity have been fittingly realized for the attainment of happiness. Which three? Here, O devas, a certain person lives associated with sensual pleasures, associated with unwholesome states. Then, at a later time, he hears the noble Dhamma, attends to it wisely, and practices in accordance with the Dhamma. Through hearing the noble Dhamma, wise attention, and practice in accordance with the Dhamma, he lives unassociated with sensual pleasures, unassociated with unwholesome states. For him, living unassociated with sensual pleasures and unassociated with unwholesome states, happiness arises, and from that happiness, still more mental joy arises. Just as, O devas, from gladness, great joy might arise, even so, O devas, for one living unassociated with sensual pleasures and unassociated with unwholesome states, happiness arises, and from that happiness, still more mental joy arises. This, O devas, is the first attainment of opportunity fittingly realized by that Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—for the attainment of happiness.

“‘Puna caparaṃ, bho, idhekaccassa oḷārikā kāyasaṅkhārā appaṭippassaddhā honti, oḷārikā vacīsaṅkhārā appaṭippassaddhā honti, oḷārikā cittasaṅkhārā appaṭippassaddhā honti. So aparena samayena ariyadhammaṃ suṇāti, yoniso manasi karoti, dhammānudhammaṃ paṭipajjati. Tassa ariyadhammassavanaṃ āgamma yonisomanasikāraṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipattiṃ oḷārikā kāyasaṅkhārā paṭippassambhanti, oḷārikā vacīsaṅkhārā paṭippassambhanti, oḷārikā cittasaṅkhārā [P 2.0215] paṭippassambhanti. Tassa oḷārikānaṃ kāyasaṅkhārānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā oḷārikānaṃ vacīsaṅkhārānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā oḷārikānaṃ cittasaṅkhārānaṃ [M 2.0174] paṭippassaddhiyā uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bho, pamudā pāmojjaṃ jāyetha, evameva kho bho oḷārikānaṃ kāyasaṅkhārānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā oḷārikānaṃ vacīsaṅkhārānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā oḷārikānaṃ cittasaṅkhārānaṃ paṭippassaddhiyā uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Ayaṃ kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dutiyo okāsādhigamo anubuddho sukhassādhigamāya.

‘Furthermore, O devas, here for a certain person, gross bodily formations are not calmed, gross verbal formations are not calmed, and gross mental formations are not calmed. Then, at a later time, he hears the noble Dhamma, attends to it wisely, and practices in accordance with the Dhamma. For him, through hearing the noble Dhamma, wise attention, and practice in accordance with the Dhamma, gross bodily formations are calmed, gross verbal formations are calmed, and gross mental formations are calmed. For him, with the calming of gross bodily formations, the calming of gross verbal formations, and the calming of gross mental formations, happiness arises, and from that happiness, still more mental joy arises. Just as, O devas, from gladness, great joy might arise, even so, O devas, with the calming of gross bodily formations, the calming of gross verbal formations, and the calming of gross mental formations, happiness arises, and from that happiness, still more mental joy arises. This, O devas, is the second attainment of opportunity fittingly realized by that Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—for the attainment of happiness.

“‘Puna caparaṃ, bho, idhekacco [T 2.0246] ‘idaṃ kusala’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, ‘idaṃ akusala’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. ‘Idaṃ sāvajjaṃ idaṃ anavajjaṃ, idaṃ sevitabbaṃ idaṃ na sevitabbaṃ, idaṃ hīnaṃ idaṃ paṇītaṃ, idaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāga’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti. So aparena samayena ariyadhammaṃ suṇāti, yoniso manasi karoti, dhammānudhammaṃ paṭipajjati. So ariyadhammassavanaṃ āgamma yonisomanasikāraṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipattiṃ, ‘idaṃ kusala’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘idaṃ akusala’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Idaṃ sāvajjaṃ idaṃ anavajjaṃ, idaṃ sevitabbaṃ idaṃ na sevitabbaṃ, idaṃ hīnaṃ idaṃ paṇītaṃ, idaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāga’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Tassa evaṃ jānato evaṃ passato avijjā pahīyati, vijjā uppajjati. Tassa avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bho, pamudā pāmojjaṃ jāyetha[V 2.0159], evameva kho, bho, avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā uppajjati sukhaṃ, sukhā bhiyyo somanassaṃ. Ayaṃ kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tatiyo okāsādhigamo anubuddho sukhassādhigamāya. Ime [T 2.0247][P 2.0216] kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tayo okāsādhigamā anubuddhā sukhassādhigamāyā”ti. Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha, imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsitvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi –

‘Furthermore, O devas, here a certain person does not know as it really is: ‘This state is wholesome’; ‘This state is unwholesome’; ‘This state is blameworthy’; ‘This state is blameless’; ‘This state is to be cultivated’; ‘This state is not to be cultivated’; ‘This state is inferior’; ‘This state is sublime’; ‘This state has both dark and bright portions.’ Then, at a later time, he hears the noble Dhamma, attends to it wisely, and practices in accordance with the Dhamma. Through hearing the noble Dhamma, wise attention, and practice in accordance with the Dhamma, he knows as it really is: ‘This state is wholesome’; ‘This state is unwholesome’; ‘This state is blameworthy’; ‘This state is blameless’; ‘This state is to be cultivated’; ‘This state is not to be cultivated’; ‘This state is inferior’; ‘This state is sublime’; ‘This state has both dark and bright portions.’ For him, knowing thus and seeing thus, ignorance is abandoned and knowledge arises. For him, with the fading of ignorance and the arising of knowledge, happiness arises, and from that happiness, still more mental joy arises. Just as, O devas, from gladness, great joy might arise, even so, O devas, with the fading of ignorance and the arising of knowledge, happiness arises, and from that happiness, still more mental joy arises. This, O devas, is the third attainment of opportunity fittingly realized by that Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—for the attainment of happiness. These, O devas, are the three attainments of opportunity fittingly realized by that Blessed One—the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One—for the attainment of happiness.’ Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra spoke this teaching. Venerable Sir, having spoken this teaching, he addressed the Tāvatiṃsa devas:

Catusatipaṭṭhānaṃ

The Four Establishments of Mindfulness.

289. “‘Taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāva supaññattā cime tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro satipaṭṭhānā paññattā kusalassādhigamāya. Katame cattāro? Idha[M 2.0175], bho, bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Ajjhattaṃ kāye kāyānupassī viharanto tattha sammā samādhiyati, sammā vippasīdati. So tattha sammā samāhito sammā vippasanno bahiddhā parakāye ñāṇadassanaṃ abhinibbatteti. Ajjhattaṃ vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati…pe… bahiddhā paravedanāsu ñāṇadassanaṃ abhinibbatteti. Ajjhattaṃ citte cittānupassī viharati…pe… bahiddhā paracitte ñāṇadassanaṃ abhinibbatteti. Ajjhattaṃ [T 2.0248] dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Ajjhattaṃ dhammesu dhammānupassī viharanto tattha sammā samādhiyati, sammā vippasīdati. So tattha sammā samāhito sammā vippasanno bahiddhā paradhammesu ñāṇadassanaṃ abhinibbatteti. Ime kho, bho, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena cattāro satipaṭṭhānā paññattā kusalassādhigamāyā”ti. Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha. Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsitvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi –

289. ‘What do you think, Sirs, devas of Tāvatiṃsa? How well proclaimed are these four establishments of mindfulness by that Blessed One who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, proclaimed for the attainment of the wholesome. What are the four? Here, Sirs, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body internally—ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. Dwelling contemplating the body in the body internally, there he rightly concentrates his mind, and it becomes rightly clear. He, being rightly concentrated and his mind rightly clear there, generates knowledge and vision externally regarding another’s body. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings internally… he generates knowledge and vision externally regarding another’s feelings. He dwells contemplating mind in mind internally… he generates knowledge and vision externally regarding another’s mind. He dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena internally—ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. Dwelling contemplating phenomena in phenomena internally, there he rightly concentrates his mind, and it becomes rightly clear. He, being rightly concentrated and his mind rightly clear there, generates knowledge and vision externally regarding another’s phenomena. These, Sirs, are the four establishments of mindfulness proclaimed by that Blessed One who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, proclaimed for the attainment of the wholesome.’ This matter, Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra spoke. This matter, Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, having spoken, addressed the devas of Tāvatiṃsa—

Satta samādhiparikkhārā

The Seven Accessories of Concentration

290. “‘Taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāva supaññattā cime tena bhagavatā [V 2.0160] jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena satta samādhiparikkhārā sammāsamādhissa paribhāvanāya sammāsamādhissa pāripūriyā. Katame satta? Sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo [P 2.0217] sammāvāyāmo sammāsati. Yā kho, bho, imehi sattahaṅgehi cittassa ekaggatā parikkhatā, ayaṃ vuccati, bho, ariyo sammāsamādhi saupaniso itipi saparikkhāro itipi. Sammādiṭṭhissa bho, sammāsaṅkappo pahoti, sammāsaṅkappassa sammāvācā pahoti, sammāvācassa sammākammanto pahoti. Sammākammantassa sammāājīvo pahoti, sammāājīvassa sammāvāyāmo pahoti, sammāvāyāmassa sammāsati pahoti[T 2.0249], sammāsatissa sammāsamādhi pahoti, sammāsamādhissa sammāñāṇaṃ pahoti, sammāñāṇassa sammāvimutti pahoti. Yañhi taṃ, bho, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhi apārutā amatassa [M 2.0176] dvārā’ti idameva taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya. Svākkhāto hi, bho, bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko, akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhi apārutā amatassa dvārā dvārāti (syā. ka.).

290. ‘What do you think, Sirs, devas of Tāvatiṃsa? How well proclaimed are these seven accessories of concentration by that Blessed One who knows and sees, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for the cultivation and for the fulfillment of right concentration? Which seven? Right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, and right mindfulness. Sirs, that unification of mind which is equipped with these seven factors is called, Sirs, the noble right concentration, said to be ‘with its supporting conditions’ and ‘with its accessories.’ For one with right view, Sirs, right intention arises; for one with right intention, right speech arises; for one with right speech, right action arises; for one with right action, right livelihood arises; for one with right livelihood, right effort arises; for one with right effort, right mindfulness arises; for one with right mindfulness, right concentration arises; for one with right concentration, right knowledge arises; for one with right knowledge, right liberation arises. Indeed, Sirs, if one were to speak rightly, one would say: ‘The Dhamma is well proclaimed by the Blessed One, visible here and now, timeless, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be experienced by the wise for themselves; the doors to the Deathless are opened.’ This is what one would rightly say. For, Sirs, the Dhamma is well proclaimed by the Blessed One, visible here and now, timeless, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be experienced by the wise for themselves; the doors to the Deathless are opened.

“‘Ye hi keci, bho, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgatā, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgatā, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā[P 2.0218], ye cime opapātikā dhammavinītā sātirekāni catuvīsatisatasahassāni māgadhakā paricārakā abbhatītā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā. Atthi cevettha sakadāgāmino.

‘Indeed, Sirs, whoever are endowed with unwavering faith in the Buddha, endowed with unwavering faith in the Dhamma, endowed with unwavering faith in the Saṅgha, and endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones; and these spontaneously reborn ones, disciplined in the Dhamma—the more than two million four hundred thousand Magadhan attendants who have passed on and died—all of them, with the destruction of the three fetters, have become stream-enterers, not subject to the lower realms, assured, with enlightenment as their destination. And among them there are also once-returners.

“Atthāyaṃ athāyaṃ (sī. syā.) itarā pajā, puññābhāgāti me mano;

Saṅkhātuṃ nopi sakkomi, musāvādassa ottappa”nti.

‘This other populace also exists—partakers in merit, so is my thought; I am unable to count them, out of moral dread of false speech.’

291. ‘Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro bhāsittha, imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhāsato vessavaṇassa mahārājassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ [T 2.0250] vata bho, evarūpopi nāma uḷāro satthā bhavissati, evarūpaṃ uḷāraṃ dhammakkhānaṃ, evarūpā uḷārā visesādhigamā paññāyissantī”ti. Atha, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro vessavaṇassa mahārājassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya vessavaṇaṃ mahārājānaṃ etadavoca – “taṃ kiṃ maññati bhavaṃ vessavaṇo mahārājā atītampi addhānaṃ evarūpo uḷāro satthā ahosi, evarūpaṃ uḷāraṃ dhammakkhānaṃ, evarūpā uḷārā visesādhigamā paññāyiṃsu. Anāgatampi [V 2.0161] addhānaṃ evarūpo uḷāro satthā bhavissati, evarūpaṃ uḷāraṃ dhammakkhānaṃ, evarūpā uḷārā visesādhigamā paññāyissantī’”ti.

291. ‘This matter, Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra spoke. While Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra was speaking this matter, Venerable Sir, this reflection arose in the mind of the great king Vessavaṇa: “It is wonderful, indeed! It is marvelous, indeed! That such a sublime Teacher could exist, such a sublime teaching of the Dhamma, and that such sublime special attainments could be made known.” Then, Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, having known with his own mind the reflection in the mind of the great king Vessavaṇa, said this to the great king Vessavaṇa: “What do you think of this, esteemed great king Vessavaṇa? In the past, too, such a sublime Teacher existed, such a sublime teaching of the Dhamma, and such sublime special attainments were made known. In the future, too, such a sublime Teacher will exist, such a sublime teaching of the Dhamma, and such sublime special attainments will be made known.”’

292. “‘Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ abhāsi, imamatthaṃ vessavaṇo mahārājā brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa devānaṃ [M 2.0177] tāvatiṃsānaṃ bhāsato [P 2.0219] sammukhā sutaṃ sutvā (sī. pī.) sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ sayaṃ parisāyaṃ ārocesi”.
