292. ‘This matter, Venerable Sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra spoke to the devas of Tāvatiṃsa. The great king Vessavaṇa heard this matter in the presence of Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra as he spoke to the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, received it in his presence, and he himself announced it in his own assembly.’

Imamatthaṃ janavasabho yakkho vessavaṇassa mahārājassa sayaṃ parisāyaṃ bhāsato sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ paṭiggahetvā (sī. pī.) bhagavato ārocesi. Imamatthaṃ bhagavā janavasabhassa yakkhassa sammukhā sutvā sammukhā paṭiggahetvā sāmañca abhiññāya āyasmato ānandassa ārocesi, imamatthamāyasmā ānando bhagavato sammukhā sutvā sammukhā paṭiggahetvā ārocesi bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ [T 2.0251] upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ. Tayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ iddhañceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitanti.

The yakkha Janavasabha reported this matter to the Blessed One, having heard and received it directly in the presence of the great king Vessavaṇa while he was speaking to his own assembly. The Blessed One, having heard and received it directly from the yakkha Janavasabha, and having known it himself through direct knowledge, reported it to the Venerable Ānanda. The Venerable Ānanda, having heard and received it directly from the Blessed One, reported it to the bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs, the laymen, and the laywomen. Thus this holy life has become successful, prosperous, widespread, known to many, and extensive, well proclaimed among devas and humans.”

Janavasabhasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.

The Janavasabha Sutta, the fifth, is concluded.

6. Mahāgovindasuttaṃ

6. The Mahāgovinda Sutta

293. Evaṃ [T 2.0252][M 2.0178][V 2.0162] me [P 2.0220] sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Atha kho pañcasikho gandhabbaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ gijjhakūṭaṃ pabbataṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho pañcasikho gandhabbaputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yaṃ kho me, bhante, devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ, ārocemi taṃ bhagavato”ti. “Ārocehi me tvaṃ, pañcasikhā”ti bhagavā avoca.

293. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha on the mountain Gijjhakūṭa. Then, when the night was well advanced, Pañcasikha, the gandhabba’s son, of surpassing beauty, illuminating the entire Gijjhakūṭa mountain, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, Pañcasikha, the gandhabba’s son, said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, that which I have heard in the presence of the Tāvatiṃsa devas, received in their presence, I shall report to the Blessed One.' 'Report it to me, Pañcasikha,' the Blessed One said.

Devasabhā

The Assembly of the Devas

294. “Purimāni, bhante, divasāni purimatarāni tadahuposathe pannarase pavāraṇāya puṇṇāya puṇṇamāya rattiyā kevalakappā ca devā tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā; mahatī ca dibbaparisā samantato nisinnā honti, cattāro ca mahārājāno catuddisā nisinnā honti; puratthimāya disāya dhataraṭṭho mahārājā pacchimābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; dakkhiṇāya disāya virūḷhako mahārājā uttarābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; pacchimāya disāya virūpakkho [P 2.0221] mahārājā puratthābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā; uttarāya disāya vessavaṇo mahārājā dakkhiṇābhimukho nisinno hoti deve purakkhatvā. Yadā bhante, kevalakappā ca devā [T 2.0253] tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā, mahatī ca dibbaparisā samantato nisinnā honti, cattāro ca mahārājāno catuddisā nisinnā honti, idaṃ nesaṃ hoti āsanasmiṃ; atha pacchā amhākaṃ āsanaṃ hoti.

294. “Venerable sir, on a former day, on a day more former still, on the fifteenth Uposatha day, on the night of the full moon Pavāraṇā, all the devas of Tāvatiṃsa were seated together and assembled in the Sudhammā assembly hall. A great divine assembly was seated all around, and the four Great Kings were seated in the four directions. In the eastern direction, the great king Dhataraṭṭha was seated facing west, with the devas before him. In the southern direction, the great king Virūḷhaka was seated facing north, with the devas before him. In the western direction, the great king Virūpakkha was seated facing east, with the devas before him. In the northern direction, the great king Vessavaṇa was seated facing south, with the devas before him. Venerable sir, when all the devas of Tāvatiṃsa were seated together and assembled in the Sudhammā assembly hall, and the great divine assembly was seated all around, and the four Great Kings were seated in the four directions, this was their seating place; only afterwards was our seating place.”

“Ye te, bhante, devā bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ caritvā adhunūpapannā tāvatiṃsakāyaṃ, te aññe [V 2.0163] deve atirocanti vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Tena sudaṃ, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā attamanā honti pamuditā [M 2.0179] pītisomanassajātā; ‘dibbā vata, bho, kāyā paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyā’ti.

“Venerable sir, those devas who, having practiced the holy life under the Blessed One, have now arisen in the Tāvatiṃsa realm, outshine the other devas in appearance and splendor. For that reason, venerable sir, the Tāvatiṃsa devas are pleased, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness, thinking: ‘Indeed, sirs, the hosts of devas are being filled, while the hosts of asuras are dwindling!’”

295. “Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sampasādaṃ viditvā imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

295. “Then, venerable sir, Sakka, lord of the devas, knowing the joyful confidence of the Tāvatiṃsa devas, expressed his appreciation with these verses:”

‘Modanti vata bho devā, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammataṃ.

“‘The Tāvatiṃsa devas, indeed, together with Sakka, rejoice, paying homage to the Tathāgata and to the excellence of the Dhamma.’”

Nave deve ca passantā, vaṇṇavante yasassine;

Sugatasmiṃ brahmacariyaṃ, caritvāna idhāgate.

“And seeing the new devas who have come here—possessing fine appearance and great splendor—after practicing the holy life under the Sugata.”

Te aññe atirocanti, vaṇṇena yasasāyunā;

Sāvakā bhūripaññassa, visesūpagatā idha.

“They, the disciples of the one of vast wisdom, having attained distinction here, outshine the others in appearance, splendor, and lifespan.”

Idaṃ disvāna nandanti, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammata’nti.

“Seeing this, the Tāvatiṃsa devas, together with their lord, delight, paying homage to the Tathāgata and to the excellent nature of the Dhamma.’”

“Tena sudaṃ[P 2.0222], bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā bhiyyoso mattāya attamanā honti pamuditā pītisomanassajātā; ‘dibbā vata, bho, kāyā [T 2.0254] paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyā’”ti.

“Because of that, venerable sir, the Tāvatiṃsa devas were all the more pleased, joyful, and filled with gladness and happiness, thinking: ‘Indeed, sirs, the hosts of devas are being filled, while the hosts of asuras are dwindling!’”

Aṭṭha yathābhuccavaṇṇā

The Eight True Qualities

296. “Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sampasādaṃ viditvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – ‘iccheyyātha no tumhe, mārisā, tassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe sotu’nti? ‘Icchāma mayaṃ, mārisa, tassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe sotu’nti. Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe payirudāhāsi – ‘taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā? Yāvañca so bhagavā bahujanahitāya paṭipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Evaṃ [V 2.0164] bahujanahitāya paṭipannaṃ bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

296. “Then, venerable sir, Sakka, the lord of the devas, knowing the joyful confidence of the Tāvatiṃsa devas, addressed the Tāvatiṃsa devas: ‘Would you wish, sirs, to hear the eight true qualities of that Blessed One?’ ‘We wish, sir, to hear the eight true qualities of that Blessed One.’ Then, venerable sir, Sakka, the lord of the devas, declared to the Tāvatiṃsa devas the eight true qualities of the Blessed One: ‘What do you think, honored Tāvatiṃsa devas? That Blessed One has practiced for the welfare of many beings, for the happiness of many beings, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. We do not see a teacher endowed with this attribute—practicing for the welfare of many beings, for the happiness of many beings, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans—either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.”

“Svākkhāto [M 2.0180] kho pana tena bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhi. Evaṃ opaneyyikassa dhammassa desetāraṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

“The Dhamma has been well-expounded by that Blessed One: it is visible here and now, timeless, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be realized personally by the wise. We do not see a teacher endowed with this attribute—one who teaches a Dhamma that leads onward—either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.”

“Idaṃ kusalanti kho pana tena bhagavatā supaññattaṃ, idaṃ akusalanti supaññattaṃ. Idaṃ sāvajjaṃ [P 2.0223] idaṃ anavajjaṃ, idaṃ sevitabbaṃ idaṃ na sevitabbaṃ, idaṃ hīnaṃ idaṃ paṇītaṃ, idaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāganti supaññattaṃ. Evaṃ kusalākusalasāvajjānavajjasevitabbāsevitabbahīna-paṇītakaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgānaṃ [T 2.0255] dhammānaṃ paññapetāraṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

By that Blessed One it has been well-proclaimed: ‘This is wholesome,’ and it has been well-proclaimed: ‘This is unwholesome.’ It has been well-proclaimed: ‘This is blameworthy, this is blameless; this is to be cultivated, this is not to be cultivated; this is inferior, this is sublime; this has dark and bright counterparts.’ We do not see a teacher endowed with this attribute—one who makes known the dhammas that are wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, to be cultivated and not to be cultivated, inferior and sublime, with dark and bright counterparts—either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

“Supaññattā kho pana tena bhagavatā sāvakānaṃ nibbānagāminī paṭipadā, saṃsandati nibbānañca paṭipadā ca. Seyyathāpi nāma gaṅgodakaṃ yamunodakena saṃsandati sameti, evameva supaññattā tena bhagavatā sāvakānaṃ nibbānagāminī paṭipadā, saṃsandati nibbānañca paṭipadā ca. Evaṃ nibbānagāminiyā paṭipadāya paññapetāraṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

The path leading to Nibbāna has been well-proclaimed by that Blessed One for his disciples; Nibbāna and the path are concordant. Just as the water of the Ganges flows together and merges with the water of the Yamunā, even so has the path leading to Nibbāna been well-proclaimed by that Blessed One for his disciples; Nibbāna and the path are concordant. We do not see a teacher endowed with this attribute—one who proclaims the path leading to Nibbāna—either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

“Abhinipphanno abhinippanno (pī. ka.) kho pana tassa bhagavato lābho abhinipphanno siloko, yāva maññe khattiyā sampiyāyamānarūpā viharanti, vigatamado kho pana so bhagavā āhāraṃ āhāreti. Evaṃ vigatamadaṃ āhāraṃ āharayamānaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva [P 2.0224] atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

Gain has been fully accomplished for that Blessed One, and renown has been fully accomplished. The khattiyas, I believe, dwell holding him in dear esteem. Yet that Blessed One, free from intoxication, partakes of food. We do not see a teacher endowed with this attribute—one who partakes of food while free from intoxication—either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

“Laddhasahāyo kho pana so bhagavā sekhānañceva paṭipannānaṃ khīṇāsavānañca vusitavataṃ. Te bhagavā apanujja ekārāmataṃ anuyutto viharati. Evaṃ ekārāmataṃ anuyuttaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

That Blessed One has obtained companions, both trainees who are practicing and canker-destroyed ones who have lived the holy life. Yet the Blessed One, setting them aside, dwells devoted to delighting in solitude. We do not see a teacher endowed with this attribute—one devoted to delighting in solitude—either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

“Yathāvādī [V 2.0165] kho pana so bhagavā tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī, iti yathāvādī tathākārī, yathākārī [T 2.0256] tathāvādī. Evaṃ dhammānudhammappaṭipannaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

As that Blessed One speaks, so he acts; as he acts, so he speaks. Thus, as he speaks, so he acts; as he acts, so he speaks. We do not see a teacher endowed with this attribute—one who has practiced in conformity with the Dhamma—either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

“Tiṇṇavicikiccho [M 2.0181] kho pana so bhagavā vigatakathaṃkatho pariyositasaṅkappo ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariyaṃ. Evaṃ tiṇṇavicikicchaṃ vigatakathaṃkathaṃ pariyositasaṅkappaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariyaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā’ti.

That Blessed One has crossed over doubt, is free from perplexity, and has his aspiration fulfilled through the supreme support, the primeval holy life. We do not see a teacher endowed with this attribute—one who has crossed over doubt, is free from perplexity, and has his aspiration fulfilled through the supreme support, the primeval holy life—either in the past or in the present, other than that Blessed One.

297. “Ime kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe payirudāhāsi. Tena sudaṃ, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā bhiyyoso mattāya attamanā honti pamuditā pītisomanassajātā bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe sutvā. Tatra, bhante, ekacce devā evamāhaṃsu – ‘aho vata, mārisā, cattāro sammāsambuddhā loke uppajjeyyuṃ dhammañca deseyyuṃ yathariva bhagavā. Tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Ekacce devā evamāhaṃsu – ‘tiṭṭhantu, mārisā, cattāro sammāsambuddhā, aho vata, mārisā, tayo sammāsambuddhā loke uppajjeyyuṃ dhammañca deseyyuṃ yathariva bhagavā. Tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Ekacce devā evamāhaṃsu – ‘tiṭṭhantu, mārisā, tayo [T 2.0257] sammāsambuddhā, aho vata, mārisā, dve sammāsambuddhā loke uppajjeyyuṃ dhammañca deseyyuṃ yathariva bhagavā. Tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti.

297. “These, venerable sir, are the eight true praises of the Blessed One that Sakka, lord of the devas, declared to the Tāvatiṃsa devas. Because of that declaration, venerable sir, the Tāvatiṃsa devas, having heard the eight true praises of the Blessed One, became exceedingly delighted, joyful, and filled with rapture and happiness. There, venerable sir, some devas said this: ‘Oh, friends, would that four Perfectly Enlightened Ones arise in the world and teach the Dhamma just as the Blessed One does! That would be for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans.’ Other devas said this: ‘Let alone four Perfectly Enlightened Ones, friends. Would that three Perfectly Enlightened Ones arise in the world and teach the Dhamma just as the Blessed One does! That would be for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans.’ Still other devas said this: ‘Let alone three Perfectly Enlightened Ones, friends. Would that two Perfectly Enlightened Ones arise in the world and teach the Dhamma just as the Blessed One does! That would be for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans.’”

298. “Evaṃ vutte[P 2.0225], bhante, sakko devānamindo deve tāvatiṃse etadavoca – ‘aṭṭhānaṃ kho etaṃ, mārisā, anavakāso, yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve arahanto sammāsambuddhā apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyuṃ, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Aho vata, mārisā, so bhagavā appābādho appātaṅko ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭheyya. Tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussāna’nti. Atha kho, bhante, yenatthena devā tāvatiṃsā sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ sannisinnā honti sannipatitā, taṃ atthaṃ cintayitvā taṃ atthaṃ mantayitvā vuttavacanāpi taṃ cattāro mahārājāno tasmiṃ atthe honti. Paccānusiṭṭhavacanāpi [M 2.0182] taṃ cattāro mahārājāno tasmiṃ atthe honti, sakesu sakesu āsanesu ṭhitā avipakkantā.

298. “When this was said, venerable sir, Sakka, lord of the devas, spoke to the Tāvatiṃsa devas: ‘Friends, it is impossible, it is out of the question, that in a single world-system two Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, should arise neither before nor after the other; such a thing is impossible. Oh, friends, would that the Blessed One might remain free from illness and free from affliction for a long, long time! That would be for the welfare of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans.’ Then, venerable sir, having considered and deliberated upon the matter for which the Tāvatiṃsa devas had seated themselves and assembled in the Sudhammā Hall, the Four Great Kings were ones whose words had been spoken and whose instructions had been received on that matter, and they remained at their respective seats, not having departed.”

Te [V 2.0166] vuttavākyā rājāno, paṭiggayhānusāsaniṃ;

Vippasannamanā santā, aṭṭhaṃsu samhi āsaneti.

“Those kings, having spoken their words and accepted the instruction, with serene minds and in tranquility, remained at their own seats.”

299. “Atha kho, bhante, uttarāya disāya uḷāro āloko sañjāyi, obhāso pāturahosi atikkammeva devānaṃ devānubhāvaṃ. Atha kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – ‘yathā kho, mārisā, nimittāni dissanti, uḷāro āloko sañjāyati, obhāso pātubhavati[T 2.0258], brahmā pātubhavissati; brahmuno hetaṃ pubbanimittaṃ pātubhāvāya, yadidaṃ āloko sañjāyati obhāso pātubhavatīti.

299. “Then, venerable sir, in the northern direction a magnificent light arose and a radiance appeared, surpassing the divine power of the devas. Then, venerable sir, Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed the Tāvatiṃsa devas: ‘Friends, as the signs are seen—a magnificent light arises and a radiance appears—Brahmā will appear. This is the preliminary sign for the appearance of Brahmā: that a light arises and a radiance appears.’”

‘Yathā nimittā dissanti, brahmā pātubhavissati;

Brahmuno hetaṃ nimittaṃ, obhāso vipulo mahā’ti.

“‘As the signs are seen, Brahmā will appear; this is the sign of Brahmā—a radiance, vast and great.’”

Sanaṅkumārakathā

The Story of Sanaṅkumāra

300. “Atha [P 2.0226] kho, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā yathāsakesu āsanesu nisīdiṃsu – ‘obhāsametaṃ ñassāma, yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva naṃ gamissāmā’ti. Cattāropi mahārājāno yathāsakesu āsanesu nisīdiṃsu – ‘obhāsametaṃ ñassāma, yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva naṃ gamissāmā’ti. Idaṃ sutvā devā tāvatiṃsā ekaggā samāpajjiṃsu – ‘obhāsametaṃ ñassāma, yaṃvipāko bhavissati, sacchikatvāva naṃ gamissāmā’ti.

300. “Then, venerable sir, the Tāvatiṃsa devas sat down in their respective seats, thinking: ‘We shall learn about this radiance and what its result will be; only after realizing it for ourselves shall we depart.’ The Four Great Kings also sat down in their respective seats, thinking: ‘We shall learn about this radiance and what its result will be; only after realizing it for ourselves shall we depart.’ Having heard this, the Tāvatiṃsa devas became one-pointed in mind, thinking: ‘We shall learn about this radiance and what its result will be; only after realizing it for ourselves shall we depart.’”

“Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, oḷārikaṃ attabhāvaṃ abhinimminitvā pātubhavati. Yo kho pana, bhante, brahmuno pakativaṇṇo, anabhisambhavanīyo so devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ cakkhupathasmiṃ. Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, so aññe deve atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Seyyathāpi, bhante, sovaṇṇo viggaho mānusaṃ viggahaṃ atirocati, evameva kho, bhante, yadā brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ [M 2.0183] tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, so aññe deve atirocati vaṇṇena ceva yasasā ca. Yadā, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pātubhavati, na tassaṃ parisāyaṃ koci devo abhivādeti vā paccuṭṭheti vā [T 2.0259] āsanena vā nimanteti. Sabbeva tuṇhībhūtā pañjalikā pallaṅkena nisīdanti – ‘yassadāni devassa pallaṅkaṃ icchissati brahmā sanaṅkumāro, tassa devassa pallaṅke nisīdissatī’ti. Yassa kho pana, bhante, devassa brahmā sanaṅkumāro [V 2.0167] pallaṅke nisīdati, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo vedapaṭilābhaṃ, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo somanassapaṭilābhaṃ[P 2.0227]. Seyyathāpi, bhante, rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto adhunābhisitto rajjena, uḷāraṃ so labhati vedapaṭilābhaṃ, uḷāraṃ so labhati somanassapaṭilābhaṃ, evameva kho, bhante, yassa devassa brahmā sanaṅkumāro pallaṅke nisīdati, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo vedapaṭilābhaṃ, uḷāraṃ so labhati devo somanassapaṭilābhaṃ. Atha, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sampasādaṃ viditvā antarahito imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

“When, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra manifests to the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, he manifests by creating a gross body. For, venerable sir, the natural appearance of a Brahmā is beyond the range of vision of the devas of Tāvatiṃsa. When, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra manifests to the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, he outshines the other devas in beauty and in glory. Just as, venerable sir, a golden figure outshines a human figure, even so, venerable sir, when Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra manifests to the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, he outshines the other devas in beauty and in glory. When, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra manifests to the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, no deva in that assembly pays homage to him, or rises for him, or invites him to a seat. All, being silent and with hands joined in reverence, sit cross-legged, thinking: ‘On whichever deva’s seat Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra now wishes to sit, on that deva’s seat he will sit.’ And, venerable sir, on whichever deva’s seat Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra sits, that deva obtains a great experience of joy, that deva obtains a great experience of happiness. Just as, venerable sir, a Khattiya king, an anointed one, newly anointed to kingship, obtains a great experience of joy and a great experience of happiness, even so, venerable sir, on whichever deva’s seat Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra sits, that deva obtains a great experience of joy and a great experience of happiness. Then, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, knowing the serene confidence of the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, vanished and expressed his appreciation with these verses:”

‘Modanti vata bho devā, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammataṃ.

“The devas of Tāvatiṃsa, together with their Indra, truly rejoice, paying homage to the Tathāgata and to the excellent nature of the Dhamma.”

‘Nave deve ca passantā, vaṇṇavante yasassine;

Sugatasmiṃ brahmacariyaṃ, caritvāna idhāgate.

They rejoice, seeing also the new devas who have come here, possessing radiance and glory, after having lived the holy life under the Sugata.

‘Te aññe atirocanti, vaṇṇena yasasāyunā;

Sāvakā bhūripaññassa, visesūpagatā idha.

“Those disciples of the One of vast wisdom, having attained distinction here, outshine the other devas in beauty, glory, and lifespan.”

‘Idaṃ disvāna nandanti, tāvatiṃsā sahindakā;

Tathāgataṃ namassantā, dhammassa ca sudhammata’nti.

“Seeing this, the devas of Tāvatiṃsa, together with their Indra, rejoice, paying homage to the Tathāgata and to the excellent nature of the Dhamma.”

301. “Imamatthaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro abhāsittha. Imamatthaṃ, bhante[T 2.0260], brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhāsato aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato saro hoti vissaṭṭho ca viññeyyo ca mañju ca savanīyo ca bindu ca avisārī ca gambhīro ca ninnādī ca. Yathāparisaṃ kho pana, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro sarena viññāpeti, na cassa bahiddhā parisāya ghoso niccharati. Yassa kho pana, bhante, evaṃ aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgato saro hoti, so vuccati ‘brahmassaro’ti. Atha kho, bhante, devā tāvatiṃsā brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ etadavocuṃ [M 2.0184] – ‘sādhu, mahābrahme, etadeva mayaṃ saṅkhāya modāma; atthi [P 2.0228] ca sakkena devānamindena tassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhuccā vaṇṇā bhāsitā; te ca mayaṃ saṅkhāya modāmā’ti.

301. “Venerable sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra spoke these words. Venerable sir, when Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra speaks, his voice is endowed with eight factors: it is distinct, intelligible, sweet, pleasant to hear, rounded, not scattered, deep, and resonant. And, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra makes himself understood to the assembly according to its extent, yet his voice does not travel outside the assembly. Indeed, venerable sir, whoever possesses a voice endowed with these eight factors is called ‘one with a Brahmā-voice.’ Then, venerable sir, the Tāvatiṃsa devas said this to Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra: ‘Excellent, Great Brahmā! Having understood this very matter, we rejoice. And there are eight true qualities of that Blessed One spoken by Sakka, lord of the devas; and having understood those, we also rejoice.’”

Aṭṭha yathābhuccavaṇṇā

The Eight True Qualities

302. “Atha[V 2.0168], bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavoca – ‘sādhu, devānaminda, mayampi tassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe suṇeyyāmā’ti. ‘Evaṃ mahābrahme’ti kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe payirudāhāsi.

302. “Then, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra said this to Sakka, lord of the devas: ‘Good, lord of the devas! May we also hear those eight true qualities of the Blessed One.’ ‘So be it, Great Brahmā,’ replied Sakka, lord of the devas, to Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, and he proclaimed the eight true qualities of the Blessed One:”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññati, bhavaṃ mahābrahmā? Yāvañca so bhagavā bahujanahitāya paṭipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Evaṃ bahujanahitāya paṭipannaṃ bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

“‘What do you think, Great Brahmā? The Blessed One has practiced for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, and for the good, welfare, and happiness of devas and humans. We do not see a Teacher endowed with this factor—one who has thus practiced for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the good, for the welfare, and for the happiness of devas and humans—either in the past or at present, other than that Blessed One.’ (1)”

“Svākkhāto kho pana tena bhagavatā dhammo [T 2.0261] sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhi. Evaṃ opaneyyikassa dhammassa desetāraṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

“‘The Dhamma has been well proclaimed by that Blessed One; it is visible here and now, timeless, inviting one to come and see, onward-leading, and to be personally experienced by the wise. We do not see a Teacher endowed with this factor—one who is a proclaimer of such an onward-leading Dhamma—either in the past or at present, other than that Blessed One.’ (2)”

“Idaṃ kusala’nti kho pana tena bhagavatā supaññattaṃ, ‘idaṃ akusala’nti supaññattaṃ, ‘idaṃ sāvajjaṃ idaṃ anavajjaṃ, idaṃ sevitabbaṃ idaṃ na sevitabbaṃ, idaṃ hīnaṃ idaṃ paṇītaṃ, idaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāga’nti supaññattaṃ. Evaṃ kusalākusalasāvajjānavajjasevitabbāsevitabbahīnapaṇītakaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgānaṃ dhammānaṃ paññāpetāraṃ. Imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva [P 2.0229] atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

“‘“This is wholesome” has been well declared by that Blessed One; “this is unwholesome” has been well declared; “this is blameworthy, this is blameless; this should be cultivated, this should not be cultivated; this is inferior, this is superior; this has a dark part and a bright part” has been well declared. We do not see a Teacher endowed with this factor—one who is a declarer of these wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, to be cultivated and not to be cultivated, inferior and superior, dark and bright dhammas—either in the past or at present, other than that Blessed One.’ (3)”

“Supaññattā kho pana tena bhagavatā sāvakānaṃ nibbānagāminī paṭipadā saṃsandati nibbānañca paṭipadā ca. Seyyathāpi nāma gaṅgodakaṃ yamunodakena saṃsandati [M 2.0185] sameti, evameva supaññattā tena bhagavatā sāvakānaṃ nibbānagāminī paṭipadā saṃsandati nibbānañca paṭipadā ca. Evaṃ nibbānagāminiyā paṭipadāya paññāpetāraṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘The practice leading to Nibbāna has indeed been well declared by the Blessed One for his disciples, and Nibbāna and the practice are in accord. Just as the water of the Ganges accords and converges with the water of the Yamunā, even so the practice leading to Nibbāna, well declared by the Blessed One for his disciples, accords with Nibbāna. We do not see any Teacher endowed with this factor—one who declares the practice leading to Nibbāna—either in the past or at present, other than the Blessed One.

“Abhinipphanno [T 2.0262] kho pana tassa bhagavato lābho abhinipphanno siloko, yāva maññe khattiyā [V 2.0169] sampiyāyamānarūpā viharanti. Vigatamado kho pana so bhagavā āhāraṃ āhāreti. Evaṃ vigatamadaṃ āhāraṃ āharayamānaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘Gain has indeed been fully accomplished for the Blessed One, and renown has been fully accomplished; so much so, I think, that the nobles dwell holding him in great affection. And yet the Blessed One partakes of food free from intoxication. We do not see any Teacher endowed with this factor—one who partakes of food free from intoxication—either in the past or at present, other than the Blessed One.

“Laddhasahāyo kho pana so bhagavā sekhānañceva paṭipannānaṃ khīṇāsavānañca vusitavataṃ, te bhagavā apanujja ekārāmataṃ anuyutto viharati. Evaṃ ekārāmataṃ anuyuttaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘The Blessed One has indeed gained companions—both trainees who are practicing and those whose taints are destroyed who have lived the holy life—yet, setting them aside, the Blessed One dwells devoted to delight in solitude. We do not see any Teacher endowed with this factor—one devoted to delight in solitude—either in the past or at present, other than the Blessed One.

“Yathāvādī kho pana so bhagavā tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī; iti yathāvādī tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī. Evaṃ dhammānudhammappaṭippannaṃ imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā.

‘As the Blessed One speaks, so he acts; as he acts, so he speaks. Thus, as he speaks, so he acts; as he acts, so he speaks. We do not see any Teacher endowed with this factor—one who has practiced in accordance with the Dhamma—either in the past or at present, other than the Blessed One.

“Tiṇṇavicikiccho kho pana so bhagavā vigatakathaṃkatho pariyositasaṅkappo ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariyaṃ[P 2.0230]. Evaṃ tiṇṇavicikicchaṃ vigatakathaṃkathaṃ pariyositasaṅkappaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariyaṃ. Imināpaṅgena samannāgataṃ satthāraṃ neva atītaṃse samanupassāma, na panetarahi, aññatra tena bhagavatā’ti.

‘The Blessed One has indeed crossed over doubt, is free from perplexity, has his resolve fulfilled, and is disposed toward the fundamental holy life. We do not see any Teacher endowed with this factor—one who has crossed over doubt, is free from perplexity, has his resolve fulfilled, and is disposed toward the fundamental holy life—either in the past or at present, other than the Blessed One.’

303. “Ime kho, bhante, sakko devānamindo brahmuno sanaṅkumārassa bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe payirudāhāsi. Tena sudaṃ, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro attamano hoti pamudito pītisomanassajāto bhagavato aṭṭha yathābhucce vaṇṇe sutvā. Atha, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro oḷārikaṃ attabhāvaṃ abhinimminitvā kumāravaṇṇī hutvā pañcasikho devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ pāturahosi[T 2.0263]. So vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīdi. Seyyathāpi, bhante, balavā [M 2.0186] puriso supaccatthate vā pallaṅke same vā bhūmibhāge pallaṅkena nisīdeyya, evameva kho, bhante, brahmā sanaṅkumāro vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā ākāse antalikkhe pallaṅkena nisīditvā deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi –

303. “Venerable sir, these are the eight true qualities of the Blessed One that Sakka, lord of the devas, recited to Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra. And so, venerable sir, upon hearing the eight true qualities of the Blessed One, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra was gladdened, delighted, and filled with joy and happiness. Then, venerable sir, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra manifested a gross physical form, appeared as a youth with five topknots, and became visible before the devas of Tāvatiṃsa. He ascended into the air and sat cross-legged in the sky. Just as, venerable sir, a strong man might sit cross-legged on a well-spread couch or on level ground, even so did Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, having ascended into the air, sit cross-legged in the sky and address the devas of Tāvatiṃsa:

Govindabrāhmaṇavatthu

The Story of Govinda the Brahmin

304. “Taṃ kiṃ maññanti, bhonto devā tāvatiṃsā, yāva dīgharattaṃ mahāpaññova so bhagavā ahosi. Bhūtapubbaṃ, bho, rājā disampati nāma ahosi. Disampatissa rañño govindo [V 2.0170] nāma brāhmaṇo purohito ahosi. Disampatissa rañño reṇu nāma kumāro putto ahosi. Govindassa brāhmaṇassa jotipālo nāma māṇavo putto ahosi. Iti reṇu ca rājaputto jotipālo ca māṇavo aññe ca cha khattiyā iccete aṭṭha sahāyā ahesuṃ. Atha [P 2.0231] kho, bho, ahorattānaṃ accayena govindo brāhmaṇo kālamakāsi. Govinde brāhmaṇe kālaṅkate rājā disampati paridevesi – “yasmiṃ vata, bho, mayaṃ samaye govinde brāhmaṇe sabbakiccāni sammā vossajjitvā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārema, tasmiṃ no samaye govindo brāhmaṇo kālaṅkato”ti. Evaṃ vutte bho reṇu rājaputto rājānaṃ disampatiṃ etadavoca – “mā kho tvaṃ, deva, govinde brāhmaṇe kālaṅkate atibāḷhaṃ paridevesi. Atthi, deva, govindassa brāhmaṇassa jotipālo nāma māṇavo [T 2.0264] putto paṇḍitataro ceva pitarā, alamatthadasataro ceva pitarā; yepissa pitā atthe anusāsi, tepi jotipālasseva māṇavassa anusāsaniyā”ti. “Evaṃ kumārā”ti? “Evaṃ devā”ti.

304. ‘What do you think, venerable devas of Tāvatiṃsa, for how very long a time has that Blessed One been of great wisdom? Once upon a time, sirs, there was a king named Disampati. King Disampati had a brahmin purohita named Govinda. King Disampati had a son, a prince named Reṇu. The brahmin Govinda had a son, a young man named Jotipāla. Thus Prince Reṇu, the young man Jotipāla, and six other khattiyas—these eight were companions. Then, sirs, after some time had passed, the brahmin Govinda died. When the brahmin Govinda had died, King Disampati lamented: “Alas, sirs, at the very time when, having duly entrusted all duties to the brahmin Govinda, we were provided with, endowed with, and enjoyed the five strands of sensual pleasure, at that very time our brahmin Govinda has died!” When this was said, sirs, Prince Reṇu said this to King Disampati: “Do not, Your Majesty, lament so excessively over the death of the brahmin Govinda. Your Majesty, the brahmin Govinda has a son, the young man Jotipāla, who is wiser than his father and more capable of discerning what is beneficial than his father. And whatever matters his father instructed on, the young man Jotipāla is also fit to give instruction on them.” “Is that so, Prince?” “It is so, Your Majesty.”’

Mahāgovindavatthu

The Story of Mahāgovinda

305. “Atha kho, bho, rājā disampati aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, yena jotipālo nāma māṇavo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘bhavamatthu bhavantaṃ jotipālaṃ, rājā disampati bhavantaṃ jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ āmantayati, rājā disampati bhoto jotipālassa māṇavassa dassanakāmo’”ti. “Evaṃ, devā”ti kho, bho, so puriso disampatissa rañño paṭissutvā yena [M 2.0187] jotipālo māṇavo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ etadavoca – “bhavamatthu bhavantaṃ jotipālaṃ, rājā disampati bhavantaṃ jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ āmantayati[P 2.0232], rājā disampati bhoto jotipālassa māṇavassa dassanakāmo”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho bho jotipālo māṇavo tassa purisassa paṭissutvā yena rājā disampati tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā disampatinā raññā saddhiṃ sammodi; sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho, bho, jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ rājā disampati etadavoca – “anusāsatu no bhavaṃ jotipālo, mā no bhavaṃ jotipālo anusāsaniyā paccabyāhāsi. Pettike taṃ ṭhāne ṭhapessāmi, govindiye [T 2.0265] abhisiñcissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho, bho, so jotipālo māṇavo disampatissa rañño paccassosi. Atha kho, bho, rājā disampati jotipālaṃ māṇavaṃ govindiye abhisiñci, taṃ pettike ṭhāne ṭhapesi. Abhisitto jotipālo māṇavo govindiye pettike ṭhāne ṭhapito yepissa pitā atthe anusāsi tepi atthe anusāsati, yepissa pitā atthe nānusāsi, tepi [V 2.0171] atthe anusāsati; yepissa pitā kammante abhisambhosi, tepi kammante abhisambhoti, yepissa pitā kammante nābhisambhosi, tepi kammante abhisambhoti. Tamenaṃ manussā evamāhaṃsu – “govindo vata, bho, brāhmaṇo, mahāgovindo vata, bho, brāhmaṇo”ti. Iminā kho evaṃ, bho, pariyāyena jotipālassa māṇavassa govindo mahāgovindotveva samaññā udapādi.

305. Then, sirs, King Disampati addressed a certain man: “Come, good man, go to where the young man Jotipāla is. Having approached him, say this to the young man Jotipāla: ‘May it be well with the venerable Jotipāla. King Disampati summons the venerable Jotipāla. King Disampati wishes to see the venerable Jotipāla.’” ‘Yes, Your Majesty,’ that man replied to King Disampati, sirs, and went to where the young man Jotipāla was. Having approached him, he said this to the young man Jotipāla: ‘May it be well with the venerable Jotipāla. King Disampati summons the venerable Jotipāla. King Disampati wishes to see the venerable Jotipāla.’ ‘Very well, sir,’ replied the young man Jotipāla to that man, sirs, and went to where King Disampati was. Having approached King Disampati, he exchanged greetings with him. After concluding a pleasant and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. To the young man Jotipāla seated to one side, sirs, King Disampati said this: “Let the venerable Jotipāla instruct us. May the venerable Jotipāla not refuse to instruct us. I will establish you in your father’s position and anoint you into the office of Govinda.” ‘Very well, sir,’ the young man Jotipāla assented to King Disampati, sirs. Then, sirs, King Disampati anointed the young man Jotipāla into the office of Govinda and established him in his father’s position. Having been anointed into the office of Govinda and established in his father’s position, Jotipāla instructed on the matters his father had instructed on, and he also instructed on matters his father had not instructed on. He managed the duties his father had managed, and he also managed duties his father had not managed. People then said of him: “Indeed, sirs, a Govinda the brahmin! Indeed, sirs, a Mahāgovinda the brahmin!” It was in this way, sirs, that the designation ‘Govinda, Mahāgovinda’ arose for the young man Jotipāla.

Rajjasaṃvibhajanaṃ

The Division of the Kingdom

306. “Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena te cha khattiyā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te cha khattiye etadavoca – “disampati kho, bho, rājā jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako addhagato [P 2.0233] vayoanuppatto, ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitaṃ? Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ disampatimhi raññe kālaṅkate rājakattāro reṇuṃ rājaputtaṃ rajje abhisiñceyyuṃ. Āyantu, bhonto, yena reṇu rājaputto tenupasaṅkamatha; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājaputtaṃ evaṃ vadetha – “mayaṃ kho bhoto reṇussa sahāyā piyā manāpā appaṭikūlā, yaṃsukho bhavaṃ [M 2.0188] taṃsukhā mayaṃ, yaṃdukkho bhavaṃ taṃdukkhā mayaṃ. Disampati kho, bho, rājā jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto, ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitaṃ? Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ disampatimhi raññe kālaṅkate rājakattāro bhavantaṃ reṇuṃ rajje abhisiñceyyuṃ. Sace bhavaṃ reṇu rajjaṃ labhetha, saṃvibhajetha no rajjenā”ti. “Evaṃ bho”ti kho, bho, te cha khattiyā mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa paṭissutvā yena reṇu rājaputto tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājaputtaṃ etadavocuṃ – “mayaṃ kho bhoto reṇussa sahāyā piyā manāpā appaṭikūlā[T 2.0266]; yaṃsukho bhavaṃ taṃsukhā mayaṃ, yaṃdukkho bhavaṃ taṃdukkhā mayaṃ. Disampati kho, bho, rājā jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto, ko nu kho pana bho jānāti jīvitaṃ? Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ disampatimhi raññe kālaṅkate rājakattāro bhavantaṃ reṇuṃ rajje abhisiñceyyuṃ. Sace bhavaṃ reṇu rajjaṃ labhetha, saṃvibhajetha no rajjenā”ti. “Ko nu kho, bho, añño mama vijite sukho bhavetha sukhā bhaveyyātha (ka.), sukhaṃ bhaveyyātha, sukhamedheyyātha (sī. pī.),sukha medhetha (?), aññatra bhavantebhi? Sacāhaṃ, bho, rajjaṃ labhissāmi, saṃvibhajissāmi vo rajjenā’”ti.

306. Then, sirs, the brahmin Mahāgovinda approached those six princes and said to them: 'Sirs, King Disampati is old, aged, mature, has lived a long life, and has reached his final years. Who, sirs, can know of life? It is possible that when King Disampati passes away, the king-makers will anoint Prince Reṇu to the kingship. Come, sirs, approach Prince Reṇu and say this to him: “We are friends of the honorable Reṇu, dear, beloved, and not disagreeable. When you are happy, we are happy; when you are suffering, we are suffering. Sir, King Disampati is old, aged, mature, has lived a long life, and has reached his final years. Who, sirs, can know of life? It is possible that when King Disampati passes away, the king-makers will anoint you, the honorable Reṇu, to the kingship. If you, the honorable Reṇu, should obtain the kingdom, you should divide the kingdom with us.”' 'Very well, sir,' said those six princes, assenting to the word of the brahmin Mahāgovinda. They then approached Prince Reṇu and said this to him: 'We are friends of the honorable Reṇu, dear, beloved, and not disagreeable. When you are happy, we are happy; when you are suffering, we are suffering. Sir, King Disampati is old, aged, mature, has lived a long life, and has reached his final years. Who, sirs, can know of life? It is possible that when King Disampati passes away, the king-makers will anoint you, the honorable Reṇu, to the kingship. If you, the honorable Reṇu, should obtain the kingdom, you should divide the kingdom with us.' 'Who else, sirs, in my domain would be happy, other than you? If I, sirs, obtain the kingdom, I will divide the kingdom with you.'

307. “Atha [P 2.0234] kho, bho, ahorattānaṃ accayena rājā disampati kālamakāsi. Disampatimhi raññe kālaṅkate rājakattāro reṇuṃ rājaputtaṃ rajje abhisiñciṃsu. Abhisitto reṇu rajjena [T 2.0267] pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena te cha khattiyā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te cha khattiye etadavoca [V 2.0172] – “disampati kho, bho, rājā kālaṅkato. Abhisitto reṇu rajjena pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti. Ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti, madanīyā kāmā? Āyantu, bhonto, yena reṇu rājā tenupasaṅkamatha; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājānaṃ evaṃ vadetha – disampati kho, bho, rājā kālaṅkato, abhisitto bhavaṃ reṇu rajjena, sarati bhavaṃ taṃ vacana’”nti?

307. Then, sirs, with the passing of days and nights, King Disampati died. When King Disampati had passed away, the king-makers consecrated Prince Reṇu to the kingship. Once consecrated to the kingship, King Reṇu enjoyed himself, being endowed and furnished with the five strands of sensual pleasure. Then, sirs, the brahmin Mahāgovinda approached those six princes and said to them: 'Sirs, King Disampati has passed away. King Reṇu has been consecrated to the kingship and enjoys himself, being endowed and furnished with the five strands of sensual pleasure. Who, sirs, can know? Sensual pleasures are intoxicating. Come, sirs, approach King Reṇu and say this to him: “Sir, King Disampati has passed away, and you, the honorable Reṇu, have been consecrated to the kingship. Do you remember that promise?”'

308. “‘Evaṃ[M 2.0189], bho”ti kho, bho, te cha khattiyā mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa paṭissutvā yena reṇu rājā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājānaṃ etadavocuṃ – “disampati kho, bho, rājā kālaṅkato, abhisitto bhavaṃ reṇu rajjena, sarati bhavaṃ taṃ vacana”nti? “Sarāmahaṃ, bho, taṃ vacanaṃ vacananti (syā. ka.). Ko nu kho, bho, pahoti imaṃ mahāpathaviṃ uttarena āyataṃ dakkhiṇena sakaṭamukhaṃ sattadhā samaṃ suvibhattaṃ vibhajitu”nti? “Ko nu kho, bho, añño pahoti, aññatra mahāgovindena brāhmaṇenā”ti? Atha kho, bho, reṇu rājā aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, yena mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ evaṃ vadehi – ‘rājā taṃ, bhante, reṇu āmantetī’”ti. “Evaṃ [P 2.0235] devā”ti kho, bho, so puriso reṇussa rañño paṭissutvā [T 2.0268] yena mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “rājā taṃ, bhante, reṇu āmantetī”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tassa purisassa paṭissutvā yena reṇu rājā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā reṇunā raññā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho, bho, mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ reṇu rājā etadavoca – “etu, bhavaṃ govindo, imaṃ mahāpathaviṃ uttarena āyataṃ dakkhiṇena sakaṭamukhaṃ sattadhā samaṃ suvibhattaṃ vibhajatū”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo reṇussa rañño paṭissutvā imaṃ mahāpathaviṃ uttarena āyataṃ dakkhiṇena sakaṭamukhaṃ sattadhā samaṃ suvibhattaṃ vibhaji. Sabbāni sakaṭamukhāni paṭṭhapesi aṭṭhapesi (sī. pī.). Tatra sudaṃ majjhe reṇussa rañño janapado hoti.

308. “Very well, sir,” said those six princes, assenting to the word of the brahmin Mahāgovinda. They then approached King Reṇu and said this to him: “Sir, King Disampati has passed away, and you, the honorable Reṇu, have been consecrated to the kingship. Do you remember that word?” “I remember that word, sirs. But who, sirs, is able to divide this great earth—long towards the north and shaped like the front of a cart towards the south—into seven equal, well-divided parts?” “Who else, sir, is able, other than the brahmin Mahāgovinda?” Then, sirs, King Reṇu addressed a certain man: “Come, good man, approach the brahmin Mahāgovinda and say this to him: ‘The king, venerable sir, King Reṇu, summons you.’” “Very well, Your Majesty,” said that man, assenting to King Reṇu’s word. He then approached the brahmin Mahāgovinda and said this to him: “The king, venerable sir, King Reṇu, summons you.” “Very well, sir,” said the brahmin Mahāgovinda, assenting to that man’s word. He then approached King Reṇu and exchanged joyful greetings with him. Having concluded the pleasant and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King Reṇu said this to the brahmin Mahāgovinda: “Come, honorable Govinda, divide this great earth—long towards the north and shaped like the front of a cart towards the south—into seven equal, well-divided parts.” “Very well, sir,” said the brahmin Mahāgovinda, assenting to King Reṇu’s word, and he divided this great earth—long towards the north and shaped like the front of a cart towards the south—into seven equal, well-divided parts. He established all the kingdoms shaped like the front of a cart. And there, in the middle, was the country of King Reṇu.

309. Dantapuraṃ kaliṅgānaṃ kāliṅgānaṃ (syā. pī. ka.), assakānañca potanaṃ.

309. Dantapura of the Kaliṅgas, and Potana of the Assakas.

Mahesayaṃ māhissati (sī. syā. pī.) avantīnaṃ, sovīrānañca rorukaṃ.

Mahesaya of the Avantīs, and Roruka of the Sovīras.

Mithilā ca videhānaṃ, campā aṅgesu māpitā;

Bārāṇasī ca kāsīnaṃ, ete govindamāpitāti.

Mithilā of the Videhas, Campā founded among the Aṅgas; Bārāṇasī of the Kāsīs—these were founded by Govinda.

310. “Atha [M 2.0190][V 2.0173][P 2.0236] kho, bho, te cha khattiyā yathāsakena lābhena attamanā ahesuṃ paripuṇṇasaṅkappā – “yaṃ vata no ahosi icchitaṃ, yaṃ ākaṅkhitaṃ, yaṃ adhippetaṃ, yaṃ abhipatthitaṃ, taṃ no laddha”nti.

310. Then, sirs, those six princes were pleased with their respective gains, their intentions fulfilled: “Indeed, what we wished for, what we hoped for, what we intended, what we yearned for—that we have obtained.”

“Sattabhū [T 2.0269] brahmadatto ca, vessabhū bharato saha;

Reṇu dve dhataraṭṭhā ca, tadāsuṃ satta bhāradhā’ti.

Sattabhū and Brahmadatta, Vessabhū together with Bharata, Reṇu and the two Dhataraṭṭhas; at that time, these seven were the burden-bearers.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The first recitation section is concluded.

Kittisaddaabbhuggamanaṃ

The Rise of Widespread Fame

311. “Atha kho, bho, te cha khattiyā yena mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavocuṃ – “yathā kho bhavaṃ govindo reṇussa rañño sahāyo piyo manāpo appaṭikūlo. Evameva kho bhavaṃ govindo amhākampi sahāyo piyo manāpo appaṭikūlo, anusāsatu no bhavaṃ govindo; mā no bhavaṃ govindo anusāsaniyā paccabyāhāsī”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tesaṃ channaṃ khattiyānaṃ paccassosi. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo satta ca rājāno khattiye muddhāvasitte rajje muddhābhisitte rajjena (syā.) anusāsi, satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsāle satta ca nhātakasatāni mante vācesi.

311. Then, sirs, those six khattiyas approached the brahmin Mahāgovinda. Having approached, they said to the brahmin Mahāgovinda: “Just as the venerable Govinda is King Reṇu’s friend—dear, beloved, and agreeable—so too, let the venerable Govinda be our friend—dear, beloved, and agreeable. Let the venerable Govinda instruct us; may the venerable Govinda not refuse to instruct us.” “So be it, sirs,” the brahmin Mahāgovinda assented to those six khattiyas. Then, sirs, the brahmin Mahāgovinda instructed the seven anointed khattiya kings in kingship, and he taught the mantras to seven brahmin magnates and seven hundred ritual bathers.

312. “Atha [P 2.0237] kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa aparena samayena evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchi abbhuggañchi (sī. pī.) – “sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti sallapati mantetī”ti. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – “mayhaṃ kho evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti [T 2.0270] sallapati mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi, na brahmunā sallapāmi[M 2.0191], na brahmunā mantemi. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ [V 2.0174] jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati brahmunā sākaccheti brahmunā sallapati brahmunā mantetī’ti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyeyyaṃ, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyeyya”nti.

312. Then, sirs, after some time, this good report spread about the brahmin Mahāgovinda: “The brahmin Mahāgovinda sees Brahmā in person; the brahmin Mahāgovinda confers, converses, and consults with Brahmā.” Then, sirs, this thought occurred to the brahmin Mahāgovinda: “This good report has spread about me: ‘The brahmin Mahāgovinda sees Brahmā in person; the brahmin Mahāgovinda confers, converses, and consults with Brahmā.’ But I do not see Brahmā, nor do I confer, converse, or consult with Brahmā. However, I have heard this from brahmins who were aged, old, teachers of teachers, and speakers of tradition: ‘Whoever lives in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and develops the meditation on compassion, he sees Brahmā, confers, converses, and consults with Brahmā.’ It would be good if I were to live in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and develop the meditation on compassion.”

313. “Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena reṇu rājā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājānaṃ etadavoca – “mayhaṃ kho, bho, evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti sallapati mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ, bho, brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi, na brahmunā sallapāmi, na brahmunā mantemi. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati, brahmunā sākaccheti brahmunā sallapati brahmunā mantetī’ti. Icchāmahaṃ, bho, vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyituṃ, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyituṃ; namhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo aññatra ekena bhattābhihārenā”ti. “Yassadāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ maññatī”ti.

313. Then, O devas, the brahmin Mahāgovinda approached King Reṇu. Having approached, he said to King Reṇu: ‘This good report, Your Majesty, has spread about me: “The brahmin Mahāgovinda sees Brahmā in person; the brahmin Mahāgovinda confers, converses, and consults with Brahmā.” But I, Your Majesty, do not see Brahmā, nor do I confer, converse, or consult with Brahmā. However, I have heard this from brahmins who were aged, old, teachers of teachers, and speakers of tradition: “Whoever lives in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and develops the meditation on compassion, he sees Brahmā, confers, converses, and consults with Brahmā.” I wish, Your Majesty, to live in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and to develop the meditation on compassion. I am not to be approached by anyone, except for one person bringing my meal.’ The king replied: ‘Let the venerable Govinda do so at the time he deems fit.’

314. “Atha [P 2.0238] kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena [T 2.0271] te cha khattiyā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te cha khattiye etadavoca – “mayhaṃ kho, bho, evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti sallapati mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ, bho, brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi, na brahmunā sallapāmi, na brahmunā mantemi. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ, ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati brahmunā sākaccheti brahmunā sallapati brahmunā mantetī’ti. Icchāmahaṃ, bho, vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyituṃ, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyituṃ; namhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo aññatra ekena bhattābhihārenā”ti. “Yassadāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ maññatī’”ti.

314. Then, O devas, the brahmin Mahāgovinda approached those six khattiyas. Having approached, he said to those six khattiyas: ‘This good report, Your Majesties, has spread about me: “The brahmin Mahāgovinda sees Brahmā in person; the brahmin Mahāgovinda confers, converses, and consults with Brahmā.” But I, Your Majesties, do not see Brahmā, nor do I confer, converse, or consult with Brahmā. However, I have heard this from brahmins who were aged, old, teachers of teachers, and speakers of tradition: “Whoever lives in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and develops the meditation on compassion, he sees Brahmā, confers, converses, and consults with Brahmā.” I wish, Your Majesties, to live in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and to develop the meditation on compassion. I am not to be approached by anyone, except for one person bringing my meal.’ Those six khattiyas replied: ‘Let the venerable Govinda do so at the time he deems fit.’

315. “Atha [M 2.0192] kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena te satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā satta ca nhātakasatāni tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsāle satta ca nhātakasatāni etadavoca – “mayhaṃ kho, bho, evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti sallapati mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ, bho, brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi, na brahmunā [V 2.0175] sallapāmi, na brahmunā mantemi. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ [T 2.0272] mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati, brahmunā sākaccheti, brahmunā sallapati, brahmunā mantetī’ti. Tena hi, bho, yathāsute yathāpariyatte mante vitthārena sajjhāyaṃ karotha, aññamaññañca mante vācetha; icchāmahaṃ, bho, vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyituṃ, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyituṃ; namhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo aññatra ekena bhattābhihārenā”ti. “Yassa dāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ maññatī”ti.

315. Then, O devas, the brahmin Mahāgovinda approached those seven brahmins of great wealth and the seven hundred initiates. Having approached, he said to the seven brahmins of great wealth and the seven hundred initiates: ‘Sirs, this good report has spread about me: “The brahmin Mahāgovinda sees Brahmā in person; the brahmin Mahāgovinda confers, converses, and consults with Brahmā.” But, sirs, I do not see Brahmā, nor do I confer, converse, or consult with Brahmā. However, I have heard this from brahmins who were aged, old, teachers of teachers, and speakers of tradition: “Whoever lives in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and develops the meditation on compassion, he sees Brahmā, confers, converses, and consults with Brahmā.” Therefore, sirs, recite the sacred texts in detail as you have heard and learned them, and teach the sacred texts to one another. I wish, sirs, to live in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and to develop the meditation on compassion. I am not to be approached by anyone, except for the one who brings my meal.’ They replied: ‘Let the venerable Govinda do so at the time he deems fit.’”

316. “Atha [P 2.0239] kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena cattārīsā bhariyā sādisiyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā cattārīsā bhariyā sādisiyo etadavoca – “mayhaṃ kho, bhotī, evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ passati, sakkhi mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmunā sākaccheti sallapati mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ, bhotī, brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi, na brahmunā sallapāmi, na brahmunā mantemi. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati, brahmunā sākaccheti, brahmunā sallapati, brahmunā mantetīti, icchāmahaṃ, bhotī, vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyituṃ, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyituṃ; namhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo aññatra ekena bhattābhihārenā”ti. “Yassa dāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ [T 2.0273] maññatī’”ti.

316. Then, O devas, the brahmin Mahāgovinda approached his forty wives of similar status. Having approached, he said to his forty wives of similar status: ‘Ladies, this good report has spread about me: “The brahmin Mahāgovinda sees Brahmā in person; the brahmin Mahāgovinda confers, converses, and consults with Brahmā.” But, ladies, I do not see Brahmā, nor do I confer, converse, or consult with Brahmā. However, I have heard this from brahmins who were aged, old, teachers of teachers, and speakers of tradition: “Whoever lives in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and develops the meditation on compassion, sees Brahmā, confers, converses, and consults with Brahmā.” I wish, ladies, to live in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and to develop the meditation on compassion; I am not to be approached by anyone, except for the one who brings my meal.’ His wives replied: ‘Let the venerable Govinda do so at the time he deems fit.’”

317. “Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo puratthimena nagarassa navaṃ sandhāgāraṃ kārāpetvā vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyi, karuṇaṃ [M 2.0193] jhānaṃ jhāyi; nāssudha koci upasaṅkamati upasaṅkami (pī.) aññatra ekena bhattābhihārena. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa catunnaṃ māsānaṃ accayena ahudeva ukkaṇṭhanā ahu paritassanā – “sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ vuddhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘yo vassike cattāro māse paṭisallīyati, karuṇaṃ jhānaṃ jhāyati, so brahmānaṃ passati, brahmunā sākaccheti brahmunā sallapati brahmunā mantetī’ti. Na kho panāhaṃ brahmānaṃ passāmi, na brahmunā sākacchemi na brahmunā sallapāmi na brahmunā mantemī’”ti.

317. “Then, sirs, the brahmin Mahāgovinda had a new assembly hall built to the east of the city. There he lived in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and cultivated the meditation on compassion. No one approached him there, except for the one who brought his meal. Then, sirs, after four months had passed, discontent and a yearning for Brahmā arose in the brahmin Mahāgovinda: ‘I have heard it said by the aged, mature brahmins, the teachers of teachers: “Whoever lives in seclusion for the four months of the rainy season and cultivates the meditation on compassion, he sees Brahmā, converses, talks, and consults with Brahmā.” But I do not see Brahmā, nor do I converse, talk, or consult with Brahmā.’”

Brahmunā sākacchā

Conversation with Brahmā

318. “Atha [V 2.0176] kho, bho, brahmā sanaṅkumāro mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya [P 2.0240] seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva, brahmaloke antarahito mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa sammukhe pāturahosi. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa ahudeva bhayaṃ ahu chambhitattaṃ ahu lomahaṃso yathā taṃ adiṭṭhapubbaṃ rūpaṃ disvā. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo bhīto saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

318. “Then, sirs, Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra, having known with his own mind the thought-reflection in the mind of the brahmin Mahāgovinda—just as a strong man might stretch out his bent arm or bend his outstretched arm—so he vanished from the Brahmā world and appeared in the presence of the brahmin Mahāgovinda. Then, sirs, fear, trembling, and his hair standing on end indeed arose in the brahmin Mahāgovinda, as happens on seeing a form never seen before. Then, sirs, the brahmin Mahāgovinda, frightened, agitated, and with his hair standing on end, addressed Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra in verse:

“‘Vaṇṇavā [T 2.0274] yasavā sirimā, ko nu tvamasi mārisa;

Ajānantā taṃ pucchāma, kathaṃ jānemu taṃ maya”nti.

“‘Possessed of beauty, glory, and majesty, who might you be, sir? Not knowing, we ask you; how may we know you?’”

“Maṃ ve kumāraṃ jānanti, brahmaloke sanantanaṃ sanantica (ka.);

Sabbe jānanti maṃ devā, evaṃ govinda jānahi”.

“‘In the Brahmā world, they know me as the eternal Youth. All the gods know me; thus, Govinda, you should know me.’”

“‘Āsanaṃ udakaṃ pajjaṃ, madhusākañca madhupākañca (sī. syā. pī.) brahmuno;

Agghe bhavantaṃ pucchāma, agghaṃ kurutu no bhavaṃ”.

“‘A seat, water, ointment for the feet, and sweet greens are offered for a Brahmā. We offer these items of hospitality to the venerable one; may the venerable one accept our hospitality.’”

“Paṭiggaṇhāma te agghaṃ, yaṃ tvaṃ govinda bhāsasi;

Diṭṭhadhammahitatthāya, samparāya sukhāya ca;

Katāvakāso pucchassu, yaṃ kiñci abhipatthita”nti.

“‘We accept your hospitality, Govinda, that which you have offered. An opportunity has been made; ask whatever you desire for your welfare in this present life and for happiness in the life to come.’”

319. “Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – “katāvakāso khomhi brahmunā sanaṅkumārena. Kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ [M 2.0194] puccheyyaṃ diṭṭhadhammikaṃ vā atthaṃ samparāyikaṃ vā’ti? Atha [P 2.0241] kho, bho, mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa etadahosi – ‘kusalo kho ahaṃ diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ atthānaṃ, aññepi maṃ diṭṭhadhammikaṃ atthaṃ pucchanti. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ samparāyikaññeva atthaṃ puccheyya’nti. Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

319. “Then, sirs, this thought occurred to the brahmin Mahāgovinda: ‘An opportunity has been made for me by Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra. What now should I ask Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra? A matter concerning the present life, or one concerning the life to come?’ Then, sirs, this thought occurred to the brahmin Mahāgovinda: ‘I am skilled in matters concerning the present life, and others also ask me about matters concerning the present life. What if I were to ask Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra only about a matter concerning the life to come?’ Then, sirs, the brahmin Mahāgovinda addressed Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra in verse:”

“Pucchāmi [V 2.0177] brahmānaṃ sanaṅkumāraṃ,

Kaṅkhī akaṅkhiṃ paravediyesu;

Katthaṭṭhito kimhi ca sikkhamāno,

Pappoti [T 2.0275] macco amataṃ brahmaloka”nti.

“I, being doubtful, ask the undoubting Brahmā Sanaṅkumāra concerning matters to be known by others: Wherein established and in what training, does a mortal attain the deathless Brahmā world?”

“Hitvā mamattaṃ manujesu brahme,

Ekodibhūto karuṇedhimutto karuṇādhimutto (sī. syā. pī.);

Nirāmagandho virato methunasmā,

Etthaṭṭhito ettha ca sikkhamāno;

Pappoti macco amataṃ brahmaloka”nti.

“O Brahmin, having abandoned possessiveness among humans, being one who dwells alone, intent upon compassion, free from the raw scent, abstaining from sexual intercourse; established in this and training in this, a mortal attains the deathless Brahmā world.”

320. “Hitvā mamatta’nti ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. Idhekacco appaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya mahantaṃ vā bhogakkhandhaṃ pahāya appaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya mahantaṃ vā ñātiparivaṭṭaṃ pahāya kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, ‘iti hitvā mamatta’nti ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. ‘Ekodibhūto’ti [P 2.0242] ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. Idhekacco vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ, iti ekodibhūto’ti ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. ‘Karuṇedhimutto’ti ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. Idhekacco karuṇāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadhotiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ karuṇāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena [T 2.0276] averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Iti ‘karuṇedhimutto’ti ahaṃ bhoto ājānāmi. Āmagandhe ca kho ahaṃ bhoto bhāsamānassa na ājānāmi.

320. “I understand from you, sir, ‘having abandoned possessiveness.’ Here, someone, having given up a small or large amount of wealth, having given up a small or large circle of relatives, having shaved off hair and beard, having put on ochre robes, goes forth from the household life into homelessness. Thus I understand from you, sir, ‘having abandoned possessiveness.’ I understand from you, sir, ‘being one who dwells alone.’ Here, someone resorts to a secluded dwelling: a forest, the foot of a tree, a mountain, a ravine, a mountain cave, a charnel ground, a jungle thicket, an open space, or a heap of straw. Thus I understand from you, sir, ‘being one who dwells alone.’ I understand from you, sir, ‘intent upon compassion.’ Here, someone dwells pervading one direction with a mind imbued with compassion, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all, one dwells pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with compassion—vast, exalted, measureless, without hostility, and without ill will. Thus I understand from you, sir, ‘intent upon compassion.’ But as for the ‘raw scent’ you speak of, sir, that I do not understand.”

“Ke [M 2.0195] āmagandhā manujesu brahme,

Ete avidvā idha brūhi dhīra;

Kenāvaṭā kenāvuṭā (syā.) vāti pajā kurutu kururū (syā.), kuruṭṭharū (pī.), kurūru (?),

Āpāyikā nivutabrahmalokā”ti.

“O Brahmā, what are the raw scents among humans? Being ignorant of these, O wise one, speak of them here. Enveloped by what does this generation emit a stench, bound for the plane of misery, with the Brahmā world obstructed?”

“Kodho [P 2.0243] mosavajjaṃ nikati ca dubbho,

Kadariyatā atimāno usūyā;

Icchā [V 2.0178] vivicchā paraheṭhanā ca,

Lobho ca doso ca mado ca moho;

Etesu yuttā anirāmagandhā,

Āpāyikā nivutabrahmalokā”ti.

“Anger, falsehood, deceit, and treachery; avarice, conceit, and envy; craving, stinginess, and harming others; greed, hatred, pride, and delusion—beings yoked to these are not free from the raw scent. They are bound for the plane of misery, with the Brahmā world obstructed.”

“Yathā kho ahaṃ bhoto āmagandhe bhāsamānassa ājānāmi. Te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā. Pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya”nti. “Yassadāni bhavaṃ govindo kālaṃ maññatī”ti.

“Just as I understand from you, sir, as you speak of the raw scents, they are not easy to dispel for one dwelling at home. I shall go forth, sir, from the household life into homelessness.” “Let Master Govinda now do as he deems the time is right.”

Reṇurājaāmantanā

Addressing King Reṇu

321. “Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena reṇu rājā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā reṇuṃ rājānaṃ etadavoca – “aññaṃ dāni bhavaṃ purohitaṃ pariyesatu, yo bhoto rajjaṃ anusāsissati. Icchāmahaṃ, bho[T 2.0277], agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā. Pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya”nti.

321. “Then, sirs, the brahmin Mahāgovinda approached King Reṇu. Having approached, he said to King Reṇu: ‘Now, Your Majesty, seek another chaplain who will instruct your kingdom. I wish, sir, to go forth from the household life into homelessness. For as I have heard from Brahmā who speaks of the stench of the raw, these are not easily eradicated by one dwelling in a house. I will go forth, sir, from the household life into homelessness.’”

“Āmantayāmi rājānaṃ, reṇuṃ bhūmipatiṃ ahaṃ;

Tvaṃ pajānassu rajjena, nāhaṃ porohicce rame”.

“I address the king, Reṇu, lord of the earth. Attend to your kingdom; I no longer delight in the office of chaplain.”

“Sace te ūnaṃ kāmehi, ahaṃ paripūrayāmi te;

Yo taṃ hiṃsati vāremi, bhūmisenāpati ahaṃ;

Tuvaṃ pitā ahaṃ putto, mā no govinda pājahi” pājehi (aṭṭhakathāyaṃ saṃvaṇṇitapāṭhantaraṃ).

“If you are deficient in sensual pleasures, I will fulfill them for you. Whoever harms you, I will restrain; I am the sovereign of this land. You are the father, I am the son; Govinda, do not abandon us.”

“Namatthi ūnaṃ kāmehi, hiṃsitā me na vijjati;

Amanussavaco sutvā, tasmāhaṃ na gahe rame”.

“I have no deficiency in sensual pleasures, nor is there anyone who harms me. Having heard the word of a non-human, therefore I do not delight in a home.”

“Amanusso [M 2.0196][P 2.0244] kathaṃvaṇṇo, kiṃ te atthaṃ abhāsatha;

Yañca sutvā jahāsi no, gehe amhe ca kevalī”.

“What was the appearance of that non-human? What meaning did he speak to you? Having heard which, you abandon our homes, and us, and everyone entirely.”

“Upavutthassa [V 2.0179] me pubbe, yiṭṭhukāmassa me sato;

Aggi pajjalito āsi, kusapattaparitthato”.

“Formerly, when I had completed my solitary retreat and was desirous of making an offering, a fire was kindled, spread with kusa grass.”

“Tato me brahmā pāturahu, brahmalokā sanantano;

So me pañhaṃ viyākāsi, taṃ sutvā na gahe rame”.

“Then Brahmā Sanantana appeared to me from the Brahmā world. He answered my question, and having heard that, I do not delight in a home.”

“Saddahāmi ahaṃ bhoto, yaṃ tvaṃ govinda bhāsasi;

Amanussavaco sutvā, kathaṃ vattetha aññathā.

“Venerable Govinda, I have faith in your words. Having heard the word of a non-human, how could one act otherwise?”

“Te taṃ anuvattissāma, satthā govinda no bhavaṃ;

Maṇi [T 2.0278] yathā veḷuriyo, akāco vimalo subho;

Evaṃ suddhā carissāma, govindassānusāsane”ti.

“We will follow you; venerable Govinda, be our teacher. As a beryl gem—smooth, stainless, and splendid—so shall we live purely under Govinda’s instruction.”

“‘Sace bhavaṃ govindo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissati, mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma. Atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī”ti.

“If the venerable Govinda goes forth from the household life into homelessness, we too will go forth from the household life into homelessness. Then whatever your destination, that will be our destination.”

Cha khattiyaāmantanā

Addressing the Six Khattiyas

322. “Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena te cha khattiyā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te cha khattiye etadavoca – “aññaṃ dāni bhavanto purohitaṃ pariyesantu, yo bhavantānaṃ rajje anusāsissati. Icchāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā. Pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya”nti. Atha kho, bho, te cha khattiyā ekamantaṃ apakkamma evaṃ [P 2.0245] samacintesuṃ – “ime kho brāhmaṇā nāma dhanaluddhā; yaṃnūna mayaṃ mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ dhanena sikkheyyāmā”ti. Te mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – “saṃvijjati kho, bho, imesu sattasu rajjesu pahūtaṃ sāpateyyaṃ, tato bhoto yāvatakena attho, tāvatakaṃ āharīyata”nti. “Alaṃ, bho, mamapidaṃ pahūtaṃ sāpateyyaṃ bhavantānaṃyeva vāhasā. Tamahaṃ sabbaṃ pahāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmi. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ [M 2.0197] ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya”nti. Atha kho, bho, te cha khattiyā ekamantaṃ apakkamma evaṃ samacintesuṃ [T 2.0279] – “ime [V 2.0180] kho brāhmaṇā nāma itthiluddhā; yaṃnūna mayaṃ mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ itthīhi sikkheyyāmā”ti. Te mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – “saṃvijjanti kho, bho, imesu sattasu rajjesu pahūtā itthiyo, tato bhoto yāvatikāhi attho, tāvatikā ānīyata”nti. “Alaṃ, bho, mamapimā mamapitā (ka.), mamapi (sī.) cattārīsā bhariyā sādisiyo. Tāpāhaṃ sabbā pahāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmi. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriyanti”.

322. “Then, sirs, the brahmin Mahāgovinda approached those six khattiyas. Having approached, he said to those six khattiyas: ‘Now, venerable sirs, seek another chaplain who will instruct your kingdoms. I wish, sirs, to go forth from the household life into homelessness. For as I have heard from Brahmā who speaks of the stench of the raw, these are not easily eradicated by one dwelling in a house. I will go forth, sirs, from the household life into homelessness.’ Then, sirs, those six khattiyas withdrew to one side and considered thus: ‘These brahmins are said to be greedy for wealth. What if we were to entice the brahmin Mahāgovinda with wealth?’ They approached the brahmin Mahāgovinda and said this: ‘Sir, in these seven kingdoms there is abundant wealth. From that, let as much as you need be taken.’ ‘Enough, sirs! I too have this abundant wealth, and it is because of you. Renouncing it all, I will go forth from the household life into homelessness. For as I have heard from Brahmā who speaks of the stench of the raw, these are not easily eradicated by one dwelling in a house. I will go forth, sirs, from the household life into homelessness.’ Then, sirs, those six khattiyas withdrew to one side and considered thus: ‘These brahmins are said to be greedy for women. What if we were to entice the brahmin Mahāgovinda with women?’ They approached the brahmin Mahāgovinda and said this: ‘Sir, in these seven kingdoms there are many women. From them, let as many as you desire be brought.’ ‘Enough, sirs! I too have forty wives of equal birth. Renouncing them all, I will go forth from the household life into homelessness. For as I have heard from Brahmā who speaks of the stench of the raw, these are not easily eradicated by one dwelling in a house. I will go forth, sirs, from the household life into homelessness.’”

323. “Sace [P 2.0246] bhavaṃ govindo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissati, mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatīti.

323. “If the venerable Govinda goes forth from the household life into homelessness, we too will go forth from the household life into homelessness. Then whatever your destination, that will be our destination.”

“Sace jahatha kāmāni, yattha satto puthujjano;

Ārambhavho daḷhā hotha, khantibalasamāhitā.

“If you abandon sensual pleasures, to which the common person is attached, arouse your energy, be firm, and be endowed with the strength of patience.”

“Esa maggo ujumaggo, esa maggo anuttaro;

Saddhammo sabbhi rakkhito, brahmalokūpapattiyāti.

“This is the straight path, this is the unsurpassed path for rebirth in the Brahmā world. It is the true teaching, guarded by the good.”

“Tena hi bhavaṃ govindo satta vassāni āgametu. Sattannaṃ vassānaṃ accayena mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī”ti.

“In that case, venerable Govinda, wait for seven years. After seven years have passed, we too will go forth from the household life into homelessness. Then whatever your destination, that will be our destination.”

“‘Aticiraṃ kho, bho, satta vassāni, nāhaṃ sakkomi, bhavante, satta vassāni āgametuṃ. Ko [T 2.0280] nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitānaṃ! Gamanīyo samparāyo, mantāyaṃ mantāya (bahūsu) boddhabbaṃ, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ, caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya’”nti. “Tena hi bhavaṃ govindo chabbassāni āgametu…pe… pañca vassāni āgametu… cattāri vassāni āgametu… tīṇi vassāni āgametu… dve vassāni āgametu… ekaṃ vassaṃ [M 2.0198] āgametu, ekassa vassassa accayena mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī”ti.

“‘Sirs, seven years is indeed too long. I am not able, honored sirs, to wait for you for seven years. For who, sirs, can possibly know of life? The next world is to be gone to. It should be understood with wisdom; what is wholesome should be done; the holy life should be practiced. For one who is born, there is no immortality. Just as I have heard in the presence of Brahmā as he spoke of the ‘raw stenches,’ they are not easily suppressed by one dwelling in a house. I shall go forth, sirs, from the household life into homelessness.’” “‘In that case, let the honorable Govinda wait for six years… let him wait for five years… let him wait for four years… let him wait for three years… let him wait for two years… let him wait for one year. After the passing of one year, we too shall go forth from the household life into homelessness. Then, whatever your destination, that will be our destination.’”

“‘Aticiraṃ kho, bho, ekaṃ vassaṃ, nāhaṃ sakkomi bhavante [P 2.0247] ekaṃ vassaṃ āgametuṃ. Ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitānaṃ! Gamanīyo samparāyo, mantāyaṃ boddhabbaṃ, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ[V 2.0181], caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya”nti. “Tena hi bhavaṃ govindo satta māsāni āgametu, sattannaṃ māsānaṃ accayena mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī”ti.

“‘Sirs, one year is indeed too long. I am not able, honored sirs, to wait for you for one year. For who, sirs, can possibly know of life? The next world is to be gone to. It should be understood with wisdom; what is wholesome should be done; the holy life should be practiced. For one who is born, there is no immortality.
