Just as I have heard in the presence of Brahmā as he spoke of the ‘raw stenches,’ they are not easily suppressed by one dwelling in a house. I shall go forth, sirs, from the household life into homelessness.’” “‘In that case, let the honorable Govinda wait for seven months. After the passing of seven months, we too shall go forth from the household life into homelessness. Then, whatever your destination, that will be our destination.’”

“‘Aticiraṃ kho, bho, satta māsāni, nāhaṃ sakkomi bhavante satta māsāni āgametuṃ. Ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitānaṃ. Gamanīyo samparāyo, mantāyaṃ boddhabbaṃ[T 2.0281], kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ, caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya”nti.

“‘Sirs, seven months is indeed too long. I am not able, honored sirs, to wait for you for seven months. For who, sirs, can possibly know of life? The next world is to be gone to. It should be understood with wisdom; what is wholesome should be done; the holy life should be practiced. For one who is born, there is no immortality. Just as I have heard in the presence of Brahmā as he spoke of the ‘raw stenches,’ they are not easily suppressed by one dwelling in a house. I shall go forth, sirs, from the household life into homelessness.’”

“‘Tena hi bhavaṃ govindo cha māsāni āgametu…pe… pañca māsāni āgametu… cattāri māsāni āgametu… tīṇi māsāni āgametu… dve māsāni āgametu… ekaṃ māsaṃ āgametu… addhamāsaṃ āgametu, addhamāsassa accayena mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī”ti.

“‘In that case, let the honorable Govinda wait for six months… let him wait for five months… let him wait for four months… let him wait for three months… let him wait for two months… let him wait for one month… let him wait for half a month. After the passing of half a month, we too shall go forth from the household life into homelessness. Then, whatever your destination, that will be our destination.’”

“‘Aticiraṃ kho, bho, addhamāso, nāhaṃ sakkomi bhavante addhamāsaṃ āgametuṃ. Ko nu kho pana, bho, jānāti jīvitānaṃ! Gamanīyo samparāyo, mantāyaṃ boddhabbaṃ, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ, caritabbaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, natthi jātassa amaraṇaṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya”nti. “Tena [P 2.0248] hi bhavaṃ govindo sattāhaṃ āgametu, yāva mayaṃ sake puttabhātaro rajjena rajje (syā.) anusāsissāma, sattāhassa [M 2.0199] accayena mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī”ti. “Na ciraṃ kho, bho, sattāhaṃ, āgamessāmahaṃ bhavante sattāha”nti.

“‘Sirs, half a month is indeed too long. I am not able, honored sirs, to wait for you for half a month. For who, sirs, can possibly know of life? The next world is to be gone to. It should be understood with wisdom; what is wholesome should be done; the holy life should be practiced. For one who is born, there is no immortality. Just as I have heard in the presence of Brahmā as he spoke of the ‘raw stenches,’ they are not easily suppressed by one dwelling in a house. I shall go forth, sirs, from the household life into homelessness.’” “‘In that case, let the honorable Govinda wait for seven days, while we instruct our own sons and brothers regarding the kingdom. After the passing of seven days, we too shall go forth from the household life into homelessness. Then, whatever your destination, that will be our destination.’” “‘Sirs, seven days is not long. I shall wait for you, honored sirs, for seven days.’”

Brāhmaṇamahāsālādīnaṃ āmantanā

Addressing the Wealthy Brahmins and Others

324. “Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena te satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā [T 2.0282] satta ca nhātakasatāni tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā te satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsāle satta ca nhātakasatāni [V 2.0182] etadavoca – “aññaṃ dāni bhavanto ācariyaṃ pariyesantu, yo bhavantānaṃ mante vācessati. Icchāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa. Te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā, pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya”nti. “Mā bhavaṃ govindo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbaji. Pabbajjā, bho, appesakkhā ca appalābhā ca; brahmaññaṃ mahesakkhañca mahālābhañcā”ti. “Mā bhavanto evaṃ avacuttha – “pabbajjā appesakkhā ca appalābhā ca, brahmaññaṃ mahesakkhañca mahālābhañcā”ti. Ko nu kho, bho, aññatra mayā mahesakkhataro vā mahālābhataro vā! Ahañhi, bho, etarahi rājāva raññaṃ brahmāva brāhmaṇānaṃ brahmānaṃ (sī. pī. ka.) devatāva gahapatikānaṃ. Tamahaṃ sabbaṃ pahāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmi. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ [P 2.0249] ajjhāvasatā. Pabbajissāmahaṃ, bho, agārasmā anagāriya”nti. “Sace bhavaṃ govindo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissati, mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī”ti.

324. Then, sirs, the brahmin Mahāgovinda approached those seven wealthy brahmins and the seven hundred graduates. Having approached, he said to those seven wealthy brahmins and seven hundred graduates: ‘Now, sirs, you should seek another teacher who will teach you the mantras. I wish, sirs, to go forth from the household life into homelessness. Just as I have heard in the presence of Brahmā as he spoke of the ‘raw stenches,’ they are not easily suppressed by one dwelling in a house. I shall go forth, sirs, from the household life into homelessness.’ ‘Do not, venerable Govinda, go forth from the household life into homelessness. Going forth, venerable sir, is of little influence and little gain, whereas the brahmin life is of great influence and great gain.’ ‘Do not speak thus, sirs: “Going forth is of little influence and little gain, whereas the brahmin life is of great influence and great gain.” For who, sirs, other than me is more influential or has greater gain? I, sirs, am now a king among kings, a Brahmā among brahmins, a deity among householders. Abandoning all that, I shall go forth from the household life into homelessness. Just as I have heard in the presence of Brahmā as he spoke of the ‘raw stenches,’ they are not easily suppressed by one dwelling in a house. I shall go forth, sirs, from the household life into homelessness.’ ‘If the venerable Govinda goes forth from the household life into homelessness, we too will go forth from the household life into homelessness. Then whatever your destination is, that will be our destination too.’”

Bhariyānaṃ āmantanā

Addressing the Wives

325. “Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo yena cattārīsā bhariyā [T 2.0283] sādisiyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā cattārīsā bhariyā sādisiyo etadavoca – “yā bhotīnaṃ icchati, sakāni vā ñātikulāni gacchatu aññaṃ vā bhattāraṃ pariyesatu. Icchāmahaṃ, bhotī, agārasmā [M 2.0200] anagāriyaṃ pabbajituṃ. Yathā kho pana me sutaṃ brahmuno āmagandhe bhāsamānassa, te na sunimmadayā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatā. Pabbajissāmahaṃ, bhotī, agārasmā anagāriya”nti. “Tvaññeva no ñāti ñātikāmānaṃ, tvaṃ pana bhattā bhattukāmānaṃ. Sace bhavaṃ govindo agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissati, mayampi agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāma, atha yā te gati, sā no gati bhavissatī”ti.

325. Then the brahmin Mahāgovinda approached his forty wives of equal standing. Having approached, he said to his forty wives of equal standing: 'Whichever of you ladies wishes may go to her own relatives' homes, or she may seek another husband. I wish, ladies, to go forth from the household life into homelessness. For I have heard from Brahmā, as he spoke of the stench of raw flesh, that these things are not easily eradicated by one dwelling in a household. I will go forth, ladies, from the household life into homelessness.' 'You alone are the relative for us who desire a relative; you alone are the husband for us who desire a husband. If the venerable Govinda goes forth from the household life into homelessness, we too will go forth from the household life into homelessness. Then whatever your destination is, that will be our destination too.'

Mahāgovindapabbajjā

The Going Forth of Mahāgovinda

326. “Atha kho, bho, mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo tassa sattāhassa accayena kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbaji. Pabbajitaṃ pana mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ satta ca rājāno khattiyā muddhāvasittā satta ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā satta ca nhātakasatāni cattārīsā ca bhariyā sādisiyo anekāni ca khattiyasahassāni anekāni [V 2.0183] ca brāhmaṇasahassāni anekāni ca gahapatisahassāni anekehi ca itthāgārehi itthiyo kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā mahāgovindaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitaṃ anupabbajiṃsu. Tāya sudaṃ, bho, parisāya parivuto mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo gāmanigamarājadhānīsu [P 2.0250] cārikaṃ carati. Yaṃ kho pana, bho, tena samayena mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo [T 2.0284] gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā upasaṅkamati, tattha rājāva hoti raññaṃ, brahmāva brāhmaṇānaṃ, devatāva gahapatikānaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena manussā khipanti vā upakkhalanti vā te evamāhaṃsu – “namatthu mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa, namatthu satta purohitassā’”ti.

326. Then, O devas, after seven days had passed, the brahmin Mahāgovinda shaved off his hair and beard, put on ochre robes, and went forth from the household life into homelessness. When the brahmin Mahāgovinda had gone forth, seven kings who were anointed khattiyas, seven wealthy brahmins, seven hundred graduates, forty wives of similar birth, and many thousands of khattiyas, many thousands of brahmins, many thousands of householders, and many women from harems shaved off their hair and beards, put on ochre robes, and followed the brahmin Mahāgovinda into homelessness. Surrounded by such an assembly, O devas, the brahmin Mahāgovinda wandered on tour among villages, market towns, and royal capitals. Whenever, O devas, the brahmin Mahāgovinda approached a village or market town at that time, there he was like a king among kings, like Brahmā among brahmins, like a deity among householders. And at that time, when people sneezed or stumbled, they would say: 'Homage to the brahmin Mahāgovinda! Homage to the purohita of the seven!'

327. “Mahāgovindo, bho, brāhmaṇo mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā vihāsi, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā vihāsi. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā…pe… abyāpajjena pharitvā vihāsi sāvakānañca brahmalokasahabyatāya maggaṃ desesi.

327. The brahmin Mahāgovinda, O devas, dwelled pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, identifying with all as with oneself, he dwelled pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness—vast, expansive, immeasurable, without enmity, without ill will. With a mind imbued with compassion… with a mind imbued with sympathetic joy… with a mind imbued with equanimity… he dwelled pervading without ill will and taught his disciples the path to companionship with the Brahma-world.

328. “Ye [M 2.0201] kho pana, bho, tena samayena mahāgovindassa brāhmaṇassa sāvakā sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājāniṃsu. Te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ brahmalokaṃ upapajjiṃsu. Ye na sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājāniṃsu, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā appekacce paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjiṃsu; appekacce nimmānaratīnaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjiṃsu; appekacce tusitānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjiṃsu; appekacce yāmānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ [P 2.0251] upapajjiṃsu; appekacce tāvatiṃsānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjiṃsu; appekacce cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjiṃsu; ye sabbanihīnaṃ kāyaṃ paripūresuṃ [T 2.0285] te gandhabbakāyaṃ paripūresuṃ. Iti kho, bho pana (syā. ka.), sabbesaṃyeva tesaṃ kulaputtānaṃ amoghā pabbajjā ahosi avañjhā saphalā saudrayā’”ti.

328. And, O devas, those disciples of the brahmin Mahāgovinda at that time who fully understood the entire teaching, at the dissolution of the body, after death, were reborn in a good destination, in the Brahma-world. Those who did not fully understand the entire teaching, at the dissolution of the body, after death, some were reborn into the company of the Paranimmitavasavattī devas; some were reborn into the company of the Nimmānaratī devas; some were reborn into the company of the Tusita devas; some were reborn into the company of the Yāma devas; some were reborn into the company of the Tāvatiṃsa devas; some were reborn into the company of the Cātumahārājika devas. Those who attained the very lowest rank were reborn into the company of the gandhabbas. Thus, O devas, for all those clansmen, their going forth was not in vain, not barren, but fruitful and beneficial.

329. “Sarati taṃ bhagavā”ti? “Sarāmahaṃ, pañcasikha. Ahaṃ tena samayena mahāgovindo brāhmaṇo ahosiṃ. Ahaṃ tesaṃ sāvakānaṃ brahmalokasahabyatāya maggaṃ desesiṃ. Taṃ kho pana me, pañcasikha, brahmacariyaṃ na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati, yāvadeva brahmalokūpapattiyā.

329. “Does the Blessed One remember that?” “I remember, Pañcasikha. At that time, I was the brahmin Mahāgovinda. I taught those disciples the path to companionship with the Brahma-world. However, Pañcasikha, that holy life of mine did not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to full enlightenment, or to Nibbāna, but only as far as rebirth in the Brahma-world.

Idaṃ [V 2.0184] kho pana me, pañcasikha, brahmacariyaṃ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Katamañca taṃ, pañcasikha, brahmacariyaṃ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo. Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Idaṃ kho taṃ, pañcasikha, brahmacariyaṃ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

This holy life of mine, Pañcasikha, leads exclusively to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to full enlightenment, and to Nibbāna. And what, Pañcasikha, is that holy life which leads exclusively to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to full enlightenment, and to Nibbāna? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, Pañcasikha, is that holy life which leads exclusively to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to full enlightenment, and to Nibbāna.

330. “Ye kho pana me, pañcasikha, sāvakā sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājānanti, te āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā [P 2.0252] sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti; ye na sabbena [T 2.0286] sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājānanti, te pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā [M 2.0202] opapātikā honti tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Ye na sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājānanti, appekacce tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino honti sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti karonti (sī. pī.). Ye na sabbena sabbaṃ sāsanaṃ ājānanti, appekacce tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā honti avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā. Iti kho, pañcasikha, sabbesaṃyeva imesaṃ kulaputtānaṃ amoghā pabbajjā pabbajā ahosi (ka.) avañjhā saphalā saudrayā”ti.

330. Now, Pañcasikha, those of my disciples who fully understand the entire teaching, through the destruction of the taints, having realized for themselves with direct knowledge in this very life, attain and abide in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom. Those who do not fully understand the entire teaching, with the destruction of the five lower fetters, are reborn spontaneously and attain final Nibbāna there, not liable to return from that world. Those who do not fully understand the entire teaching, some, with the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of lust, hatred, and delusion, are once-returners, who will come back to this world only once to make an end of suffering. Those who do not fully understand the entire teaching, some, with the destruction of the three fetters, are stream-enterers, not liable to fall to a state of woe, fixed in destiny, with enlightenment as their destination. Thus, Pañcasikha, for all these clansmen, the going forth is not in vain, not barren, but fruitful and beneficial.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano pañcasikho gandhabbaputto bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyīti.

The Blessed One said this. Pleased, Pañcasikha, son of a gandhabba, delighting in and rejoicing at the Blessed One’s words, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him respectfully, and vanished on that very spot.

Mahāgovindasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Mahāgovinda Sutta, the sixth, is concluded.

7. Mahāsamayasuttaṃ

7. The Great Assembly Sutta

331. Evaṃ [T 2.0287][M 2.0203][V 2.0185] me [P 2.0253] sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ mahāvane mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi; dasahi ca lokadhātūhi devatā yebhuyyena sannipatitā honti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca. Atha kho catunnaṃ suddhāvāsakāyikānaṃ devatānaṃ devānaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ mahāvane mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi sabbeheva arahantehi; dasahi ca lokadhātūhi devatā yebhuyyena sannipatitā honti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca. Yaṃnūna mayampi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato santike paccekaṃ gāthaṃ paccekagāthaṃ (sī. syā. pī.), paccekagāthā (ka. sī.) bhāseyyāmā”ti.

331. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Great Wood, together with a great assembly of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus, all of them arahants. And deities from the ten world-systems had, for the most part, assembled to see the Blessed One and the assembly of bhikkhus. Then this thought occurred to four deities of the Pure Abodes: 'This Blessed One is dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Great Wood, together with a great assembly of bhikkhus, with five hundred bhikkhus, all of them arahants; and deities from the ten world-systems have, for the most part, assembled to see the Blessed One and the assembly of bhikkhus. What if we too were to approach the Blessed One and, having approached, each recite a verse in his presence?'

332. Atha kho tā devatā seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya[P 2.0254], evameva suddhāvāsesu devesu antarahitā bhagavato purato pāturahesuṃ. Atha kho tā devatā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho ekā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

332. Then those deities, just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, even so, disappeared from the Pure Abode realms and appeared before the Blessed One. Then those deities, having paid homage to the Blessed One, stood to one side. Standing to one side, one deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Mahāsamayo pavanasmiṃ, devakāyā samāgatā;

Āgatamha [T 2.0288] imaṃ dhammasamayaṃ, dakkhitāye aparājitasaṅgha”nti.

“A great assembly is in the forest; the hosts of deities have gathered. We have come to this Dhamma assembly to see the unconquered Saṅgha.”

Atha kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then another deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Tatra bhikkhavo samādahaṃsu, cittamattano ujukaṃ akaṃsu ujukamakaṃsu (sī. syā. pī.);

Sārathīva nettāni gahetvā, indriyāni rakkhanti paṇḍitā”ti.

“Therein the bhikkhus have composed their minds, they have made their own minds straight; like a charioteer holding the reins, the wise ones guard their faculties.”

Atha [V 2.0186] kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then another deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Chetvā khīlaṃ chetvā palighaṃ, indakhīlaṃ ūhacca uhacca (ka.) manejā;

Te caranti suddhā vimalā, cakkhumatā sudantā susunāgā”ti.

“Having cut the stake, having severed the cross-bar, and having uprooted the city-post, they are without craving. They wander pure and stainless—young nāgas well-tamed by the One with Vision.”

Atha [M 2.0204][P 2.0255] kho aparā devatā bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi –

Then another deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

“Yekeci buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gatāse, na te gamissanti apāyabhūmiṃ;

Pahāya mānusaṃ dehaṃ, devakāyaṃ paripūressantī”ti.

“Whoever has gone to the Buddha for refuge, they will not go to a plane of woe. Having abandoned the human body, they will fill the host of deities.”

Devatāsannipātā

The Assembly of Deities

333. Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “yebhuyyena, bhikkhave, dasasu lokadhātūsu devatā sannipatitā honti ( ) sī. ipotthakesu natthi, tathāgataṃ dassanāya bhikkhusaṅghañca[T 2.0289]. Yepi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etaṃparamāyeva etaparamāyeva (sī. syā. pī.) devatā sannipatitā ahesuṃ seyyathāpi mayhaṃ etarahi. Yepi te, bhikkhave, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etaṃparamāyeva devatā sannipatitā bhavissanti seyyathāpi mayhaṃ etarahi. Ācikkhissāmi, bhikkhave, devakāyānaṃ nāmāni; kittayissāmi, bhikkhave, devakāyānaṃ nāmāni; desessāmi, bhikkhave, devakāyānaṃ nāmāni. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasikarotha, bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ.

333. Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: 'For the most part, bhikkhus, deities from the ten world-systems have assembled to see the Tathāgata and the assembly of bhikkhus. Bhikkhus, for those who were Blessed Ones, Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the past, for those Blessed Ones also, there were assemblies of deities of just this great a measure, just as there is for me now. Bhikkhus, for those who will be Blessed Ones, Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the future, for those Blessed Ones also, there will be assemblies of deities of just this great a measure, just as there is for me now. I shall announce, bhikkhus, the names of the hosts of deities; I shall proclaim, bhikkhus, the names of the hosts of deities; I shall declare, bhikkhus, the names of the hosts of deities. Listen to that, attend to it well; I shall speak.' 'So be it, venerable sir,' those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One.

334. Bhagavā etadavoca –

334. The Blessed One said this:

“Silokamanukassāmi, yattha bhummā tadassitā;

Ye sitā girigabbharaṃ, pahitattā samāhitā.

“I shall recite a verse. Where the earth-deities are based, there are those who resort to mountain clefts, with minds sent forth and composed;

“Puthūsīhāva sallīnā, lomahaṃsābhisambhuno;

Odātamanasā suddhā, vippasannamanāvilā” vippasannāmanāvilā (pī. ka.).

many, like secluded lions, having overcome hair-raising terror, with minds bright and pure, exceedingly serene and untroubled.”

Bhiyyo [V 2.0187][P 2.0256] pañcasate ñatvā, vane kāpilavatthave;

Tato āmantayī satthā, sāvake sāsane rate.

Knowing the more than five hundred disciples delighting in the Dispensation in the forest of Kapilavatthu, the Teacher then addressed them:

“Devakāyā abhikkantā, te vijānātha bhikkhavo”;

Te ca ātappamakaruṃ, sutvā buddhassa sāsanaṃ.

“‘Hosts of deities have approached; know them, O bhikkhus!’ And they, having heard the Buddha's instruction, made an ardent effort.

Tesaṃ pāturahu ñāṇaṃ, amanussānadassanaṃ;

Appeke satamaddakkhuṃ, sahassaṃ atha sattariṃ.

To them arose the knowledge for seeing non-human beings. Some saw a hundred, others a thousand, and still others seventy thousand.

Sataṃ [M 2.0205] eke sahassānaṃ, amanussānamaddasuṃ;

Appekenantamaddakkhuṃ[T 2.0290], disā sabbā phuṭā ahuṃ.

Some saw a hundred thousand non-human beings, while others saw a countless number. All directions were pervaded by them.

Tañca sabbaṃ abhiññāya, vavatthitvāna vavakkhitvāna (sī. syā. pī.), avekkhitvāna (ṭīkā) cakkhumā;

Tato āmantayī satthā, sāvake sāsane rate.

And having directly known and ascertained all that, the One with Vision, the Teacher, then addressed the disciples delighting in the Dispensation:

“Devakāyā abhikkantā, te vijānātha bhikkhavo;

Ye vohaṃ kittayissāmi, girāhi anupubbaso.

“Hosts of deities have approached; O bhikkhus, know them! I shall announce them to you in sequence with these verses.

335.“Sattasahassā te yakkhā, bhummā kāpilavatthavā.

335. “Seven thousand yakkhas there are, terrestrial, of Kapilavatthu,

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

Possessed of psychic power, radiant, beautiful, and glorious; rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Chasahassā hemavatā, yakkhā nānattavaṇṇino;

Iddhimanto jutīmanto jutīmanto (sī. pī.), vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“Six thousand yakkhas from Himavanta, of varied hue; possessed of psychic power, radiant, beautiful, and glorious; rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Sātāgirā tisahassā, yakkhā nānattavaṇṇino;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“Three thousand yakkhas from Sātāgiri, of varied hue; possessed of psychic power, radiant, beautiful, and glorious; rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Iccete [V 2.0188] soḷasasahassā, yakkhā nānattavaṇṇino;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“Thus these sixteen thousand yakkhas, of varied hue; possessed of psychic power, radiant, beautiful, and glorious; rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Vessāmittā [P 2.0257] pañcasatā, yakkhā nānattavaṇṇino;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā [T 2.0291] abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“Five hundred yakkhas from Vessāmitta, of varied hue; possessed of psychic power, radiant, beautiful, and glorious; rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Kumbhīro rājagahiko, vepullassa nivesanaṃ;

Bhiyyo naṃ satasahassaṃ, yakkhānaṃ payirupāsati;

Kumbhīro rājagahiko, sopāgā samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“Kumbhīra of Rājagaha, whose dwelling is Vepulla; more than a hundred thousand yakkhas wait upon him. That Kumbhīra of Rājagaha also came to the assembly in the forest.

336.“Purimañca disaṃ rājā, dhataraṭṭho pasāsati.

336. “The eastern direction is ruled by King Dhataraṭṭha,

Gandhabbānaṃ adhipati, mahārājā yasassiso.

Lord of the Gandhabbas, a great and glorious king.

“Puttāpi [M 2.0206] tassa bahavo, indanāmā mahabbalā;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“His sons are also many, named Inda, of great strength; possessed of psychic power, radiant, beautiful, and glorious; rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Dakkhiṇañca disaṃ rājā, virūḷho taṃ pasāsati tappasāsati (syā.);

Kumbhaṇḍānaṃ adhipati, mahārājā yasassiso.

“And the southern direction is ruled by King Virūḷha; he is the lord of the Kumbhaṇḍas, a great and glorious king.

“Puttāpi tassa bahavo, indanāmā mahabbalā;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“His sons are also many, named Inda, of great strength; possessed of psychic power, radiant, beautiful, and glorious; rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Pacchimañca disaṃ rājā, virūpakkho pasāsati;

Nāgānañca adhipati, mahārājā yasassiso.

“And the western direction is ruled by King Virūpakkha; he is the lord of the Nāgas, a great and glorious king.

“Puttāpi [V 2.0189][P 2.0258] tassa bahavo, indanāmā mahabbalā;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā [T 2.0292] abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“His sons are also many, named Inda, of great strength; possessed of psychic power, radiant, beautiful, and glorious; rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Uttarañca disaṃ rājā, kuvero taṃ pasāsati;

Yakkhānañca adhipati, mahārājā yasassiso.

“And the northern direction is ruled by King Kuvera; he is the lord of the Yakkhas, a great and glorious king.

“Puttāpi tassa bahavo, indanāmā mahabbalā;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“His sons are also many, named Inda, of great strength; possessed of psychic power, radiant, beautiful, and glorious; rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Purimaṃ disaṃ dhataraṭṭho, dakkhiṇena virūḷhako;

Pacchimena virūpakkho, kuvero uttaraṃ disaṃ.

“Dhataraṭṭha is in the eastern direction, Virūḷhaka in the southern, Virūpakkha in the western, and Kuvera in the northern direction.

“Cattāro te mahārājā, samantā caturo disā;

Daddallamānā daddaḷhamānā (ka.) aṭṭhaṃsu, vane kāpilavatthave.

“Those four great kings, covering the four directions all around, stood blazing in the forest of Kapilavatthu.

337.“Tesaṃ māyāvino dāsā, āguṃ āgū (syā.), āgu (sī. pī.) evamuparipi vañcanikā saṭhā.

337. “Their servants came—illusionists, deceitful, and fraudulent:

Māyā kuṭeṇḍu viṭeṇḍu veṭeṇḍu (sī. syā. pī.), viṭucca viṭū ca (syā.) viṭuṭo saha.

Māyā, Kuṭeṇḍu, Viṭeṇḍu, Viṭucca, and with them Viṭuṭo.

“Candano kāmaseṭṭho ca, kinnighaṇḍu kinnughaṇḍu (sī. syā. pī.) nighaṇḍu ca;

Panādo opamañño ca, devasūto ca mātali.

“Candana and Kāmaseṭṭha, Kinnighaṇḍu and Nighaṇḍu; Panāda and Opamañña, and Mātali the deva's charioteer.

“Cittaseno [M 2.0207] ca gandhabbo, naḷorājā janesabho janosabho (syā.);

Āgā pañcasikho ceva, timbarū sūriyavaccasā suriyavaccasā (sī. pī.).

“Cittasena the Gandhabba, King Naḷa, Janesabha; Pañcasikha also came, and Timbaru, and Sūriyavacchasā.

“Ete caññe ca rājāno, gandhabbā saha rājubhi;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“These and other gandhabba kings, together with the great kings, rejoicing, approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

338.“Athāguṃ [V 2.0190] nāgasā nāgā, vesālā sahatacchakā.

338. “Then came the Nāgas from Nāgasā, and those from Vesālī together with the Tacchakas.

Kambalassatarā [T 2.0293] āguṃ, pāyāgā saha ñātibhi.

Kambala and Assatara came, and those from Pāyāga with their kinsmen.

“Yāmunā dhataraṭṭhā ca, āgū nāgā yasassino;

Erāvaṇo mahānāgo, sopāgā samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“The glorious Nāgas from the Yamunā and of the Dhataraṭṭha clan came; the great Nāga Erāvaṇa also came to the assembly in the forest.

“Ye nāgarāje sahasā haranti, dibbā dijā pakkhi visuddhacakkhū;

Vehāyasā [P 2.0259] vehāsayā (sī. pī.) te vanamajjhapattā, citrā supaṇṇā iti tesa nāmaṃ.

“Those who forcibly seize the Nāga kings—divine, twice-born, winged, with purified eyes; soaring through the sky, they arrived in the midst of the forest. ‘Citrā Supaṇṇā’ is their name.

“Abhayaṃ tadā nāgarājānamāsi, supaṇṇato khemamakāsi buddho;

Saṇhāhi vācāhi upavhayantā, nāgā supaṇṇā saraṇamakaṃsu buddhaṃ.

“Then there was safety for the Nāga kings from the Supaṇṇas; the Buddha had made them secure. Addressing one another with gentle words, the Nāgas and Supaṇṇas took refuge in the Buddha.

339.“Jitā vajirahatthena, samuddaṃ asurāsitā.

339. “Conquered by the wielder of the thunderbolt were the Asuras dwelling in the ocean;

Bhātaro vāsavassete, iddhimanto yasassino.

These brothers of Vāsava are possessed of psychic power and are glorious.

“Kālakañcā mahābhismā kālakañjā mahābhiṃsā (sī. pī.), asurā dānaveghasā;

Vepacitti sucitti ca, pahārādo namucī saha.

“The Kālakañcā, greatly terrifying, the Dānaveghasa Asuras; Vepacitti and Sucitti, Pahārāda, and with them Namucī.

“Satañca baliputtānaṃ, sabbe verocanāmakā;

Sannayhitvā balisenaṃ balīsenaṃ (syā.), rāhubhaddamupāgamuṃ;

Samayodāni bhaddante, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“And a hundred sons of Bali, all named Verocana, having marshalled Bali's army, approached Rāhubhadda, saying: ‘Now is the time, good sir, for the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.’

340.“Āpo ca devā pathavī, tejo vāyo tadāgamuṃ.

340. “The devas of Water, Earth, Fire, and Wind then came.

Varuṇā vāraṇā vāruṇā (syā.) devā, somo ca yasasā saha.

The Varuṇa and Vāraṇa devas, and Soma together with Yasa, came.

“Mettā [T 2.0294] karuṇā kāyikā, āguṃ devā yasassino;

Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino.

“The glorious devas of Mettā and Karuṇā came. These ten hosts, in ten divisions, were all of varied hues.

“Iddhimanto [M 2.0208] jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

“Possessed of psychic power, radiant, beautiful, and glorious; rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Veṇḍudevā [V 2.0191] sahali ca veṇhūca devā sahalīca (sī. pī.), asamā ca duve yamā;

Candassūpanisā devā, candamāguṃ purakkhatvā.

“The Veṇḍu devas, Sahali, the Asamās, and the two Yamas came. The devas attendant on the moon came, with the moon at their forefront.

“Sūriyassūpanisā suriyassūpanisā (sī. syā. pī.) devā, sūriyamāguṃ purakkhatvā;

Nakkhattāni purakkhatvā, āguṃ mandavalāhakā.

“The devas attendant on the sun came, with the sun at their forefront. The devas attendant on the constellations came, with the constellations at their forefront. The Mandavalāhakas also came.

“Vasūnaṃ [P 2.0260] vāsavo seṭṭho, sakkopāgā purindado;

Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino.

“Vāsava, chief of the Vasus, Sakka the Purindada, came. These ten hosts, in ten divisions, were all of varied hues.

“Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

Endowed with power, radiant, splendid, and glorious, rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Athāguṃ sahabhū devā, jalamaggisikhāriva;

Ariṭṭhakā ca rojā ca, umāpupphanibhāsino.

Then came the Sahabhū devas, blazing like a flame of fire; the Ariṭṭhakas and Rojās, and those shining like the umā flower.

“Varuṇā sahadhammā ca, accutā ca anejakā;

Sūleyyarucirā āguṃ, āguṃ vāsavanesino;

Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino.

Varuṇa and Sahadhamma, Accuta and Anejaka, Sūleyya and Rucira came, and the Vāsavanesī devas came; these ten groups, in ten divisions, were all of diverse hues.

“Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

Endowed with power, radiant, splendid, and glorious, rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Samānā mahāsamanā, mānusā mānusuttamā;

Khiḍḍāpadosikā [T 2.0295] āguṃ, āguṃ manopadosikā.

The Samānā and Mahāsamānā, the Mānusā and Mānusuttamā; the Khiḍḍāpadosikā devas came, and the Manopadosikā devas came.

“Athāguṃ harayo devā, ye ca lohitavāsino;

Pāragā mahāpāragā, āguṃ devā yasassino;

Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino.

Then came the Hari devas, and those clothed in red; the glorious Pāragā and Mahāpāragā devas also came; these ten groups, in ten divisions, were all of diverse hues.

“Iddhimanto [V 2.0192] jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

Endowed with power, radiant, splendid, and glorious, rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Sukkā karambhā karumhā (sī. syā. pī.) aruṇā, āguṃ veghanasā saha;

Odātagayhā pāmokkhā, āguṃ devā vicakkhaṇā.

The Sukkā, Karambhā, and Aruṇā came, along with the Veghanasā; the chief Odātagayhā devas came, and the Vicakkhaṇā devas arrived.

“Sadāmattā [M 2.0209] hāragajā, missakā ca yasassino;

Thanayaṃ āga pajjunno, yo disā abhivassati.

The Sadāmattā and Hāragajā, and the glorious Missaka devas; Pajjunna, who rains upon the regions, came thundering.

“Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

These ten groups, in ten divisions, were all of diverse hues; endowed with power, radiant, splendid, and glorious, rejoicing, they approached the assembly of bhikkhus in the forest.

“Khemiyā [P 2.0261] tusitā yāmā, kaṭṭhakā ca yasassino;

Lambītakā lāmaseṭṭhā, jotināmā ca āsavā;

Nimmānaratino āguṃ, athāguṃ paranimmitā.

The Khemiyā, Tusitā, and Yāmā deities, and the glorious Kaṭṭhaka deities; the Lambītakā and Lāmaseṭṭhā, the Jotināmā and Āsavā; the Nimmānaratī deities came, and then came the Paranimmitā deities.

“Dasete dasadhā kāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino;

Iddhimanto jutimanto, vaṇṇavanto yasassino;

Modamānā abhikkāmuṃ, bhikkhūnaṃ samitiṃ vanaṃ.

These ten groups of deities, established in ten divisions, all of diverse hues; endowed with power, radiant, splendid, and glorious, rejoicing, they approached the assembly of monks in the forest.

“Saṭṭhete [T 2.0296] devanikāyā, sabbe nānattavaṇṇino;

Nāmanvayena āgacchuṃ āgañchuṃ (sī. syā. pī.), ye caññe sadisā saha.

These sixty groups of deities, all of diverse hues, came according to their name-grouping, along with others who were similar.

“‘Pavuṭṭhajātimakhilaṃ pavutthajātiṃ akhilaṃ (sī. pī.), oghatiṇṇamanāsavaṃ;

Dakkhemoghataraṃ nāgaṃ, candaṃva asitātigaṃ’.

‘Let us see the one whose rebirth is finished, who is without a stake, who has crossed the flood, free from taints; let us see the Great Being who has crossed over the flood, who has gone beyond darkness, like the moon.’

341.“Subrahmā paramatto ca paramattho ca (ka.), puttā iddhimato saha.

341. Subrahmā and Paramatta, sons of the Powerful One, came together.

Sanaṅkumāro tisso ca, sopāga samitiṃ vanaṃ.

Sanaṅkumāra and Tissa, they too came to the assembly in the forest.

“Sahassaṃ [V 2.0193] brahmalokānaṃ, mahābrahmābhitiṭṭhati;

Upapanno jutimanto, bhismākāyo yasassiso.

A thousand from the Brahmā worlds came. A Great Brahmā stands supreme over them, arisen there, radiant, of awesome form, and glorious.

“Dasettha issarā āguṃ, paccekavasavattino;

Tesañca majjhato āga, hārito parivārito.

Among them, ten lords came, each wielding their own power; and from their midst came Hārita, surrounded by his retinue.

342.“Te ca sabbe abhikkante, sainde sinde (syā.) deve sabrahmake.

342. When all of them had arrived—the deities with Indra and the Brahmās—

Mārasenā abhikkāmi, passa kaṇhassa mandiyaṃ.

Māra’s army advanced. Behold the foolishness of the Dark One!

“‘Etha [P 2.0262] gaṇhatha bandhatha, rāgena baddhamatthu vo;

Samantā parivāretha, mā vo muñcittha koci naṃ’.

‘Come, seize them, bind them! Let them be bound by your passion! Surround them on all sides! Let not a single one of you release any of them!’

“Iti [M 2.0210] tattha mahāseno, kaṇho senaṃ apesayi;

Pāṇinā talamāhacca, saraṃ katvāna bheravaṃ.

Thus there the great general, the Dark One, sent forth his army, striking the ground with his palm and making a terrifying sound.

“Yathā pāvussako megho, thanayanto savijjuko; +

Tadā so paccudāvatti, saṅkuddho asayaṃvase asayaṃvasī (sī. pī.).

Like a storm cloud in the rainy season, thundering and with lightning; then he retreated, enraged and unable to gain control.

343. Tañca sabbaṃ abhiññāya, vavatthitvāna cakkhumā.

343. Having directly known and ascertained all that, the One with Vision...

Tato [T 2.0297] āmantayī satthā, sāvake sāsane rate.

Then the Teacher addressed his disciples, who delighted in his Dispensation.

“Mārasenā abhikkantā, te vijānātha bhikkhavo;

Te ca ātappamakaruṃ, sutvā buddhassa sāsanaṃ;

Vītarāgehi pakkāmuṃ, nesaṃ lomāpi iñjayuṃ.

‘Māra’s armies have advanced; recognize them, O monks!’ And having heard the Buddha’s instruction, they exerted themselves. The armies retreated from those free of passion; they could not stir even a single hair of theirs.

“‘Sabbe vijitasaṅgāmā, bhayātītā yasassino;

Modanti saha bhūtehi, sāvakā te janesutā”ti.

‘All are victorious in battle, having gone beyond fear, and are glorious; they, your disciples, renowned among the people, rejoice together with the noble beings.’

Mahāsamayasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Mahāsamaya Sutta, the seventh, is concluded.

8. Sakkapañhasuttaṃ

8. The Sutta on Sakka's Questions

344. Evaṃ [T 2.0298][M 2.0211][V 2.0194][P 2.0264] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā magadhesu viharati, pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena sakkassa devānamindassa ussukkaṃ udapādi bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Atha kho sakkassa devānamindassa etadahosi – “kahaṃ nu kho bhagavā etarahi viharati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho”ti? Addasā kho sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṃ magadhesu viharantaṃ pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṃ. Disvāna deve tāvatiṃse āmantesi – “ayaṃ, mārisā, bhagavā magadhesu viharati, pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṃ. Yadi pana, mārisā, mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyāma arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti? “Evaṃ bhaddantavā”ti kho devā tāvatiṃsā sakkassa devānamindassa paccassosuṃ.

344. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Magadhans, to the east of Rājagaha, in a brahmin village named Ambasaṇḍa. To the north of it, on Vediyaka Mountain, he was in the Indasāla Cave. Now on that occasion, an eagerness to see the Blessed One arose in Sakka, the lord of the devas. Then this thought occurred to Sakka, the lord of the devas: ‘Where might the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, be dwelling now?’ Sakka, the lord of the devas, then saw the Blessed One dwelling among the Magadhans, to the east of Rājagaha, in the brahmin village named Ambasaṇḍa, and to the north of it, on Vediyaka Mountain, in the Indasāla Cave. Having seen him, he addressed the Tāvatiṃsa devas: ‘Sirs, the Blessed One is dwelling among the Magadhans, to the east of Rājagaha, in the brahmin village named Ambasaṇḍa, and to the north of it, on Vediyaka Mountain, in the Indasāla Cave. Suppose, sirs, we were to approach that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for a visit?’ ‘So be it, venerable sir,’ the Tāvatiṃsa devas replied to Sakka, the lord of the devas.

345. Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcasikhaṃ gandhabbadevaputtaṃ gandhabbaputtaṃ (syā.) āmantesi – “ayaṃ, tāta pañcasikha, bhagavā magadhesu viharati pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate indasālaguhāyaṃ. Yadi pana[T 2.0299], tāta pañcasikha, mayaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyāma arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti? “Evaṃ bhaddantavā”ti kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāya sakkassa devānamindassa anucariyaṃ upāgami.

345. Then Sakka, the lord of the devas, addressed Pañcasikha, the gandhabba deva-son: ‘Dear Pañcasikha, the Blessed One is dwelling among the Magadhans, to the east of Rājagaha, in the brahmin village named Ambasaṇḍa, and to the north of it, on Vediyaka Mountain, in the Indasāla Cave. Suppose, dear Pañcasikha, we were to approach that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for a visit?’ ‘So be it, venerable sir,’ Pañcasikha, the gandhabba deva-son, replied to Sakka, the lord of the devas. Taking his lute, which was the color of a ripe wood-apple, he went to accompany Sakka, the lord of the devas.

346. Atha kho sakko devānamindo devehi tāvatiṃsehi parivuto pañcasikhena gandhabbadevaputtena purakkhato seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya; evameva devesu tāvatiṃsesu antarahito magadhesu pācīnato rājagahassa ambasaṇḍā nāma brāhmaṇagāmo, tassuttarato vediyake pabbate paccuṭṭhāsi. Tena kho pana [V 2.0195] samayena vediyako pabbato [M 2.0212] atiriva obhāsajāto hoti ambasaṇḍā ca brāhmaṇagāmo yathā taṃ devānaṃ devānubhāvena. Apissudaṃ parito gāmesu manussā evamāhaṃsu – “ādittassu nāmajja vediyako pabbato jhāyatisu jhāyatassu (syā.), pajjhāyitassu (sī. pī.) nāmajja vediyako pabbato jalatisu jalatassu (syā.), jalitassu (sī. pī.) nāmajja vediyako pabbato kiṃsu nāmajja vediyako pabbato atiriva obhāsajāto ambasaṇḍā ca brāhmaṇagāmo”ti saṃviggā lomahaṭṭhajātā ahesuṃ.

346. Then Sakka, lord of the devas, surrounded by the Tāvatiṃsa devas and preceded by Pañcasikha, the gandhabba deva-son, just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, vanished from among the Tāvatiṃsa devas and reappeared in Magadha, to the east of Rājagaha, at the brahmin village named Ambasaṇḍa, on Mount Vediyaka to its north. On that occasion, Mount Vediyaka and the brahmin village of Ambasaṇḍa were exceedingly radiant, as if by the divine power of the devas. And the people in the surrounding villages said this: ‘Today Mount Vediyaka is ablaze! Today Mount Vediyaka is burning! Today Mount Vediyaka is in flames! What is the reason that today Mount Vediyaka and the brahmin village of Ambasaṇḍa are so exceedingly radiant?’ They were alarmed, and their hair stood on end.

347. Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcasikhaṃ gandhabbadevaputtaṃ āmantesi – “durupasaṅkamā [P 2.0265] kho, tāta pañcasikha, tathāgatā mādisena, jhāyī jhānaratā, tadantaraṃ tadanantaraṃ (sī. syā. pī. ka.) paṭisallīnā. Yadi pana tvaṃ, tāta pañcasikha, bhagavantaṃ paṭhamaṃ pasādeyyāsi, tayā, tāta, paṭhamaṃ pasāditaṃ pacchā mayaṃ [T 2.0300] taṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkameyyāma arahantaṃ sammāsambuddha”nti. “Evaṃ bhaddantavā”ti kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāya yena indasālaguhā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā “ettāvatā me bhagavā neva atidūre bhavissati nāccāsanne, saddañca me sossatī”ti ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi.

347. Then Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed Pañcasikha, the gandhabba deva-son: ‘Dear Pañcasikha, the Tathāgatas are difficult for one like me to approach. They are absorbed in meditation, delight in meditation, and remain in seclusion in the intervals. If you, dear Pañcasikha, would first gain the Blessed One’s favor, then after you have gained his favor, we may approach that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for a sight of him.’ ‘So be it, Your Reverence,’ replied Pañcasikha, the gandhabba deva-son, to Sakka, lord of the devas. Taking his lute, pale-yellow like a ripe beluva fruit, he approached the Indasāla Cave. Having approached, he stood to one side, thinking: ‘From this spot, the Blessed One will be neither too far from me nor too near, and he will hear my sound.’”

Pañcasikhagītagāthā

The Verses of Pañcasikha's Song

348. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ veḷuvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāya (syā.) assāvesi, imā ca gāthā abhāsi buddhūpasañhitā dhammūpasañhitā saṅghūpasañhitā arahantūpasañhitā kāmūpasañhitā –

348. Standing to one side, Pañcasikha, the gandhabba deva-son, played upon his pale-yellow beluva-wood lute and sang these verses connected with the Buddha, connected with the Dhamma, connected with the Saṅgha, connected with the Arahants, and connected with sensual desire:

“Vande te pitaraṃ bhadde, timbaruṃ sūriyavacchase;

Yena jātāsi kalyāṇī, ānandajananī mama.

“I pay homage to your father, Timbaru, O gracious Sūriyavacchasā; by whom you were born, O lovely one, who brings delight to me.

“Vātova sedataṃ kanto, pānīyaṃva pipāsato;

Aṅgīrasi piyāmesi, dhammo arahatāmiva.

“As the wind is dear to one who sweats, as water to one who is thirsty, you are dear to me, O Aṅgīrasī, as the Dhamma is to the Arahants.

“Āturasseva [P 2.0266] bhesajjaṃ, bhojanaṃva jighacchato;

Parinibbāpaya maṃ bhadde, jalantamiva vārinā.

“As medicine to the sick, as food to the hungry, O gracious one, extinguish this fire in me, as one quenches a blazing fire with water.

“Sītodakaṃ [M 2.0213][V 2.0196] pokkharaṇiṃ, yuttaṃ kiñjakkhareṇunā;

Nāgo ghammābhitattova, ogāhe te thanūdaraṃ.

“As an elephant tormented by heat plunges into a lotus pond of cool water, fragrant with pollen, so would I plunge into your bosom.

“Accaṅkusova nāgova, jitaṃ me tuttatomaraṃ;

Kāraṇaṃ nappajānāmi, sammatto lakkhaṇūruyā.

“Like an elephant that has overcome the goad, thinking, ‘I have conquered the prod and the spear,’ I know no reason, maddened by your shapely thighs.

“Tayi [T 2.0301] gedhitacittosmi, cittaṃ vipariṇāmitaṃ;

Paṭigantuṃ na sakkomi, vaṅkaghastova ambujo.

“My mind is enthralled by you, my mind is transformed; I am unable to turn back, like a fish that has swallowed a hook.

“Vāmūru saja maṃ bhadde, saja maṃ mandalocane;

Palissaja maṃ kalyāṇi, etaṃ me abhipatthitaṃ.

“O one with shapely thighs, embrace me, gracious one; embrace me, O one with gentle eyes; embrace me fully, O lovely one—this is my heart’s desire.

“Appako vata me santo, kāmo vellitakesiyā;

Anekabhāvo samuppādi, arahanteva dakkhiṇā.

“Though my desire was but small, for you, the one with curling hair, it has grown a thousandfold, like an offering made to an Arahant.

“Yaṃ me atthi kataṃ puññaṃ, arahantesu tādisu;

Taṃ me sabbaṅgakalyāṇi, tayā saddhiṃ vipaccataṃ.

“Whatever merit I have made toward such Arahants, O one beautiful in every limb, may that merit of mine ripen together with you.

“Yaṃ [P 2.0267] me atthi kataṃ puññaṃ, asmiṃ pathavimaṇḍale;

Taṃ me sabbaṅgakalyāṇi, tayā saddhiṃ vipaccataṃ.

“Whatever merit I have made on this earthly sphere, O one beautiful in every limb, may that merit ripen together with you.

“Sakyaputtova jhānena, ekodi nipako sato;

Amataṃ muni jigīsāno jigiṃsāno (sī. syā. pī.), tamahaṃ sūriyavacchase.

“As the sage, the Sakyan son, unified through jhāna, prudent and mindful, strives for the Deathless, so do I strive for you, O Sūriyavacchasā.

“Yathāpi muni nandeyya, patvā sambodhimuttamaṃ;

Evaṃ nandeyyaṃ kalyāṇi, missībhāvaṃ gato tayā.

“Just as the sage would rejoice, having attained supreme enlightenment, so would I rejoice, O lovely one, having come into union with you.

“Sakko ce me varaṃ dajjā, tāvatiṃsānamissaro;

Tāhaṃ bhadde vareyyāhe, evaṃ kāmo daḷho mama.

“If Sakka, lord of the Tāvatiṃsa, were to grant me a boon, it is you, gracious one, that I would choose; so strong is my desire for you.

“Sālaṃva [V 2.0197] na ciraṃ phullaṃ, pitaraṃ te sumedhase;

Vandamāno namassāmi, yassā setādisī pajā”ti.

“I pay homage to your father, O one of good wisdom, who is like a sāla tree in fresh bloom, and whose offspring is such as you.”

349. Evaṃ vutte bhagavā pañcasikhaṃ gandhabbadevaputtaṃ etadavoca – “saṃsandati [T 2.0302] kho te, pañcasikha, tantissaro gītassarena, gītassaro ca tantissarena; na ca pana neva pana (syā.) te pañcasikha, tantissaro gītassaraṃ ativattati, gītassaro ca tantissaraṃ. Kadā saṃyūḷhā pana te, pañcasikha, imā gāthā buddhūpasañhitā dhammūpasañhitā [M 2.0214] saṅghūpasañhitā arahantūpasañhitā kāmūpasañhitā”ti? “Ekamidaṃ, bhante, samayaṃ bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhe paṭhamābhisambuddho[P 2.0268]. Tena kho panāhaṃ, bhante, samayena bhaddā nāma sūriyavacchasā timbaruno gandhabbarañño dhītā, tamabhikaṅkhāmi. Sā kho pana, bhante, bhaginī parakāminī hoti; sikhaṇḍī nāma mātalissa saṅgāhakassa putto, tamabhikaṅkhati. Yato kho ahaṃ, bhante, taṃ bhaginiṃ nālatthaṃ kenaci pariyāyena. Athāhaṃ beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ ādāya yena timbaruno gandhabbarañño nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā beluvapaṇḍuvīṇaṃ assāvesiṃ, imā ca gāthā abhāsiṃ buddhūpasañhitā dhammūpasañhitā saṅghūpasañhitā arahantūpasañhitā kāmūpasañhitā –

349. When this was said, the Blessed One said this to Pañcasikha, the gandhabba deva-son: ‘Pañcasikha, the sound of your strings is in harmony with the sound of your song, and the sound of your song is in harmony with the sound of your strings. The sound of your strings does not overwhelm the sound of your song, nor does the sound of your song overwhelm the sound of your strings. When, Pañcasikha, did you compose these verses connected with the Buddha, the Dhamma, the Saṅgha, the Arahants, and with sensual desire?’ ‘On one occasion, venerable sir, the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā on the bank of the river Nerañjarā, at the foot of the Goatherd’s Banyan Tree, right after his full enlightenment. At that time, venerable sir, I was in love with Bhaddā Sūriyavacchasā, the daughter of Timbaru, king of the gandhabbas. But that young lady, venerable sir, was in love with another; she desired Sikhaṇḍī, the son of Mātali the charioteer. As I was unable to win that young lady by any means, venerable sir, I took my pale-yellow beluva-wood lute and went to the dwelling of Timbaru, king of the gandhabbas. Having gone there, I played upon my lute and sang these verses connected with the Buddha, the Dhamma, the Saṅgha, the Arahants, and with sensual desire:

“Vande te pitaraṃ bhadde, timbaruṃ sūriyavacchase;

Yena jātāsi kalyāṇī, ānandajananī mama. …pe…

“‘I pay homage to your father, Timbaru, O gracious Sūriyavacchasā; by whom you were born, O lovely one, who brings delight to me. …and so on…

Sālaṃva na ciraṃ phullaṃ, pitaraṃ te sumedhase;

Vandamāno namassāmi, yassā setādisī pajā”ti.

“‘…I pay homage to your father, O one of good wisdom, who is like a sāla tree in fresh bloom, and whose offspring is such as you.’”

“Evaṃ vutte, bhante, bhaddā sūriyavacchasā maṃ etadavoca – ‘na kho me, mārisa, so bhagavā sammukhā diṭṭho api ca sutoyeva me so bhagavā [T 2.0303] devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sudhammāyaṃ sabhāyaṃ upanaccantiyā. Yato kho tvaṃ, mārisa, taṃ bhagavantaṃ kittesi, hotu no ajja samāgamo’ti. Soyeva [P 2.0269] no, bhante, tassā bhaginiyā saddhiṃ samāgamo ahosi. Na ca dāni tato pacchā”ti.

“When this was said, venerable sir, Bhaddā Sūriyavacchasā said this to me: ‘Indeed, good sir, I have not seen that Blessed One face to face, but I have only heard of that Blessed One while dancing in the Sudhammā assembly hall of the Tāvatiṃsa devas. Since you, good sir, praise that Blessed One, let there be a meeting for us today.’ And so, venerable sir, that very meeting with that sister took place for us. And there has been no meeting since then until now.”

Sakkūpasaṅkama

Sakka’s Approach

350. Atha [V 2.0198] kho sakkassa devānamindassa etadahosi – “paṭisammodati pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto bhagavatā, bhagavā ca pañcasikhenā”ti. Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcasikhaṃ gandhabbadevaputtaṃ āmantesi – “abhivādehi me tvaṃ, tāta pañcasikha, bhagavantaṃ – ‘sakko, bhante, devānamindo sāmacco saparijano bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti”. “Evaṃ bhaddantavā”ti kho pañcasikho gandhabbadevaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādeti – “sakko, bhante, devānamindo sāmacco saparijano bhagavato [M 2.0215] pāde sirasā vandatī”ti. “Evaṃ sukhī hotu, pañcasikha, sakko devānamindo sāmacco saparijano; sukhakāmā hi devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā ye caññe santi puthukāyā”ti.

350. Then it occurred to Sakka, the lord of the devas: “Pañcasikha the gandhabba-deva is exchanging joyful speech with the Blessed One, and the Blessed One with Pañcasikha.” Then Sakka, the lord of the devas, addressed Pañcasikha the gandhabba-deva: “Pay homage to the Blessed One on my behalf, dear Pañcasikha, saying: ‘Venerable sir, Sakka, the lord of the devas, together with his ministers and retinue, bows with his head at the Blessed One’s feet.’” “So be it, your reverence,” replied Pañcasikha the gandhabba-deva to Sakka, the lord of the devas. Then he paid homage to the Blessed One, saying: “Venerable sir, Sakka, the lord of the devas, together with his ministers and retinue, bows with his head at the Blessed One’s feet.” “May Sakka, the lord of the devas, together with his ministers and retinue, be happy, Pañcasikha; for devas, humans, asuras, nāgas, gandhabbas, and whatever other diverse beings there are, all desire happiness.”

351. Evañca pana tathāgatā evarūpe mahesakkhe yakkhe abhivadanti. Abhivadito sakko devānamindo bhagavato indasālaguhaṃ pavisitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Devāpi tāvatiṃsā indasālaguhaṃ pavisitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Pañcasikhopi gandhabbadevaputto indasālaguhaṃ pavisitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi.

351. And thus do the Tathāgatas welcome such powerful yakkhas. Having been welcomed, Sakka, the lord of the devas, entered the Indasāla Cave, paid homage to the Blessed One, and stood to one side. The Tāvatiṃsa devas also entered the Indasāla Cave, paid homage to the Blessed One, and stood to one side. Pañcasikha the gandhabba-deva also entered the Indasāla Cave, paid homage to the Blessed One, and stood to one side.

Tena kho pana samayena indasālaguhā [T 2.0304] visamā santī samā samapādi, sambādhā santī urundā uruddā (ka.) samapādi, andhakāro guhāyaṃ antaradhāyi, āloko udapādi yathā taṃ devānaṃ [P 2.0270] devānubhāvena.

At that time, the Indasāla Cave, being uneven, became level; being cramped, it became spacious. The darkness in the cave disappeared, and light arose, by the divine power of the devas.

352. Atha kho bhagavā sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ etadavoca – “acchariyamidaṃ āyasmato kosiyassa, abbhutamidaṃ āyasmato kosiyassa tāva bahukiccassa bahukaraṇīyassa yadidaṃ idhāgamana”nti. “Cirapaṭikāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamitukāmo; api ca devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ kehici kehici kehici (syā.) kiccakaraṇīyehi byāvaṭo; evāhaṃ nāsakkhiṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṃ. Ekamidaṃ, bhante, samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati salaḷāgārake. Atha khvāhaṃ, bhante, sāvatthiṃ agamāsiṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Tena kho pana, bhante, samayena bhagavā aññatarena samādhinā nisinno hoti, bhūjati bhuñjatī ca (sī. pī.), bhujagī (syā.) ca nāma vessavaṇassa mahārājassa paricārikā bhagavantaṃ paccupaṭṭhitā hoti, pañjalikā namassamānā tiṭṭhati. Atha khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhūjatiṃ etadavocaṃ [V 2.0199] – ‘abhivādehi me tvaṃ, bhagini, bhagavantaṃ – “sakko, bhante, devānamindo [T 2.0305] sāmacco saparijano bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī”ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhante, sā bhūjati maṃ etadavoca – ‘akālo kho, mārisa, bhagavantaṃ dassanāya; paṭisallīno bhagavā’ti. ‘Tena [P 2.0271] hī, bhagini, yadā bhagavā tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhito hoti, atha mama vacanena bhagavantaṃ abhivādehi – “sakko, bhante, devānamindo [M 2.0216] sāmacco saparijano bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī”ti. Kacci me sā, bhante, bhaginī bhagavantaṃ abhivādesi? Sarati bhagavā tassā bhaginiyā vacana”nti? “Abhivādesi maṃ sā, devānaminda, bhaginī, sarāmahaṃ tassā bhaginiyā vacanaṃ. Api cāhaṃ āyasmato nemisaddena cakkanemisaddena (syā.) tamhā samādhimhā vuṭṭhito”ti. “Ye te, bhante, devā amhehi paṭhamataraṃ tāvatiṃsakāyaṃ upapannā, tesaṃ me sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘yadā tathāgatā loke uppajjanti arahanto sammāsambuddhā, dibbā kāyā paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyā’ti. Taṃ me idaṃ, bhante, sakkhidiṭṭhaṃ yato tathāgato loke uppanno arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, dibbā kāyā paripūrenti, hāyanti asurakāyāti.

352. Then the Blessed One said this to Sakka, the lord of the devas: “It is wonderful, venerable Kosiya, it is marvelous, venerable Kosiya, that you, with so many duties and tasks, have come here.” “For a long time, venerable sir, I have wished to approach the Blessed One for a visit. But I was occupied with various duties and tasks of the Tāvatiṃsa devas; thus I was unable to approach the Blessed One for a visit. On one occasion, venerable sir, the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Salaḷāgāra. Then, venerable sir, I went to Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One. At that time, venerable sir, the Blessed One was seated in a certain meditation, and a female attendant of the great king Vessavaṇa named Bhūjati was attending upon the Blessed One, standing with joined palms, paying homage. Then, venerable sir, I said this to Bhūjati: ‘Sister, please pay homage to the Blessed One on my behalf, saying: “Venerable sir, Sakka, lord of the devas, with his ministers and retinue, bows with his head at the feet of the Blessed One.”’ When this was said, venerable sir, that Bhūjati replied to me: ‘It is not the right time, good sir, to see the Blessed One; the Blessed One is in seclusion.’ ‘Then, sister, when the Blessed One has arisen from that meditation, please pay homage to the Blessed One with my words, saying: “Venerable sir, Sakka, lord of the devas, with his ministers and retinue, bows with his head at the feet of the Blessed One.”’ Did that sister of mine, venerable sir, pay homage to the Blessed One? Does the Blessed One remember that sister’s words?” “She did pay homage to me, lord of the devas, that sister. I remember that sister’s words. Moreover, I arose from that meditation at the sound of the venerable one’s wheel-rim.” “Those devas, venerable sir, who arose in the Tāvatiṃsa realm before us—from them I have heard in their presence, received in their presence: ‘When Tathāgatas, Arahants, Perfectly Self-Enlightened Ones, arise in the world, the divine hosts are filled, and the asura hosts decline.’ This, venerable sir, I have witnessed myself: since the Tathāgata has arisen in the world, an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, the divine hosts are filled, and the asura hosts decline.”

Gopakavatthu

The Story of Gopaka

353. “Idheva, bhante, kapilavatthusmiṃ gopikā nāma sakyadhītā ahosi buddhe pasannā dhamme pasannā saṅghe pasannā sīlesu paripūrakārinī. Sā itthittaṃ itthicittaṃ (syā.) virājetvā purisattaṃ purisacittaṃ (syā.) bhāvetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā. Devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyataṃ amhākaṃ puttattaṃ ajjhupagatā. Tatrapi naṃ evaṃ jānanti – ‘gopako devaputto, gopako devaputto’ti. Aññepi, bhante, tayo bhikkhū bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ caritvā hīnaṃ gandhabbakāyaṃ upapannā. Te pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārayamānā amhākaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ āgacchanti amhākaṃ pāricariyaṃ. Te amhākaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ āgate amhākaṃ pāricariyaṃ gopako devaputto paṭicodesi [P 2.0272] – ‘kutomukhā nāma tumhe[T 2.0306], mārisā, tassa bhagavato dhammaṃ assuttha āyuhittha (syā.) – ahañhi nāma itthikā samānā buddhe pasannā dhamme pasannā saṅghe pasannā sīlesu paripūrakārinī itthittaṃ virājetvā purisattaṃ bhāvetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā, devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyataṃ sakkassa devānamindassa puttattaṃ ajjhupagatā. Idhāpi maṃ evaṃ jānanti “gopako devaputto gopako devaputto’ti. Tumhe pana, mārisā, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ caritvā hīnaṃ gandhabbakāyaṃ upapannā. Duddiṭṭharūpaṃ vata, bho, addasāma, ye mayaṃ addasāma [M 2.0217] sahadhammike hīnaṃ gandhabbakāyaṃ upapanne’ti. Tesaṃ, bhante, gopakena devaputtena paṭicoditānaṃ dve [V 2.0200] devā diṭṭheva dhamme satiṃ paṭilabhiṃsu kāyaṃ brahmapurohitaṃ, eko pana devo kāme ajjhāvasi.

353. “Venerable sir, right here in Kapilavatthu, there was a Sakyan daughter named Gopikā. She had faith in the Buddha, faith in the Dhamma, faith in the Sangha, and was one who fulfilled the precepts. Having become dispassionate towards the female state and having cultivated the male state, upon the breakup of the body, after death, she was reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. She arose in the company of the Tāvatiṃsa devas and attained the state of being our son. There, too, they know him thus: ‘Gopaka the devaputta, Gopaka the devaputta.’ Furthermore, venerable sir, three other bhikkhus, having lived the holy life under the Blessed One, were reborn into the lowly retinue of gandhabbas. They, endowed and furnished with the five strands of sensual pleasure, enjoying themselves, come to attend on us, for our service. When they had come to attend on us for our service, Gopaka the devaputta rebuked them: ‘Sirs, with what purpose did you listen to the Dhamma of that Blessed One? For I, though a woman, had faith in the Buddha, faith in the Dhamma, faith in the Sangha, and was one who fulfilled the precepts. Having become dispassionate towards the female state and having cultivated the male state, upon the breakup of the body, after death, I was reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. I arose in the company of the Tāvatiṃsa devas and attained the state of being a son to Sakka, lord of the devas. Here, too, they know me thus: “Gopaka the devaputta, Gopaka the devaputta.” But you, sirs, having lived the holy life under the Blessed One, have been reborn into the lowly retinue of gandhabbas. Truly, sirs, we have seen an unfitting sight! We have seen our companions in the Dhamma reborn into the lowly retinue of gandhabbas!’ Of them, venerable sir, being rebuked by Gopaka the devaputta, two devas regained mindfulness in this very life and attained the Brahma-ministerial body; but one deva remained dwelling in sensual pleasures.”

354.“‘Upāsikā cakkhumato ahosiṃ,

354. “‘I was a female lay follower of the One with Vision,

Nāmampi mayhaṃ ahu ‘gopikā’ti;

Buddhe ca dhamme ca abhippasannā,

Saṅghañcupaṭṭhāsiṃ pasannacittā.

My name was Gopikā; with supreme faith in the Buddha and the Dhamma, and with a faithful mind, I attended upon the Sangha.

“‘Tasseva buddhassa sudhammatāya,

Sakkassa puttomhi mahānubhāvo;

Mahājutīko tidivūpapanno,

Jānanti maṃ idhāpi ‘gopako’ti.

‘By the very goodness of that Buddha’s Dhamma, I am Sakka’s son, of great power and great radiance, reborn in the celestial realm; here too they know me as ‘Gopaka.’

“‘Athaddasaṃ [T 2.0307] bhikkhavo diṭṭhapubbe,

Gandhabbakāyūpagate vasīne;

Imehi te gotamasāvakāse,

Ye ca mayaṃ pubbe manussabhūtā.

‘Then I saw bhikkhus, seen before, residing, having reached the retinue of the gandhabbas. These were those disciples of Gotama, and we too were formerly human beings.

“‘Annena pānena upaṭṭhahimhā,

Pādūpasaṅgayha sake nivesane;

Kutomukhā [P 2.0273] nāma ime bhavanto,

Buddhassa dhammāni paṭiggahesuṃ buddhassa dhammaṃ na paṭiggahesuṃ (syā.).

‘We attended upon them with food and drink in our own home, ministering to their feet. With what purpose did these venerable ones receive the Buddha’s truths?

“‘Paccattaṃ veditabbo hi dhammo,

Sudesito cakkhumatānubuddho;

Ahañhi tumheva upāsamāno,

Sutvāna ariyāna subhāsitāni.

‘For the Dhamma, well-proclaimed and realized by the One with Vision, is to be known for oneself. I, too, attending upon you, heard the well-spoken truths of the Noble Ones.

“‘Sakkassa [V 2.0201] puttomhi mahānubhāvo,

Mahājutīko tidivūpapanno;

Tumhe pana seṭṭhamupāsamānā,

Anuttaraṃ brahmacariyaṃ caritvā.

‘I am Sakka’s son, of great power, of great radiance, arisen in the celestial realm. But you, attending upon the Supreme One, having lived the unsurpassed holy life,

“‘Hīnaṃ [M 2.0218] kāyaṃ upapannā bhavanto,

Anānulomā bhavatūpapatti;

Duddiṭṭharūpaṃ vata addasāma,

Sahadhammike hīnakāyūpapanne.

‘—were reborn into a lowly retinue, venerable sirs. How unfitting is your rebirth! Truly, we have seen an unfitting sight: our companions in the Dhamma reborn into a lowly retinue.

“‘Gandhabbakāyūpagatā [T 2.0308] bhavanto,

Devānamāgacchatha pāricariyaṃ;

Agāre vasato mayhaṃ,

Imaṃ passa visesataṃ.

‘Having reached the retinue of the gandhabbas, venerable sirs, you come to serve the devas. Behold this distinction of mine, who dwelt in a celestial mansion.

“‘Itthī hutvā svajja pumomhi devo,

Dibbehi kāmehi samaṅgibhūto’;

Te coditā gotamasāvakena,

Saṃvegamāpādu samecca gopakaṃ.

‘Formerly a woman, today I am a male, a deva, endowed with divine sensual pleasures.’ Rebuked by the disciple of Gotama, they experienced spiritual urgency and approached Gopaka together.

“‘Handa viyāyāma vigāyāma (syā.), vitāyāma (pī.) byāyāma viyāyamāma (sī. pī.),

Mā no mayaṃ parapessā ahumhā’;

Tesaṃ [P 2.0274] duve vīriyamārabhiṃsu,

Anussaraṃ gotamasāsanāni.

‘Come now, let us strive, let us exert ourselves! Let us not be the servants of others!’ Two of them roused their energy, recollecting the teaching of Gotama.

“Idheva cittāni virājayitvā,

Kāmesu ādīnavamaddasaṃsu;

Te kāmasaṃyojanabandhanāni,

Pāpimayogāni duraccayāni.

‘Right here, having become dispassionate in their minds, they saw the danger in sensual pleasures; those bonds and fetters of sensual desire, the yokes of the Evil One, so hard to overcome—

“Nāgova [V 2.0202] sannāni guṇāni sandānaguṇāni (sī. pī.), santāni guṇāni (syā.) chetvā,

Deve tāvatiṃse atikkamiṃsu;

Saindā devā sapajāpatikā,

Sabbe sudhammāya sabhāyupaviṭṭhā.

‘—like a great elephant shattering its strong bonds, they transcended the Tāvatiṃsa devas. All the devas, with Inda and Pajāpati, were seated in the Sudhammā assembly hall.

“Tesaṃ [T 2.0309] nisinnānaṃ abhikkamiṃsu,

Vīrā virāgā virajaṃ karontā;

Te disvā saṃvegamakāsi vāsavo,

Devābhibhū devagaṇassa majjhe.

‘As they were seated, those heroes, dispassionate, producing the stainless state, went beyond them. Seeing them, Vāsava, the overlord of devas, expressed his spiritual urgency amidst the host of devas.

“‘Imehi [M 2.0219] te hīnakāyūpapannā,

Deve tāvatiṃse abhikkamanti’;

Saṃvegajātassa vaco nisamma,

So gopako vāsavamajjhabhāsi.

‘These who were reborn into a lowly retinue now surpass the Tāvatiṃsa devas.’ Having heeded the words of him in whom spiritual urgency had arisen, that Gopaka addressed Vāsava.

“‘Buddho janindatthi manussaloke,

Kāmābhibhū sakyamunīti ñāyati;

Tasseva te puttā satiyā vihīnā,

Coditā mayā te satimajjhalatthuṃ.

‘O lord of beings, there is a Buddha in the human world, known as the Sakyan Sage, the conqueror of sensual pleasures. These are his sons who were devoid of mindfulness; rebuked by me, they afterwards gained mindfulness.

“‘Tiṇṇaṃ [P 2.0275] tesaṃ āvasinettha avasīnettha (pī.) eko,

Gandhabbakāyūpagato vasīno;

Dve ca sambodhipathānusārino,

Devepi hīḷenti samāhitattā.

‘Of those three beings, one remains here, a resident, having gone to the retinue of the gandhabbas. But two, followers of the path to awakening, with composed minds, look down even upon the devas.

“‘Etādisī dhammappakāsanettha,

Na tattha kiṃkaṅkhati koci sāvako;

Nitiṇṇaoghaṃ vicikicchachinnaṃ,

Buddhaṃ namassāma jinaṃ janindaṃ’.

‘Such is the proclamation of the Dhamma here that no disciple has any doubt. We pay homage to the Buddha, the Conqueror, the Lord of Beings, who has crossed the flood and cut off uncertainty.’

“Yaṃ [T 2.0310][V 2.0203] te dhammaṃ idhaññāya,

Visesaṃ ajjhagaṃsu ajjhagamaṃsu (syā.) te;

Kāyaṃ brahmapurohitaṃ,

Duve tesaṃ visesagū.

“Venerable sir, of those devas, two, by understanding your Dhamma here, realized a special state and attained the Brahma-ministerial body.

“Tassa dhammassa pattiyā,

Āgatamhāsi mārisa;

Katāvakāsā bhagavatā,

Pañhaṃ pucchemu mārisā”ti.

‘For the attainment of that Dhamma, we have come, venerable sir. Having been given the opportunity by the Blessed One, let us ask a question, venerable sir.’”

355. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – “dīgharattaṃ visuddho kho ayaṃ yakkho sakko (sī. syā. pī.), yaṃ kiñci maṃ pañhaṃ pucchissati, sabbaṃ taṃ atthasañhitaṃyeva pucchissati, no anatthasañhitaṃ. Yañcassāhaṃ puṭṭho byākarissāmi, taṃ khippameva ājānissatī”ti.

355. Then it occurred to the Blessed One: “This yakkha has been pure for a long time. Whatever question he asks me will all be connected with what is beneficial, not with what is unbeneficial. And whatever I answer when asked, he will quickly understand.”

356. Atha [M 2.0220] kho bhagavā sakkaṃ devānamindaṃ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi –

356. Then the Blessed One addressed Sakka, lord of the devas, in verse:

“Puccha vāsava maṃ pañhaṃ, yaṃ kiñci manasicchasi;

Tassa tasseva pañhassa, ahaṃ antaṃ karomi te”ti.

“Ask me, Vāsava, whatever question you wish for in your mind. Of each and every question, I will make an end for you.”

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

The First Recitation Section is finished.

357. Katāvakāso [P 2.0276] sakko devānamindo bhagavatā imaṃ bhagavantaṃ devānamindo bhagavantaṃ imaṃ (sī. pī.) paṭhamaṃ pañhaṃ apucchi –

357. Having been given leave by the Blessed One, Sakka, the ruler of the devas, asked the Blessed One this first question:

“Kiṃ saṃyojanā nu kho, mārisa, devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā ye [T 2.0311] caññe santi puthukāyā, te – ‘averā adaṇḍā asapattā abyāpajjā viharemu averino’ti iti ca nesaṃ hoti, atha ca pana saverā sadaṇḍā sasapattā sabyāpajjā viharanti saverino”ti? Itthaṃ sakko devānamindo bhagavantaṃ pañhaṃ imaṃ paṭhamaṃ pañhaṃ (sī. pī.) apucchi. Tassa bhagavā pañhaṃ puṭṭho byākāsi –

‘Venerable sir, by what fetters are devas, humans, asuras, nāgas, gandhabbas, and whatever other diverse beings there are, bound? Though they wish, “May we dwell without enmity, without violence, without rivalry, without ill will, and free from foes,” yet they dwell with enmity, with violence, with rivalry, with ill will, and with foes.’ Thus Sakka, the ruler of the devas, asked the Blessed One this question. The Blessed One, having been asked, answered him:

“Issāmacchariyasaṃyojanā kho, devānaminda, devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā ye caññe [V 2.0204] santi puthukāyā, te – ‘averā adaṇḍā asapattā abyāpajjā viharemu averino’ti iti ca nesaṃ hoti, atha ca pana saverā sadaṇḍā sasapattā sabyāpajjā viharanti saverino”ti. Itthaṃ bhagavā sakkassa devānamindassa pañhaṃ puṭṭho byākāsi. Attamano sakko devānamindo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandi anumodi – “evametaṃ, bhagavā, evametaṃ, sugata. Tiṇṇā mettha kaṅkhā vigatā kathaṃkathā bhagavato pañhaveyyākaraṇaṃ sutvā”ti.

‘Ruler of the devas, it is by the fetters of envy and stinginess that devas, humans, asuras, nāgas, gandhabbas, and whatever other diverse beings there are, are bound. Though they wish, “May we dwell without enmity, without violence, without rivalry, without ill will, and free from foes,” yet they dwell with enmity, with violence, with rivalry, with ill will, and with foes.’ Thus the Blessed One, having been asked, answered the question of Sakka, the ruler of the devas. Delighted, Sakka, the ruler of the devas, rejoiced in and approved of the Blessed One’s words, saying: ‘So it is, Blessed One! So it is, Well-Spoken One! Having heard the Blessed One’s explanation of the question, my doubt is crossed over, my uncertainty is gone.’

358. Itiha sakko devānamindo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā [P 2.0277] anumoditvā bhagavantaṃ uttariṃ uttariṃ (sī. syā. pī.) pañhaṃ apucchi –

358. Thus Sakka, the ruler of the devas, having rejoiced in and approved of the Blessed One’s words, asked the Blessed One a further question:

“Issāmacchariyaṃ pana, mārisa, kiṃnidānaṃ kiṃsamudayaṃ kiṃjātikaṃ kiṃpabhavaṃ; kismiṃ sati issāmacchariyaṃ hoti; kismiṃ asati issāmacchariyaṃ na hotī”ti? “Issāmacchariyaṃ kho, devānaminda, piyāppiyanidānaṃ piyāppiyasamudayaṃ piyāppiyajātikaṃ piyāppiyapabhavaṃ; piyāppiye sati issāmacchariyaṃ hoti, piyāppiye asati issāmacchariyaṃ na hotī”ti.

‘Venerable sir, what is the source of envy and stinginess, what is their origin, what is their birth, and what is their provenance? When what exists do envy and stinginess come to be? When what does not exist do envy and stinginess not come to be?’ ‘Ruler of the devas, envy and stinginess have what is liked and disliked as their source, what is liked and disliked as their origin, what is liked and disliked as their birth, and what is liked and disliked as their provenance. When what is liked and disliked exists, envy and stinginess come to be. When what is liked and disliked does not exist, envy and stinginess do not come to be.’

“Piyāppiyaṃ [M 2.0221] kho pana, mārisa, kiṃnidānaṃ kiṃsamudayaṃ kiṃjātikaṃ kiṃpabhavaṃ; kismiṃ sati piyāppiyaṃ hoti; kismiṃ asati piyāppiyaṃ na hotī”ti? “Piyāppiyaṃ kho, devānaminda, chandanidānaṃ chandasamudayaṃ chandajātikaṃ chandapabhavaṃ; chande sati piyāppiyaṃ hoti; chande asati piyāppiyaṃ na hotī”ti.

‘But, venerable sir, what is the source of what is liked and disliked, what is its origin, what is its birth, and what is its provenance? When what exists does what is liked and disliked come to be? When what does not exist does what is liked and disliked not come to be?’ ‘Ruler of the devas, what is liked and disliked has desire as its source, desire as its origin, desire as its birth, and desire as its provenance. When desire exists, what is liked and disliked comes to be. When desire does not exist, what is liked and disliked does not come to be.’

“Chando kho pana, mārisa, kiṃnidāno kiṃsamudayo kiṃjātiko kiṃpabhavo; kismiṃ sati chando [T 2.0312] hoti; kismiṃ asati chando na hotī”ti? “Chando kho, devānaminda, vitakkanidāno vitakkasamudayo vitakkajātiko vitakkapabhavo; vitakke sati chando hoti; vitakke asati chando na hotī”ti.

‘But, venerable sir, what is the source of desire, what is its origin, what is its birth, and what is its provenance? When what exists does desire come to be? When what does not exist does desire not come to be?’ ‘Ruler of the devas, desire has thought as its source, thought as its origin, thought as its birth, and thought as its provenance. When thought exists, desire comes to be. When thought does not exist, desire does not come to be.’

“Vitakko kho pana, mārisa, kiṃnidāno kiṃsamudayo kiṃjātiko kiṃpabhavo; kismiṃ sati vitakko hoti; kismiṃ asati vitakko na hotī”ti? “Vitakko kho, devānaminda, papañcasaññāsaṅkhānidāno papañcasaññāsaṅkhāsamudayo papañcasaññāsaṅkhājātiko papañcasaññāsaṅkhāpabhavo; papañcasaññāsaṅkhāya sati vitakko hoti; papañcasaññāsaṅkhāya asati vitakko na hotī”ti.

‘But, venerable sir, what is the source of thought, what is its origin, what is its birth, and what is its provenance? When what exists does thought come to be? When what does not exist does thought not come to be?’ ‘Ruler of the devas, thought has the aggregate of perceptions of proliferation as its source, the aggregate of perceptions of proliferation as its origin, the aggregate of perceptions of proliferation as its birth, and the aggregate of perceptions of proliferation as its provenance. When the aggregate of perceptions of proliferation exists, thought comes to be. When the aggregate of perceptions of proliferation does not exist, thought does not come to be.’

“Kathaṃ [V 2.0205] paṭipanno pana, mārisa, bhikkhu papañcasaññāsaṅkhānirodhasāruppagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ paṭipanno hotī”ti?

‘But, venerable sir, how is a monk practicing the path that is suitable for and leads to the cessation of the aggregate of perceptions of proliferation?’

Vedanākammaṭṭhānaṃ

The Meditation Subject of Feeling

359. “Somanassaṃpāhaṃ [P 2.0278] pahaṃ (sī. pī.), cāhaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampi. Domanassaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampi. Upekkhaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi, asevitabbampi.

359. “Ruler of the devas, I declare mental pleasure to be of two kinds: that which should be cultivated and that which should not be cultivated. Ruler of the devas, I declare mental pain to be of two kinds: that which should be cultivated and that which should not be cultivated. Ruler of the devas, I declare equanimity to be of two kinds: that which should be cultivated and that which should not be cultivated.”

360. “Somanassaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi sevitabbampi, asevitabbampīti iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ, kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Tattha yaṃ jaññā somanassaṃ ‘imaṃ kho me somanassaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpaṃ somanassaṃ na sevitabbaṃ. Tattha yaṃ jaññā somanassaṃ ‘imaṃ kho [T 2.0313] me somanassaṃ sevato [M 2.0222] akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpaṃ somanassaṃ sevitabbaṃ. Tattha yaṃ ce savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ, yaṃ ce avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ, ye avitakke avicāre, te se (sī. pī.) paṇītatare. Somanassaṃpāhaṃ, devānaminda, duvidhena vadāmi sevitabbampi, asevitabbampīti. Iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

360. “‘Ruler of the devas, I declare mental pleasure to be of two kinds: that which should be cultivated and that which should not be cultivated.’ Now, in reference to what was this said? In this regard, should one know of a certain mental pleasure: ‘When I cultivate this mental pleasure, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline,’ such a mental pleasure should not be cultivated.
