Then the deva Pāyāsi approached the Venerable Gavampati; having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Gavampati and stood to one side. The Venerable Gavampati said to the deva Pāyāsi, who was standing to one side: “Who are you, friend?” “I, venerable sir, am Pāyāsi the chieftain.” “Were you not, friend, one who held the view: ‘There is no other world, there are no spontaneously arisen beings, there is no fruit or result of good and bad deeds’?” “Indeed, venerable sir, I was one who held that view: ‘There is no other world, there are no spontaneously arisen beings, there is no fruit or result of good and bad deeds.’ However, I was led away from that evil view by the noble Kumārakassapa.” “And the young man named Uttara, who was in charge of your donation—where was he reborn?” “Venerable sir, the young man named Uttara, who was in charge of my donation, having given gifts respectfully, with his own hand, with reverence, and not as if discarded, upon the breakup of the body, after death, was reborn in a good destination, the heavenly world, in the company of the Tāvatiṃsa gods. But I, venerable sir, having given gifts disrespectfully, not with my own hand, without reverence, and as if discarded, upon the breakup of the body, after death, was reborn in the company of the gods of the Four Great Kings in the empty Serīsaka mansion. Therefore, Venerable Gavampati, go to the human world and announce this: ‘Give gifts respectfully, give with your own hand, give with reverence, and give not as if discarded. Pāyāsi the chieftain, having given gifts disrespectfully, not with his own hand, without reverence, and as if discarded, upon the breakup of the body, after death, was reborn in the company of the gods of the Four Great Kings in the empty Serīsaka mansion. But the young man named Uttara, who was in charge of that donation, having given gifts respectfully, with his own hand, with reverence, and not as if discarded, upon the breakup of the body, after death, was reborn in a good destination, the heavenly world, in the company of the Tāvatiṃsa gods.’”

Atha kho āyasmā gavampati manussalokaṃ āgantvā evamārocesi – “sakkaccaṃ dānaṃ detha, sahatthā dānaṃ detha, cittīkataṃ dānaṃ detha, anapaviddhaṃ dānaṃ detha. Pāyāsi rājañño asakkaccaṃ dānaṃ datvā asahatthā dānaṃ datvā acittīkataṃ dānaṃ datvā apaviddhaṃ dānaṃ datvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapanno suññaṃ serīsakaṃ vimānaṃ. Yo pana tassa dāne vāvaṭo ahosi uttaro [M 2.0283] nāma māṇavo, so sakkaccaṃ dānaṃ datvā [V 2.0263] sahatthā dānaṃ datvā cittīkataṃ dānaṃ datvā anapaviddhaṃ [P 2.0358] dānaṃ datvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapanno devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyata”nti.

Then the Venerable Gavampati, having come to the human world, announced thus: ‘Give gifts respectfully, give with your own hand, give with reverence, and give not as if discarded. Pāyāsi the chieftain, having given gifts disrespectfully, not with his own hand, without reverence, and as if discarded, upon the breakup of the body, after death, was reborn in the company of the gods of the Four Great Kings in the empty Serīsaka mansion. But the young man named Uttara, who was in charge of that donation, having given gifts respectfully, with his own hand, with reverence, and not as if discarded, upon the breakup of the body, after death, was reborn in a good destination, the heavenly world, in the company of the Tāvatiṃsa gods.’”

Pāyāsisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dasamaṃ.

The tenth, the Pāyāsi Sutta, is concluded.

Mahāvaggo niṭṭhito.

The Great Chapter is concluded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of it:

Mahāpadāna nidānaṃ, nibbānañca sudassanaṃ;

Janavasabha govindaṃ, samayaṃ sakkapañhakaṃ;

Mahāsatipaṭṭhānañca, pāyāsi dasamaṃ bhave satipaṭṭhānapāyāsi, mahāvaggassa saṅgaho (sī. pī.) satipaṭṭhānapāyāsi, mahāvaggoti vuccatīti (syā.).

The Mahāpadāna and Nidāna, Nibbāna and Sudassana; Janavasabha and Govinda, Samaya and Sakkapañha; and the Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna, with Pāyāsi as the tenth.

Mahāvaggapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Pāli of the Great Chapter is concluded.
